desc: A security flaw has been discovered in uvwt agentdock up to 1.1.1. This impacts the function runtimeAPIHandler of the file internal/httpx/runtime_api.go of the component Runtime Management API. Performing a manipulation results in missing authentication. The attack can be initiated remotely. The patch is named 69cc02fabbd35f980d471d67306a035f9a5c9a9e. Applying a patch is the recommended action to fix this issue.
title: uvwt agentdock Runtime Management API runtime_api.go runtimeAPIHandler missing authentication

desc: A vulnerability was identified in Gimanh taskview-community up to 1.56.0. This affects the function loginByCode of the file api/src/tv-modules/auth/AuthController.ts of the component Magic-link Login. Such manipulation leads to improper restriction of excessive authentication attempts. It is possible to launch the attack remotely. The attack requires a high level of complexity. The exploitability is reported as difficult. Upgrading to version 1.57.0 mitigates this issue. The name of the patch is 3e30a70d662c36b3dfad0f45a4ef8a5030536fa7. It is suggested to upgrade the affected component.
title: Gimanh taskview-community Magic-link Login AuthController.ts loginByCode excessive authentication

desc: emailjs 3.2.0 before 5.0.4 contains an address parsing vulnerability in addressparser that allows attackers to inject hidden recipients by abusing nested comments, semicolons, or backslash escapes. Attackers can craft recipient strings that pass conformant-parser allow lists but make emailjs send RCPT TO commands to attacker-chosen addresses, disclosing message content.
title: emailjs 3.2.0 before 5.0.4 Recipient Injection via addressparser Tokenizer

desc: GPAC before 26.07.0 contains a path traversal vulnerability in the httpout filter that allows unauthenticated remote attackers to read files outside the rdirs root by sending unnormalized request paths. Attackers can send GET or HEAD requests containing ../ or %2e%2e%2f sequences to read configuration files, TLS private keys, or credentials readable by the gpac process.
title: GPAC before 26.07.0 Path Traversal via httpout Server Filter

desc: Net-SNMP snmpd through 5.9.5.2 and 5.10.pre1 before 5.10.pre3 contains a heap out-of-bounds write vulnerability in view_parse_oid() that allows authenticated attackers with SNMP write access to corrupt heap memory. Attackers can send a single SET to vacmViewTreeFamilyTable whose index begins with sub-identifier 4294967295, causing a one-byte write before a malloc(0) allocation and crashing snmpd.
title: Net-SNMP snmpd through 5.9.5.2 and 5.10.pre1 before 5.10.pre3 Heap Out-of-Bounds Write via view_parse_oid()

desc: CherryTree through 1.7.3 contains a LaTeX rendering filter bypass vulnerability in _is_latex_text_safe() that allows attackers to read local files by building blocked command names with TeX macro expansion. Attackers can craft a document with a LaTeX node using \csname verbatiminput\endcsname to render user-readable files into the embedded note image when opened.
title: CherryTree through 1.7.3 Local File Read via LaTeX Filter Bypass

desc: CherryTree through 1.7.3 contains a denial of service vulnerability that allows attackers to crash the application through uncaught std::stoi/std::stoll exceptions on malformed XML attributes. Attackers can craft a document with non-numeric or out-of-range char_offset, frame_width, frame_height, col_max, or time attributes to repeatedly crash CherryTree and block access to content.
title: CherryTree through 1.7.3 Denial of Service via Malformed XML Attributes

desc: Assimp through 6.0.6 contains an integer overflow vulnerability in OgreBinarySerializer::ReadGeometryVertexBuffer that allows attackers to crash applications via crafted Ogre binary .mesh files. Attackers can supply a large vertex count that wraps the 32-bit size calculation, desynchronising parsing and causing aiScene teardown to delete uninitialised mesh pointers.
title: Assimp through 6.0.6 Integer Overflow via OgreBinarySerializer::ReadGeometryVertexBuffer

desc: A vulnerability was found in go-dev-frame sponge up to 1.16.1. The affected element is an unknown function of the file pkg/jwt/option.go of the component JWT. The manipulation results in use of hard-coded cryptographic key . The attack may be performed from remote. The exploit has been made public and could be used. The project maintainer announces, that a separate auth certification center will be used to replace this old JWT package.
title: go-dev-frame sponge JWT option.go hard-coded key

desc: A vulnerability was determined in shopizer-ecommerce shopizer up to 3.2.5. The impacted element is an unknown function of the file sm-core/src/main/resources/authentication.properties. This manipulation causes use of hard-coded cryptographic key . It is possible to initiate the attack remotely. The exploit has been publicly disclosed and may be utilized. The pull request to fix this issue awaits acceptance.
title: shopizer-ecommerce shopizer authentication.properties hard-coded key

desc: Listmonk 2.3.0 through 7.0.0-beta.2 contains an information disclosure vulnerability that allows unauthenticated visitors to view draft, scheduled or cancelled campaigns marked for archiving via the public archive page. Attackers who know or guess the campaign UUID or predictable subject-derived archive slug can request the archive page and read unpublished campaign content before it is sent.
title: Listmonk 2.3.0 through 7.0.0-beta.2 Unpublished Campaign Disclosure via Public Archive

desc: WinFsp before 2.2.26323 contains a kernel pool out-of-bounds write vulnerability in FspEaBufferFromFileSystemValidate that allows unprivileged local users to corrupt kernel memory via crafted extended-attribute responses. Attackers can mount a WinFsp file system and answer QueryEa or SetEa requests with malformed NextEntryOffset values, writing zero bytes past the pool allocation to crash the system.
title: WinFsp before 2.2.26323 Kernel Pool Out-of-Bounds Write via FspEaBufferFromFileSystemValidate

desc: A vulnerability has been found in itsourcecode Insurance Management System 1.0. The impacted element is an unknown function of the file search.php. Such manipulation of the argument key leads to sql injection. The attack may be performed from remote. The exploit has been disclosed to the public and may be used.
title: itsourcecode Insurance Management System search.php sql injection

desc: A vulnerability was found in Cloud-CV EvalAI up to 30128ca50ab24a0c65e556d78199309e8ecc3eae. This affects an unknown function of the file settings/common.py of the component JWT Authentication. Performing a manipulation of the argument SECRET_KEY results in use of hard-coded cryptographic key . It is possible to initiate the attack remotely. The exploit has been made public and could be used. The patch is named 9c430a7c8675b1d4ae83925ec0da044c703d8441. It is suggested to install a patch to address this issue.
title: Cloud-CV EvalAI JWT Authentication common.py hard-coded key

desc: A vulnerability was determined in SonicJs-Org SonicJS up to 3.0.1. This impacts the function AuthManager.verifyToken of the file packages/core/src/middleware/auth.ts. Executing a manipulation can lead to use of hard-coded cryptographic key . It is possible to launch the attack remotely. The exploit has been publicly disclosed and may be utilized. A patch should be applied to remediate this issue. Vendor confirmed remediation by adding a bootstrap.ts security check that logs a warning in development and throws a hard error in production when JWT_SECRET is missing or still the default value.
title: SonicJs-Org SonicJS auth.ts AuthManager.verifyToken hard-coded key

desc: A flaw has been found in itsourcecode Event Management System 1.0. The affected element is an unknown function of the file /admin/manage_venue.php. This manipulation of the argument ID causes sql injection. The attack is possible to be carried out remotely. The exploit has been published and may be used.
title: itsourcecode Event Management System manage_venue.php sql injection

desc: Apprise before 1.12.0 contains an improper certificate validation vulnerability in NotifyEmail.send that ignores verify_certificate for SMTPS and STARTTLS connections. Network-positioned attackers can present self-signed or mismatched certificates to intercept SMTP AUTH credentials and notification contents, or modify and suppress notifications.
title: Apprise before 1.12.0 Missing TLS Certificate Validation in mailtos:// SMTP

desc: A security vulnerability has been detected in OpenAirInterface oai-cn5g-upf up to 2.2.2. This issue affects the function pfcp_user_id_ie::load_from of the file pfcp/3gpp_29.244.hpp of the component PFCP N4 User ID IE Type 141 Parser. The manipulation leads to heap-based buffer overflow. Remote exploitation of the attack is possible. The exploit has been disclosed publicly and may be used. The vendor was contacted early about this disclosure.
title: OpenAirInterface oai-cn5g-upf PFCP N4 User ID IE Type 141 3gpp_29.244.hpp load_from heap-based overflow

desc: A vulnerability was detected in OpenAirInterface oai-cn5g-amf up to 2.2.2. Impacted is the function amf_sbi::discover_smf of the file src/amf-app/amf_sbi.cpp of the component AMF. The manipulation results in denial of service. The attack can be executed remotely. The exploit is now public and may be used. The patch is identified as 1eabe18bf0cb5a248e0429f4daac91dee51c8a43. It is best practice to apply a patch to resolve this issue.
title: OpenAirInterface oai-cn5g-amf AMF amf_sbi.cpp discover_smf denial of service

desc: ELADMIN through 2.7 contains an authorization bypass vulnerability in the user export endpoint that allows department-scoped users to export user records from other departments. Authenticated attackers holding user:list permission can request GET /api/users/download to obtain an XLSX containing usernames, roles, emails, and phone numbers across all departments.
title: ELADMIN through 2.7 Data Scope Bypass via /api/users/download Export

desc: A weakness has been identified in OpenAirInterface oai-cn5g-udr up to 2.2.2. This vulnerability affects unknown code of the file src/udr_app/database/mysql_db.cpp of the component Nudr_DR. Executing a manipulation of the argument ueId can lead to sql injection. The attack may be launched remotely. The exploit has been made available to the public and could be used for attacks. The vendor was contacted early about this disclosure.
title: OpenAirInterface oai-cn5g-udr Nudr_DR mysql_db.cpp sql injection

desc: A vulnerability was identified in dcatadmin Dcat-Admin 2.2.2-beta. Affected by this issue is the function getDatabaseColumns of the file src/Http/Controllers/ScaffoldController.php. Such manipulation of the argument tb leads to sql injection. The attack can be launched remotely. The exploit is publicly available and might be used.
title: dcatadmin Dcat-Admin ScaffoldController.php getDatabaseColumns sql injection

desc: A security flaw has been discovered in OpenAirInterface oai-cn5g-nrf up to 2.2.1. This affects the function notify_subscribed_event of the file src/nrf_app/nrf_client.cpp of the component NRF. Performing a manipulation results in null pointer dereference. The attack may be initiated remotely. The exploit has been released to the public and may be used for attacks. Upgrading to version 2.2.2 is able to mitigate this issue. The patch is named 2065c6f80ca9ffdacc0064e768db90d04d9d6ca8. It is advisable to upgrade the affected component.
title: OpenAirInterface oai-cn5g-nrf NRF nrf_client.cpp notify_subscribed_event null pointer dereference

desc: A vulnerability was found in Open5GS up to 2.8.0. Affected is the function smf_ue_find_by_imsi of the file src/smf/context.c of the component SMF. The manipulation results in denial of service. It is possible to launch the attack remotely. The exploit has been made public and could be used. The patch is identified as df92296dbf60c21a2dd09e74f4903cee995cd2c2. Applying a patch is advised to resolve this issue.
title: Open5GS SMF context.c smf_ue_find_by_imsi denial of service

desc: The Loco Translate plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Arbitrary File Write/Overwrite via Path Traversal in all versions up to, and including, 2.8.4. This is due to the normalize() function processing '..' segments in user-supplied paths without verifying that the resolved absolute path remains within the base directory. This makes it possible for authenticated attackers, with Custom+ level access and above, to write translation files to arbitrary locations on the filesystem.
title: Loco Translate <= 2.8.4 - Authenticated (Custom+) Limited Arbitrary File Write via 'path' Parameter

desc: A flaw has been found in Open5GS up to 2.8.0. This affects the function ogs_pfcp_handle_create_urr of the file lib/pfcp/handler.c of the component UPF PFCP N4. Executing a manipulation of the argument URR ID can lead to reachable assertion. The attack may be performed from remote. The exploit has been published and may be used. This patch is called 08e0940e14ec41284e4270084694549de43dc219. It is best practice to apply a patch to resolve this issue.
title: Open5GS UPF PFCP N4 handler.c ogs_pfcp_handle_create_urr assertion

desc: A vulnerability has been found in Open5GS 2.8.0. This impacts the function nrf_nnrf_handle_nf_discover of the file src/nrf/nnrf-handler.c of the component NRF. The manipulation leads to reachable assertion. It is possible to initiate the attack remotely. The exploit has been disclosed to the public and may be used. The identifier of the patch is dbc35e6aadeb3f6ef3e028a8b52ee3cf5920082e. It is recommended to apply a patch to fix this issue.
title: Open5GS NRF nnrf-handler.c nrf_nnrf_handle_nf_discover assertion

desc: A vulnerability was detected in TRENDnet TEW-751DR 1.03B01. Affected by this vulnerability is the function gena.php::GENA_notify_init of the file htdocs/upnpinc/gena.php of the component UPnP Event Handler. Performing a manipulation of the argument uri results in os command injection. It is possible to initiate the attack remotely. The exploit is now public and may be used.
title: TRENDnet TEW-751DR UPnP Event gena.php GENA_notify_init os command injection

desc: A vulnerability was detected in Free5GC up to 4.3.0. The impacted element is the function PostPoliciesProcedure of the file internal/sbi/processor/ampolicy.go of the component PCF. Performing a manipulation of the argument supi results in incomplete cleanup. The attack is possible to be carried out remotely. The exploit is now public and may be used. The patch is named eba1c481300df4e7ac8000c99d0cc36dd73b941e. Applying a patch is the recommended action to fix this issue.
title: Free5GC PCF ampolicy.go PostPoliciesProcedure cleanup

desc: The Popup Builder  WordPress plugin through 4.4.6 does not properly sanitize and escape a popup shortcode attribute before it is reflected into a page and evaluated client-side, allowing users with the Contributor role and above to inject arbitrary JavaScript that executes in the session of any higher-privileged user, such as an administrator, who views the affected content.
title: Popup Builder <= 4.4.6 - Contributor+ Stored XSS via Shortcode Event Attribute

desc: The Popup Builder  WordPress plugin through 4.4.6 does not check the publish status or the visitor's capabilities before rendering a popup requested by its ID in the URL, allowing unauthenticated users to read the content and configuration of popups that are still drafts or are marked private.
title: Popup Builder <= 4.4.6 - Unauthenticated Draft and Private Popup Content Disclosure via 'sg_popup_id' Parameter

desc: The Popup Builder  WordPress plugin through 4.4.6 does not validate a user-supplied URL before requesting it server-side and storing the fetched response so that it can be read back, allowing users with Administrator privileges to perform Server-Side Request Forgery (SSRF) attacks and read the responses of internal services.
title: Popup Builder <= 4.4.6 - Admin+ SSRF via sgpb-background-image

desc: The Popup Builder  WordPress plugin through 4.4.6 does not properly check authorization before allowing a user to store popup preview data against arbitrary posts, nor restrict who can read that content back on public requests, allowing users granted access to the Popup Builder  WordPress plugin through 4.4.6 to disclose the private and draft content of posts they do not own to unauthenticated visitors.
title: Popup Builder <= 4.4.6 - Authenticated Private and Draft Post Content Disclosure via Popup Preview

desc: Themify Base WordPress theme through 1.2.4 does not perform capability checks on its option save and read AJAX actions, which are protected only by a generic nonce that other  commonly expose on the front end, allowing users with a role as low as Subscriber to update arbitrary blog options such as the default role and open registration, and gain administrator access when such a  is active.
title: Themify Base <= 1.2.4 - Subscriber+ Privilege Escalation

desc: The Popup Builder  WordPress plugin through 4.4.6 does not sanitise or escape a custom styling value before storing it and printing it back into the pages a popup loads on, allowing users who are allowed to manage popups (an ability that can be delegated to lower-privileged roles) to inject JavaScript that executes in the browser of every visitor, including logged-in administrators.
title: Popup Builder <= 4.4.6 - Authenticated Stored XSS via Custom CSS Field

desc: Gammu before 1.45.2 contains a buffer overflow vulnerability in LoadBackup() that allows attackers to corrupt memory by supplying an overlong MD5 value in a crafted backup file. Attackers can overwrite adjacent phonebook and calendar entry pointers via strcpy() into MD5Original when files are loaded with convertbackup or restore, causing crashes or potential code execution.
title: Gammu before 1.45.2 Buffer Overflow via LoadBackup() MD5 Checksum

desc: Gammu before 1.45.2 contains a stack-based buffer overflow vulnerability in ALCATEL_EncodeString() that allows attackers to overwrite stack memory via oversized encoded phonebook text. Attackers can supply a crafted backup restored with gammu restore or addnew to an attached Alcatel phone, using GSM extension characters to crash Gammu or potentially execute code.
title: Gammu before 1.45.2 Stack-Based Buffer Overflow via ALCATEL_EncodeString()

desc: Gammu before 1.45.2 contains a heap-based buffer overflow in ReadWAPSettingsEntry() that allows attackers to corrupt heap memory via crafted backup files with excess WAP or MMS settings entries. Attackers can supply a backup with more than four TitleNN keys in a [WAPSettings] or [MMSSettings] section, loaded via convertbackup, restore, or GSM_ReadBackupFile, causing crashes or potential code execution.
title: Gammu before 1.45.2 Heap Buffer Overflow via ReadWAPSettingsEntry()

desc: Gammu before 1.45.2 contains a stack-based buffer overflow vulnerability in SaveBackupText() in backtext.c that allows attackers to corrupt stack memory by supplying long text fields. Attackers can craft a backup with long calendar or note fields that, when converted with gammu convertbackup, writes hex digits past the 10,000-byte stack buffer.
title: Gammu before 1.45.2 Stack-Based Buffer Overflow via SaveBackupText()

desc: libgphoto2 through 2.5.34 contains a stack buffer overflow in sierra_get_string_register() that lets a malicious sierra-protocol camera or USB device overwrite stack memory. When files are listed, the device can answer the file-name register with an oversized packet, writing up to 32 KB past small stack buffers to cause crashes or possible code execution.
title: libgphoto2 through 2.5.34 Stack Buffer Overflow via sierra_get_string_register()

desc: edbrowse through 3.8.19 contains an integer overflow in stringAndBytes() that allows malicious servers to write past a heap buffer by sending response bodies larger than 2 GB. When a user browses to an attacker-controlled HTTP, FTP, or gopher server, the oversized body skips reallocation and corrupts the heap, causing crashes or potentially code execution.
title: edbrowse through 3.8.19 Heap Buffer Overflow via stringAndBytes() Integer Overflow

desc: Gammu before 1.45.2 contains a stack-based buffer overflow vulnerability in ReadBackupTextLen() that allows attackers to overwrite stack memory via crafted backup files. Attackers can supply overlong quoted text values decoded into a 10,000-byte stack array during convertbackup, restore, or GSM_ReadBackupFile calls, causing crashes or potential code execution.
title: Gammu before 1.45.2 Stack-Based Buffer Overflow via ReadBackupTextLen()

desc: POSTAL 2 before build 26810491 contains a sandbox escape vulnerability that allows malicious Steam Workshop mods to execute code by calling ConsoleCommand with a start file URI. Attackers can ship a batch file in a mod at the predictable workshop install path and launch it via ShellExecuteW, executing commands as the player on Windows.
title: POSTAL 2 before build 26810491 Workshop Mod Sandbox Escape Code Execution via ConsoleCommand

desc: Otter – Page Builder Blocks & Extensions for Gutenberg before 3.2.12 contains an incorrect authorization vulnerability in the Posts Grid block and Atomic Wind query loop that allows Contributor-level attackers to read non-public post type entries. Attackers can set the postTypes or queryPostType block attributes to types like flamingo_inbound or shop_coupon to expose titles and text, while the Atomic Wind custom_field path also leaks protected post meta.
products: themeisle:otter – page builder blocks & extensions for gutenberg
title: Otter Blocks before 3.2.12 Incorrect Authorization via Posts Grid and Atomic Wind

desc: ClassroomIO through 1.0.0 contains an insecure direct object reference vulnerability that allows authenticated course members to access other tenants' newsfeed posts by supplying a foreign feedId under their own courseId. Attackers can read, react to, and comment on cross-organization posts, while team members or org admins can also overwrite content, pin flags, and delete them.
title: ClassroomIO through 1.0.0 IDOR via Course Newsfeed API Routes

desc: picomatch through 4.0.7 contains a glob filter bypass vulnerability because globstar (**) patterns are compiled without the dotAll flag and fail to match line terminators. Attackers who control file, object key or archive entry names containing newline characters can evade ** deny patterns, causing excluded resources to be included and exposed.
title: picomatch through 4.0.7 Glob Filter Bypass via Globstar Line Terminators

desc: FeatBit before 6.1.3 contains an authorization bypass vulnerability that allows authenticated members of one organization to read other organizations' segments by supplying foreign segment identifiers. Attackers can query the SegmentController segment, by-ids, and flag-references endpoints with their own envId to retrieve end-user keys, targeting rules, and referencing feature flag keys.
title: FeatBit before 6.1.3 Authorization Bypass via SegmentController Segment Read Endpoints

desc: SimGear through 2024.1.7 contains an infinite loop vulnerability in sgSimpleBuffer::resize() where an unsigned 32-bit wraparound in the size-doubling loop leaves the size at zero. Attackers can supply a crafted .btg scenery file with an oversized byte count exceeding 2^31 to hang the loading process in FlightGear.
title: SimGear through 2024.1.7 Infinite Loop DoS via sgSimpleBuffer::resize()

desc: bgpq4 before 1.17 contains an integer overflow vulnerability in expander.c that allows malicious IRR servers to corrupt heap memory by sending crafted A<len> replies. Attackers controlling the IRR server or tampering with the plaintext TCP connection can announce a ULONG_MAX or -1 length, wrapping the allocation to one byte and crashing bgpq4.
title: bgpq4 before 1.17 Heap Buffer Overflow via IRRd A<len> Reply Handling

desc: Otter – Page Builder Blocks & Extensions for Gutenberg before 3.2.12 contains a server-side request forgery vulnerability that allows Contributor-level attackers to make the server contact arbitrary hosts via crafted Mailchimp API keys. Attackers can POST to the otter/v1/form/editor REST route with an apiKey whose data-center segment embeds a host, following redirects to internal services and reading partial responses.
products: themeisle:otter – page builder blocks & extensions for gutenberg
title: Otter Blocks before 3.2.12 SSRF via Mailchimp API Key Validation

desc: HyperSpy from 1.2.0 before 2.6.0 contains a code execution vulnerability that allows attackers to run Python code by embedding malicious expression strings evaluated with sympy.sympify(). Attackers can craft .hspy or .zspy files with malicious axis, Expression component, or twin function expressions that execute when victims call hs.load() or restore models.
title: HyperSpy before 2.6.0 Code Execution via sympy.sympify() in HSPY/ZSPY Files

desc: HyperSpy from 1.4.0 before 2.6.0 contains an insecure deserialization vulnerability that allows attackers to execute arbitrary Python code by supplying crafted stored-model data in .hspy or .zspy files. Attackers can embed a malicious pickle payload in a component's _class_dump or a 'fn'-flagged _whitelist entry, which cloudpickle.loads() (dill in 1.x) runs when the victim restores the model.
title: HyperSpy 1.4.0 before 2.6.0 Insecure Deserialization RCE via Stored Model Restoration

desc: Kestra before 1.3.36 contains a reflected cross-site scripting vulnerability that allows unauthenticated attackers to execute JavaScript by injecting HTML into the executions page sort parameter. Attackers can lure logged-in users to a crafted link whose invalid sort value is rendered unsanitized in an error toast, stealing the non-HttpOnly BASIC_AUTH credential cookie to take over the instance.
title: Kestra before 1.3.36 Reflected XSS via Executions Page Sort Parameter

desc: Kestra 1.3.24 before 2.0.0 contains a timing side-channel vulnerability in BasicAuthService.isAuthenticated() that allows unauthenticated attackers to enumerate the administrator username. Attackers can send Basic-auth requests with candidate usernames to protected API endpoints and detect slower bcrypt checks to identify the valid account for password guessing.
title: Kestra 1.3.24 before 2.0.0 Username Enumeration via Basic-Auth Timing

desc: Kestra 1.3.24 before 1.3.41 contains an insufficient credential expiration vulnerability that allows holders of a revoked administrator password to keep authenticating on peer webserver nodes through BasicAuthService's process-local verified-token cache. Attackers whose token remains cached on a peer node can call POST /api/v1/{tenant}/basicAuth to overwrite the shared administrator credentials and lock out the legitimate administrator.
title: Kestra 1.3.24 before 1.3.41 Insufficient Credential Expiration via Basic-Auth Token Cache

desc: Improper Content Security Policy (CSP) configuration in the BigFix MCM WebUI allowed the data: URI scheme as a source in the img-src directive of the CSP header. This potentially weakens the application's defense-in-depth security mechanism.
title: An improper Content Security Policy configuration in the BigFix MCM WebUI affects HCL BigFix Modern Client Management

desc: HCL Verse for Android included a decryption code for compatibility with locally stored values and attachment files created by older application versions (no longer used for data stored by newer versions). HCL Verse for Android version 14.5.16 (November 2026) removed the legacy decryption code.
title: HCL Verse for Android is affected by use of a weak cryptographic algorithm

desc: A security vulnerability has been detected in TRENDnet TEW-751DR and TEW-733GR 1.03B01. Affected is the function soapcgi_main of the file /soap.cgi of the component UPnP Igd Control Endpoint. Such manipulation of the argument service leads to os command injection. The attack may be performed from remote. The exploit has been disclosed publicly and may be used.
title: TRENDnet TEW-751DR/TEW-733GR UPnP Igd Control Endpoint soap.cgi soapcgi_main os command injection

desc: A weakness has been identified in TRENDnet TEW-751DR 1.03B01. This impacts the function FUN_0040ed90 of the file wfadev.cgi of the component UPnP/WFA. This manipulation of the argument SOAPAction causes stack-based buffer overflow. The attack is possible to be carried out remotely. A high degree of complexity is needed for the attack. The exploitability is said to be difficult. The exploit has been made available to the public and could be used for attacks.
title: TRENDnet TEW-751DR UPnP/WFA wfadev.cgi FUN_0040ed90 stack-based overflow

desc: A flaw was found in GIMP. The Levels configuration setter does not validate the channel enum before using it to index fixed-size per-channel arrays. A crafted XCF file with a non-destructive Levels filter can set an out-of-range channel (LUMINANCE or RGB), causing a heap out-of-bounds read and write when the file is opened. This may lead to a crash or arbitrary code execution.
title: Gimp: gimp: heap out-of-bounds write via unvalidated levels channel property

desc: A flaw was found in tuned. This vulnerability allows local privilege escalation because the spindown-disk profile script does not properly validate filesystem mount sources before executing remount operations with root privileges. A local user capable of creating user-space filesystems can craft a malicious mount entry to execute arbitrary commands as root.
title: Tuned: local privilege escalation through untrusted mount table parsing in the spindown-disk profile

desc: mcp-video-analyzer 0.2.0 before 0.10.1 contains a server-side request forgery vulnerability that allows attackers to reach internal addresses by supplying any http(s) URL ending in a video extension. Attackers can use prompt injection to make tools like get_frames fetch loopback, private, or cloud metadata addresses directly or via redirects, writing responses to disk or returning rendered screenshots.
title: mcp-video-analyzer 0.2.0 before 0.10.1 SSRF via Direct Video URLs

desc: bigcommerce-api-mcp before 1.0.1 contains a missing authentication vulnerability that allows remote unauthenticated attackers to invoke MCP tools because the /sse and /messages routes skip the authenticateRequest middleware. Attackers can open /sse to obtain a session id and POST JSON-RPC tool calls to /messages to retrieve store product, order and customer records using the operator's BigCommerce API key.
title: bigcommerce-api-mcp before 1.0.1 Missing Authentication via SSE Transport Routes

desc: ntfy before v2.38.3 contains a server-side request forgery vulnerability that allows remote attackers to bypass the web push endpoint allow-list by crafting a URL containing '#' or '?' characters that satisfy the [^/]+ regex pattern used to validate mozaws.net and notify.windows.com hosts. Attackers can submit an endpoint .example#.mozaws.net/push, which passes validation while Go parses the actual host as attacker.example, causing the server to send subsequent web push POST requests to an attacker-controlled or internal host.
title: ntfy before 2.38.3 SSRF via Web Push Endpoint Allow-list Bypass

desc: Bagel (bagel-mcp) before 2.5.5 exposes unsandboxed DuckDB SQL execution through the read-only annotated query_messages MCP tool, allowing file access and network requests. Attackers who prompt-inject the driving LLM via recorded logs or topics can invoke read_csv_auto, COPY TO, or httpfs to read and write files and perform server-side request forgery.
title: Bagel before 2.5.5 Unsandboxed DuckDB SQL Execution via query_messages

desc: Bagel (bagel-mcp) before 2.5.5 contains an argument injection vulnerability in RsyncFilesToLocalDirectory that allows attackers to inject rsync options because only --quiet and --log-format values are rejected. Attackers who influence the LLM through prompt-injected content can trigger run_pipeline with -e/--rsh or --rsync-path options to execute commands as the Bagel server process.
title: Bagel before 2.5.5 Argument Injection via rsync Pipeline Task Options

desc: Wazuh-MCP-Server before commit 2bbfe12 contains a server-side request forgery vulnerability in the blueteam_check_webshell tool because WebshellCheckInput.validate_url accepts DNS hostnames without resolving them. Attackers can supply URLs whose hostnames resolve or redirect to loopback, private, or link-local addresses, making curl reach internal services and cloud metadata endpoints and leak response details.
title: Wazuh-MCP-Server before commit 2bbfe12 SSRF via blueteam_check_webshell Hostname Bypass

desc: SylphxAI pdf-reader-mcp 2.4.1 through 3.0.14, 3.0.16, and 3.1.2 through 3.1.4 contains a server-side request forgery vulnerability in its PDF URL loader, which validates the resolved address but does not pin it for fetch(). desc: Typebot from 2.14.0 before 3.19.0 contains an authorization flaw that allows authenticated bot authors to reference another workspace's legacy webhook by saving a foreign webhookId in an HTTP request block. Attackers can have executeHttpRequestBlock return the victim's URL, headers and body client-side, or use handleSubscribeHttpRequest to overwrite the victim's webhook URL and redirect its data.
title: Typebot from 2.14.0 before 3.19.0 Cross-Workspace Webhook Disclosure via Unscoped webhookId

desc: WhoDB from 0.88.0 before 0.132.0 contains an access control bypass in the MCP whodb_query tool, letting callers run file-writing statements without approval because the sqlguard keyword classifier omits INTO, OUTFILE and DUMPFILE. MCP clients or prompt-injected models can execute PostgreSQL lo_export or MySQL SELECT INTO OUTFILE to create files on the database host and create tables, bypassing confirmation and read-only modes.

desc: A flaw was found in pam. When built with libeconf and an unconfigured vendor directory, the pam_econf configuration handler misinterprets the search path, causing it to look for configuration files in a relative directory within the current working directory. A local attacker can exploit this by placing crafted environment configuration files in a world-writable location. If an administrator executes a privileged command from that directory, the malicious variables are loaded into the privileged process, resulting in local privilege escalation.
products: red hat:red hat openshift container platform 4
red hat:red hat openshift container platform 5
title: Pam: linux-pam pam_econf local privilege escalation via relative "(null)" config directory from empty vendor directory handling

desc: Crypto APIs MCP server packages (@cryptoapis-io/mcp-*) before 0.4.0, mcp-blockchain-events, mcp-blockchain-fees, mcp-broadcast and mcp-prepare-transactions before 0.5.0, and mcp-aml before 0.2.0 contain a missing authentication vulnerability that allows unauthenticated network attackers to invoke tools using the operator's API key. Exploitation depends on conditions beyond the attacker's control and requires user interaction in that a victim must open a malicious file. Scope is changed.

HCIPy through 0.7.1 contains an insecure deserialization vulnerability that allows attackers to execute code by supplying crafted .pkl files to read_field, read_grid or read_mode_basis. Because hcipy/util/io.py selects pickle by file extension and calls pickle.load, a __reduce__ gadget in a pupil, apodizer, PSF or mode-basis file runs code with the user's privileges.
title: HCIPy through 0.7.1 Insecure Deserialization via Pickle Files in io.py

desc: Detoxify 0.5.3 through 0.5.4 contains an insecure deserialization vulnerability in load_checkpoint that allows attackers to execute code by supplying a crafted checkpoint file. Attackers can embed a pickle __reduce__ gadget in a .ckpt file loaded via torch.load with weights_only=False to run code with the user's privileges.
title: Detoxify 0.5.3 through 0.5.4 Insecure Deserialization RCE via load_checkpoint

desc: JSONSchema2PoPo2 through 3.0.3 contains a code injection vulnerability that allows attackers to inject Python code by supplying JSON Schema default or format values that are written unescaped. Attackers can place a single quote in a string property default to break out of the literal in the generated __init__ signature, executing injected code when the generated module is imported.
title: JSONSchema2PoPo2 through 3.0.3 Code Injection via python_class.tmpl Template

desc: libexpat through 2.11.0 contains a denial of service vulnerability in defineAttribute() of lib/xmlparse.c that fails to detect duplicate non-ID #IMPLIED or #REQUIRED attribute declarations. Attackers can supply a crafted XML document with repeated ATTLIST declarations in an internal DTD subset to cause quadratic CPU consumption in storeAtts() during parsing.
title: libexpat through 2.11.0 Denial of Service via defineAttribute Duplicate Declarations

desc: django-allauth 65.17.0 before 65.23.0 contains a denial of service vulnerability in truncate_ip() that collapses all IPv4-mapped IPv6 clients into one shared rate-limit key. Unauthenticated attackers on dual-stack deployments can exhaust per-IP limits for login, signup or password reset, blocking legitimate IPv4 users.
title: django-allauth 65.17.0 before 65.23.0 Denial of Service via truncate_ip() Rate-Limit Key

desc: Leo through 6.8.10 contains an insecure deserialization vulnerability that allows attackers to execute code by embedding pickled data in unknown XML attributes of .leo outlines. Attackers can place a pickle __reduce__ gadget in a <t> or <v> element attribute that resolveUa passes to pickle.loads, executing code with user privileges when the outline is opened.
title: Leo through 6.8.10 Insecure Deserialization RCE via .leo Outline Attributes

desc: FOG Project before 1.6.0.119 contains an information disclosure vulnerability that allows unauthenticated attackers to obtain host tokens from status/hostgetkey.php by supplying a host MAC address. Attackers can present the token to service/hostinfo.php to retrieve decrypted Active Directory join credentials and Windows product keys during deployment windows.
title: FOG Project before 1.6.0.119 Credential Disclosure via status/hostgetkey.php Token Endpoint

desc: Zettlr before 4.11.0 fails to validate URI schemes in Markdown link targets, allowing attackers to launch arbitrary registered protocol handlers via Electron shell.openExternal without confirmation. Attackers can craft documents whose Ctrl/Cmd-clicked links use smb:// to leak NTLM credential hashes on Windows or invoke custom protocol handlers with attacker-controlled parameters.
title: Zettlr before 4.11.0 Unvalidated URI Scheme Handling via Markdown Links

desc: A security flaw has been discovered in eosphoros-ai DB-GPT up to 0.8.3. This affects the function editor_sql_run of the file packages/dbgpt-app/src/dbgpt_app/openapi/api_v1/editor/api_editor_v1.py of the component Editor SQL Run API. Performing a manipulation of the argument db_name results in authorization bypass. It is possible to initiate the attack remotely. The exploit has been released to the public and may be used for attacks. The pull request to fix this issue awaits acceptance.
title: eosphoros-ai DB-GPT Editor SQL Run API api_editor_v1.py editor_sql_run authorization

desc: Dell Secure Connect Gateway - Virtual Edition, versions prior to 5.36.00.16, contains an Improper Limitation of a Pathname to a Restricted Directory ('Path Traversal') vulnerability. ToolJet before 3.21.96-LTS contains a server-side request forgery vulnerability in ssrf-protection.ts that fails to classify NAT64 (64:ff9b::/96, 64:ff9b:1::/48) and 6to4 (2002::/16) IPv6 addresses embedding internal IPv4. Authenticated users can set REST API, GraphQL, OpenAPI, or OAuth data-source URLs to attacker hostnames whose AAAA records resolve to these forms, bypassing pre-request and dial-time guards to reach cloud metadata and internal hosts.
title: ToolJet before 3.21.96-LTS SSRF Protection Bypass via IPv6 NAT64/6to4 Addresses

desc: ToolJet before 3.21.96-LTS contains a server-side request forgery vulnerability in the n8n, nocodb, baserow, couchdb, elasticsearch, influxdb, and databricks datasource plugins, which skip the validateUrlForSSRF check. Authenticated builders, or unauthenticated visitors of public apps with templated URLs, can supply internal URLs or hosts to read cloud metadata credentials and internal service responses.
title: ToolJet before 3.21.96-LTS SSRF via Unprotected Datasource Plugins

desc: Heym from 0.0.95 before 0.0.154 contains a stored cross-site scripting vulnerability that allows authenticated users to run script on the application origin by publishing HTML output mapper workflows. Attackers can set a workflow to anonymous GET and share the /api/workflows/{id}/execute link, causing visitors' browsers to send authenticated API requests to read or modify their workflows, credentials, and settings.
title: Heym 0.0.95 before 0.0.154 Stored XSS via htmlOutputMapper Workflows

desc: Nmap before 7.992 contains a use-after-free vulnerability in DNS::ResolverImpl::handle_write in libnetutil/massdns.cc that dereferences freed request objects after writes complete. Attackers controlling or on-path to a DNS server can send timed DNS responses with forged ICMP port-unreachable messages to crash scans, disclose memory, or hijack execution.
title: Nmap before 7.992 Use-After-Free via DNS Resolver handle_write

desc: Nmap before 7.992 contains a use-after-free vulnerability in DNS::ResolverImpl::process_request in libnetutil/massdns.cc that frees still-referenced requests when rescheduling after DNS server disconnects. Attackers answering for at least two configured DNS servers can force a disconnect and send a precisely timed response to crash the scan, possibly enabling code execution.
title: Nmap before 7.992 Use-After-Free via Parallel DNS Resolver process_request

desc: Nmap before 7.992 contains an information disclosure vulnerability in the Nmap Scripting Engine because nse_main.lua does not explicitly seed Lua's math.random generator. Malicious scanned hosts can observe math.random-derived values in NSE script traffic during -sC scans, brute-force the seed, and recover a heap address that weakens ASLR.
title: Nmap before 7.992 Heap Address Disclosure via Predictable NSE Lua Seed

desc: Heym before 0.0.154 contains a cross-site request forgery vulnerability in the workflow execute endpoint: anonymous workflows run as any signed-in caller, without an access check, using that caller's credentials and global variables. Authenticated attackers can lure signed-in users to a GET execute link for an attacker-owned anonymous workflow, which the SameSite=Lax session cookie authenticates. The attacker then reads the victim's decrypted credentials from the workflow's run history.
title: Heym before 0.0.154 Credential Theft via Anonymous Workflow Execute Endpoint

desc: ToolJet before 3.21.96-LTS contains a command injection vulnerability in its GitHub Actions release workflow, which interpolates the pull request title directly into a shell run block. Attackers can submit a pull request against a release branch with shell metacharacters in its title that, once merged, executes commands with a cross-repository GITHUB_TOKEN, enabling unauthorized merges into enterprise repositories.
title: ToolJet before 3.21.96-LTS Command Injection via Release Workflow Pull Request Title

desc: ToolJet before 3.21.96-LTS contains a server-side request forgery vulnerability that allows authenticated users with the TEST_CONNECTION ability to reach arbitrary hosts by supplying body-controlled datasource options. Attackers can set kind, plugin_id, and host options for plugins like influxdb or elasticsearch to reach loopback, internal services, or cloud metadata endpoints exposing IAM credentials.
title: ToolJet before 3.21.96-LTS SSRF via Data Source test-connection Endpoint

desc: ToolJet before 3.21.96-LTS contains an arbitrary file read and SSRF vulnerability in the SMTP plugin that allows authenticated app builders to pass object values to Nodemailer. Attackers can set textContent or htmlContent to path or href content objects to email server files or internal cloud metadata responses to themselves.
title: ToolJet before 3.21.96-LTS SMTP Plugin Arbitrary File Read and SSRF

desc: ToolJet before 3.21.96-LTS contains a server-side request forgery vulnerability in the OAuth token exchange for custom datasources, which sends requests to an unvalidated, user-configured access_token_url. Authenticated users can trigger the authorize_oauth2 endpoint to reach loopback, cloud metadata, or private network services, with internal response bodies reflected in some API error responses.
title: ToolJet before 3.21.96-LTS SSRF via OAuth access_token_url Token Exchange

desc: ToolJet before 3.21.96-LTS contains a server-side request forgery protection bypass because getSSRFProtectionOptions passes its safe resolver as dnsLookup instead of lookup. Attackers controlling datasource hostnames can use DNS rebinding in REST API, GraphQL, OpenAPI, or OAuth requests to reach blocked private addresses.
title: ToolJet before 3.21.96-LTS SSRF Protection Bypass via DNS Rebinding

desc: ToolJet before 3.21.96-LTS contains a server-side request forgery vulnerability that allows authenticated users to make the server fetch internal URLs via the gRPC v2 proto_file_url option. Attackers can target loopback, private, cloud metadata, or redirect-controlled addresses, or serve oversized responses that are buffered and parsed synchronously, causing denial of service.
title: ToolJet before 3.21.96-LTS SSRF via gRPC v2 proto_file_url Import

desc: n8n before 1.123.96, 2.x before 2.47.6, 2.48.x before 2.48.3, and 3.x before 3.2.2 does not verify that the user activating a workflow can access the credentials set on its trigger nodes. An authenticated member who knows another user's credential ID can activate a workflow whose trigger uses it, causing n8n to create or delete webhooks on the connected service with that credential's privileges and deliver events from attacker-chosen resources to the member's workflow.
title: n8n before 1.123.96, 2.47.6, 2.48.3, and 3.2.2 Improper Authorization in Workflow Activation Trigger Credentials

desc: Budibase backend-core before 3.49.0 contains a server-side request forgery vulnerability that allows authenticated Builder/Creator users to bypass the outbound-fetch deny list by targeting the IPv6 unspecified address. Attackers can supply URLs with host [::] to features like Outgoing Webhook or REST datasources to reach IPv6 loopback services and read reflected internal responses.
title: Budibase backend-core before 3.49.0 SSRF via IPv6 Unspecified Address Bypass

desc: Budibase before 3.51.0 contains a path traversal vulnerability in the workspace create handler that allows authenticated CREATOR users to probe server paths by supplying an unvalidated body.file.path value. Attackers can enumerate filesystem existence and type, and for directories containing db.txt, copy contents into their object store namespace before the directory is recursively deleted.
title: Budibase before 3.51.0 Filesystem Oracle and Directory Deletion via body.file.path

desc: n8n before 2.47.6, 2.48.x before 2.48.3, and 3.x before 3.2.2 contains a server-side request forgery vulnerability in the AWS Bedrock Chat Model and Embeddings AWS Bedrock nodes, where requests to a custom Bedrock runtime endpoint set in an AWS credential bypass n8n's SSRF protection. desc: ToolJet before 3.21.96-LTS contains a hard-coded credentials vulnerability where the Helm chart values.yaml sets secret_key_base and lockbox_key to a static published constant. desc:
The MCUmgr SMP client matched an incoming response to a pending command in smp_client_response_discover() (subsys/mgmt/mcumgr/smp_client/src/client.c) using only the 8-bit sequence number and the operation. It did not check the transport the response arrived on, or the group and command ID. smp_process_request_packet() hands every MGMT_OP_READ_RSP/MGMT_OP_WRITE_RSP packet received on any SMP transport to smp_client_single_response(), so a response from any SMP peer could complete any pending client command.

On a device that is both an SMP server (for example over Bluetooth LE or UDP) and an SMP client (CONFIG_SMP_CLIENT, for example using img_mgmt_client to update a companion MCU over UART), a peer on the server transport can send up to 256 forged response packets while a client operation is pending and have one of them accepted as the reply from the managed device. Non-matching responses are dropped silently. The response path bypasses the server command handlers, so restricting which server groups a peer may use does not prevent it.

The attacker can forge the results of client operations. For example, a forged image-upload offset makes img_mgmt_client_upload() report success after only part of the image was sent, a forged image-state response can report arbitrary versions or flags, and any pending command can be forced to fail. No memory corruption results: the response callbacks bound-check the decoded data. The target's own image validation limits the result to failed or suppressed updates and disrupted management operations. The fix restricts matching to commands sent on the same transport with the same group and command ID. Responses from a different peer on the same transport are still not distinguished.
title: MCUmgr SMP client accepts responses from any transport, allowing spoofed command results

desc:
dns_resolve_cancel_with_name() in subsys/net/lib/dns/resolve.c looks up the pending query to cancel by DNS id plus a hash of the name the caller originally asked for. When a reply contains only a CNAME, the resolver sends a new query for the alias and overwrites the slot's query_hash with the hash of the alias name. After one or more CNAME hops, cancelling by the original name silently fails with -ENOENT and the query stays pending.

zsock_getaddrinfo() (exec_query() in subsys/net/lib/sockets/getaddrinfo.c) passes a pointer to its stack-local ai_state as the resolver callback context. When its semaphore wait times out, it calls dns_cancel_addr_info_with_name(), ignores the result, and returns. The CNAME re-query restarts the resolver timer, so a CNAME-only response that arrives more than about 100 ms after the query lets the getaddrinfo() wait expire first. The cancel then fails and getaddrinfo() returns. An attacker who can supply DNS responses can trigger this reliably: a malicious or compromised DNS server, an on-path attacker, or any host on the link for mDNS/LLMNR lookups. The device only has to resolve a name with getaddrinfo().

When the orphaned query later times out, dns_resolve_cb() writes the status and calls k_sem_give() on the dead stack frame. If the attacker answers the alias query instead, the callback copies attacker-supplied address data through a stale ai_arr pointer read from the reused stack. The result is a kernel fault (denial of service) or memory corruption in the calling thread's stack and whatever memory the stale pointer references.
title: Use-after-return in getaddrinfo() when a DNS query that followed a CNAME cannot be cancelled

desc:
The system call verifier z_vrfy_k_thread_stack_space_get() in kernel/thread.c checked the result of K_SYSCALL_OBJ(thread, K_OBJ_THREAD) with the CHECKIF() macro instead of K_OOPS(). CHECKIF() compiles to if (0) when CONFIG_NO_RUNTIME_CHECKS is selected, and becomes an assertion when CONFIG_ASSERT_ON_ERRORS is selected. In both cases, the kernel-object validation result for the user-supplied thread pointer is ignored, or is a no-op when assertions are disabled.

On builds with CONFIG_USERSPACE, CONFIG_INIT_STACKS and CONFIG_THREAD_STACK_INFO plus one of those check modes, a user-mode thread can call k_thread_stack_space_get() with an arbitrary pointer. That pointer can be a fake struct k_thread in its own memory, or a thread object it has no permission on. z_impl_k_thread_stack_space_get() then dereferences thread->stack_info in supervisor mode and scans memory starting at the attacker-chosen stack_info.start.

The syscall returns the number of leading 0xAA bytes at that address. This gives an unprivileged thread a limited oracle on arbitrary kernel or peripheral memory, and allows privileged reads of attacker-selected addresses, including MMIO. No write primitive results. The default CONFIG_RUNTIME_ERROR_CHECKS configuration is not affected. The fix replaces the CHECKIF() with K_OOPS() so the object check is always enforced.
title: Kernel object validation bypass in k_thread_stack_space_get syscall verifier with CONFIG_NO_RUNTIME_CHECKS

Affected versions of Mendix Runtime do not end existing sessions when a user account is set to inactive. The account state is checked at sign-in, but not on later requests made with a session that already exists. A user who is deactivated while signed in can keep using that session for as long as the client keeps it alive.

This could allow an authenticated remote attacker to read and change data within previous permissions for a persistent session.

title: Wrong remote DoH client IP passed to proxy-protocol-enabled backend

desc: When DNS over HTTPS is enabled and configured to trust incoming X-Forwarded-For headers, and the reverse proxy placed in front of DNSdist does not replace existing X-Forwarded-For headers but merely append a new header to the query, the first header was used by DNSdist instead of the last one, making it possible for a client to spoof its own IP address.
title: Duplicate X-Forwarded-For DNS over HTTPS headers are not properly handled

desc: When DNS over HTTPS is enabled and a caching HTTP reverse proxy is used in front of DNSdist, it is possible to pollute the cache of the HTTP reverse proxy by sending DNS over HTTPS GET queries with a body. DNSdist should either refuse the query or ignore the HTTP body, but instead was processing the content of the HTTP body rather than the query present in the HTTP path.
title: HTTP body should not be processed on DNS over HTTPS GET queries

desc: FFmpeg before 9.1 contains an out-of-bounds read vulnerability in pcx_encode_frame() in libavcodec/pcxenc.c that rounds each row up to an even number of bytes and run-length encodes that many bytes from the input frame. Attackers who control the width of images encoded to PCX by an application that supplies tightly packed frames can make the encoder read past the end of the frame buffer, crashing the application or leaking heap contents into the output image.
title: FFmpeg before 9.1 Out-of-Bounds Read via PCX Encoder Odd-Width Rows

desc: FFmpeg before 9.1 contains an out-of-bounds read vulnerability in xwd_encode_frame() in libavcodec/xwdenc.c that copies each RGB24 or BGR24 row using the padded XWD scanline size instead of the pixel row size. Attackers who control the width of video encoded to XWD by an application that supplies tightly packed frames can make the encoder read past the frame buffer, crashing the application or leaking heap contents into the output image.
title: FFmpeg before 9.1 Out-of-Bounds Read via XWD Encoder Scanline Padding

desc: FFmpeg 5.0 before 8.1.3 contains a NULL pointer dereference vulnerability in parse_imf_asset_map_from_xml_dom() in libavformat/imfdec.c that does not check for a missing or empty Path element in an asset map Chunk. Attackers can supply a crafted IMF ASSETMAP.xml whose Chunk lacks a Path, passing a NULL URI to the path handling functions and crashing the process.

desc: FFmpeg 5.0 before 8.1.3 contains a NULL pointer dereference vulnerability in the IMF demuxer in libavformat/imfdec.c because open_virtual_track() accepts a virtual track with no resources. desc: FFmpeg before 9.1 contains a NULL pointer dereference vulnerability in xsub_encode() in libavcodec/xsubenc.c that only warns when a subtitle has no rectangles and then dereferences rects[0]. desc: FFmpeg 7.1 before 9.1 contains a memory leak vulnerability in eb_receive_packet() in libavcodec/libsvtav1.c that returns without unreferencing the queued input frame when eb_send_frame() fails. desc: Lookyloo is a web-based malware analysis and sandboxing platform. The pull-from-remote-instance feature allows a user to request a previously captured sample from another Lookyloo instance by specifying the target instance's URL and a capture UUID. Prior to the fix, the only restriction on the target URL was a check that the hostname, if it was a literal IP address, was not in a private range. Hostnames that resolved to private or internal addresses were not blocked, and no authentication or allowlist was enforced for anonymous users. This allowed any unauthenticated user to direct the Lookyloo server to issue HTTP requests (HEAD to the root path and GET to /json/<uuid>/status, followed by a capture download) to arbitrary internal or external hosts, effectively enabling a Server-Side Request Forgery (SSRF) attack. An attacker could use this to probe internal network topology, access captures stored on internal Lookyloo instances, or leverage the server as a proxy to reach otherwise unreachable services. The vulnerability is in the website/web/__init__.py module, specifically the __get_remote_capture function and the associated pull endpoint. The security impact is unauthorized disclosure of capture data and internal service information from Lookyloo instances that are not intended to be publicly accessible.
title: Lookyloo: Unrestricted Remote Instance Pull Allows Anonymous SSRF to Internal Lookyloo Instances

desc:
Flowintel contains a Server-Side Request Forgery (SSRF) vulnerability in its HedgeDoc case-notes integration. When a user with editor or administrator privileges associates a HedgeDoc URL with a case, the application later issues a server-side HTTP GET request to that URL to retrieve note content. Before the fix, the stored URL was used directly without validation of its scheme, host, port, path, or userinfo, and the HTTP client followed redirects by default with no connect or read timeouts.

An authenticated attacker could therefore cause the Flowintel server to issue requests to arbitrary internal or external endpoints (for example, cloud instance-metadata services, internal management interfaces, or other intranet hosts) and receive the response body, or follow a redirect chain to an unintended destination. The absence of timeouts also permitted resource-exhaustion against the server's outbound connection pool.

Preconditions:
- An authenticated account with editor or administrator role on the target case.
- The HedgeDoc integration feature is enabled (no explicit configuration gate existed before the fix).

Impact:
- Disclosure of sensitive data served by internal or cloud-metadata endpoints.
- Potential denial of service through unbounded outbound requests.

Affected versions: Flowintel prior to 4.1.0.
title: Flowintel SSRF via Unvalidated HedgeDoc Note URL in Case Notes Download

Alternatively, set principalSuffix on the realm, or disable anonymous binds on the directory server.

The country manager page of the JTL-Shop administration backend (/admin/countries) writes the request parameter activeSortOrder without output encoding into a single-quoted JavaScript string and into HTML attributes. The overview page requires no CSRF token. An unauthenticated remote attacker can thereby cause script code to be executed in the browser of a logged-in backend user who opens a crafted link in the same browser (the session cookie carries no SameSite attribute by default); the code runs with the privileges of that user and can use the backend token of the same page to send requests to the backend. Visitors and customers are not affected.
title: JTL-Shop: Reflected cross-site scripting in the backend country manager via the activeSortOrder parameter

desc: In Eclipse Krazo Extensions up to and including 3.0.0, AsciiDocViewEngine passes MVC model values to Asciidoctor as document attributes without encoding them. Asciidoctor substitutes attribute references after it escapes HTML special characters and before it processes inline macros. As a result, attacker-controlled model values end up in the output as raw HTML and can inject AsciiDoc inline macros. This allows cross-site scripting in applications that render untrusted data through AsciiDoc views.

MONEO ERP exposes the Ping method of its _slave JSON-RPC service over WebSocket as @rpc.openpublic, so it can be called without a valid session. The method's only guard compares the calling application name with "_login", but that value is taken from the client-controlled params.appname field of the request. When the check passes, Ping stores an attacker-chosen session ID, user number and company in the server session store, and subsequent session validation accepts that session. An unauthenticated remote attacker can therefore create a valid session as any user, including administrators, in any company (tenant) hosted on the server and invoke authenticated RPC methods with that user's privileges, gaining read and write access to that company's data.
title: MONEO ERP unauthenticated session forging via the public Ping JSON-RPC method

In Eclipse Dataspace Components (EDC) Connector 1.0.0-RC2 through 1.0.0-RC7, the HashiCorp Vault extension does not reject .. path segments in secret aliases. In a multi-participant (virtual) control plane where vault partitions share the runtime's Vault token, an authenticated participant can set a callback secret alias that escapes its own vault partition. The connector then reads secrets of other participants or of the runtime, such as STS client secrets or the encryption key, and sends them to an endpoint the attacker chooses.

A flaw was found in Flatpak’s flatpak-system-helper. When a system-wide app, runtime, or extension uses the extra-data mechanism and its apply_extra logic creates a deeply nested directory tree, permission canonicalization can fail (for example with EMFILE). Affected Flatpak versions can still report success without clearing setuid/setgid bits, leaving a setuid-root executable under /var/lib/flatpak. A local attacker who can install or update such content system-wide, or who can already execute code as a local user in cooperation with that content, can escalate privileges to root.
products: red hat:red hat openshift container platform 5
title: Flatpak: flatpak: flatpak-system-helper extra-data privilege escalation if canonicalizing permissions fails with emfile

desc: A flaw was found in Flatpak’s flatpak-portal. When a sandboxed application invokes Spawn() and maps two different file descriptors to the same handle, dup2() can fail. Affected Flatpak versions do not handle that failure, so a file descriptor that was open inside flatpak-portal (commonly the unfiltered D-Bus session bus) can be passed into the subsandbox. A malicious or compromised Flatpak app with no special privileges can use this to escape the sandbox.
products: red hat:red hat openshift container platform 5
title: Flatpak: flatpak: sandbox escape via fd conflict in flatpak-portal spawn()

desc: The backend language switch action (quick_change_language) of the JTL-Shop administration backend is executed without a CSRF token check, and the supplied language value is neither validated against the installed backend languages nor encoded on output. The value is stored in the session and in the account data of the administrator and rendered without output encoding in JavaScript strings and HTML attributes of backend pages. desc:
A path traversal (ZIP slip) vulnerability exists in Epiphany when installing WebExtension packages from .xpi files.

In src/webextension/ephy-web-extension-manager.c, the decompress_xpi_thread() function extracts XPI archives (ZIP format) to disk using libarchive. For each archive entry, the output path is built by concatenating the intended extraction directory with the raw pathname from the archive:

    full_path = g_build_filename(path, archive_entry_pathname(entry), NULL);
    archive_entry_set_pathname(entry, full_path);
    ret = archive_write_header(ext, entry);

The libarchive extraction options did not include ARCHIVE_EXTRACT_SECURE_NODOTDOT or ARCHIVE_EXTRACT_SECURE_SYMLINKS. As a result, archive entries containing parent-directory traversal sequences (for example "../../../../../.bashrc") are written outside the intended web_extensions extraction directory.

A malicious .xpi file can therefore overwrite arbitrary files writable by the user running Epiphany, such as ~/.bashrc, ~/.config/autostart/*.desktop, or ~/.ssh/authorized_keys. This can lead to persistent code execution on subsequent shell startup or GNOME login.

Exploitation requires the victim to install or open a crafted .xpi file. The reporter notes that opening an XPI can trigger extraction even when the WebExtensions feature is not enabled by default.

Affected versions: Epiphany >= 47.rc.
Fixed upstream in epiphany 50.6 and 49.9 via merge request !2143, which adds ARCHIVE_EXTRACT_SECURE_NODOTDOT and ARCHIVE_EXTRACT_SECURE_SYMLINKS to archive_write_disk_set_options().
Upstream report: https://gitlab.gnome.org/GNOME/epiphany/-/issues/2922
title: epiphany: path traversal in WebExtension XPI extraction (ZIP slip)

desc:
A code injection vulnerability exists in Epiphany when the user invokes form autofill from the context menu on a page containing a malicious HTML form.

In embed/web-process-extension/resources/js/ephy_autofill.js, getSelector() builds a CSS selector by directly interpolating an element's id attribute:

    path.unshift(`#${el.id}`);

When the user selects an autofill entry, the browser process in embed/ephy-web-view.c previously constructed JavaScript using sprintf with the selector embedded in single quotes:

    EphyAutofill.fill(PAGE_ID, 'SELECTOR', FILL_CHOICE);

Because SELECTOR comes from attacker-controlled page content and is not escaped, a crafted id such as a'); PAYLOAD; var _=(' breaks out of the string literal and executes arbitrary JavaScript when the script is evaluated.

The injected code runs in Epiphany's private autofill script world, which hosts EphyAutofill credential APIs and password manager save/request handlers. The reporter demonstrated a proof of concept that injects credentials into another domain and uses Ephy.permissionsManager to enumerate domains with special permissions. Full exfiltration of all saved passwords was not demonstrated but may be possible given the privileges of this context.

Exploitation requires the victim to visit a malicious page, right-click on a form field, and choose an Autofill context menu item. This is a deliberate user action but does not require installing software or entering credentials manually.

Affected versions: Epiphany >= 47.beta.
Fixed upstream in epiphany 50.6 and 49.9 via merge request !2147, which replaces sprintf-based script evaluation with a WebKit user message and jsc_value_object_invoke_method() passing the selector as a typed string argument.
Upstream report: https://gitlab.gnome.org/GNOME/epiphany/-/issues/2921
title: epiphany: JavaScript code injection in autofill via unsanitized CSS selector from element id

desc: A **NULL pointer dereference** flaw has been found in the vlv_value_compare() function in vlv_pagination.c of the Virtual List View module in the **Samba** package. A low-privileged network attacker or user who can search the directory sends a Virtual List View search by value, sorted on an attribute the matching entries do not have. desc: The W3 Total Cache plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to unauthorized File Deletion in all versions up to, and including, 2.11.0 via the `ajax_revert()` AJAX handler. The vulnerability exists because the `remove_optimizations()` function reads attacker-controlled values from the unprotected `w3tc_imageservice` post meta key — which carries no underscore prefix and no registered authorization callback, making it writable by any user with `edit_post` capability via WordPress's built-in custom-fields AJAX endpoint — and passes those values directly to `wp_delete_attachment()` with no check that the referenced ID is a child of the caller's own post, is an actual attachment, or that the caller holds `delete_post` capability on it. This makes it possible for authenticated attackers with Author-level access or above to permanently delete any WordPress attachment in the media library, including media files owned by other users along with their associated files on disk, regardless of ownership — a capability not available through the normal WordPress interface. The revert nonce is exposed via `wp_localize_script` on `/wp-admin/upload.php` to any user with `upload_files` capability, ensuring the nonce check that is present does not serve as a meaningful barrier to Author-level exploitation.

The file server reserves memory for a named-pipe response using a size chosen by the client. It does not keep that size within the maximum the client and the server have already agreed. A low-privileged network attacker or user who can open a named pipe can request a very large response. The file server reserves that memory before it reads the pipe and holds it until the request ends. Repeating this on more connections can exhaust memory and keep the file service unavailable while those requests continue.

desc: @fastify/express is the plugin that lets an application run Express middleware and Express applications inside the Fastify web framework. In versions from 4.0.3 before 4.0.14, the plugin decodes certain percent-encoded characters in the request path that Express would otherwise keep encoded, including the Unicode line separator and paragraph separator characters, and leaves them raw. A JavaScript regular expression treats those two characters as line terminators, so a regular-expression mount path that relies on the dot metacharacter fails to match a request containing them while Fastify's own router still routes the request to its handler, and the middleware mounted on that regular-expression path is therefore skipped. An attacker can use this to bypass authentication or other middleware-based access controls on routes guarded by a regular-expression mount; string mount paths are not affected. The issue is fixed in @fastify/express 4.0.14, and users should upgrade to 4.0.14 or later. As a workaround, use string mount paths, avoid the dot metacharacter in regular-expression mounts by using a character class or the dotAll flag, or enforce authentication in a Fastify hook such as preHandler that runs after the router resolves the request.
title: @fastify/express vulnerable to RegExp middleware bypass via encoded line terminators

desc: @fastify/express is the plugin that lets an application run Express middleware and Express applications inside the Fastify web framework. In versions from 4.0.7 before 4.0.14, when middleware is mounted on a nested array of mount paths the plugin rewrites only the top level of the array, so paths inside a nested array are not adjusted for a plugin registered under a prefix and the middleware never runs for them, a nested regular-expression mount keeps its global or sticky flag and is matched statefully so it is skipped on alternating requests, a nested regular expression is not matched case-insensitively when case sensitivity is disabled, and nested dynamic paths are not covered by the earlier empty-segment check. An attacker can use any of these to bypass authentication or other middleware-based access controls on the affected routes. The issue is fixed in @fastify/express 4.0.14, and users should upgrade to 4.0.14 or later. As a workaround, flatten mount path arrays before passing them to the plugin, or enforce authentication in a Fastify hook such as preHandler that runs after the router resolves the request.
title: @fastify/express vulnerable to middleware bypass via nested arrays of mount paths

desc: @fastify/express is the plugin that lets an application run Express middleware and Express applications inside the Fastify web framework. In versions from 4.0.5 before 4.0.14, a mount path that begins with an Express 5 optional leading segment written as a group is treated as relative and has a slash prepended when it is joined to the plugin prefix, which changes what the pattern matches so the middleware ends up mounted on a path that no longer corresponds to the real request paths. The middleware therefore never runs for requests that match the intended routes, while the Fastify routes still resolve to their handlers. An attacker can use this to bypass authentication or other middleware-based access controls on the affected routes. The issue is fixed in @fastify/express 4.0.14, and users should upgrade to 4.0.14 or later. As a workaround, mount the middleware on each path spelling explicitly, or enforce authentication in a Fastify hook such as preHandler that runs after the router resolves the request.
title: @fastify/express vulnerable to middleware bypass via mount paths starting with an optional group

desc: @fastify/express is the plugin that lets an application run Express middleware and Express applications inside the Fastify web framework. In versions before 4.0.14, a request with an empty dynamic route parameter reaches a Fastify route handler while middleware mounted for that path inside an Express Router or sub-application is skipped, because Fastify's router accepts an empty value where Express requires a non-empty one, and an unanchored regular-expression mount passed to the plugin is bypassed the same way. An earlier fix covered only the mount paths passed to the plugin directly, not middleware mounted inside a routed Express application. An attacker can use this to bypass authentication or other middleware-based access controls on the affected routes, with the practical impact depending on what the empty value selects in the application. The issue is fixed in @fastify/express 4.0.14, and users should upgrade to 4.0.14 or later. As a workaround, enforce authentication in a Fastify hook such as preHandler that runs after routing, mount the middleware on a static parent path, or require non-empty values in the route params schema.
title: @fastify/express vulnerable to middleware bypass via empty route parameters in Express routers and sub-applications

desc: @fastify/express is the plugin that lets an application run Express middleware and Express applications inside the Fastify web framework. In versions before 4.0.14, when an application enables case-insensitive routing, middleware mounted on a path can still be skipped in two cases: a string mount path or plugin prefix containing a Unicode character whose case folding differs from a plain lowercase conversion fails to match the lowercased request path, and a matcher that stays case-sensitive inside an Express Router or application, such as a regular expression without the ignore-case flag or an explicitly case-sensitive router, only matches its own casing. In both cases a request reaches the Fastify route handler while the path-scoped middleware does not run. An attacker can use this to bypass authentication or other middleware-based access controls on the affected routes, and only applications that enable case-insensitive routing are affected. The issue is fixed in @fastify/express 4.0.14, and users should upgrade to 4.0.14 or later. As a workaround, enforce authentication in a Fastify hook such as preHandler that runs after routing, avoid such Unicode characters in mount paths, and match case-insensitively inside Express routers and applications.
title: @fastify/express vulnerable to middleware bypass with case-insensitive routing via Unicode mount paths and case-sensitive matchers
