title: Easy Form Builder by WhiteStudio <= 4.2.0 - Unauthenticated Stored Cross-Site Scripting via Map Field 'address' Parameter

desc: The WebP Express plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Authorization Bypass via Malformed Bcrypt Salt in all versions up to, and including, 0.25.15. This is due to insufficient validation of the attacker-supplied `salt` POST parameter in the `runAccessChecks()` function, which passes the unvalidated salt directly to PHP's `crypt()` — causing it to return an empty string when the salt contains characters outside the valid bcrypt alphabet `[./0-9A-Za-z]` — and then loosely compares the resulting empty string against the attacker-controlled `api-key-crypted` POST parameter using `==`, allowing an empty submission to match and satisfy the check. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to bypass the web service API-key authentication check and upload arbitrary image files to the cloud-conversion endpoint, where they persist at a predictable, publicly reachable path under `wp-content/webp-express/webp-images/wpc/`. The 'Require api-key to be crypted in transfer?' whitelist setting does not mitigate this bypass, as it only gates the plaintext API-key comparison branch and has no effect on the crypted-key branch containing the vulnerable logic.
title: WebP Express <= 0.25.15 - Unauthenticated Authorization Bypass via Malformed Bcrypt Salt via 'salt' and 'api-key-crypted' Parameters

desc: The ZarinPal Payment Gateway for WooCommerce plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Insecure Direct Object Reference in versions up to, and including, 5.1.1 via the `Return_from_ZarinPal_Gateway()` handler registered on the `woocommerce_api_wc_zpal` (`?wc-api=wc_zpal`) endpoint. The handler accepts a `wc_order` parameter from the query string, loads the corresponding WooCommerce order without any authentication, nonce, session, capability, or ownership check, and — when the order is paid — issues a 302 redirect to `get_return_url($order)`, whose `Location` header embeds the order's secret `order_key`. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to harvest order keys for arbitrary orders (regardless of payment method) and then use those keys against the WooCommerce order-received, order-pay and download endpoints to read the associated customer's PII, including billing name, street address, phone number, email, purchased items, and totals.
products: zarinpal:افزونه پرداخت امن زرین‌پال برای ووکامرس (zarinpal for woocommerce)
title: افزونه پرداخت امن زرین‌پال برای ووکامرس (ZarinPal for WooCommerce) <= 5.1.1 - Insecure Direct Object Reference to Unauthenticated Sensitive Information Exposure via 'wc_order' Parameter

desc: The SumUp Payment Gateway For WooCommerce plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Insecure Direct Object Reference in versions up to, and including, 2.17.1 via the 'sumup-validate-order' query parameter handled by the check_redirect_flow() / resolve_payment_redirect_validation() functions. The template_redirect handler accepts an arbitrary numeric order ID from an unauthenticated GET request and, without any ownership or capability check, loads the corresponding WooCommerce order and issues a 302 redirect whose Location header is built by get_return_url(), disclosing the target order's secret order_key. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to enumerate order IDs, harvest each order's WooCommerce order_key, and use those keys against the plugin's create_checkout endpoint and WooCommerce's own order-received/order-pay pages to read customer PII (name, email, phone, billing address, order total) for any order in the store.
title: SumUp Payment Gateway For WooCommerce <= 2.17.1 - Insecure Direct Object Reference to Unauthenticated Sensitive Information Exposure via 'sumup-validate-order' Parameter

desc: The Lenix Leads Collector plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via Form Field Name in all versions up to, and including, 2.0.0 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page. This is exploitable because the plugin's CF7 integration accepts and stores any extra field name not defined in the CF7 form — including HTML/JS payloads — submitted by an unauthenticated user via a public CF7 form submission, with the raw field name later echoed unescaped in two separate admin-side sinks.
title: Lenix Leads Collector <= 2.0.0 - Unauthenticated Stored Cross-Site Scripting via Form Field Name

desc: Web-token jwt-framework and jwt-library before 3.4.13, 4.0.x before 4.0.9, 4.1.x before 4.1.11, and 4.2.x before 4.2.6, and jwt-core through 3.2.10, perform unblinded RSA private key operations in RSAKey::exponentiate(), so CRT recombination time reveals whether a decrypted RSA-OAEP, RSA-OAEP-256, or RSA1_5 value is below the prime q. Attackers who can submit JWEs can time rejections of crafted tokens to binary search q, factor the modulus, and decrypt all JWEs encrypted to that key.
title: Web-token jwt-framework before 3.4.13 RSA Private Key Timing Side Channel

desc: web-token jwt-framework and jwt-library before 3.4.13, 4.0.x before 4.0.9, 4.1.x before 4.1.11, and 4.2.x before 4.2.6 parse JSON General serialized JWS tokens in quadratic time because JSONGeneralSerializer::unserialize() adds each signature via JWS::addSignature(), which clones the token. Unauthenticated remote attackers can send large tokens holding thousands of empty signatures to exhaust CPU and occupy PHP workers without any valid key or token.
title: web-token jwt-framework before 3.4.13 Denial of Service via JSONGeneralSerializer

desc: web-token jwt-framework and jwt-library before 3.4.13, 4.0.x before 4.0.9, 4.1.x before 4.1.11, and 4.2.x before 4.2.6, and jwt-encryption and jwt-signature through 3.2.10, contain a denial of service vulnerability because the JWS and JWE serializers pass attacker-controlled tokens and protected headers to json_decode() without bounds before verification. Unauthenticated attackers can submit large tokens with colliding header member names or deeply nested arrays to cause quadratic decoding time or fatal memory exhaustion.
title: web-token jwt-framework before 3.4.13 Denial of Service via Unbounded JSON Decoding

desc: The Warehouse Cargo theme for WordPress is vulnerable to Arbitrary File Upload in versions up to, and including, 2.7.4 via the warehouse_cargo_install_and_activate_plugin() AJAX handler. The handler is registered on wp_ajax_ but performs no nonce verification and no capability check, allowing any authenticated user to supply an attacker-controlled URL that the server fetches, writes into wp-content/plugins/ with file_put_contents(), extracts with unzip_file() (which does not filter file extensions), and then activates via activate_plugin(). This makes it possible for authenticated attackers, with Subscriber-level access and above, to upload arbitrary files on the affected site's server which makes remote code execution possible.
title: Warehouse Cargo <= 2.7.4 - Authenticated (Subscriber+) Arbitrary File Upload via 'plugin_details[plugin_url]' Parameter

desc: web-token jwt-framework before 3.4.13, 4.0.x before 4.0.9, 4.1.x before 4.1.11, and 4.2.x before 4.2.6 allows denial of service because JWELoader and JWSLoader try every recipient or signature of a JSON General serialized token without limiting their number. Unauthenticated attackers can send a small JWE with many empty recipients inheriting a maximal PBES2 p2c value, forcing repeated key derivations that exhaust worker CPU.
title: Web-token jwt-framework before 3.4.13 DoS via JWE/JWS Multiple Recipients

desc: Web-token jwt-framework and jwt-library before 3.4.13, 4.0.x before 4.0.9, 4.1.x before 4.1.11, and 4.2.x before 4.2.6 contain a denial of service vulnerability in RSAKey, which accepts RSA keys with a modulus and public exponent of unbounded length. Remote attackers can supply a crafted key, such as in the jwk header of a DPoP proof, to force seconds of CPU per PS256/PS384/PS512 verification or RSA encryption, or per any RSA operation when GMP is unavailable.
title: Web-token jwt-framework before 3.4.13 Denial of Service via Unbounded RSA Key Size

desc: Web-Token jwt-framework and jwt-library before 3.4.13, 4.0.0 before 4.0.9, 4.1.0 before 4.1.11, and 4.2.0 before 4.2.6, and jwt-encryption through 3.2.10, contain a token malleability flaw because JWEDecrypter does not reject a non-empty JWE Encrypted Key with the dir, ECDH-ES and ECDH-SS algorithms, which the authentication tag does not cover. Attackers holding one token can fill the Encrypted Key with arbitrary bytes to derive unlimited distinct token strings that still decrypt, bypassing replay caches, single-use registries or revocation deny-lists keyed on the token string.
title: Web-Token jwt-framework before 3.4.13 JWE Token Malleability via Non-Empty Encrypted Key

desc: web-token jwt-framework before 3.4.13, 4.0.0 before 4.0.9, 4.1.0 before 4.1.11, and 4.2.0 before 4.2.6 does not check oct key length in the AESKW, AESGCMKW, and experimental AESCTR and chacha20-poly1305 key encryption algorithms, so OpenSSL zero-pads short or empty keys. When an application uses an empty key, anyone can unwrap content encryption keys under the all-zero key to read issued tokens and forge accepted ones.
title: web-token jwt-framework before 3.4.13 Missing Key Length Check in AES Key Wrapping

desc: web-token jwt-framework from 4.2.1 before 4.2.6 contains an information disclosure vulnerability that exposes decryption keys in exception stack traces when JWE tokens are rejected. Attackers can submit crafted JWE tokens so JWELoader and JWEDecrypter record dir, AES key wrapping, PBES2-derived or content encryption keys in logged trace arguments readable by others.
title: web-token jwt-framework 4.2.1 before 4.2.6 Key Exposure via JWE Exception Traces

desc: web-token jwt-framework and jwt-library before 3.4.13, 4.0.x before 4.0.9, 4.1.x before 4.1.11, and 4.2.x before 4.2.6 allow CPU exhaustion because, on PHP without GMP, AbstractECDH falls back to pure PHP curve code that converts unbounded ECDH-ES epk x and y coordinates to big integers before any length check. Unauthenticated attackers who know only the recipient key's curve can send small JWEs with oversized epk coordinates, keeping workers busy for seconds to minutes per token.
title: web-token jwt-framework before 3.4.13 ECDH-ES DoS via Oversized epk Coordinate

desc: web-token jwt-framework and jwt-library before 3.4.13, 4.0.x before 4.0.9, 4.1.x before 4.1.11, and 4.2.x before 4.2.6 (and jwt-encryption through 3.2.10) do not check the key length in JWEBuilder and JWEDecrypter for direct (dir) encryption, so undersized keys are zero-padded. Anyone holding a token issued with a half-size AES-CBC-HMAC key can decrypt it, and an empty key also allows forging tokens the decrypter accepts.
title: web-token jwt-framework before 3.4.13 Missing Key Size Check in Direct Encryption

desc: Frappe Framework before 15.121.1 and 16.x before 16.35.0 accepts an undocumented OAuth2 Resource Owner Password Credentials (password) grant at its token endpoint, which does not enforce two-factor authentication or forced password resets. An attacker with a user's valid credentials can use this grant to obtain a full-access OAuth token, bypassing 2FA.
title: Frappe Framework before 16.35.0 2FA Bypass via OAuth2 Password Grant

desc: Frappe Framework before 15.120.0 and 16.x before 16.33.0 contains a blind SQL injection vulnerability in the handling of the X-Frappe-Request-Id HTTP header when monitoring is enabled. Remote unauthenticated attackers can send crafted header values to infer database contents through blind SQL injection techniques.
title: Frappe before 15.120.0 and 16.x before 16.33.0 Blind SQL Injection via X-Frappe-Request-Id Header

desc: Dockhand before 1.0.57 contains a path traversal vulnerability in validateStackPath, which omits the isProtectedPath() check and permits writes to protected system directories. Authenticated users with stacks:edit permission can send a crafted composePath to PUT /api/stacks/[name]/compose to write arbitrary files, such as cron payloads, achieving remote code execution as root.
title: Dockhand before 1.0.57 Path Traversal RCE via composePath

desc: web-token jwt-framework and jwt-library before 3.4.13, 4.0.0 before 4.0.9, 4.1.0 before 4.1.11, and 4.2.0 before 4.2.6 contain a decryption oracle in RSACrypt::decryptWithRSAOAEP(), which accepts a JWE Encrypted Key made of multiple RSA blocks instead of a single RSAES-OAEP ciphertext. Attackers holding the recipient's public key can embed a captured encrypted key among crafted blocks and, using an accepted AES-CBC-HMAC algorithm and a decryption success signal, recover its CEK byte by byte to decrypt the captured JWE.
title: web-token jwt-framework before 3.4.13 RSA-OAEP Multi-Block Decryption Oracle

desc: Frappe Framework before 15.119.0 and 16.x before 16.32.0 does not neutralize spreadsheet formula elements in user-supplied data included in CSV and XLSX exports, resulting in stored formula injection. Authenticated attackers can store crafted values that are interpreted as formulas when another user opens the exported file in a spreadsheet application.
title: Frappe Framework before 16.32.0 Stored Formula Injection in CSV and XLSX Exports

desc: SunEditor from 3.0.0 before 3.4.3 contains a stored cross-site scripting vulnerability in the codeBlock plugin that allows attackers to inject script via entity-encoded pre language class values. Attackers can store content whose language- class decodes to HTML written via innerHTML into the hover button, executing script when victims hover over the block.
title: SunEditor 3.0.0 before 3.4.3 Stored XSS via codeBlock Language Hover Button

desc: Coder before 2.29.27, 2.30.0 before 2.34.19, 2.35.0 before 2.37.11, 2.38.0 before 2.38.7, and 2.39.0 before 2.39.1 returns database connection errors containing a temporary AWS IAM database password in API key middleware responses. During database connection failures, unauthenticated attackers can send a well-formed but invalid API key to obtain the password and access the PostgreSQL database for 15 minutes.
title: Coder from 2.39.0 before 2.39.1 Database Password Exposure via API Errors

desc: Coder before 2.29.27, 2.30.0 before 2.34.19, 2.35.0 before 2.37.11, and 2.38.0 before 2.38.7 does not validate the URL scheme of the agent-supplied uri field in app status updates, which the dashboard renders as a clickable link. An attacker holding a workspace agent token, including a prompt-injected AI agent, can show workspace or task viewers links that send them to phishing sites or non-web applications.
title: Coder from 2.38.0 before 2.38.7 Unsafe URL Scheme in App Status Links

desc: Frappe Framework before 15.122.0 and 16.x before 16.50.0 contains a missing authorization vulnerability in Document.update() that fails to validate whether the caller is permitted to submit or modify the target document. Attackers can invoke document update operations to submit or alter documents they are not authorized to change.
title: Frappe Framework before 15.122.0 Authorization Bypass via Document.update()

desc: Frappe Framework before 15.121.2 and 16.x before 16.36.0 exposes functions imported into module-path-hooked modules as Jinja globals, making them callable from sandboxed templates. Authenticated users who can author rendered templates, such as Print Formats, can invoke these functions by name to achieve server-side code execution that bypasses the Jinja sandbox.
title: Frappe before 16.36.0 Jinja Sandbox Bypass via Module-Path Hooks

desc: pypdf before 7.0.1 contains a resource exhaustion vulnerability in image loading because data size estimates for some image modes are too low, defeating limits for filters without their own size limit. Attackers can craft a PDF whose images, when loaded, cause large memory usage and denial of service.
title: pypdf before 7.0.1 Excessive Memory Usage via Crafted PDF Images

desc: LaraDashboard before 1.5.2 contains a missing authorization vulnerability in the QuickDraft Livewire component that allows any authenticated user to create posts without the post.create permission. Attackers such as self-registered Subscriber accounts can submit the dashboard Quick Draft widget to inject draft posts, bypassing the PostPolicy check enforced by PostController.
title: LaraDashboard before 1.5.2 Missing Authorization via Quick Draft Dashboard Widget

desc: LaraDashboard before 1.5.2 contains an information disclosure vulnerability in SettingObserver that writes full Setting models, including plaintext secret option_value fields, into the action_logs table. Users holding only actionlog.view can read API keys, SMTP passwords, and OAuth client secrets through the action log API without settings permissions.
title: LaraDashboard before 1.5.2 Secret Settings Exposure via SettingObserver Action Log

desc: LaraDashboard before 1.5.2 contains a server-side request forgery vulnerability that allows authenticated users to reach internal services by abusing the unvalidated ai_ollama_base_url setting. Once a settings.edit user points the Ollama base URL internally, any post.create user can call /admin/ai/generate-seo with provider=ollama to fetch internal data reflected in SEO fields.
title: LaraDashboard before 1.5.2 SSRF via ai_ollama_base_url and generate-seo endpoint

desc: LaraDashboard before 1.5.0 contains a path traversal vulnerability in module.json providers and composer.json psr-4 namespace parsing that derives destination folder names without excluding traversal characters. Attackers with module.create permission can upload a crafted module ZIP to write PHP files into the public directory, achieving unauthenticated remote code execution.
title: LaraDashboard before 1.5.0 Path Traversal RCE via module.json Namespace Parsing

desc: Coder 2.29.17 before 2.29.27, 2.32.7 before 2.33.0, 2.33.8 before 2.34.0, 2.34.2 before 2.34.19, 2.35.0 before 2.37.11, 2.38.0 before 2.38.7, and 2.39.0 before 2.39.1 contains a credential exposure vulnerability that allows malicious template authors to steal session tokens because coder open app substitutes $SESSION_TOKEN into template-defined external app URLs without validating scheme or destination. Attackers can define an external app URL or IDE link pointing to an attacker server so users running coder open app leak their token, enabling impersonation of shared users or administrators.
title: Coder from 2.39.0 before 2.39.1 Session Token Leak via coder open app

desc: Coder 2.9.0 before 2.29.27, 2.30.0 before 2.34.12, 2.35.0 before 2.35.9, 2.36.0 before 2.36.7, and 2.37.0 before 2.37.3 contains a nil pointer dereference in the tailnet coordinator, which reads UpdateSelf.Node fields during authorization without checking that Node is set. An authenticated user or workspace agent token holder can send a CoordinateRequest with UpdateSelf present but Node empty to crash coderd, disconnecting all users on the affected replica.
title: Coder 2.37.0 before 2.37.3 DoS via nil Node in tailnet UpdateSelf

desc: ToolJet before 3.21.96-LTS contains an information disclosure vulnerability that allows low-privilege app/query viewers to obtain plaintext workspace secrets by running REST queries. Attackers can execute queries via POST /data-queries/:id/run whose URL params or non-redacted headers reference secrets, reading resolved values from metadata.request despite lacking decrypted constants access.
title: ToolJet before 3.21.96-LTS Secret Disclosure via REST Query Metadata

desc: ToolJet before 3.21.94-beta contains an authentication bypass in its server OAuth SSO sign-in module, which resolves Google and Git SSO logins solely by the provider-asserted email without checking email_verified or binding the SSO subject. Unauthenticated attackers can submit a trusted-issuer token carrying a victim's unverified email to the SSO callback to obtain the victim's session, including admin accounts.
title: ToolJet before 3.21.94-beta Account Takeover via SSO Email-Based Account Linking

desc: ToolJet before 3.21.96-LTS contains a missing authorization vulnerability that allows authenticated End Users to execute data queries of apps in other organizations via POST /api/data-queries/:id/run. Attackers can supply a target data-query id and runtime resolvedOptions to run queries with the datasource's decrypted credentials, reading cross-tenant query results.
title: ToolJet before 3.21.96-LTS Cross-Tenant Data Query Execution via Data-Queries Run Endpoint

desc: ToolJet before 3.21.96-LTS contains an insufficient session expiration vulnerability that allows attackers to reuse expired JWTs because the passport-jwt strategy sets ignoreExpiration to true. Attackers holding a leaked tj_auth_token can keep sessions alive through auto-extended expiry and two-year cookies to persistently access victim accounts.
title: ToolJet before 3.21.96-LTS JWT Expiration Bypass via jwt.strategy.ts

desc: ToolJet before 3.21.96-LTS contains an information disclosure vulnerability that allows authenticated low-privilege users to recover plaintext workspace secret constants through OAuth URL generation. Attackers can send POST /api/data-sources/fetch-oauth2-base-url with {{secrets.*}} in source_options and arbitrary organization_id and environment_id to receive secrets, including other workspaces' secrets, in the returned authorization URL.
title: ToolJet before 3.21.96-LTS Secret Disclosure via fetch-oauth2-base-url

desc: Tornado before 6.6.1 contains an information disclosure vulnerability in StaticFileHandler on Windows that allows unauthenticated attackers to read NTFS Alternate Data Streams by appending :streamname to URL paths. Attackers can request stream paths that pass the get_absolute_path and _check_in_root prefix checks to read hidden stream content, such as stored secrets or Zone.Identifier source data.
title: Tornado before 6.6.1 NTFS Alternate Data Stream Disclosure via StaticFileHandler

desc: ToolJet before 3.21.96-LTS contains an authorization bypass in the internal database (TJDB) PostgREST proxy, which grants proxy access to every logged-in user and derives the database role and schema from the client-supplied tj-workspace-id header. Any authenticated workspace member can send requests to /api/tooljet-db/proxy/<tableId> to read and modify TJDB tables, bypassing app, query, and table permissions, and in SQL-mode-disabled (Cloud) deployments can access all tenants' tables.
title: ToolJet before 3.21.96-LTS Authorization Bypass via TJDB PostgREST Proxy

desc: ToolJet before 3.21.96-LTS contains a cross-workspace authorization bypass in the organization-users archive and unarchive endpoints, which take the target organizationId from the request body without validating it against the caller's authorized workspaces. An admin of any workspace who knows a target organization-user ID and workspace UUID can archive or unarchive users in other tenants' workspaces, locking them out of those workspaces and tampering with the audit trail.
title: ToolJet before 3.21.96-LTS Cross-Workspace IDOR via Organization Users Archive/Unarchive

desc: ToolJet before 3.21.94-beta contains an authorization bypass vulnerability in getVersionsByEnvironment that allows authenticated users to read another organization's application versions due to missing organizationId scoping. Attackers can request the app-environments versions route with their own priority-1 production environment id and a victim app_id to retrieve the victim's version list and structure.
title: ToolJet before 3.21.94-beta Cross-Tenant App Version Disclosure via getVersionsByEnvironment

desc: ToolJet before 3.21.96-LTS contains an authorization bypass vulnerability that allows view-only workspace users to execute queries in restricted environments by supplying an arbitrary environmentId. Attackers can call the data-queries run endpoint for draft app versions to execute queries with stored datasource credentials, exposing development or staging data.
title: ToolJet before 3.21.96-LTS Authorization Bypass via Data Query Run Endpoint

desc: ToolJet before 3.21.96-LTS contains an insecure direct object reference vulnerability that allows authenticated users to read cross-workspace files by requesting a known File UUID. Attackers can request GET /api/files/:id with another workspace's File UUID to retrieve stored file bytes, such as avatars, without parent resource authorization checks.
title: ToolJet before 3.21.96-LTS IDOR via GET /api/files/:id Endpoint

desc: ToolJet before 3.21.96-LTS contains an authorization bypass vulnerability that allows authenticated same-organization users to invoke OAuth2 authorization on data sources they cannot configure. Attackers can send POST requests to /api/data-sources/:id/authorize_oauth2 to bind attacker-controlled OAuth credentials or overwrite token state for foreign data sources.
title: ToolJet before 3.21.96-LTS Authorization Bypass via authorize_oauth2 Data Source Route

desc: ToolJet before 3.21.96-LTS is missing the ValidateDataSourceGuard on the dependent-queries route of the data-sources controller and does not scope the datasource lookup to the caller's organization. An authenticated admin or builder with dataSourceDelete can request /api/data-sources/dependent-queries/<datasource_uuid> to confirm a datasource exists in another organization and learn its dependent-query count.
title: ToolJet before 3.21.96-LTS Cross-Organization Information Disclosure via dependent-queries Route

desc: ToolJet before 3.21.96-LTS contains an insecure direct object reference vulnerability that allows authenticated builders to read, modify, or delete other organizations' app-builder components, pages, and events. Attackers can target their own app/version in the URL to pass ValidAppGuard, then supply victim resource ids that services query without appVersionId or organizationId scoping.
title: ToolJet before 3.21.96-LTS Cross-Organization IDOR via App-Builder Component, Page, Event APIs

desc: ToolJet before 3.21.96-LTS contains an authorization bypass vulnerability in QueryAuthGuard that allows unauthenticated attackers to execute queries from unreleased app versions. Attackers can POST to the data-queries run endpoint with a draft query ID from any public app to execute unpublished queries against connected datasources.
title: ToolJet before 3.21.96-LTS Unauthenticated Draft Query Execution via QueryAuthGuard

desc: ToolJet before 3.21.96-LTS contains an authentication bypass in instance-level Google SSO because the id_token audience is not verified when no Google OAuth client ID is configured, the shipped default. Unauthenticated attackers can submit a Google-signed id_token minted for their own OAuth client to /api/sso/sign-in/common/google without an organizationId, obtaining a session as any existing user with the matching email.
title: ToolJet through 3.20.213-lts Authentication Bypass via Google SSO Audience Check

desc: ToolJet before 3.21.96-LTS contains an information disclosure vulnerability that allows users with TEST_CONNECTION ability to exfiltrate organization secrets by resolving secret placeholders in test-connection options. Attackers can point the host and port at a listener they control and set the password option to a secrets template, causing the server to send the plaintext secret to them.
title: ToolJet before 3.21.96-LTS Secrets Exfiltration via Datasource test-connection Endpoint

desc: ToolJet from 3.20.84 before 3.21.96-LTS contains an authentication bypass vulnerability in the instance-level SSO sign-in path that hardcodes signup as enabled, ignoring all signup-disable controls. Any user with an account on the configured GitHub or Google identity provider can sign in via the OAuth endpoint to obtain an admin session in a newly created workspace.
title: ToolJet 3.20.84 before 3.21.96-LTS Signup Control Bypass via Instance-Level SSO

desc: AzuraCast before 0.24.1 contains a missing authorization vulnerability in RelaysController::updateAction that allows any authenticated user to modify shared relays and delete other stations' relay associations. Attackers can POST a relay base_url to /internal/relays to rename the relay, wipe StationRemote rows of unmanaged stations, and spoof public now-playing data.
title: AzuraCast before 0.24.1 Missing Authorization via POST /internal/relays

desc: AzuraCast before 0.24.0 contains a missing authorization vulnerability in the StationPublicApi middleware that allows any authenticated user to access non-public stations without per-station permissions. Attackers can change the station_id path parameter to list and download on-demand media, read schedule data, and submit song requests to unauthorized stations.
title: AzuraCast before 0.24.0 Missing Authorization in Station API Anonymous Functions Routes

desc: ToolJet from 3.8.0 before 3.21.96-LTS contains an authorization bypass vulnerability that allows authenticated builders to modify queries in view-only apps by supplying cross-app query IDs. Attackers can send PATCH requests to /api/data-queries/versions/:versionId naming an editable app version with another app's query ID, then run the overwritten query using that app's data source connection.
title: ToolJet 3.8.0 before 3.21.96-LTS Authorization Bypass via Bulk Query Update

desc: Nodemailer 9.1.0 before 10.4.1 lowercases recipient domains with JavaScript toLowerCase() in _normalizeAddress before UTS-46 mapping, which converts U+1E9E and word-final U+03A3 differently than WHATWG/UTS-46 validators. An unprivileged attacker can submit an address an application's allow-list approves, causing invites or shared links to reach an attacker-registered domain.
title: Nodemailer 9.1.0 before 10.4.1 IDN Allow-List Bypass via toLowerCase() Domain Normalization

desc: ToolJet before 3.21.94-beta contains an improper authorization vulnerability that allows Builders with only data source Delete permission to update global data sources via the PUT /api/data-sources endpoint. Attackers can change a REST data source base URL so later query executions send stored Bearer credentials to an attacker-controlled endpoint.
title: ToolJet before 3.21.94-beta Improper Authorization in Data Source Update

desc: Scriban before 7.6.0 contains a memory exhaustion vulnerability in object.to_json that allows template authors to bypass the LimitToString string length limit by serializing into an unbounded MemoryStream. Attackers can repeatedly apply object.to_json to escape-heavy strings in a tiny template, amplifying output to multi-gigabyte heap allocations and causing denial of service.
title: Scriban before 7.6.0 Memory Exhaustion DoS via object.to_json

desc: Scriban and Scriban.Signed before 7.6.0 allow template authors to bypass the LimitToString string length limit because the string.literal, string.base64_encode, html.escape, html.newline_to_br, html.url_encode, and html.url_escape builtins lack allocation guards. An attacker who can supply a small template can repeatedly call these builtins under the default TemplateContext to force multi-gigabyte allocations and exhaust host memory.
title: Scriban before 7.6.0 Memory Exhaustion via Unguarded String and HTML Builtins

desc: Scriban before 7.6.0 contains a state isolation vulnerability because TemplateContext.Reset() does not clear the Tags dictionary holding array.cycle and math.random state. Attackers supplying templates to a reused context can observe or influence cycle positions and random sequences across renders, and accumulate unbounded cycle entries to exhaust memory.
title: Scriban before 7.6.0 State Leakage via TemplateContext.Reset() Tags

desc: Scriban before 7.6.0 contains a resource exhaustion vulnerability that allows attackers to bypass LoopLimit by supplying large JSON input to object.from_json. Attackers can pass a flat JSON array or object with hundreds of thousands of elements, which JsonElementExtensions materializes without loop checks, exhausting CPU and memory.
title: Scriban before 7.6.0 LoopLimit Bypass via object.from_json Resource Exhaustion

desc: justhtml before 3.17.0 contains a denial of service vulnerability in decode_entities_in_text that allows unauthenticated attackers to crash parsing via non-ASCII Unicode digits in numeric character references. Attackers can submit a payload like &#² in HTML text or attributes, causing an uncaught ValueError from int() that aborts JustHTML() and stream() parsing.
title: justhtml before 3.17.0 Denial of Service via Unicode Digit Numeric Entity

desc: Scriban before 7.6.0 contains a resource exhaustion vulnerability that allows template authors to bypass LimitToString by rendering a ScriptObject with many members. Attackers can supply a small template whose ScriptObject.ToString concatenates large member values without length tracking, allocating multi-gigabyte strings and causing memory exhaustion.
title: Scriban before 7.6.0 LimitToString Bypass via ScriptObject String Conversion

desc: Budibase Server from 3.39.18 before 4.0.0 contains a prototype pollution vulnerability that allows unauthenticated attackers to erase MongoDB query filters by supplying __proto__ as a dynamic JSON key in PUBLIC queries. Attackers can send a single request to the query execution endpoint, reducing the filter to {} to read, update, or delete every document in the collection.
title: Budibase Server 3.39.18 before 4.0.0 MongoDB Filter Erasure via __proto__ Keys

desc: Budibase from 3.41.0 before 4.0.0 contains an authentication bypass vulnerability that allows unauthenticated attackers to take over password-less global Builder accounts via unverified-email OIDC/SSO account linking. Attackers can assert a victim's email with email_verified=false at a trusted IdP, bypassing the isAccountLinkable allowlist to control all apps, datasources, and automations.
title: Budibase 3.41.0 before 4.0.0 Account Takeover via Unverified-Email OIDC Linking

desc: Budibase before 4.0.0 contains a privilege escalation vulnerability that allows non-admin Creator or app-builder users to read pending invite bearer codes via GET /api/global/users/invites. Attackers can submit a stolen code with a chosen password to the public /api/global/users/invite/accept endpoint, hijacking invited identities up to global admin.
title: Budibase before 4.0.0 Privilege Escalation via Invite Code Disclosure

desc: Budibase Server before 4.0.0 contains an authorization bypass in its single-row read and attachment endpoints, which fetch rows by ID without enforcing the requesting view's row filter. Authenticated users with read access to a filtered view can request GET /api/:viewId/rows/:rowId or GET /api/:viewId/rows/:rowId/attachment/:columnName with a hidden row ID to retrieve that row's data and attachments.
title: Budibase Server before 4.0.0 View Row-Filter Bypass via Single-Row Read Endpoints

desc: actix-multipart (actix-web) before 0.8.7 contains a resource exhaustion vulnerability in the MultipartForm extractor that allows unauthenticated attackers to exhaust memory or file descriptors by sending unlimited parts. Attackers can stream many zero-byte parts uncounted by total_limit and memory_limit, pinning 128 KiB buffers or opening temporary files to crash workers.
title: actix-multipart before 0.8.7 Denial of Service via Unlimited MultipartForm Parts

desc: actix-http before 3.20.4 contains a response desynchronization vulnerability in its HTTP/1 client response decoder, which reads bodies on 1xx, 204 and 304 responses based on Content-Length or Transfer-Encoding headers. Servers sending such responses with framing headers cause awc clients to consume subsequent keep-alive responses, causing request failures or misattributing responses across users in proxies.
title: actix-http before 3.20.4 HTTP/1 Response Desync via 1xx/204/304 Body Parsing

desc: Budibase before 4.0.0 contains a JSON injection vulnerability that allows attackers to inject JSON structure into S3 delete and Google Sheets row fields via unescaped template parameters. Attackers can submit crafted parameters to the queries endpoint to add extra Key entries, deleting chosen S3 objects or overriding Sheets row columns.
title: Budibase before 4.0.0 JSON Injection via S3 Delete and Google Sheets Query Fields

desc: Budibase before 4.0.0 contains an insecure direct object reference vulnerability in the bulkDestroy function that allows authenticated users to delete rows from any workspace table by supplying foreign row IDs. Attackers with TABLE WRITE on one table can send row _id values from other tables to the DELETE /api/:sourceId/rows endpoint, causing data loss and workspace metadata deletion.
title: Budibase before 4.0.0 Cross-Table IDOR via bulkDestroy Row Deletion

desc: Budibase before 4.0.0 contains a server-side template injection vulnerability that allows authenticated users with table read permission to execute JavaScript by injecting Handlebars js helpers into row search query values. Attackers can submit base64-encoded JavaScript through the search endpoint, which enrichSearchContext() runs in an isolated-vm sandbox, to read OAuth2 access and refresh tokens of SSO users or cause denial of service.
title: Budibase before 4.0.0 SSTI via enrichSearchContext in Row Search

desc: Budibase before 4.0.0 contains an information disclosure vulnerability that allows unauthenticated attackers to retrieve legacy LiteLLM credentials by querying the public settings endpoint. Attackers can send unauthenticated GET requests to /api/global/configs/public to obtain liteLLM.keyId and secretKey, enabling unauthorized use of tenant LiteLLM resources.
title: Budibase before 4.0.0 Information Disclosure via /api/global/configs/public

desc: SurrealDB before 4.0.0 contains a server-side request forgery vulnerability in the remote HTTP client router that passes raw model names to Url::join during ML export. Attackers can supply an absolute URL as the model name in ExportMl or ExportBytesMl commands to redirect authenticated requests and capture session tokens.
title: SurrealDB before 4.0.0 SSRF and Credential Leakage via ML Model Export

desc: SurrealDB before 4.0.0 contains an authorization bypass vulnerability that allows restricted subjects to execute arbitrary queries by calling the JavaScript surrealdb.query() bridge. Attackers permitted to run a specific script can bypass the Capabilities::allows_query() gate in the query module to execute unrestricted queries beyond their predefined operations.
title: SurrealDB before 4.0.0 Authorization Bypass via JavaScript surrealdb.query() Bridge

desc: Budibase before 4.0.0 contains a query injection vulnerability that allows low-privilege or anonymous users to inject AQL or SQL by supplying unescaped parameters to ArangoDB and Snowflake queries. Attackers can execute published queries with crafted parameter values to bypass filters, read entire datasources, and modify or delete all stored documents.
title: Budibase before 4.0.0 Query Injection in ArangoDB and Snowflake Datasources

desc: Budibase before 4.0.0 contains an authorization bypass vulnerability that allows workspace-scoped builders to access other workspaces' backups by supplying a foreign backupId. Attackers can substitute predictable backup IDs in backup download, import, update, or delete routes to steal archives, restore victim data into their workspace, or delete backups.
title: Budibase before 4.0.0 Workspace Backup Authorization Bypass via backupId

desc: Budibase before 4.0.0 contains a broken object-level authorization vulnerability that allows authenticated users with table write access to reference other tenants' files by supplying arbitrary attachment keys on row save. Attackers can inject a victim app's attachment key into a row, then update or delete the row to delete that object from the shared APPS bucket or read it via presigned URLs.
title: Budibase before 4.0.0 Cross-Tenant File Deletion via Attachment Key

desc: Budibase server from 3.0.0 before 4.0.0 contains an authorization bypass vulnerability that allows view users and anonymous visitors to access entire base tables by passing a view id to the /api/:viewId/rows routes. Attackers can read, export, modify, and delete rows outside the view filter, including hidden columns, or read the full table unauthenticated through PUBLIC views.
title: Budibase from 3.0.0 before 4.0.0 Authorization Bypass via View Row Routes

desc: Hono from 4.13.11 before 4.13.18 contains a middleware bypass vulnerability in serveStatic that allows unauthenticated attackers to skip prefix middleware by exploiting a second path decode when allowPercentInPath is enabled. Attackers can send malformed percent-encoded sequences so the router matches an encoded path while serveStatic serves the real file, bypassing authentication checks.
title: Hono 4.13.11 before 4.13.18 Middleware Bypass via serveStatic allowPercentInPath

desc: Hono from 4.5.1 before 4.13.18 contains a validation bypass vulnerability in validator('json') and validator('form') that allows unauthenticated attackers to skip validation by formatting Content-Type parameters differently. Attackers can add whitespace before semicolons, trailing semicolons, or underscored parameter names so validators receive empty objects while handlers still read rejected fields.
title: Hono 4.5.1 before 4.13.18 Validation Bypass via Content-Type Formatting

desc: Hono from 4.13.16 before 4.13.18 contains an authorization bypass vulnerability in mount() and app.mount() that forwards an incorrect path when a custom getPath adds a prefix. Unauthenticated attackers can request crafted paths that the mounted application resolves differently, reaching routes protected by path-scoped middleware such as authentication checks.
title: Hono 4.13.16 before 4.13.18 Middleware Bypass via mount() Path Forwarding

desc: OpenWrt LuCI luci-app-unbound through 26.288.56989~75a306d contains a stored cross-site scripting vulnerability because the Unbound Configure page inserts the dhcp.odhcpd.leasetrigger value into a warning notification without escaping. Users with delegated network configuration access can store an HTML event handler in that option through the permitted uci RPC, which executes in an administrator's browser session when the page renders.
title: OpenWrt LuCI Unbound Stored XSS via odhcpd leasetrigger Notice

desc: Hono from 4.12.16 before 4.13.18 contains a memory exhaustion vulnerability in the bodyLimit() middleware that retains every transfer chunk as a separate array. Unauthenticated attackers can send a within-limit request body in one-byte chunks to create millions of retained objects, terminating Bun or Node.js processes.
title: Hono 4.12.16 before 4.13.18 Memory Exhaustion via bodyLimit() Middleware

desc: SurrealDB before 4.0.0 contains an information disclosure vulnerability that allows authenticated users to read SELECT-hidden edge endpoints through InOverride/OutOverride error messages. Attackers with CREATE and UPDATE permission on an edge table can re-RELATE an existing edge with mismatched endpoints to recover stored in/out record ids despite row- or field-level restrictions.
title: SurrealDB before 4.0.0 Information Disclosure via RELATE Endpoint Override Errors

desc: Traefik before 2.11.62, 3.x before 3.7.18, and 3.8.0-rc.1 contain an authentication bypass in the ForwardAuth middleware because connection isolation for NTLM and Negotiate credentials checks only the Authorization header, not Proxy-Authorization. Unauthenticated attackers can send such credentials in Proxy-Authorization to reuse a shared authentication-server connection already authenticated by another user, receive that user's identity via authResponseHeaders, and access backends as that user.
title: Traefik before 2.11.62 ForwardAuth NTLM Authentication Bypass via Proxy-Authorization

desc: Traefik 3.7.15 before 3.7.18 and 3.8.0-rc.1 before 3.8.0-rc.2 contains a client certificate authentication bypass in the Kubernetes Ingress NGINX provider because, on hosts shared by multiple Ingresses using auth-tls-secret, Ssl-Client-* headers are built per Ingress while the TLS handshake uses the first Ingress's settings. Unauthenticated remote attackers can obtain Ssl-Client-Verify: SUCCESS with a client-chosen subject and issuer for an unverified certificate, or inject Ssl-Client-* headers directly, presenting forged identities to backends that trust the proxy.
title: Traefik 3.7.15 before 3.7.18 Client Certificate Verification Bypass via Ssl-Client Headers

desc: Traefik before 2.11.62, 3.x before 3.7.18, and 3.8.0-rc.1 contain an authorization bypass because the sanitizePath entry point option leaves dot-segments carrying path parameters, such as /..;x/, unresolved when matching routers and applying middlewares. Unauthenticated attackers can send requests like /public/..;x/admin to a parameter-stripping backend shared with a protected router, bypassing authentication or authorization middlewares to reach protected resources.
title: Traefik before 2.11.62 Authorization Bypass via sanitizePath Path-Parameter Dot-Segments

desc: Traefik before 2.11.62, 3.x before 3.7.18, and 3.8.0-rc.1 before 3.8.0-rc.2 contain a denial of service vulnerability in the BasicAuth middleware, which does not limit password length before MD5-crypt ($apr1$, $1$) hashing. Unauthenticated attackers can send passwords up to the entry point maxHeaderBytes limit (1 MiB by default), consuming excessive CPU per request and degrading availability.
title: Traefik before 2.11.62 Denial of Service via BasicAuth Password Length

desc: Traefik 3.1.0 before 3.7.18 and 3.8.0-rc.1 contain a memory exhaustion vulnerability in the Compress middleware, which creates zstd encoders with library default options that retain about 18 MiB of state per response until it is fully written. Unauthenticated remote attackers can open many concurrent requests and read responses slowly to exhaust memory and crash Traefik.
title: Traefik from 3.1.0 before 3.7.18 Memory Exhaustion DoS via Compress Middleware

desc: SiYuan from 3.6.2 before 3.8.10 contains a path traversal vulnerability that allows admin token holders to read files outside the workspace because the globalCopyFiles and workspaceCopyFiles denylist omits /home, /mnt, /media, and /snap. Attackers can copy other users' SSH authorized_keys, Docker and AWS configs, or mounted files into the workspace and retrieve them via the getFile API.
title: SiYuan 3.6.2 before 3.8.10 Path Traversal via globalCopyFiles Denylist Gaps

desc: SiYuan from 3.8.6-beta.1 before 3.8.10 contains a missing authorization vulnerability that allows read-only publish users (RoleReader) to modify persistent workspace configuration via /api/system/getChangelog. Attackers can send POST requests through the publish service proxy, even anonymously when basic authentication is disabled, to persist ShowChangelog = false to conf.json.
title: SiYuan 3.8.6-beta.1 before 3.8.10 Missing Authorization via /api/system/getChangelog

desc: SiYuan 3.8.8 before 3.8.10 contains an incorrect permission assignment vulnerability that creates workspace directories with mode 0755 and conf.json with mode 0644, exposing the cleartext AccessAuthCode administrator credential. Local users able to traverse the SiYuan user's home path can read it and authenticate as administrator via Basic authentication, for example calling /api/system/setAPIToken to change the API token.
title: SiYuan 3.8.8 before 3.8.10 World-Readable conf.json Exposes Administrator AccessAuthCode

desc: vLLM 0.3.0 before 0.30.0 contains a response amplification vulnerability in the OpenAI-compatible API server's shared RequestValidationError handler, which renders every Pydantic validation error, each of which can include the full offending input, in its HTTP 400 response. Unauthenticated attackers can send a malformed request to endpoints such as POST /v1/responses to trigger a disproportionately large error response that consumes server CPU and memory and can disrupt downstream clients and proxies.
title: vLLM 0.3.0 before 0.30.0 Response Amplification via OpenAI Validation Error Handler

desc: vLLM 0.16.0 before 0.21.0 leaks token data between users when the V1 model runner uses async scheduling with pipeline parallelism, because non-last pipeline ranks never write generated tokens to token_ids_cpu and reset num_tokens_no_spec each step. When the fallback path is triggered, such as by mixed prefill/decode batches, stale tokens from a prior request in the same batch slot become model input and are written to the KV cache, exposing fragments of one user's context in another user's response.
title: vLLM 0.16.0 before 0.21.0 Cross-User Data Leak via Async Scheduling

desc: vLLM 0.21.0 before 0.28.0, when using the V1 model runner, contains a state aliasing flaw in ThinkingBudgetStateHolder.sync_batch(), whose SWAP branch copies thinking-budget state to the destination batch row without removing the source entry. Attackers submitting requests with thinking_token_budget can force the reasoning-end token sequence into a concurrent co-batched request's output during a mixed batch reorder.
title: vLLM 0.21.0 before 0.28.0 Cross-Request State Aliasing via thinking_token_budget

desc: SiYuan before 3.8.11 uses DejaVu sync code that accepts a non-hexadecimal 40-byte remote index ID from WebDAV responses and joins it into the repository indexes path unchecked, allowing path traversal. An on-path attacker altering plaintext HTTP WebDAV sync responses can overwrite a workspace data file, such as a .sy note, with compressed index data.
title: SiYuan before 3.8.11 Path Traversal via WebDAV Sync Index ID

desc: SiYuan from 3.8.0 before 3.8.11 contains a lockout bypass vulnerability that allows remote attackers to brute-force publish passwords by forging client-computable publish-auth-<ID> cookies. Attackers can compute SHA-256(ID + candidate) locally and send it on content requests like /api/filetree/getDoc to guess passwords without throttling and read protected documents.
title: SiYuan from 3.8.0 before 3.8.11 Publish Password Lockout Bypass via Cookie

desc: SiYuan 3.7.0 before 3.8.11 contains a DOM-based cross-site scripting vulnerability in the AI agent chat panel, which renders final and saved assistant replies into innerHTML without HTML sanitisation. Attackers influencing model replies via indirect prompt injection or a configured model endpoint can inject event-handler markup, executing OS commands through Node.js integration in desktop local-kernel mode.
title: SiYuan 3.7.0 before 3.8.11 DOM XSS via AI Agent Chat Panel

desc: SiYuan before 3.8.10 contains a cross-site scripting vulnerability where WebDAV sync error formatting skips HTML escaping for certain malformed-response errors, passing raw markup to the Electron notification renderer. A network attacker who alters a cleartext HTTP WebDAV response can inject event-handler markup that, when the victim manually starts sync, executes JavaScript with Node integration as the logged-in user.
title: SiYuan before 3.8.10 XSS via WebDAV Sync Error Notification

desc: Parse Server before 9.12.0-alpha.2 matches $in, $nin, $all and $containedBy constraints in LiveQuery with a cost proportional to the product of the constraint list size and the saved array size. A client that can subscribe to a class and save objects in it can use large lists and arrays to block the event loop for seconds or longer, stalling LiveQuery and, when it runs in the same process, Parse Server.
title: Parse Server before 9.12.0-alpha.2 LiveQuery Denial of Service via List Constraints

desc: SiYuan before 3.8.11 contains a stored cross-site scripting vulnerability that allows attackers to inject DOM event handlers by storing handler-named block attributes such as onmouseover. Attackers can share crafted .sy.zip packages or Markdown files whose attributes reach renderCustom or the unsanitised preview pane, executing OS commands via Node integration in the desktop app.
title: SiYuan before 3.8.11 Stored XSS to RCE via Block Attribute Names

desc: FreeRDP from 3.10.0 before 3.33.0 contains an invalid free vulnerability in rdg.c because the websocket context pointer shares a union with chunked transfer-encoding decoder state. A malicious RD Gateway answering the data channel with chunked encoding can control the overwritten pointer via chunk sizes, causing rdg_free to free an attacker-influenced value and crash the client.
title: FreeRDP 3.10.0 before 3.33.0 Invalid Free via RD Gateway Chunked Encoding

desc: FreeRDP before 3.33.0 contains a heap out-of-bounds read in WinPR's save_png_to_buffer(), which selects an RGB PNG color type for 9–16 bpp images but fills only 2 bytes per pixel per row. A malicious RDP server can send 9–16 bpp CF_DIB clipboard data that, when a local application requests image/png, yields a PNG containing adjacent client heap memory.
title: FreeRDP before 3.33.0 Heap Out-of-Bounds Read via WinPR PNG Writer

desc: HKUDS nanobot from 0.1.4 before 0.4.1 contains an improper certificate validation vulnerability in the OpenAI Codex provider that retries authenticated requests without TLS certificate or hostname verification. Attackers able to intercept the connection can trigger a certificate failure and impersonate the endpoint to steal bearer tokens, read request contents, or alter responses.
title: HKUDS nanobot 0.1.4 before 0.4.1 TLS Verification Bypass in OpenAI Codex Provider

desc: ImageMagick 7.0.0 before 7.1.2-35 and before 6.9.13-60 contains an information disclosure vulnerability in the distributed pixel cache server, which transmits pixel and metadata content in cleartext. Attackers who can observe traffic between a DPC client and server can read transmitted image data.
title: ImageMagick 7.0.0 before 7.1.2-35 and before 6.9.13-60 Information Disclosure via Distributed Pixel Cache

desc: Parse Server 3.10.0 before 8.6.123 and 9.0.0 before 9.11.1-alpha.4 contains an authentication bypass in the Google Play Games authentication adapter, which does not verify that the supplied player ID belongs to the presented access token. Attackers can sign in with their own Google Play Games credential while claiming another user's player ID to take over that account or link that player ID to their own account.
title: Parse Server 9.0.0 before 9.11.1-alpha.4 Account Takeover via Google Play Games Adapter

desc: FreeRDP from 3.0.0 before 3.33.0 contains a use-after-free vulnerability in cert_write_server_certificate_v1() that computes the proprietary certificate signature over a freed stream buffer after reallocation. Clients negotiating Standard RDP Security with many static channels against servers using 3072- or 4096-bit keys trigger freed heap reads, producing invalid certificate signatures.
title: FreeRDP 3.0.0 before 3.33.0 Use-After-Free in Server Certificate Signing

desc: FreeRDP before 3.33.0 contains an out-of-bounds read in the client smartcard channel because SCARD_IOCTL_LISTREADERSW decoding accepts an odd cBytes value, leaving the mszGroups wide-string buffer without an aligned NUL terminator. A malicious RDP server can send a crafted IRP_MJ_DEVICE_CONTROL request causing the client to read beyond a heap allocation, potentially crashing it.
title: FreeRDP before 3.33.0 Out-of-Bounds Read via SCARD_IOCTL_LISTREADERSW

desc: The FreeRDP proxy in FreeRDP before 3.33.0 dereferences a NULL backend client context in pf_server_refresh_rect and pf_server_suppress_output, which are guarded only by a debug-only WINPR_ASSERT, when a REFRESH_RECT or SUPPRESS_OUTPUT data PDU arrives before connection activation. An unauthenticated remote client that completes licensing without sending Confirm Active can crash the proxy process, terminating all hosted sessions.
title: FreeRDP before 3.33.0 Proxy NULL Pointer Dereference via Early REFRESH_RECT PDU

desc: FreeRDP before 3.33.0 contains an integer overflow in the client GDI handling of accumulated drawing-order bounds: wrapped INT32 coordinates yield a zero-width clip region that causes clipping to be skipped in gdi_FillRect. A malicious RDP server can send many ORDER_BOUNDS orders followed by an OPAQUE_RECT order to trigger a heap out-of-bounds write past the client's drawing bitmap, potentially leading to code execution.
title: FreeRDP before 3.33.0 Heap Out-of-Bounds Write via ORDER_BOUNDS Integer Overflow

desc: FreeRDP from 3.0.0 before 3.33.0 contains a reachable assertion in remdesk_server_thread that allows authenticated clients to abort freerdp-shadow-cli by sending oversized remdesk messages. Attackers can send one message longer than 4096 bytes with a shorter declared PDU length, forcing Stream_Seek past capacity and terminating every served session.
title: FreeRDP 3.0.0 before 3.33.0 Reachable Assertion DoS via remdesk Server Channel

desc: FreeRDP 2.11.2 before 3.33.0 contains unbounded resource consumption in the Progressive codec because progressive_decompress() resets the tile update batch only when frameId changes. A malicious RDP server can repeat RDPGFX_CAPROGRESSIVE WireToSurface2 commands with a constant frameId to cause unbounded memory growth, quadratic CPU cost, a heap out-of-bounds write on tile-cache allocation failure, and client crashes.
title: FreeRDP 2.11.2 before 3.33.0 Heap Corruption via Progressive Codec Stale frameId

desc: FreeRDP from 3.0.0 before 3.33.0 contains a missing authentication vulnerability in the shadow server's fast-path input handlers in fastpath.c that allows unauthenticated attackers to inject input before activation. Attackers can negotiate TLS-only RDP, skip Confirm Active, and send Fast-Path Input Event PDUs to inject keystrokes and mouse movement into the host X11 session via XTEST.
title: FreeRDP 3.0.0 before 3.33.0 Missing Authentication via Fast-Path Input PDUs

desc: A weakness has been identified in SourceCodester Syllabus-Aligned Learning Management & Examination System 1.0. Affected by this vulnerability is an unknown functionality of the file approve_enrollment.php. This manipulation causes open redirect. Remote exploitation of the attack is possible. The exploit has been made available to the public and could be used for attacks.
title: SourceCodester Syllabus-Aligned Learning Management & Examination System approve_enrollment.php redirect

desc: FreeRDP before 3.33.0 contains a credential disclosure vulnerability that allows malicious RDP servers to obtain client passwords because rdp_write_info_packet() omits a Remote Credential Guard check. When a victim connects using /remoteGuard with a configured /p password, the client sends the password in the Client Info packet after CredSSP, exposing reusable credentials to the destination.
title: FreeRDP before 3.33.0 Credential Disclosure via Remote Credential Guard Client Info

desc: A security flaw has been discovered in SourceCodester Online Food Ordering System 1.0. Affected is the function move_uploaded_file of the file /admin/add_food.php of the component File Upload Handler. The manipulation of the argument image/new_image/update_image results in unrestricted upload. The attack may be launched remotely. The exploit has been released to the public and may be used for attacks.
title: SourceCodester Online Food Ordering System File Upload add_food.php move_uploaded_file unrestricted upload

desc: FreeRDP before 3.33.0 contains a race condition in asynchronous RDPDR IRP processing that allows malicious RDP servers to leak client memory through non-atomic wStream reference count updates. Attackers can send repeated IRPs, such as smartcard redirection requests, so concurrent Stream_Release() calls lose decrements and accumulate unreleased streams, exhausting memory and causing denial of service.
title: FreeRDP before 3.33.0 Memory Leak via Non-Atomic RDPDR IRP Stream Refcount

desc: The Optimole – Optimize Images | Convert WebP & AVIF | CDN & Lazy Load | Image Optimization plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via the 'author' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 4.2.20 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page. This vulnerability is only reachable when the plugin's 'Enable generic placeholder color' option is disabled, as only that configuration invokes the build_url() code path that constructs $low_url from attacker-controlled input.
products: optimole:optimole – optimize images | convert webp & avif | cdn & lazy load | image optimization
title: Optimole <= 4.2.20 - Unauthenticated Stored Cross-Site Scripting via Comment Author Name

desc: The WPC Admin Columns plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via the 'form_data (attacker-controlled array keys under wpcac_columns[...])' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 2.3.8 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. This makes it possible for authenticated attackers, with subscriber-level access and above, to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page. Successful exploitation beyond self-XSS requires an administrator to have set the 'Personalized' setting to 'No', which causes column configurations to be stored in a shared option accessible to all users rather than a per-user option.
title: WPC Admin Columns <= 2.3.8 - Authenticated (Subscriber+) Stored Cross-Site Scripting via 'wpcac_save_columns' AJAX Action

desc: The WP Go Maps – Google Map, OpenStreetMap, Leaflet & Store Locator plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to generic SQL Injection via the 'query' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 10.2.05 due to insufficient escaping on the user supplied parameter and lack of sufficient preparation on the existing SQL query. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to append additional SQL queries into already existing queries that can be used to extract sensitive information from the database. Exploitation requires that the site administrator has enabled the plugin's 'Enable Dynamic SQL Refactors' setting and that the database server is running with a sql_mode containing NO_BACKSLASH_ESCAPES; neither condition is enabled by default.
products: wpgmaps:wp go maps – google map, openstreetmap, leaflet & store locator
title: WP Go Maps <= 10.2.05 - Unauthenticated SQL Injection via 'query' Parameter

desc: The User Frontend – Membership, User Registration, User Profile, User Directory & Content Restriction with Frontend Post Submission plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via the 'post_title' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 4.3.14 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page. Exploitation requires that an administrator has configured a wpuf Post Form with guest post submission enabled and placed its shortcode on a public page, from which an unauthenticated attacker can scrape the required nonce before submitting the malicious payload.
products: wedevs:user frontend – membership, user registration, user profile, user directory & content restriction with frontend post submission
title: User Frontend <= 4.3.14 - Unauthenticated Stored Cross-Site Scripting via 'post_title' Parameter via Guest Post Submission

desc: The WPForms (Contact Form by WPForms / wpforms-lite) plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via the Multiple Choice field's 'Other' option value on payment forms in all versions up to, and including, 2.0.4 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a privileged user such as an administrator accesses the injected payment entry on the WPForms > Payments details page. desc: A **server-side request forgery** flaw has been found in the get_remote_artifact_url() function in pulp_python/app/models.py of the pull-through caching feature in the **pulp_python** package. The function uses the redirect query parameter from the client request as the URL to download. A network attacker or user who can reach the content app of a Python distribution that has a remote can choose that URL. The content app downloads it and returns the response. When the remote has a username and password, the download sends those credentials to the host in the URL. When the remote policy is immediate, the default, or on_demand, the file is saved into the distribution's repository and later clients are served that file. The project name and version come from the file, and the filename comes from the request path. A filename the repository already stores is served from the stored file.
title: Pulp_python: pulp_python: pull-through caching fetches a client-supplied url with the remote's credentials

desc: The App Builder – Create Native Android & iOS Apps On The Flight plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Authentication Bypass via Google ID Token Audience Validation Bypass in all versions up to, and including, 5.7.1. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to authenticate as any existing WordPress user — including Administrators — whose email address is known, by supplying a Google-signed ID token obtained from an entirely unrelated OAuth client containing the target user's email claim, which causes the plugin to issue a signed App Builder JWT granting that user's full privileges. Exploitation requires the attacker to obtain a valid Google-signed ID token carrying the target user's email address, which can be achieved by operating a separate Google OAuth client and inducing the target user to authenticate through it.

desc: The WP STAGING – Backups & Restore, Migration & Clone Plugin – Cloud Backups, Scheduled Backups plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Authorization Bypass in all versions up to, and including, 4.17.0 via the `REQUEST_URI` query parameter. This is due to a parser-differential flaw in `showLoginForm()`: the plugin's `isRestUrl()` function performs an unanchored `strpos()` prefix match against the full `REQUEST_URI` — including the query string — and short-circuits all authorization checks (including `isStagingSite()` and `current_user_can('manage_options')`) whenever it detects a REST-like URL, while WordPress core only treats a request as a REST API call when the `rest_route` query variable is non-empty. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to bypass the staging-site login gate entirely by appending an empty `rest_route` parameter (e.g. `/wp-json/?rest_route=`), causing the plugin to skip its gate while core proceeds to render the ordinary theme front end, exposing the full theme-rendered contents of the staging site — including private post content, page-builder output, WooCommerce pages, and site search results over the staging database. This bypass only affects staging sites where the login gate is active, which is the default state for any site cloned by the plugin when the `wpstg_is_staging_site` option is set to `true` or the `.wp-staging` marker file is present in `ABSPATH`.
products: renehermi:wp staging – backups & restore, migration & clone plugin – cloud backups, scheduled backups
title: WP STAGING <= 4.17.0 - Unauthenticated Authorization Bypass via 'rest_route' Query Parameter

desc: The WP Job Portal – AI-Powered Recruitment System for Company or Job Board website plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Authentication Bypass leading to Account Takeover in all versions up to, and including, 2.7.2 This is due to a flaw in `WPJOBPORTALuser::__construct()` where the non-empty guard on the `wpjobportal-socialid` cookie is evaluated against the raw cookie value before `sanitize_key()` is applied — allowing a value composed entirely of characters outside `[a-z0-9_-]` to pass the guard, be reduced to an empty string by `sanitize_key()`, and be used as the literal value in a `WHERE socialid = ''` database query that matches the first portal account whose `socialid` column is empty. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to be bound to an existing WP Job Portal Employer or Jobseeker account, gaining the ability to create, edit, and delete the victim's companies, job listings, resumes, and applications, as well as overwrite the linked WordPress user's first name, last name, and display name via the `saveuser`→`syncWPUserName()` path. Exploitation is viable on virtually all installations because every portal account not registered through the social-login flow retains the default empty `socialid` value; nonce checks on downstream actions such as `savecompany` and `saveuser` do not mitigate this issue because those nonces are minted within the already-hijacked session and validate against the attacker's own subsequent requests. Successful exploitation gives the attacker control of a distinct, already-privileged WP Job Portal Employer / Jobseeker (bound to a specific WordPress user) account; it does not promote the attacker's original account.
products: wpjobportal:wp job portal – ai-powered recruitment system for company or job board website
title: WP Job Portal <= 2.7.2 - Unauthenticated Privilege Escalation via Account Takeover to 'wpjobportal-socialid' Cookie

desc: The Simple Membership plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Privilege Escalation in versions up to, and including, 4.8.9 This is due to the site-wide signing secret `swpm_private_key_one` being generated at install time with PHP's non-cryptographic `uniqid('', true)` function in `SwpmInstallation::installer()`, whose timestamp-derived keyspace (~10^15 candidates / ~50 bits) can be constrained via the public WordPress REST API date of the plugin's auto-created registration page, combined with a single-MD5 oracle (`md5(key|level)`) that the public registration form prints as `swpm_level_hash` and a non-constant-time `!=` comparison in `SwpmFrontRegistration::register_front_end()` as the sole authorization gate on which membership level a visitor may register into; `SwpmUtils::get_free_level()` then honors an attacker-posted `level_identifier=md5(level)` regardless of the configured free-membership setting, and `prepare_and_create_wp_user_front_end()` creates the WordPress account with whatever role the level is configured to grant (only the `administrator` role is refused). This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers, after an offline brute-force recovery of the install-time secret against the public MD5 oracle, to forge a valid `swpm_level_hash` for any configured membership level and self-register into that level, elevating their newly created WordPress account to the level's assigned role — e. Successful exploitation causes the attacker's own account to receive the complete editor role.
title: Simple Membership <= 4.8.9 - Unauthenticated Privilege Escalation to Editor via Forged 'swpm_level_hash'

desc: The WordPress File Upload plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Arbitrary File Deletion in versions up to, and including, 5.3.1 via the 'wfu_ajax_action_handshake' and 'wfu_ajax_action_send_email_notification' AJAX Actions. This is due to the unauthenticated handshake accepting a 'sid' parameter sanitized only with sanitize_text_field(), which does not strip '[', ']', '{', or '}', allowing the sid to be crafted as an item name containing embedded delimiter pairs that plant forged records for arbitrary other item names — including the per-session file path list and the consent flag — in the plugin's shared concatenated user-state option store, combined with the notification handler being gated only by a nonce freely minted by the same nopriv handshake. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to delete arbitrary files on the affected site's server which may make remote code execution possible.
title: Iptanus File Upload <= 5.3.1 - Unauthenticated Arbitrary File Deletion via 'wfu_ajax_action_handshake' and 'wfu_ajax_action_send_email_notification' AJAX Actions

desc: The WP Review Slider plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Arbitrary File Read in versions up to, and including, 15.5 via the wprp_twitter_savetweet and wpfb_avatar_tolocal AJAX actions. This is due to the handlers only verifying a WordPress nonce without any current_user_can() capability check and accepting an attacker-supplied local filesystem path in the 'tw_img' parameter, which is later passed directly to PHP's copy() to write byte-identical data into a publicly accessible uploads directory under an attacker-chosen name. The nonce action 'randomnoncestring' is shared with the same vendor's companion plugin (WP Google Review Slider), which emits it to every visitor of every front-end page, making it obtainable by any logged-in user including Subscribers whenever that companion plugin is active. This makes it possible for authenticated attackers, with subscriber-level access and above, to read arbitrary files on the affected site's server, including sensitive files such as wp-config.
title: WP Review Slider <= 15.5 - Missing Authorization to Authenticated (Subscriber+) Arbitrary File Read via 'wprp_twitter_savetweet' and 'wpfb_avatar_tolocal' AJAX Actions

desc: The NextMove Lite – Thank You Page for WooCommerce plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via the 'billing_address.email' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 2.24.0 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page. The injected script fires without any victim interaction because the builder page's JavaScript calls $(".preview_order_id").trigger("change") on page load, immediately executing any attribute-injected event handler.

title: NextMove Lite <= 2.24.0 - Unauthenticated Stored Cross-Site Scripting via Billing Email

desc: The Drag and Drop Multiple File Upload (Pro) - WooCommerce plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to generic SQL Injection via the 'wc-upload-file (array key)' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 1.7.2 due to insufficient escaping on the user supplied parameter and lack of sufficient preparation on the existing SQL query. Exploitation requires that the site administrator has enabled the 'Count no. of pages?' option (drag_n_drop_count_pdf set to 'yes') and that the uploaded filename stored in the cart resolves to a file with a .pdf extension.
products: codedropz:drag and drop multiple file upload (pro) - woocommerce
title: Drag and Drop Multiple File Upload (Pro) - WooCommerce <= 1.7.2 - Unauthenticated SQL Injection via 'wc-upload-file' Parameter Array Key

desc: The PDF Invoices & Packing Slips for WooCommerce plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via the 'billing_address.first_name / company / address_1 / address_2 / city' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 6.0.0 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping.
