products: wpovernight:pdf invoices & packing slips for woocommerce
title: PDF Invoices & Packing Slips for WooCommerce <= 6.0.0 - Unauthenticated Stored Cross-Site Scripting via Billing Fields

desc: The WP Statistics – Simple, privacy-friendly Google Analytics alternative plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Local File Inclusion in all versions up to, and including, 14.16.19 via the 'tab' parameter parameter. This makes it possible for authenticated attackers, with subscriber-level access and above, to include and execute arbitrary .php files on the server, allowing the execution of any PHP code in those files. This can be used to bypass access controls, obtain sensitive data, or achieve code execution in cases where .php file types can be uploaded and included. The exploitability of this vulnerability depends on the Minimum Role to View Statistics setting; when set to a low-privilege role such as Subscriber (read capability), unauthenticated-equivalent access is effectively granted to any registered user, while the default Administrator setting limits exposure to higher-privileged accounts.
products: veronalabs:wp statistics – simple, privacy-friendly google analytics alternative
title: WP Statistics <= 14.16.19 - Authenticated (Subscriber+) Local File Inclusion via 'tab' Parameter

desc: The Easy Social Share Buttons for WordPress plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via the 'position' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 11.6.1 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page. The payload is stored via the unauthenticated wp_ajax_nopriv_ ESSB stat log AJAX action, which performs no nonce or capability check, and executes when the attacker-controlled position value is rendered verbatim into a double-quoted HTML data-* attribute where the unescaped quote allows attribute breakout.
products: appscreo:easy social share buttons for wordpress
title: Easy Social Share Buttons for WordPress <= 11.6.1 - Unauthenticated Stored Cross-Site Scripting via 'service' and 'position' Parameters

desc: The LiteSpeed Cache plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via the 'comment' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 7.9.3 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page. Exploitation requires CDN Mapping to be enabled with at least one Original URLs entry containing a '*' wildcard character, a non-default configuration; the attacker's comment must also be approved, which is satisfied immediately when moderation is disabled or automatically after one prior approved comment from the same name and email address.
title: LiteSpeed Cache <= 7.9.3 - Unauthenticated Stored Cross-Site Scripting via Comment Content via CDN URL Rewriter

desc: The Fluent Forms – Customizable Contact Forms, Survey, Quiz, & Conversational Form Builder plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Account Pre-Hijacking via Unverified Identifier in all versions up to, and including, 6.2.15. The vulnerability exists because the `PaymentHandler::maybeAssignTransactions()` function, registered on the `user_register` hook at priority 99, resolves the lookup email solely from the newly created user record via the `user_email` parameter with no prior verification that the registrant actually controls that address, then bulk-updates all guest transactions and submissions in `wp_fluentform_transactions` and `wp_fluentform_submissions` whose `payer_email` matches and whose `user_id` is NULL to assign ownership to the attacker's new account. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to pre-hijack a victim's prior guest payment history — reading their payment receipts and cancelling their active subscriptions via the `[fluentform_payments]` shortcode and the `wp_ajax_fluentform_user_payment_endpoints` `cancel_transaction` route — by simply registering an account under the victim's email address before the legitimate owner does. Exploitation requires that the WordPress site has open user registration enabled and that the targeted victim previously submitted at least one payment as a guest under their email address.
products: wpmanageninja:fluent forms – customizable contact forms, survey, quiz, & conversational form builder
title: Fluent Forms <= 6.2.15 - Unauthenticated Account Pre-Hijacking via Unverified Identifier via 'payer_email' / 'user_register' Hook Reassignment

desc: The SlimStat Analytics plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via the 'filter_array' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 6.1.1 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. title: SlimStat Analytics <= 6.1.1 - Authenticated (Subscriber+) Stored Cross-Site Scripting via 'filter_array' Parameter

desc: The VK Blocks plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via the 'comment' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 1.130.0 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. desc: The Postie plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via the 'email HTML body' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 1.9.91 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. desc: The SlimStat Analytics – Real-Time Stats, Heatmaps & Ecommerce plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via the 'HTTP_USER_AGENT' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 6.1.2 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. desc: The LA-Studio Element Kit for Elementor plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Sensitive Information Exposure in all versions up to, and including, 1.6.3 via the 'actions[*][data][autocomplete][query][fields] (and [get_titles][query][fields])' parameter. The elementor_ajax nonce used as the sole access control is available to any logged-in user via the globally exposed elementorCommonConfig JavaScript object, making both AJAX actions trivially reachable at Subscriber privilege level.

desc: The Product Input Fields for WooCommerce plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Arbitrary File Upload in all versions up to, and including, 2.1.0 via the process_file_input_field function. This is due to missing file type validation in the process_file_input_field function, which accepts the client-supplied multipart Content-Type header as the sole type gate and writes the uploaded file to the unprotected pif_temp directory using the verbatim client-supplied filename. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to upload files that may be executable, which makes remote code execution possible. Exploitation requires that an administrator has configured at least one product with a File-type Product Input Field with the "Show thumbnail" option enabled, which is a standard use of the feature; additionally, the pif_temp/ upload directory is created without .htaccess or index.php restrictions, leaving written files directly web-accessible and executable on default Apache/mod_php configurations.

desc:
GNU screen is vulnerable to a global buffer overflow in the SendCmdMessage() function within attacher.c. Due to the use of an unchecked sprintf() call when appending the STY environment variable to the global SocketPath buffer. The vulnerability occurs when GNU screen is executed in an environment where the HOME and STY environment variables contain attacker-controlled values that are sufficiently long. Successful exploitation may result in an application crash or potentially arbitrary code execution.


This issue was fixed in version 5.0.2.
title: Global Buffer Overflow in GNU screen

desc:
GNU Screen is vulnerable to a Use-After-Free in the utf8_handle_comb() function in encoding.c. Due to improper error handling during memory allocation failure, the global combchars pointer is freed but not reset to NULL. When a subsequent combining Unicode character arrives at the terminal, the function dereferences the freed pointer. An attacker who controls terminal content sent to the screen session, such as via a rogue SSH server or crafted escape sequences, can exploit this vulnerability to perform heap grooming and achieve arbitrary code execution.



This issue was fixed in version 5.0.2.
title: Use-After-Free in GNU Screen

desc:
GNU Screen is vulnerable to a Time-of-Check/Time-of-Use (TOCTOU) race condition in the hardcopy file handler. Due to checking write permissions using the real user ID and subsequently opening the file using the effective user ID, a local unprivileged attacker can atomically replace the target path with a symbolic link pointing to an arbitrary system file. Successfully exploiting this race condition allows the attacker to write to arbitrary files with root privileges, leading to local privilege escalation



This issue was fixed in version 5.0.2.
title: Time-of-check Time-of-use (TOCTOU) Race Condition leading to privilege escalation in GNU screen

desc: Bazarr 1.4.4 before 1.6.1-beta.29 on Windows contains an unauthenticated path traversal vulnerability in the catch_all() handler in bazarr/app/ui.py. Attackers can append percent-encoded '..' segments after the 'workbox-' prefix to read files like config.yaml containing stored API keys and credentials.
title: Bazarr 1.4.4 before 1.6.1-beta.29 Path Traversal via PWA Workbox Route

desc: LibreChat 0.7.3 before 0.8.9 contains an improper input type validation vulnerability in the requireLdapAuth middleware of the /api/auth/login route that allows unauthenticated attackers to crash the server. title: LibreChat 0.7.3 before 0.8.9 Denial of Service via LDAP Login Password

desc: LIVE555 Streaming Media before 2026.08.25 contains a heap out-of-bounds read vulnerability in parseVorbisOrTheoraConfigStr() that trusts attacker-supplied 16-bit header length fields. A malicious RTSP server or crafted SDP Vorbis or Theora configuration can crash clients or leak heap memory through proxied SDP configurations.
title: LIVE555 before 2026.08.25 Heap Out-of-Bounds Read via parseVorbisOrTheoraConfigStr()

desc:
MISP contains an authorization flaw in the SharingGroup model's checkIfAuthorisedExtend method. The method grants sync users (those with the perm_sync role) an exemption from the extend flag requirement when modifying sharing group membership. However, this exemption was applied unconditionally to all sharing groups, including those created locally on the instance (local = 1). The intended behavior, consistent with the sync push path, is that the exemption should only apply to sharing groups received through sync from another instance (local = 0).

As a result, an authenticated sync user whose organization was a plain member (extend flag = 0) of a locally-created sharing group could add or remove organizations and servers from that group via the quick-edit actions or the edit form. This bypassed the extend-flag authorization that is required for non-owner members to modify a sharing group's membership.

Preconditions: the attacker must possess an authenticated account with the sync role (perm_sync) and the sharing group permission (perm_sharing_group), and must be a member of the target locally-created sharing group without the extend flag set. The attacker does not need to be the group owner or a site administrator.

Security impact: an unauthorized modification of sharing group membership can alter which organizations and servers are permitted to exchange threat intelligence data through that group. An attacker could add their own organization to gain access to shared indicators, or remove other organizations to disrupt their data exchange. The scope of impact is limited to the integrity of the sharing group membership configuration and does not directly expose or corrupt stored threat intelligence data.
title: MISP: Sync user authorization bypass allows modification of locally-created sharing group membership

desc: Twenty through 2.63.0 in multi-workspace mode contains an authentication bypass vulnerability that allows unauthenticated attackers to obtain pending invitation tokens by registering an invitee's email via the signUp GraphQL mutation. Attackers can submit the leaked personalInviteToken to signUpInWorkspace to join the workspace with the invitation's role, including Admin, and obtain a verified email.
title: Twenty through 2.63.0 Invitation Takeover via Unauthenticated signUp Mutation

desc: Iceburg CRM through 5.0.0 contains an uncontrolled resource consumption vulnerability that allows authenticated users to exhaust disk space by uploading files to the POST /data/import route. Attackers without import permission can repeatedly upload input_file payloads that are stored in storage/app/temp and parsed before permission checks, never deleted, causing denial of service.
title: Iceburg CRM through 5.0.0 Storage Exhaustion via /data/import Endpoint

desc: Iceburg CRM through 5.0.0 contains an authorization bypass vulnerability that allows authenticated low-privileged users to modify any user record by supplying arbitrary record_id values to POST /data/save. Attackers can submit a save request for the ice_users module with the administrator's record_id to change their password or email and take over the account.
title: Iceburg CRM through 5.0.0 Authorization Bypass Through User-Controlled Key via /data/save

desc: FacturaONE para WooCommerce con VeriFactu before 5.61 contains an authenticated SQL injection vulnerability that allows Contributor-level users to inject SQL through the fone_client_id user meta value. Attackers can store a payload in their own profile via FONE_update_tarifa_user(), which FONE_product_ids_ocultos_para_usuario() concatenates unquoted, enabling time-based blind extraction of password hashes.
title: FacturaONE para WooCommerce con VeriFactu before 5.61 SQL Injection via fone_client_id

desc: Juspay Hyperswitch 1.8.0 before 1.129.0 uses a hardcoded default webhook secret that allows unauthenticated attackers to forge Stripe webhooks when no merchant webhook secret is configured. title: Juspay Hyperswitch 1.8.0 before 1.129.0 Hardcoded Webhook Secret Allows Forged Stripe Webhooks

desc: Listmonk 4.1.0 through 7.0.0-beta.2 contains an authorization bypass vulnerability in CSV subscriber import that allows list-scoped users to overwrite subscribers outside their permitted lists. Attackers holding subscribers:import and list:manage on one list can import CSV rows with victims' emails and overwrite enabled to modify names, attributes, and list memberships.
title: listmonk 4.1.0 through 7.0.0-beta.2 Incorrect Authorization via CSV Subscriber Import

desc: Golift xtractr before 0.4.1 contains a path traversal vulnerability that allows attackers to write files outside the extraction root because a strings.HasPrefix output directory check lacks separator awareness. Attackers can supply ZIP, TAR, 7z, RAR, or other archives with entries like ../<outputdir>_evil/file to create or overwrite files in sibling directories.
title: xtractr before 0.4.1 Path Traversal via Output Prefix Check

desc: Open Policy Agent before 1.20.0 contains an insecure temporary file vulnerability that allows local users to overwrite files by abusing the fixed OCI store path used when persistence_directory is unset. Attackers can pre-create the opa/oci temp directory with index.json or oci-layout symlinks so OPA overwrites the target files with OCI JSON using its privileges.
title: Open Policy Agent before 1.20.0 Symlink File Overwrite via Predictable OCI Store Path

desc: Iceburg CRM through 5.0.0 contains a missing authorization vulnerability that allows any authenticated user to modify workflows by calling the workflow save and delete endpoints. Attackers can send an empty workflow array to /data/workflow/save or call DELETE /data/workflow/{id} to wipe or rewrite the module conversion workflow.
title: Iceburg CRM through 5.0.0 Missing Authorization via Workflow Save and Delete Endpoints

desc: KodeRover Zadig before 5.1.0 contains a missing authorization vulnerability in aslan environment kube.go handlers that allows authenticated users to query Kubernetes clusters of other projects. Attackers can supply arbitrary clusterID and namespace values to /api/aslan/environment/kube/ routes to enumerate namespaces, nodes, deployments, workloads, canary mappings, and resource names.
title: KodeRover Zadig before 5.1.0 Missing Authorization in Aslan Kubernetes Resource Handlers

desc: Iceburg CRM through 5.0.0 contains a missing authorization vulnerability in the related_fields and related_field_name routes in routes/data.php that lets authenticated users read restricted module data. Attackers can enumerate field_id values to query related module tables without Permission::checkPermission checks, reading id and name pairs such as user names from ice_users.
title: Iceburg CRM through 5.0.0 Missing Authorization in Related-Field Lookup Endpoints

desc: Iceburg CRM through 5.0.0 contains an information disclosure vulnerability that allows unauthenticated attackers to view server configuration through public/v.php calling phpinfo(). Attackers can request v.php directly, bypassing Laravel routing, to obtain PHP version, extensions, INI settings, DOCUMENT_ROOT, and environment variables.
title: Iceburg CRM through 5.0.0 Information Disclosure via public/v.php phpinfo()

desc:
When authenticating through the Web HMI or Desktop HMI with POSIX LDAP, an attacker can bypass some of Panorama Suite's injection protections. The attacker must know the username and password of a valid account in the LDAP directory. An authenticated attacker may then gain access to areas or business roles they are not authorized to use, or obtain unauthorized permissions in Panorama. Installations that do not use POSIX LDAP authentication are not affected. LDAP Active Directory authentication is not affected.



Affected versions:

  *  Panorama Suite 2020
  *  Panorama Suite 2022-SP1
  *  Panorama Suite 2023
  *  Panorama Suite 2025
  *  Panorama Suite 2025 Updated Dec. 25 (before update PS-2510-02-1317)




Remediation: For Panorama Suite 2025 Updated Dec. 25, install update PS-2510-02-1317 or later. For the other affected versions, upgrade to Panorama Suite 2025 Updated Dec. 25 and install update PS-2510-02-1317 or later.



Please refer to security bulletin BS-040 on the Panorama CSIRT website:  https://my.codra.net/en-gb/csirt .
title: Privilege escalation in Panorama Suite with POSIX LDAP authentication

desc:
Chainlit is vulnerable to a file upload block bypass in the "spontaneous_file_upload" functionality. Disabling the feature with the "enabled = false" option only affects the frontend, while the backend upload endpoints remain active and can be abused directly. An attacker with a valid session ID can send requests to these backend endpoints to upload arbitrary file types and then generate a retrieval URL that is accessible to anyone who obtains the link. This allows the attacker to serve malicious content, such as a fake login pages, from the application's trusted domain, which can be used for phishing attacks against users.




The vulnerability has only been confirmed in versions 2.10.0 and 2.12.0 but may also affect other versions.
title: File Upload Block Bypass in Chainlit

desc:
Allocation of resources without limits or throttling vulnerability in Apache SkyWalking BanyanDB.



Uncontrolled resource consumption in Apache SkyWalking BanyanDB's query API allows a remote unauthenticated attacker to cause the server to exhaust memory and terminate. A query request can specify an arbitrarily large result limit and offset, which the server uses to pre-allocate result buffers without an upper bound; a single request may force an allocation of tens of gigabytes and cause the process to be killed



This issue affects Apache SkyWalking BanyanDB: from 0.11.0 before 0.11.1.



Users are recommended to upgrade to version 0.11.1, which fixes the issue.
title: Apache SkyWalking BanyanDB: PropertyService.Query accepts a client-controlled limit without an upper bound.

desc:
Relative Path Traversal vulnerability in ex-aws ex_aws_lambda (ExAws.Lambda module) allows an attacker to redirect an AWS Lambda control-plane request at an unintended resource by injecting path traversal sequences into a caller-supplied identifier.

This vulnerability is associated with program file lib/ex_aws/lambda.ex and program routines ExAws.Lambda.add_permission/5, ExAws.Lambda.delete_event_source_mapping/1, ExAws.Lambda.delete_function/1, ExAws.Lambda.get_event_source_mapping/1, ExAws.Lambda.get_function/1, ExAws.Lambda.get_function_configuration/1, ExAws.Lambda.get_policy/1, ExAws.Lambda.invoke/4, ExAws.Lambda.invoke_async/2, ExAws.Lambda.remove_permission/2, ExAws.Lambda.update_event_source_mapping/2, ExAws.Lambda.update_function_code/2, ExAws.Lambda.update_function_configuration/2.

ExAws.Lambda builds every request path by interpolating caller-supplied identifiers (function names, ARNs, UUIDs, statement IDs) directly into the URL with plain string interpolation, without percent-encoding or validation. The shared request helper only encodes query parameters, never the path, so path metacharacters such as / and .. reach the wire unchanged. An application that passes an untrusted or user-influenced identifier into an ExAws.Lambda operation can therefore have its request steered at a different Lambda resource: a ../ segment climbs out of the intended /2015-03-31/functions/<name> slot and, once the .. is normalized by the HTTP client or the AWS endpoint, addresses a sibling function in the same account. The signed credentials and the HTTP method are unchanged, so the request still succeeds against the wrong resource. Affected operations include function deletion, invocation, configuration updates, and permission changes. Applications that only pass hardcoded or strictly validated identifiers are not affected.

This issue affects ex_aws_lambda: from 2.0.1 before 2.2.0.
title: ex_aws_lambda relative path traversal via unencoded identifiers in ExAws.Lambda request paths

desc: The Everest Forms – Contact Form, Payment Form, Quiz, Survey & Custom Form Builder with AI plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to File Deletion in all versions up to, and including, 3.6.4 This is due to the `delete_entry_files()` function gating file cleanup on a loose `preg_match('/signature_/', $meta_key)` substring check against the entry's meta-key rather than verifying the actual field type, which allows an ordinary Text field whose label begins with "Signature" to generate a qualifying meta-key such as `signature_1` — causing the attacker-controlled value submitted via `everest_forms[form_fields][<field_id>]` to be stored verbatim and later passed to `wp_delete_file()`. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to delete files within the `wp-content/uploads/` directory on the server, as `safe_delete_file()` enforces a realpath boundary that prevents deletion of files outside that directory such as `wp-config.php`. Exploitation requires an administrator to permanently delete the attacker's submitted entry, as the unauthenticated attacker cannot trigger the deletion themselves; the targeted file must also reside within `wp-content/uploads/`. Successful exploitation additionally requires an action by an administrator — the attacker cannot trigger the vulnerability on their own.
products: wpeverest:everest forms – contact form, payment form, quiz, survey & custom form builder with ai
title: Everest Forms <= 3.6.4 - Unauthenticated File Deletion via 'everest_forms[form_fields][<id>]' Parameter via Signature-Keyed Text Field

This makes it possible for authenticated attackers, with subscriber-level access and above, to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page. This is only exploitable when the plugin is configured in FontAwesome 4.x or 5.x compatibility mode and the icon field's return format is set to 'Icon Class', which is the documented usage pattern for rendering icon classes in theme templates.

title: Advanced Custom Fields: Font Awesome Field <= 6.2.2 - Authenticated (Subscriber+) Stored Cross-Site Scripting via Font Awesome Icon Field 'Icon Class' Return Value in 4.x/5.x Compatibility Mode

desc: The MoreConvert Wishlist for WooCommerce plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via the 'empty_icon' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 2.0.4 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. This makes it possible for authenticated attackers, with contributor-level access and above, to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page. This vulnerability is exploitable even in version 2.0.4 where a patch was attempted, because the sanitizer's single html_entity_decode pass combined with esc_attr()'s double_encode=false behavior leaves entity-encoded inner markup intact, which the counter JavaScript then decodes and assigns to innerHTML, turning inert encoded text back into executable DOM elements.
title: MoreConvert Wishlist for WooCommerce <= 2.0.4 - Authenticated (Contributor+) Stored Cross-Site Scripting via 'empty_icon' Shortcode Attribute

desc: The Drag and Drop Multiple File Upload for Contact Form 7 plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via the 'upload-file' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 1.4.1 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page. This requires that the targeted contact form be configured to accept a non-script extension such as .gpx (or any extension outside the HTML/XML/PHP blocklist), and the uploaded file is served without a Content-Type header, causing browsers to MIME-sniff and execute it as text/html.
products: glenwpcoder:drag and drop multiple file upload for contact form 7
title: Drag and Drop Multiple File Upload for Contact Form 7 <= 1.4.1 - Unauthenticated Stored Cross-Site Scripting via File Upload with <title>-Prefixed HTML Payload

desc: The Timetics – Appointment Booking Calendar & Scheduling System plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to unauthorized modification of data and user account creation in versions up to, and including, 1.0.67 This is due to the public `POST /wp-json/timetics/v1/bookings` route being registered with `permission_callback => function () { return true; }` and the handler (`create_item()` → `save_bookings()` → `booking_appointment()`) passing the attacker-controlled `email` directly into `Customer::make()`, which (a) grants the `timetics-customer` role to any existing WordPress user matched by email — including administrators and staff — and overwrites that account's `first_name`/`last_name` user meta, and (b) calls `wp_insert_user()` with role `timetics-customer` when the email is new, regardless of the site's `users_can_register` setting. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to create arbitrary WordPress user accounts, assign the `timetics-customer` role to existing accounts (including administrators), and overwrite their profile metadata.
title: Timetics <= 1.0.67 - Missing Authorization to Unauthenticated Arbitrary User Creation and Role Assignment via 'email' Parameter

desc: The Duplicate Post plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via the 'data[custom][names][prefix]' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 1.5.7 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. This makes it possible for authenticated attackers, with subscriber-level access and above, to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page. Exploitation requires the site owner to have enabled both 'User Level Permissions' for the Subscriber role and the 'Show reference to original item?' option, and the targeted administrator must view the edit screen of the chained copy post in the classic editor.
title: Duplicate Post <= 1.5.7 - Authenticated (Subscriber+) Stored Cross-Site Scripting via 'prefix' Copy-Name Parameter

desc: The AutomatorWP – No-Code Workflow Automation, Integration & Webhooks Plugin, now with AI plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to generic SQL Injection via the 'post_field_conditions[0][field]' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 6.1.2 due to insufficient escaping on the user supplied parameter and lack of sufficient preparation on the existing SQL query. This makes it possible for authenticated attackers, with administrator-level access and above, to append additional SQL queries into already existing queries that can be used to extract sensitive information from the database. The vulnerability requires a two-step exploit: a crafted field value must first be stored via the wp_ajax_automatorwp_update_item_option AJAX endpoint, and then the target automation must be triggered to fire the vulnerable SQL query.
products: rubengc:automatorwp – no-code workflow automation, integration & webhooks plugin, now with ai
title: AutomatorWP <= 6.1.2 - Authenticated (Administrator+) SQL Injection via 'post_field_conditions' Parameter

desc: The CubeWP Framework plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Privilege Escalation in all versions up to, and including, 1.1.32 This is due to the `cubewp_frontend_role_caps()` function, registered on the `user_has_cap` filter, which excludes REST API requests via a `REST_REQUEST` guard but omits a corresponding `XMLRPC_REQUEST` check, causing it to unconditionally widen capabilities for any Subscriber or Contributor on XML-RPC and admin-ajax.php request paths. This makes it possible for authenticated attackers with Subscriber-level access and above to escalate their privileges to the full Contributor role capability set — gaining `edit_posts`, `delete_posts`, and `read` — allowing them to create, edit, and delete posts through core XML-RPC methods such as `wp.newPost`. Critically, the capability widening is not scoped to CubeWP's own submission handlers but applies globally to all core capability gates on affected request paths, meaning any Subscriber account can exploit this with a single standard XML-RPC call and no CubeWP-specific interaction. Successful exploitation causes the attacker's own account to receive every capability defined for the Contributor role.
title: CubeWP Framework <= 1.1.32 - Authenticated (Subscriber+) Limited Privilege Escalation via 'user_has_cap' Filter

desc: The Download Manager plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via the 'file[files][]' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 3.3.78 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. This makes it possible for authenticated attackers, with author-level access and above, to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page. Exploitation requires that the affected package uses a link template containing the [play_button] shortcode, such as the bundled 'With Audio Preview' template, since the vulnerable audioPlayer() output path is only triggered when that placeholder is rendered.
title: Download Manager <= 3.3.78 - Authenticated (Author+) Stored Cross-Site Scripting via 'file[files][]' Parameter

desc: The Download Manager plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via the 'file[page_template], file[files][]' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 3.3.78 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. This makes it possible for authenticated attackers, with author-level access and above, to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page.
title: Download Manager <= 3.3.78 - Authenticated (Author+) Stored Cross-Site Scripting via 'file[page_template]' and 'file[files][]' Parameters

desc: The Download Manager plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Local File Inclusion in all versions up to, and including, 3.3.78 via the 'file[page_template]' parameter parameter. This makes it possible for authenticated attackers, with author-level access and above, to include and execute arbitrary .php files on the server, allowing the execution of any PHP code in those files. This can be used to bypass access controls, obtain sensitive data, or achieve code execution in cases where .php file types can be uploaded and included. The malicious page_template value is stored when an Author creates or edits a package post, and the inclusion is triggered on any subsequent page view of the package permalink, meaning the include() can be fired by unauthenticated visitors after the payload is planted.
title: Download Manager <= 3.3.78 - Authenticated (Author+) Local File Inclusion via 'file[page_template]' Parameter

desc: JobRouter Premium, version 2025.1.11, has a stored Cross-Site Scripting (XSS) vulnerability in the Favorites feature. An authenticated user with low privileges can inject JavaScript code that is persistently stored on the server. When other users access the affected page, the code executes in their browsers. A successful exploit could allow an attacker to perform unauthorized actions on behalf of the victim, access sensitive information, or compromise the integrity of their sessions.
title: Stored Cross-Site Scripting in JobRouter Premium by JobRouter

desc: The Music Player for WooCommerce plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Directory Traversal in all versions up to, and including, 1.9.4 via the '_downloadable_files' parameter parameter. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to read the contents of arbitrary files on the server, which can contain sensitive information. Staging the attack requires storing a crafted downloadable file URL against a product, which requires the edit_products capability (Shop Manager or above); however, triggering the file read via the ?wcmp-action=play handler is fully unauthenticated once the crafted URL is saved to a published product.
title: Music Player for WooCommerce <= 1.9.4 - Unauthenticated Arbitrary File Read via '_downloadable_files' Post Meta

desc: The Funnelforms Free – Multi Step Form, Contact Form & Lead Funnel Builder plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via the 'document.settings.heading' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 5.0.9 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. This makes it possible for authenticated attackers, with administrator-level access and above, to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page. This is exploitable on standard single-site WordPress installs only when the DISALLOW_UNFILTERED_HTML constant is set, the site is a WordPress multisite network (where administrators lack the unfiltered_html capability by default), or an administrator has explicitly granted the funnelforms_edit_forms capability to a lower-privileged role. Exploitation by attackers with administrator-level access and above requires that the site is a WordPress multisite install (site admins automatically lack unfiltered_html). On a default installation, where that is not configured, the vulnerability requires attackers with custom-level access and above.

desc:
Bizum Pay for Android incorporates static values within the APK to authenticate and sign requests to its API, including those for user registration. These values are common across different installations and can be extracted from the APK. An attacker who obtains the application could reuse them to generate requests that the server accepts as authenticated. The potential scope of these requests was limited to querying auxiliary information and certain configuration statuses. Under no circumstances could they generate unauthorised payments via Bizum Pay, nor could they carry out illegitimate activations of the app (which always require access to the customer’s banking channels, thereby protecting them from this type of potential vulnerability). Furthermore, requests are always limited to a set number of attempts and are closely monitored to prevent potential mass queries.



The correction implemented uses site-specific material and removes support for the previous format in the backend. Consequently, previous versions are no longer operational for the services affected.
title: Using encrypted credentials in Bizum Pay for Android

desc: The Groundhogg plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Cross-Site Request Forgery in versions up to, and including, 4.11 This is due to the Admin_Page::page() callback dispatching methods named directly by the $_REQUEST['action'] parameter via call_user_func([$this, $action]) without verifying a nonce: the only nonce check lives in process_action() (admin_init), which prefixes the action with 'process_' before dispatching, so an attacker who supplies action=process_delete causes process_action() to look up the nonexistent 'process_process_delete' method and bail without ever calling wp_verify_nonce(), while page() subsequently invokes the real process_delete() (and other process_* methods such as process_spam, process_status_change, process_edit) with no CSRF token of its own. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to delete arbitrary contacts, change contact opt-in status (including marking contacts as spam, which also appends their IP to the site-wide disallowed_keys option), and perform other state-changing actions via a forged request granted they can trick a site administrator (or any user holding the relevant Groundhogg capability such as delete_contacts/edit_contacts) into performing an action such as clicking on a link.
products: trainingbusinesspros:groundhogg — ai crm, newsletters, and marketing automation
title: Groundhogg <= 4.11 - Cross-Site Request Forgery

desc: The AI Engine – MCP Server & AI Chatbot for WordPress, with Claude, ChatGPT & Gemini plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Limited Arbitrary File Upload in all versions up to, and including, 3.9.4 via the `url` parameter of the `/mwai/v1/helpers/create_image` REST API endpoint. The vulnerability exists because the `add_image_from_url()` function applies the `get_allowed_mime_types()` extension allow-list only on the custom-filename branch; when the request omits a `filename` value, the empty-filename branch derives the stored file's extension directly from the URL basename via `sanitize_file_name()` without any MIME or extension validation, then writes the downloaded response body verbatim to the WordPress uploads directory via `file_put_contents()`. This makes it possible for authenticated attackers with Editor-level access and above to place attacker-controlled HTML, SVG, or JavaScript files into `wp-content/uploads/YYYY/MM/` under an attacker-chosen extension, enabling stored cross-site scripting against any administrator who opens the resulting attachment URL. The download routine accepts any HTTP response whose `Content-Type` header begins with `image/`, a value freely controlled by the attacker-owned origin server, meaning the written content need not be a valid image.
products: tigroumeow:ai engine – mcp server & ai chatbot for wordpress, with claude, chatgpt & gemini
title: AI Engine <= 3.9.4 - Authenticated (Editor+) Limited Arbitrary File Upload via 'url' Parameter

desc: The ShopMagic – email automation for WordPress plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Improper Verification of Cryptographic Signature in all versions up to, and including, 4.9.5 Although `CurrentCustomer::encode_tracking_data()` appends an md5 hash to the `shopmagic_visitor_<COOKIEHASH>` cookie to make it tamper-resistant, `CookiePersistence::get_tracking_data()` returns the raw `json_decode()`'d cookie value directly without computing or verifying that hash, leaving the cookie's `user_id`, `email`, and `meta` fields fully under attacker control. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to forge the visitor cookie — which is predictable because its name is derived as `md5(siteurl)` from the public site URL — and submit it to the unprotected `wp_ajax_nopriv_capture_email_url` endpoint (which is registered without a nonce check or capability check) to impersonate any WordPress user including administrators in ShopMagic's customer-identity context, and to overwrite the stored profile metadata — including name, phone number, and billing address — of any existing guest record in `wp_shopmagic_guest` and `wp_shopmagic_guest_meta` via `GuestManager::save()`.
title: ShopMagic <= 4.9.5 - Unauthenticated Improper Verification of Cryptographic Signature to Guest Impersonation and Arbitrary Guest Profile Modification via 'shopmagic_visitor_<COOKIEHASH>' Cookie

desc: The Widgets for Social Photo Feed plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via the 'widget-id' shortcode attribute of the [trustindex-feed] shortcode in versions up to, and including, 1.8.3 This is due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping in the registerWidget() function, which concatenates the raw shortcode attribute directly into a double-quoted JavaScript string literal that is then enqueued via wp_add_inline_script() and rendered in wp_footer/admin_footer. This makes it possible for authenticated attackers, with Contributor-level access and above, to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page.

desc: The theme for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via the 'metavalue (via wp-admin/post.php add_meta → post_meta key 'my_field')' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 8.3 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. desc: The Ninja Tables – Responsive Table Builder for Data, Pricing & Product Tables plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to SQL Injection via the 'dateFormat' column metadata parameter in versions up to, and including, 5.5.1 This is due to insufficient escaping on the stored 'dateFormat' value in DefaultProvider::orderByJsonQuery(); convertDateFormatToMysql() only performs str_replace on date-format tokens and leaves SQL metacharacters (including single quotes) intact, after which the value is concatenated directly into an orderByRaw() ORDER BY clause inside single quotes. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to append additional SQL queries into already existing queries that can be used to extract sensitive information from the database; the payload is stored in the _ninja_table_columns post meta and executed on every unauthenticated request to the wp_ajax_ninja_tables_public_action AJAX endpoint when the table uses sorting_type='by_column' with a date column.

desc:
Pydantic AI Harness's PlaywrightBrowser applies an egress policy to the requests a page makes. It treated any URL containing a backslash as having no host, and it allows script and asset requests with no host. A page script could therefore add a backslash to a URL's query to send requests to private addresses, to hosts outside allowed_domains, and to hosts in blocked_domains.

This affects applications that use PlaywrightBrowser to open pages or follow instructions an attacker can influence. It applies to fetch, XHR, sendBeacon, WebSocket and passive asset requests. Navigation and frames were not affected. A policy that limits every request kind to an allowlist did not prevent data from being sent to another host.

Responses from private services could be read only when the service permits cross-origin reads or accepts the WebSocket connection. Current Chromium versions separately block many requests from public pages to private addresses, but not requests between public hosts, and not when the browser runs behind a forward proxy.

The assumed attacker is a third party with no access to the application who controls script on a page the agent opens, or content that steers the agent's browser tools.

Upgrade pydantic-ai-harness to 0.74.0 or later. Until then, enforce egress outside the browser with a firewall or a filtering proxy, and do not rely on the browser's domain lists for untrusted pages.
title: PlaywrightBrowser egress policy skips requests whose URL query contains a backslash

A local attacker can exploit this issue by sending log messages through the local log socket with crafted process names to inject forged identity attributes.

desc: In Revive Adserver through 6.0.9, an advertiser can put XML syntax in fields of its own video creative. Unescaped MediaFile attributes and CDATA terminators allow the advertiser to inject elements into VAST responses served for a publisher's zone. A crafted TrackingEvents block can suppress the ad server's video playback event records and redirect tracking requests to an attacker-controlled endpoint.

In Revive Adserver through 6.0.9, user-controlled entity names in XLS report exports can be interpreted as spreadsheet formulas. A user with permission to rename a zone can place a formula in the zone name, which is then included in another user's Conversion Tracking report. Opening the affected spreadsheet can evaluate the formula and alter displayed report contents.

In Revive Adserver through 6.0.9, unauthenticated request parameters in ad delivery can cause reflected cross-site scripting. A crafted delivery URL places a macro token in the source or target parameter and malicious markup in the referer parameter. Macro replacement after initial input encoding can insert the unescaped markup into generated banner output, causing JavaScript execution in the delivery origin when a visitor follows the URL. An active banner is required.

In Revive Adserver through 6.0.9, deleting an agency, advertiser, or publisher through affected API paths can leave the associated account and user session active because the deletion path does not load the entity's account identifier before cleanup. A user whose entity has been deleted can continue accessing pages of the orphaned account. Access to data belonging to another agency was not demonstrated.

In Revive Adserver through 6.0.9, the zone banner-linking page (zone-include.php) does not cast the keys of the includebanner request array to integers. An authenticated manager, or a trafficker with the zone-linking permission, who owns the submitted website and zone can place SQL in an array key, which is concatenated unquoted into the banner-lookup query, resulting in time-based blind SQL injection bounded by the privileges of the application's database account.

In Revive Adserver through 6.0.9, the ct0 request parameter of the delivery scripts is only required to start with http:// or https:// and is prepended unescaped to banner click URLs. An unauthenticated attacker can craft a delivery URL that executes JavaScript in the delivery origin when a visitor follows it. An active banner using the raw {clickurl} macro is required.

In Revive Adserver through 6.0.9, an authenticated manager with access to two advertisers can associate a conversion tracker owned by one advertiser with a campaign owned by the other. The tracker-campaign page checks access to each object but does not verify that their actual owners match. The resulting association can expose the first advertiser's tracker name and identifier in the second advertiser's restricted conversion report.

In Revive Adserver through 6.0.9, the public conversion-variable endpoint does not verify that a caller-supplied conversion belongs to the supplied tracker. An unauthenticated attacker can submit a unique variable for a different tracker's conversion, causing that conversion to be classified as a duplicate and excluded from conversion reports.

In Revive Adserver through 6.0.9, the zone-linking page can disclose campaign and banner names and identifiers belonging to another agency. An authenticated manager, or a website user with permission to link banners to zones, can supply another agency's advertiser and campaign identifiers because the selection lists are not restricted to the agency owning the zone.

In Revive Adserver through 6.0.9, an authenticated manager can supply another agency's advertiser or website identifier as a report scope and obtain that entity's name in an XLS report header. Submitted scope identifiers are not checked against the manager's permitted selections. The demonstrated disclosure is limited to entity names.

desc: NetBird is a zero-trust networking platform that connects people, machines, and AI agents across any network. desc:
Crypt::JWT versions before 0.037_1 for Perl compare HMAC signatures and JWE authentication tags in non-constant time.

decode_jwt compares HS256, HS384 and HS512 signatures, and the authentication tag of A128CBC-HS256, A192CBC-HS384 and A256CBC-HS512 encrypted tokens, against the computed value with Perl's eq operator. Its run time depends on the number of matching leading bytes.

An attacker who can submit many candidate tokens and measure the timing precisely enough may recover the expected signature or tag byte by byte and forge a token that verifies.

desc:
Crypt::JWT versions before 0.037_1 for Perl allow memory exhaustion via unbounded inflation of zip DEF payloads.

When a token header sets "zip" to "DEF", decode_jwt inflates the payload with no limit on the output size. A signed token is inflated after its signature verifies. An encrypted token is inflated after decryption, and with RSA-OAEP or ECDH-ES key management anyone who holds the recipient's public key can produce a token that decrypts.
title: Crypt::JWT versions before 0.037_1 for Perl allow memory exhaustion via unbounded inflation of zip DEF payloads

desc:
Crypt::JWT versions before 0.037_1 for Perl allow CPU exhaustion via an unbounded PBES2 iteration count.

For a token using a PBES2 key management algorithm, decode_jwt passes the p2c header parameter to PBKDF2 as the iteration count without a range check, and derives the key before any integrity check. Unless accepted_alg rules it out, a token can select PBES2 whenever decode_jwt is given a symmetric key.
title: Crypt::JWT versions before 0.037_1 for Perl allow CPU exhaustion via an unbounded PBES2 iteration count

desc:
psqlODBC did not check that a server reply matches the query it sent: that a FETCH returns no more rows than it asked for, that each row has the described number of columns, that one query produces one result, and that a COPY, a transaction or the connection ends where the protocol says. By sending replies that do not match, a hostile or compromised server, or anyone on the network path of a connection that does not use sslmode=verify-full (the default is disable) can corrupt memory in the application:

- A FETCH reply with more rows than requested overflows the row cache.
- Extra results in reply to a FETCH, or to the queries of a keyset-driven cursor, are freed while still in use.
- A key query of a keyset-driven cursor answered with extra columns, or a re-read row with fewer columns, overflows the row cache.
- Replies without columns or rows, or with NULL values, to the driver's internal queries at connect time and in catalog functions are dereferenced.
- A malformed relacl value in SQLTablePrivileges() makes the driver write past a buffer.
- On Windows with MSDTC, a long transaction name returned by the server overflows a buffer during recovery.
- Values in replies to the driver's internal queries are used without checking their range: an empty column name, a parameter count, a large-object size, a function's or trigger's argument count, and a result of exactly 32767 columns. They are dereferenced, read past, returned to the application or sent back to the server as stack memory, or make the driver loop forever.
- A reply that ends a COPY, the connection or the transaction at an unexpected point leaves freed results, keysets or table information in use: a CopyOutResponse followed by a lost connection, a ROLLBACK command tag under UseDeclareFetch=1, or a lost connection while a cursor with positioned updates is closed. Eight extra bytes in a reply also make the driver wait forever for a COPY to end.
- On Windows, a start-up reply without client_encoding crashes the driver, and with MSDTC a failed connection makes the XA library use a connection it has already freed.
- An error message ending in the first byte of a multibyte character leaves the SQLSTATE returned by SQLGetDiagRecW() unterminated.
- When a string value did not fit the application's buffer, eight Unicode entry points filled the buffer and wrote no null terminator, so a caller that reads to the terminator, as ODBC allows, read past the end of its own buffer.

This continues the fixes for CVE-2026-120058 and CVE-2026-120060, which covered other replies. The demonstrated results are crashes and heap corruption; code execution has not been demonstrated.

Versions up to and including psqlODBC 18.00.0006 are affected.
title: Driver does not check that server replies match the queries it sent

desc:
A parameter-array execution that fails part-way leaves the rows it has already
queued on the statement handle, and the next execution on that handle sends
them. After a data-at-execution batch is abandoned, by SQLCancel or a
rejected SQLPutData, the next SQLExecDirect sends the failed batch's rows
and returns SQL_SUCCESS without sending its own statement.

So an application that logs the failure on the same handle has its log entry
turned into a silent no-op, while rows it was told had failed are stored. An
end user who controls one value in an application's array insert can arrange
both halves of that.

A second route needs no data-at-execution parameter: when building a later row
fails in parameter conversion, the queued rows go to the server ahead of the
next parameter array on the handle, inside whatever transaction and session
settings are current by then. One variant also writes past the end of a shorter
SQL_ATTR_PARAM_STATUS_PTR array supplied by the next statement.

The statements that run are the application's own, correctly quoted; no SQL
text comes from outside.

Versions from psqlODBC 12.02.0000, which introduced batched parameter-array
execution, up to and including 18.00.0006 are affected.
title: Statement after an abandoned parameter array sends the abandoned batch's rows instead of its own

desc:
psqlODBC mapped an SSLmode value in a connection string that it did not recognise, such as SSLmode=Require, SSLmode=Verify-Full, SSLmode={require} or SSLmode={verify-full}, to disable. SQLDriverConnect() then returned SQL_SUCCESS with no diagnostic, and the connection was not encrypted.

An attacker on the network path of such a connection can read and change its traffic.

Versions up to and including psqlODBC 18.00.0006 are affected.
title: An SSLmode value written with capitals or braces connects without TLS

desc:
With SQL_C_DEFAULT, the C type of a bound column or parameter follows its SQL type. An application sizes its buffer from the type it was told when it described the statement. When the column had another type at fetch time, because the server reported another type, the table was altered, or an output parameter's result column had another type, psqlODBC wrote the larger type into the smaller buffer: 12 bytes past a 4-byte buffer for a uuid, and more in multi-row fetches, where the driver also steps through the array by the larger size.

Other conversions wrote past the application's buffer as well:

- With Int8As set to a smaller type, an int8 column fetched as SQL_C_DEFAULT was still written as 8 bytes.
- An int2vector column fetched as SQL_C_DEFAULT returned unterminated binary data instead of text.
- An output parameter that the application discards by binding a NULL buffer overflowed a stack buffer in the driver.
- SQLGetData() with BufferLength 0 on a column the driver reads as a large object wrote a NUL byte past the buffer.
- Adding a row with SQLBulkOperations(SQL_ADD) on a static updatable cursor before the first fetch, then changing that row, rolling back and fetching it, made the keyset index arithmetic free a pointer that was never allocated and corrupt the heap.

This can be triggered by a hostile or compromised server, or anyone on the network path of a connection that does not use sslmode=verify-full (the default is disable), and by the owner of a table the application reads.

Versions up to and including psqlODBC 18.00.0006 are affected.
title: Buffer overflows when a converted value does not fit the application's buffer

desc:
When Debug or CommLog is enabled and the log directory cannot be used, psqlODBC falls back to a directory under the user's home directory. It wrote that path with an unexpanded ~, which is resolved relative to the process's current directory. Another local user who controls a directory on that path can make the driver create the victim's mylog_*.log and psqlodbc_*.log files in any directory the victim can write to, or leave the victim's process blocked in open().

This completes the fix for CVE-2026-120066 in 18.00.0006.

Versions up to and including psqlODBC 18.00.0006 are affected.
title: Another local user can redirect log files (incomplete fix for CVE-2026-120066)

desc:
psqlODBC assumed that a table it reads keeps the definition it had when the statement was described or parsed. A database user who owns a table or view another user's application reads can crash that application, with an honest server and default options, in these cases:

- Columns dropped or added in another session while the application updates rows through an updatable cursor, or describes the columns with Parse=1.
- A view whose ctid is NULL, read through an updatable cursor, which writes past the row cache, and a view with a volatile filter scrolled backward with UseDeclareFetch=1.
- Rows added through an updatable cursor to a table with child tables or partitions.
- A column whose type is named lo, written with data-at-execution parameters.
- A DROP TABLE or ALTER TABLE on the connection while another statement still uses the table's column information.
- NULL key columns in rows the driver re-reads for an updatable cursor.
- A function called with more output parameters than its result has columns.
- SQLTables() and SQLTablesW() dereferenced NULL when called with empty strings for the catalog, schema and table names together with a NULL TableType, which kills the process that loaded the driver and every session it serves.

The demonstrated results are crashes; one case writes past a heap buffer, but code execution has not been demonstrated.

Versions up to and including psqlODBC 18.00.0006 are affected.
title: Another database user can crash applications by changing a table they own

desc:
psqlODBC rewrites statement text for keyset-driven cursors and ODBC escapes using positions it found in the text. These positions could lie outside the text or describe another statement:

- After SQLExecDirect() failed on a statement handle, the FROM and WHERE positions of the failed statement were applied to the next, shorter statement on that handle.
- The parser could record a FROM position with no text after it, and the rewrite then copied a negative length.
- An {fn …} escape whose arguments contain FOR UPDATE, ; or INTO … FROM made the driver remove a cursor prefix from the wrong buffer.
- {fn CONVERT(?, …)} with an output parameter produced a negative argument length.
- An unclosed {fn …} escape made the driver read past the statement, and a few thousand nested ones exhausted the stack.
- Translating @@identity in long statement text read an uninitialised pointer, and {? = call …} with nothing bound for the return value dereferenced NULL.

Whoever supplies the text of a statement that an application opens on a keyset-driven or dynamic cursor with a concurrency other than read-only, or calls with an output parameter, can corrupt the application's heap and end it. That includes the users of query tools, report builders and other applications that run SQL their users type. Code execution has not been demonstrated.

Versions up to and including psqlODBC 18.00.0006 are affected.
title: Memory corruption and crashes when the driver rewrites statements for cursors and escapes

desc:
To build positioned updates and to describe columns, psqlODBC matches the names in a statement against the catalog. Where it matched differently from the server, it used another table or column:

- Table and schema names were compared case-insensitively in its column-information cache, so users could be taken for another user's "Users", and the driver then evaluated that table's column default to answer @@IDENTITY.
- In FROM ONLY t, ONLY was taken for the table name.
- Column names were compared case-insensitively, so with Parse=1 the type of another column could decide the size of the application's buffer, which a fetch then overflowed.
- In a database whose encoding is single-byte, such as LATIN1 or SQL_ASCII, the server folds the accented letters of an unquoted name by its own locale, while the driver folded only A-Z, so ÉTAT could be taken for another user's "État" instead of état.
- On systems other than Windows, in a Turkish or Azeri locale, an unquoted I was not folded to i, and keywords and ODBC function names did not match.
- Without a schema name, SQLSpecialColumns() could report the key columns of another user's same-named temporary table, and SQLPrimaryKeys() could take another user's index named <table>_pkey for the primary key of a table without one.
- After search_path changed other than through a plain SET statement, positioned writes went to the same-named table in the previously current schema.
- SQLBulkOperations() trusted the ctid stored inside a variable-length bookmark handed back by the application, and ignored the WHERE clause that restricted the cursor, so a forged bookmark read, updated or deleted any row of the cursor's table.

A database user who can create a table in a schema on another user's search_path can redirect that user's positioned updates, inserts and deletes to a table of their choosing, where they run with the victim's rights, or run an expression of their choosing under the victim's role.

Versions up to and including psqlODBC 18.00.0006 are affected.
title: Positioned writes go to another user's table through name and case matching

desc:
psqlODBC scans statement text itself to substitute parameters, translate ODBC escapes, join batched statements and rewrite queries for updatable cursors. Where it read the text differently from the server, text the driver took for data ran as SQL, or a positioned write went to another table:

- An escape string constant written e'…' in lower case was not recognised as one, and '…' after a keyword ending in E, as in LIKE'…', was taken for one.
- A } inside a quoted literal ended an ODBC {d …}, {t …}, {ts …} or {escape …} sequence.
- Dollar-quote tags containing _ were not recognised, and an identifier starting with _ followed by $, such as _$$, was taken for the start of a dollar quote, so a parameter marker inside a literal was substituted.
- A trailing -- comment in one statement of a batched parameter array swallowed the next statement.
- Comments, literals longer than 255 bytes and escape strings were misread when the driver located the FROM and WHERE clauses of a query for an updatable cursor, and the text copied into the cursor's own queries could include SQL from inside a literal.
- A table name containing $ was cut at the $, and a quoted table name starting with , or ; ended the table list, so positioned updates, inserts and deletes went to another table.
- An integer parameter with an embedded NUL byte cut the query short.
- /*/ was taken for a comment that opens and closes, while the server reads it as one that only opens.
- ConnSettings was split at every semicolon, including one inside a quoted literal, so an application that puts an end user's value into a SET command there ran the rest of the value as SQL at connect time.

An end user who controls text the application puts into a statement, or a parameter value, can run SQL with the rights of the application's database role. A database user who can create a table with a crafted name can redirect another user's positioned writes to a table of their choosing.

Versions up to and including psqlODBC 18.00.0006 are affected.
title: SQL injection and redirected writes because the driver reads SQL text differently from the server

desc:
psqlODBC frees memory that is still in use, frees it twice, or writes outside an application buffer in these cases:

- The clean-up the driver runs at commit and rollback sends queries of its own, and the reply to one of them can start the clean-up again while it is running. The nested run frees the rollback log, or the list of cursors and prepared statements to close, and the outer run uses and frees it again.
- The callback through which libpq delivers notices could run that clean-up, and close the connection, while libpq was still using the connection.
- Freeing a statement whose result holds several cursors (FetchRefcursors=1, or UseDeclareFetch=1) used the freed first result while the later cursors were closed.
- With UseDeclareFetch=1, after a rollback closed an updatable cursor, rows added or deleted through it were counted but not stored, so freeing the statement freed uninitialised pointers, and adding a row wrote past the keyset.
- After a multi-row fetch failed on a row other than the first of its rowset, SQLGetData() wrote at an offset past the buffer the application passed.
- SQLProcedureColumns() freed the result of its catalog query twice when the query failed.
- In a process named sqlservr (SQL Server linked servers), a server version below 8.4 made the statement parser free a buffer twice.
- A failed SQLPutData in the middle of a SQLSetPos() or SQLBulkOperations() data-at-execution sequence left the whole operation pending, with the internal statement still allocated and autocommit silently off, so later statements were rolled back at disconnect. The next positioned update ran the stale callback against a statement that was never executed and dereferenced NULL.

Most of these can be triggered by a hostile or compromised server, or anyone on the network path of a connection that does not use sslmode=verify-full (the default is disable). A database user who can make a statement fail, or who controls the contents of a row the application reads, can trigger the UseDeclareFetch=1 and SQLGetData() cases against an honest server. The demonstrated results are crashes and heap corruption; code execution has not been demonstrated.

Versions up to and including psqlODBC 18.00.0006 are affected.
title: Use after free, double free and out-of-bounds writes in result and transaction clean-up

desc:
With the driver's debug log (MyLog) turned on, two paths write the database
password to the log in clear text, both beside a line where the driver's own
redaction masks it as PWD=xxxxx:

- Pressing "Test" in the Windows data source setup dialog (psqlsetup.dll)
  logs the whole connection string, which carries PWD= percent-encoded,
  which is reversible, and any password= or sslpassword= inside pqopt.
- The Unicode connect functions SQLDriverConnectW, SQLConnectW and
  SQLBrowseConnectW log their arguments as they convert them between UTF-16
  and UTF-8, before the masking happens. The ANSI entry points are unaffected.

Turning the log on takes an administrator, and MyLog is off by default. The
exposure is the person who later reads the log, which in practice means a log
attached to a bug report or handed to support. Making that safe is the purpose
of the driver's redaction, and these two sites bypassed it.

Versions up to and including psqlODBC 18.00.0006 are affected.
title: Debug log records the database password in clear text

desc:
psqlODBC uses sizes and counts without checking their range, or keeps them in types too small for them:

- A row array size of 0, set with SQLSetStmtAttr() or on the ARD, makes SQLSetPos() with SQL_REFRESH write past the bound arrays.
- SQL_DESC_COUNT above 32767 on an APD or IPD writes before the start of a heap buffer.
- A numeric parameter with a negative scale overflows a stack buffer.
- SQLGetData() of a text value of 2 GiB or more into a wide-character buffer computes a wrapped size and overflows the heap.
- The 16-bit reference count and size of the statement parser's column-information cache wrap, which frees a cache entry still in use or overflows the cache, and a statement with more than 32768 columns overflows the parser's field array.
- An updatable cursor that records more than 65535 changes in one transaction wraps the 16-bit capacity of its rollback log, which overflows it and frees it twice.
- A statement with 32769 or more parameter markers overflows a 16-bit parameter count.
- A wide-character string of more than 2 GiB wraps the size of its UTF-8 conversion, which is then written below the start of a heap buffer.
- SQLGetDiagField() and SQLGetDiagFieldW() always stored the five-character SQLSTATE plus its terminator and checked BufferLength only afterwards, overrunning a buffer shorter than six bytes.
- The ANSI SQLSetDescField(SQL_DESC_NAME) on an IPD ignored BufferLength and copied the name with strdup(), reading a name passed as pointer plus length past its end.
- SQLFetchScroll(SQL_FETCH_BOOKMARK) did not check the bookmark it was given, so whoever chooses the bookmark value read out of bounds and crashed the process.
- Four places in the parameter conversion read one byte past the end of a bound character parameter, and one of them rewrote it.
- Binding a date, time or timestamp C value to an SQL_INTEGER or SQL_SMALLINT parameter dereferenced NULL instead of returning the conversion error.

Depending on the case, the values come from the application, from the data or statement text an end user supplies, or from a database user who controls the size of a table or value. The demonstrated results are crashes and heap corruption; code execution has not been demonstrated.

Versions up to and including psqlODBC 18.00.0006 are affected.
title: Unchecked sizes and counters overflow driver buffers
SQL injection through names the driver puts into its own queries

desc:
psqlODBC parsed and built connection strings in ways that let a value end early:

- In a braced value, such as PWD={…}, a trailing byte 0x7d of a GBK, Big5 or SJIS character was taken for the closing brace.
- A braced value that ended right after an escaped }} was not reported as unterminated, and its contents were parsed as further keywords.
- SQLConnectW(), SQLDriverConnectW() and SQLBrowseConnectW() cut a connection string whose UTF-8 form is longer than 32767 bytes, which changes how the rest of it is parsed.
- On Windows with MSDTC, the password and user name were put into the XA open string without escaping, and the XA library copied each item of that string into a 64-byte stack buffer.
- Percent-encoding a long password wrote one byte past a 4096-byte stack buffer.

An end user who supplies a password, or another value the application puts into the connection string, can set other connection keywords, for example to connect the application to a server of their choosing. The MSDTC case can also overflow a stack buffer in the process that loads the XA library.

Versions up to and including psqlODBC 18.00.0006 are affected.
title: Connection string injection in SQLDriverConnect and the MSDTC XA open string

desc:
On Windows, when a connection takes part in a distributed transaction, psqlODBC and its XA library open further connections of their own to finish the transaction. These connections did not keep the security settings of the application's connection:

- When the XA library's first connection attempt failed, it tried again with sslmode=allow, even for a data source configured with sslmode=verify-full or verify-ca.
- The connections the driver opens itself ignored every libpq option given through pqopt, such as channel_binding=require, and the open string it registers with MSDTC carried no pqopt, so the XA library's connections dropped those options too.

An attacker on the network path between the MSDTC host and the PostgreSQL server, without a certificate or credentials, can make those connections go to a server of their choosing without TLS, read and change what they send, and decide the outcome MSDTC records for the transaction.

Versions up to and including psqlODBC 18.00.0006 are affected.
title: MSDTC connections drop the connection's TLS and channel binding settings

desc:
PDF::API2 versions before 2.049 for Perl allow unbounded recursion via circular cross-reference chains in readxrtr.

When a PDF is opened, readxrtr reads each cross-reference table and calls itself on the offset in the trailer's /Prev entry. Nothing records which offsets it has already read, so a /Prev entry pointing back to an earlier table, or to its own, makes it recurse without end.

An attacker who supplies a crafted PDF can cause a denial of service in any application that opens it.
title: PDF::API2 versions before 2.049 for Perl allow unbounded recursion via circular cross-reference chains in readxrtr

desc:
psqlODBC read memory it had not written, or memory past the end of an application buffer, and sent it to the server or returned it to the application:

- Text bound as SQL_C_CHAR to a large-object parameter was read past the end of the application's buffer, and the extra bytes were stored in the large object.
- After a fetch truncated a long bytea or large-object value, positioned updates and inserts read past the bound buffer and wrote that memory into the row.
- Hex text with a NUL byte, bound to a binary parameter with an explicit length, sent uninitialised heap memory as the parameter value.
- With RowVersioning=1, SQLColumns() on a table that does not exist returned uninitialised stack memory as the schema and table names.
- With UseDeclareFetch=1, bookmarks of updatable block cursors contained uninitialised heap memory, and a malformed ctid from the server sent stale heap bytes in positioned updates and deletes.
- With UseServerSidePrepare=0, calling SQLNumResultCols(), SQLDescribeCol() or SQLColAttribute() on a prepared statement before SQLExecute() read the application's bound parameter buffers and sent their current contents to the server as literals, although ODBC lets the application fill those buffers after the describe.
- The driver named the prepared statements, savepoints, cursors and keyset plans it creates on the server after the heap addresses of its own objects, so the server, or anyone reading an unencrypted connection, learned exact heap addresses inside the client.

Depending on the case, an end user who supplies a parameter value, a database user who stores a long value in a row, or a hostile server can obtain memory of the application process, which may hold data of other users or credentials.

Versions up to and including psqlODBC 18.00.0006 are affected.
title: Driver sends application memory to the server or returns it to the caller

desc:
To escape a bound parameter, or a name passed to a catalog function, psqlODBC has to know where each multibyte character of the client encoding ends. It treated a client encoding named by an alias the server accepts, such as WIN950, Windows950 or big-5 for BIG5, as single-byte, and it accepted too narrow a range of lead bytes for JOHAB, EUC_TW, EUC_CN and EUC_KR. A quote byte that the server reads as part of such a character was then not doubled, or a quote the server reads on its own was taken for part of a character, and the literal ended early.

An end user who controls one bound character parameter, or a name the application passes to a catalog function such as SQLTables(), can run SQL with the rights of the application's database role. This requires a connection that is not in UTF-8: the ANSI driver, or the ANSI entry points, with one of these client encodings. For bound parameters the driver must also be substituting parameters itself, as it does with UseServerSidePrepare=0 or a cursor type other than forward-only.

Versions up to and including psqlODBC 18.00.0006 are affected.
title: SQL injection with BIG5 aliases and the JOHAB, EUC_TW, EUC_CN and EUC_KR client encodings

desc:

A remote client that sends a query string or request body with many pairs to an application parsing it with parse_urlencoded can corrupt memory and crash the process.
title: WWW::Form::UrlEncoded::XS versions before 0.28 for Perl write past the end of the Perl argument stack when parse_urlencoded returns many pairs

desc:
The ITE it51xxx I2C driver, when operating as an I2C target (slave) in buffer mode (CONFIG_I2C_TARGET + CONFIG_I2C_TARGET_BUFFER_MODE), transmits response data from the fixed-size data->target_out_buffer inside its target FIFO interrupt handler target_i2c_isr_fifo() in drivers/i2c/i2c_ite_it51xxx.c. On every data interrupt of a host read transaction the handler pushes a fixed 16 bytes from target_out_buffer[i + data->r_index] into the hardware FIFO and then advances data->r_index by 16, without ever checking that index against the size of the buffer.

data->r_index is reset to zero only on a STOP or timeout condition, so within a single transaction it only accumulates. An I2C host that keeps clocking read bytes without issuing STOP drives data->r_index past the end of the buffer after sixteen interrupts (default CONFIG_I2C_TARGET_IT51XXX_MAX_BUF_SIZE = 256 bytes), and every interrupt after that reads 16 bytes from beyond target_out_buffer and places them on the bus. What follows the buffer in the driver's device data structure is data->target_shared_fifo and the remaining static device state, so a sufficiently long read transaction streams adjacent firmware memory to the host.

The same handler, and the shared-FIFO arm of target_i2c_isr_pio(), also declare the transfer length uninitialised and invoke the optional buf_read_requested() callback without checking that it is registered. A target that supplies no read callback leaves the source pointer NULL and the length indeterminate; when that length compares below the destination size, memcpy() runs with a NULL source. Because the transmit path feeds the FIFO whether or not the callback provided data, such a target also places whatever the previous request left in the buffer onto the bus.

The trigger is a malicious or misbehaving I2C master on the same bus (for example a compromised application processor or a rogue device on an exposed I2C bus); no software privilege on the victim is required and the handler runs in the target's kernel/firmware context. The disclosed bytes are not attacker-chosen, but their extent is: the host controls how long the transaction runs and therefore how far past the buffer the driver reads.

This is the read-direction counterpart of CVE-2026-14986, which closed the write direction of the same routine without adding the matching bound on the read path.
title: Out-of-bounds read in it51xxx I2C target FIFO ISR on oversized read transaction
