desc: AutoGPT is a workflow automation platform for creating, deploying, and managing continuous artificial intelligence agents. In versions 0.6.5 through 0.10.0, marketplace and shared agents can capture a user's saved SMTP or database login. SendEmailBlock and SQLQueryBlock logged in with the running user's saved SMTP or database credential to whatever server the graph's author put in the node's inputs, with no check that the login belonged to that server. Anyone who publishes a marketplace listing or shares an agent file can capture the saved login of each user who adds it to their library and runs it once, in plaintext. This issue is fixed in version 0.11.0.
title: AutoGPT: Shared and marketplace agents can leak saved SMTP or database logins

desc:
When sftpEnabled=true (the default configuration in etc/org.apache.karaf.shell.cfg), the SSH server exposes the karaf.base directory tree through the MINA SSHD SFTP subsystem and SCP command factory without verifying the authenticated user's roles beyond the initial sshRole login check. Consequently, an authenticated user with only low-privileged roles (such as viewer and ssh) can read sensitive configuration and key files (including etc/users.properties and etc/host.key) or write arbitrary bundles/configurations into monitored directories (such as deploy/ or etc/), leading to privilege escalation and arbitrary code execution.


Apache Karaf 4.4.13 and 4.5.0 introduce the sftpRole configuration property in org.apache.karaf.shell (defaulting to admin) and enforce role-based access control on SFTP subsystem creation, SCP command execution, and virtual filesystem access.

Mitigation / WorkaroundUsers are recommended to upgrade to Apache Karaf 4.4.13 or 4.5.0.




On earlier versions where SFTP/SCP access is not required, set sftpEnabled=false in etc/org.apache.karaf.shell.cfg and restart the SSH server bundle (or Karaf instance).
title: Apache Karaf: SFTP SCP file transfer on the SSH port bypasses the command ACL entirely

desc: AutoGPT is a workflow automation platform for creating, deploying, and managing continuous artificial intelligence agents. In versions 0.6.41 through 0.11.1, the OAuth provider endpoints check a calling application's client secret against a scrypt hash synchronously on the REST API event loop. Anyone who knows the client ID of an active confidential OAuth application can stall the REST API for all users by sending a stream of requests with a wrong secret. No account or token is required. This issue is fixed in version 0.11.2.
title: AutoGPT: Any user with an active OAuth app's client ID can stall the REST API by sending wrong client secrets

desc:
A vulnerability in Apache Jena Fuseki allows SERVICE operations to bypass restrictions on administration operations.

Users are recommended to upgrade to version 6.3.0, which fixes the issue.
title: Apache Jena Fuseki: SERVICE bypasses localhost-only administration controls

desc: Joomla Extension - regularlabs.com - PHP code injection via content inserted during article preparation in Sourcerer extension < 18.0.0 - Sourcerer decided whether PHP may run based on the author or last editor of the host article and applied that decision to complete code blocks that other extensions, such as Users Anywhere, inserted into the article while it was prepared. A user able to edit a value rendered by such an extension, for example the display name in their own user profile, could therefore have PHP executed in the context of a trusted article. Sourcerer 18.0.0 authorizes each executable block against its own source; Users Anywhere 3.1.0, ReReplacer 16.4.0 and Snippets 11.2.0 supply the source information needed to keep executing eligible saved content.
title: Joomla Extension - regularlabs.com - PHP code injection via content inserted during article preparation in Sourcerer extension < 18.0.0

desc: AutoGPT is a workflow automation platform for creating, deploying, and managing continuous artificial intelligence agents. In versions 0.6.67 to 0.11.2, organization and team billing-manager roles intended only for spend management are treated as ordinary members across workflow, run, library, and marketplace routes. Although the role matrix in autogpt_platform/autogpt_libs/autogpt_libs/auth/permissions.py withholds run access and workflow creation, those routes do not enforce the matrix and their underlying membership lookups ignore the caller's role. As a result, a team billing manager can read team workflows and other members' runs (including inputs, outputs, and per-node data), while an organization billing manager can view shared workflows and runs and create workflows and marketplace listings; neither can modify or delete other members' workflows. This issue is fixed in version 0.11.3.

desc: InDesign Desktop is affected by a Divide By Zero vulnerability that could result in an application denial-of-service. An attacker could exploit this vulnerability to crash the application, leading to a denial-of-service condition. Exploitation of this issue requires user interaction in that a victim must open a malicious file.
title: InDesign Desktop | Divide By Zero (CWE-369)

desc:
Parallels Desktop inittool2 Link Following Local Privilege Escalation Vulnerability. This vulnerability allows local attackers to escalate privileges on affected installations of Parallels Desktop. An attacker must first obtain the ability to execute low-privileged code on the target host system in order to exploit this vulnerability.

The specific flaw exists within the inittool2 component. By creating a symbolic link, an attacker can abuse the component to take ownership of critical folders. An attacker can leverage this vulnerability to escalate privileges and execute arbitrary code in the context of root on the host system. Was ZDI-CAN-30268.
title: Parallels Desktop inittool2 Link Following Local Privilege Escalation Vulnerability

desc:
Parallels Desktop Handle-based Rename Time-Of-Check Time-Of-Use Information Disclosure Vulnerability. This vulnerability allows local attackers to disclose sensitive information on affected installations of Parallels Desktop. An attacker must first obtain the ability to execute low-privileged code on the target guest system in order to exploit this vulnerability.

The specific flaw exists within the implementation of handle-based rename functionality. The issue results from the lack of proper locking when performing operations on an object. An attacker can leverage this vulnerability to disclose information in the context of the current user on the host system. Was ZDI-CAN-30608.
title: Parallels Desktop Handle-based Rename Time-Of-Check Time-Of-Use Information Disclosure Vulnerability

desc:
Parallels Desktop CSHAShellExt Improper Access Control Local Privilege Escalation Vulnerability. This vulnerability allows local attackers to escalate privileges on affected installations of Parallels Desktop. An attacker must first obtain the ability to execute low-privileged code on the target guest system in order to exploit this vulnerability.

The specific flaw exists within the CSHAShellExt component. The issue results from improper access control. An attacker can leverage this vulnerability to escalate privileges and execute arbitrary code in the context of the hypervisor. Was ZDI-CAN-30030.
title: Parallels Desktop CSHAShellExt Improper Access Control Local Privilege Escalation Vulnerability

desc: Joomla! Core - [20261101] - Core - Improper ACL checks in webservice endpoints in Joomla 4.0.0-5.4.10, 6.0.0-6.2.0 - Read actions on webservice endpoints did not require a dedicated permission, allowing API users to read content they are not allowed to see in other application contexts.
title: Joomla! Core - [20261101] - Core - Improper ACL checks in webservice endpoints in Joomla 4.0.0-5.4.10, 6.0.0-6.2.0

desc: Joomla! Core - [20261102] - Core - Improper ACL checks in com_newsfeeds delete action in Joomla 1.6.0-5.4.10, 6.0.0-6.2.0 - An improper access check allows users without delete permission on a category to delete trashed newsfeeds.

Failure to sanitize special elements into a different plane (special element injection) in Azure App Service allows an unauthorized attacker to elevate privileges over a network.

Dell PowerStore contains a weak password-storage vulnerability that could allow an attacker with access to the credential store to recover user passwords by offline brute force.

desc: Genetec Security Center can expose access control unit credentials in plain text in server log files when specific non-default logging options are enabled. An attacker with local access to the affected log files could retrieve and use these credentials.

Allot's Subscriber Management Platform (SMP) v18.3.53 stores sensitive configuration credentials protected by a product‑wide, hard‑coded master password. The master key is constructed using a hard-coded string value plus a default key value. This results in an effective encryption key that is recoverable from shipped scripts and configuration files. The platform uses a deprecated and cryptographically insecure algorithm (PBEWithMD5AndDES) and no documented mechanism exists to change the key. An attacker with read access to configuration files, backups, or diagnostic bundles can recover credentials and TLS keystore/truststore passwords, and access to subscriber-management operations and subscriber PII.
title: CVE-2026-136271

desc: UWAS before 0.11.16 contains a WAF bypass vulnerability in the isAPContentType() function within internal/middleware/security.go that allows unauthenticated attackers to evade SQL injection, XSS, and shell/RCE body pattern detection by setting the Content-Type header to application/json, multipart/form-data, or other exempted types. Attackers can relabel the Content-Type of malicious requests to skip WAF body scanning entirely, causing the unfiltered payload to pass through byte-for-byte to the backend application without being logged as a WAF event.
title: UWAS before 0.11.16 WAF Body-Scan Bypass via Content-Type

desc: GPAC through 26.07.0 contains a heap out-of-bounds read vulnerability in gf_rtp_parse_mpeg4 that allows remote attackers to crash clients by sending MP4V-ES RTP payloads shorter than 4 bytes. A remote RTP sender or malicious RTSP server can send a short packet after a marker-bit packet, causing an unsigned wraparound in the VOP start-code search loop that reads past the buffer and causes denial of service.
title: GPAC through 26.07.0 Heap Out-of-Bounds Read via gf_rtp_parse_mpeg4

desc: GPAC through 26.07.0 contains an integer underflow vulnerability in gf_rtp_parse_mpeg4 that allows remote attackers to trigger excessive looping by advertising an undersized AU-headers-length. Attackers can send a crafted 22-byte AAC-hbr RTP packet from an RTP sender or malicious RTSP server to run about 2^28 iterations, pinning a CPU core and stalling clients.
title: GPAC through 26.07.0 Integer Underflow DoS via gf_rtp_parse_mpeg4

desc: Assimp 6.0.0 through 6.0.6 contains an invalid mesh reference vulnerability in glTF2Exporter::ExportMeshes that causes out-of-bounds access when meshes without faces are skipped during export. Attackers can supply a PLY point cloud or degenerate glTF 2.0 TRIANGLE_STRIP model exported to gltf2 or glb2 to crash the application or trigger out-of-bounds memory reads and writes.
title: Assimp 6.0.0 through 6.0.6 Out-of-Bounds Access via glTF2Exporter::ExportMeshes

desc: Assimp through 6.0.6 contains an out-of-bounds read vulnerability in the glTF 1.0 importer that allows attackers to read adjacent heap memory by supplying an unchecked KHR_binary_glTF image bufferView. Attackers can craft a glTF or GLB file whose bufferView byteOffset or byteLength exceeds its buffer, disclosing heap memory through embedded texture data or crashing the process.
title: Assimp through 6.0.6 Out-of-Bounds Read via glTF::Image::Read KHR_binary_glTF bufferView

desc: libical before 4.0.7 contains a denial of service vulnerability because icalparser_clean() does not reset the parser nesting level when reusing an icalparser. Attackers can submit a single malformed calendar with unclosed or mismatched BEGIN/END lines, causing later calendars to be silently dropped and memory to grow unbounded.
title: libical before 4.0.7 Denial of Service via icalparser_clean() Nesting Level

desc: Schmitech ORBIT before 2.17.15 contains an improper authorization vulnerability in the permission_or_api_key dependency that allows any valid API key to access /admin management routes. Attackers holding a chat inference API key can read other keys in plaintext, rewrite config.yaml, and manage adapters and prompts to take over server administration.
title: Schmitech ORBIT before 2.17.15 Improper Authorization via Admin Routes API Key

desc: GPAC through 26.07.0 contains an infinite loop vulnerability in gf_rtsp_do_deinterleave that allows malicious RTSP servers to hang clients by sending non-RTSP, non-interleaved data. Attackers can answer a client request with a few bytes not starting with '$', 'RTSP', or 'HTTP', causing the RTSP client thread to spin forever and consume a full CPU core.
title: GPAC through 26.07.0 Infinite Loop in gf_rtsp_do_deinterleave via RTSP Data

desc: GPAC through 26.07.0 contains a heap out-of-bounds read vulnerability in the STAP-A handling of gf_rtp_parse_h264 in rtp_depacketizer.c due to unchecked aggregation unit sizes. A malicious RTP sender or RTSP server can send STAP-A packets with oversized NAL unit lengths to disclose adjacent heap memory or crash the client.
title: GPAC through 26.07.0 Heap Out-of-Bounds Read via gf_rtp_parse_h264 STAP-A

desc: GPAC through 26.07.0 contains an infinite loop vulnerability in SDP_ParseAttribute that allows attackers to cause unbounded memory growth via a NUL byte in an a=fmtp line. Attackers can supply a crafted .sdp file or malicious RTSP DESCRIBE response to hang gf_sdp_info_parse and exhaust memory, causing denial of service.
title: GPAC through 26.07.0 Infinite Loop DoS via SDP_ParseAttribute fmtp Parsing

desc: RayLabsHQ gitea-mirror before 3.38.1 contains an authorization bypass vulnerability in the /api/sso/providers handlers that allows any authenticated user to access other users' SSO providers without ownership checks. Attackers can read every OIDC client secret in clear text and overwrite or delete providers, redirecting authorization and token endpoints to attacker-controlled servers.
title: RayLabsHQ gitea-mirror before 3.38.1 Authorization Bypass via SSO Provider API

desc: GPAC through 26.07.0 contains a heap out-of-bounds read vulnerability in gf_rtp_parse_amr that allows remote RTP senders or malicious RTSP servers to read beyond packet buffers by sending crafted AMR/AMR-WB payloads. Attackers can send short packets whose TOC entries all set the F bit, causing out-of-bounds frame data to be copied into decoder output, disclosing memory or crashing the client.
title: GPAC through 26.07.0 Heap Out-of-Bounds Read via gf_rtp_parse_amr

desc: compose-farm 0.19.0 before 1.22.0 contains a cross-site WebSocket hijacking and cross-site request forgery vulnerability because its unauthenticated web UI performs no Origin validation. Malicious websites visited by users can open /ws/shell/{host} or /ws/exec sockets, or abuse unquoted service parameters and PUT /api/console/file, to execute commands on all managed hosts.
title: compose-farm 0.19.0 before 1.22.0 Cross-Site WebSocket Hijacking RCE via Web UI

desc: plugNmeet-server before 2.5.3 contains an authorization flaw in PollsController.HandleUserSubmitResponse that allows authenticated room participants to submit poll votes as other users by supplying an arbitrary UserId. Attackers can set UserId to another participant's id to cast votes on their behalf or block their legitimate votes, manipulating poll results.
title: plugNmeet-server before 2.5.3 Poll Vote Spoofing via /api/polls/submitResponse

desc: Spug 4.0.0 before 4.1.1 contains an OS command injection vulnerability that allows any authenticated user to execute commands by supplying a crafted git URL to the /api/credential/check/ endpoint. Attackers can inject shell metacharacters into the data field passed to git ls-remote with shell=True, executing commands as the Spug service account, which is root in Docker deployments.
title: Spug 4.0.0 before 4.1.1 OS Command Injection via Credential Check Endpoint

desc: Mercur @mercurjs/core before 2.3.2 contains a missing object-level authorization vulnerability that allows authenticated vendors to access other sellers by substituting the :id path parameter. Attackers can read payment and tax details, overwrite profiles and addresses, and invite, remove, or re-role team members to take over another vendor's store.
title: Mercur @mercurjs/core before 2.3.2 Missing Authorization via /vendor/sellers/:id

desc: Spug before 4.1.1 contains an information disclosure vulnerability that allows authenticated non-administrator users to read per-host SSH private keys through the GET /api/host/ endpoint. Users granted a host can read the cleartext pkey field returned by Host.to_view and log in directly over SSH, bypassing Spug's permissions and audit trail even after revocation.
title: Spug before 4.1.1 SSH Private Key Disclosure via Host API

desc: Prismor before 1.57.0 contains a wildcard CORS misconfiguration and missing authentication in its local HTTP API that allows remote attackers to overwrite security policies via cross-origin requests. Attackers can lure a developer to a malicious page that sends PUT requests to /api/policy/global or /api/policy/project, disabling AI agent guardrails and reading session and event data.
title: Prismor before 1.57.0 Cross-Site Policy Overwrite via Wildcard CORS Local API

desc: RayLabsHQ gitea-mirror before 3.38.1 contains a server-side request forgery vulnerability that allows unauthenticated attackers to make the server send HTTP requests by supplying a url to /api/gitea/test-connection or /api/github/test-connection. Attackers can target internal network services and cloud instance metadata endpoints, reading response content leaked through upstream error messages returned by httpGet.
title: gitea-mirror before 3.38.1 Unauthenticated SSRF via Connection Test Endpoints

desc: Movary before 0.78.0 contains a server-side request forgery vulnerability that allows authenticated non-admin users to make the server request internal hosts by submitting crafted Jellyfin or Plex server URLs. Attackers can target internal services directly since URL validation is disabled by default, or bypass it via DNS rebinding, redirects, or AAAA records to probe internal network state.
title: Movary before 0.78.0 Authenticated SSRF via Jellyfin and Plex Server URL Endpoints

desc: HarnessRouter 0.4.2 before 0.32.2 contains an open redirect vulnerability in the self-hosted sign-in UI that allows unauthenticated attackers to redirect users via the unvalidated next query parameter. Attackers can send crafted login links with an external, protocol-relative, or backslash-prefixed next value so victims are sent to attacker sites after signing in, enabling phishing.
title: HarnessRouter 0.4.2 before 0.32.2 Open Redirect via next Parameter

desc: Endurain before 0.20.0 contains a missing authentication vulnerability in the PUT /api/v1/strava/link endpoint that allows unauthenticated attackers to modify Strava integrations using only a victim's strava_state value. Attackers can submit a leaked state with their own OAuth code to link an attacker-controlled Strava account, or an invalid code to remove the victim's integration.
title: Endurain before 0.20.0 Missing Authentication in Strava OAuth Link Endpoint

desc: EpicStaff 1.2.0 before 1.3.1 contains an insecure direct object reference vulnerability in DocumentViewSet download and copy endpoints that allows authenticated users to access other organizations' documents. Attackers holding Knowledge Sources permissions in one organization can enumerate sequential document IDs to download or copy foreign documents, or insert documents into another organization's collection.
title: EpicStaff 1.2.0 before 1.3.1 IDOR via Document Download and Copy Endpoints

desc: cnpmcore 3.46.0 before 3.84.3 and 4.0.0 before 4.37.3 contains an information disclosure vulnerability that allows unauthenticated attackers to obtain upstream registry authTokens via the GET /-/registry endpoints lacking AdminAccess middleware. Attackers can request /-/registry or /-/registry/:id and replay the leaked authToken as a Bearer credential to enumerate, download, or publish packages upstream.
title: cnpmcore 3.46.0 before 3.84.3 and 4.0.0 before 4.37.3 Registry authToken Disclosure

desc: A security vulnerability has been detected in D-Link R95 101B06. Affected by this issue is the function GetBluetoothAdapterSettings/GetBluetoothBloodPressure/GetBluetoothDeviceList/GetBluetoothScanDeviceList/SetBluetoothAdapterSettings/SetBluetoothUnpairDevice/SetTriggerBluetoothScan/SetBluetoothPairDevice of the file /bin/ssi of the component DHMAPI SOAP Handler. desc: A vulnerability was detected in Panabit Smart Application Gateway TANGr7p10. This affects an unknown part of the file /cgi-bin/dashboard/ajax_chart_dump. The manipulation of the argument isntmeye results in os command injection. The attack can be launched remotely. The exploit is now public and may be used. desc: A weakness has been identified in D-Link DIR-X1860 4.5.2. Affected by this vulnerability is an unknown functionality of the file /usr/sbin/anweb. Executing a manipulation can lead to os command injection. It is possible to launch the attack remotely. The exploit has been made available to the public and could be used for attacks.
