desc: Frappe ERPNext 11.0.0-beta before 15.121.4 contains a missing authorization vulnerability that allows authenticated users to read POS Profile cashier lists by calling a POS endpoint lacking record permission checks. Attackers, including portal users or users with no roles, can send crafted requests naming out-of-scope POS Profiles to retrieve their cashier data.
title: Frappe ERPNext 11.0.0-beta before 15.121.4 Missing Authorization in POS Profile Cashiers Endpoint

desc: Frappe ERPNext 8.0.0 before 15.123.0 and 16.0.0 before 16.51.0 contains a missing authorization vulnerability in a Stock module endpoint that allows authenticated users to read restricted warehouse data. Attackers with a common operational role can send crafted requests naming warehouses excluded by their User Permissions to obtain stock quantities and stock values.
title: Frappe ERPNext 8.0.0 before 15.123.0 and 16.0.0 before 16.51.0 Missing Authorization in Stock Module Endpoint

desc: Frappe ERPNext 13.0.0 before 15.122.0 and 16.x before 16.50.0 contains a missing authorization vulnerability in an Accounts module endpoint that returns Bank Transaction metadata of other companies without checking whether the caller may read the requested records. Authenticated attackers, including portal users or users with no assigned roles, can send crafted requests naming out-of-scope records to retrieve that metadata.
title: Frappe ERPNext 13.0.0 before 15.122.0 Missing Authorization in Accounts Bank Transactions Endpoint

desc: Frappe ERPNext 11.0.0-beta before 15.124.0 and 16.x before 16.52.0 contains an authorization flaw in the customer portal Issue list, which scopes records differently from the detail view and skips permission checks on requested records. Authenticated users, including portal users without roles, can send crafted requests naming out-of-scope records to read other customers' Issues.
title: Frappe ERPNext 11.0.0-beta before 15.124.0 Unauthorized Issue Access via Customer Portal

desc: Frappe ERPNext 5.0.0 before 15.122.0 and 16.x before 16.50.0 contains a missing authorization vulnerability in a Projects module endpoint that returns employee costing and billing rates without record-level permission checks. Authenticated users, including portal users or users without roles, can send crafted requests naming out-of-scope records to read other employees' activity cost rates.
title: Frappe ERPNext 5.0.0 before 15.122.0 Missing Authorization in Projects Activity Cost Rates

desc: Frappe ERPNext 15.0.0 before 15.122.0 and 16.x before 16.50.0 contains a missing authorization vulnerability in a Stock module endpoint that returns Serial No and Batch ledger entries without checking whether the caller may read the requested records. Authenticated attackers, including portal users or users without roles, can send crafted requests naming out-of-scope records to obtain item codes, quantities, warehouses, batch and serial numbers.
title: Frappe ERPNext 15.0.0 before 15.122.0 Missing Authorization in Stock Serial No and Batch Ledger

desc: Frappe ERPNext 15.94.2 before 15.122.0 and 16.x before 16.50.0 contains an incorrect authorization vulnerability in a supplier portal endpoint whose party identity check ignores party type, failing to distinguish a Customer and a Supplier that share a name. Authenticated users, including portal users or users with no assigned roles, can send crafted requests naming records outside their permitted scope to read buying-portal records.
title: ERPNext 15.94.2 before 15.122.0 Unauthorized Supplier Portal Record Access via Party Name Collision

desc: Frappe ERPNext 16.0.1 before 16.50.0 contains a missing authorization vulnerability in a Stock dashboard chart endpoint that returns site-wide stock value when the caller has no permitted warehouse. Authenticated users with common operational roles can send crafted requests naming records outside their scope to read stock value data beyond their permissions.
title: Frappe ERPNext 16.0.1 before 16.50.0 Missing Authorization in Stock Dashboard Chart

desc: Frappe ERPNext 15.87.0 before 15.121.4 and 16.x before 16.36.0 contains a missing authorization vulnerability in an Accounts module endpoint that changes Period Closing Voucher job status without permission checks and accepts a request method triggerable cross-site. Authenticated users without an Accounts role, or cross-site pages opened by authenticated users, can send requests naming a scheduled job to stop accounting jobs from completing.
title: Frappe ERPNext 15.87.0 before 15.121.4 Missing Authorization in Period Closing Voucher Status

desc: Frappe ERPNext 8.11.1 before 15.124.0 and 16.x before 16.52.0 is missing an authorization check in print and portal views, which fail to apply desk users' User Permissions to customer documents. Authenticated desk users with an ordinary job role can send crafted requests naming records outside their permitted scope to read documents of customers their User Permissions exclude.
title: Frappe ERPNext 8.11.1 before 15.124.0 Unauthorized Document Access via Print and Portal Views

desc: Frappe ERPNext 7.0.0 before 15.124.0 and 16.x before 16.52.0 contains a missing authorization vulnerability in the customer portal Projects list, which returns every field without checking permission on the requested records. Authenticated users, including portal users or users with no assigned roles, can send crafted requests naming out-of-scope records to read project costing and margin data.
title: Frappe ERPNext 7.0.0 before 15.124.0 Unauthorized Project Costing Access via Customer Portal

desc: Frappe ERPNext 13.49.0 before 14.0.0, 14.17.2 before 15.124.0, and 16.x before 16.52.0 contains a missing authorization vulnerability in a Selling module endpoint that returns Sales Order line items without checking whether the caller may read the requested records. Authenticated attackers, including portal users or users with no assigned roles, can send crafted requests naming out-of-scope Sales Orders to read their line item data.
title: Frappe ERPNext 13.49.0 before 14.0.0 and 14.17.2 before 15.124.0 Missing Authorization in Selling Module Sales Order Items

desc: Frappe ERPNext 15.10.4 before 15.122.0 and 16.x before 16.50.0 contains a missing authorization vulnerability in a Stock module endpoint that checks whether an inventory number exists and creates missing Serial No and Batch master records without verifying create permission. Authenticated users can send a crafted request with a new number to create these records outside their role, affecting inventory data integrity.
title: Frappe ERPNext 15.10.4 before 15.122.0 Missing Authorization in Stock Module Record Creation

desc: Frappe ERPNext 6.3.0 before 15.124.0 and 16.x before 16.52.0 contains a missing authorization vulnerability in the customer and supplier portal list endpoint, which returns complete selling documents and RFQs without checking permission on the requested records. Authenticated attackers, including portal users or users without roles, can request out-of-scope records to read valuation, margin, and other bidder details.
title: Frappe ERPNext 6.3.0 before 15.124.0 Missing Authorization in Customer and Supplier Portals

desc: Frappe ERPNext 15.0.0 before 15.122.0 and 16.x before 16.50.0 contains a missing validation vulnerability in a Stock module endpoint that fails to verify reserved item rows belong to the target Sales Order. Authenticated users with the Stock User role can send crafted reservation requests naming another order's item row to reserve stock beyond that order's limits, creating mismatched Stock Reservation Entries.
title: Frappe ERPNext 15.0.0 before 15.122.0 Stock Reservation Validation Bypass

desc: Frappe ERPNext 14.44.0 before 15.122.0 and 16.x before 16.50.0 contains a missing authorization vulnerability in the Accounts module's payment unreconciliation endpoint, which does not check the caller's permission on the vouchers it unreconciles. Authenticated users with the Accounts User role can send crafted Unreconcile Payment requests naming vouchers from other companies or outside their User Permissions to remove their reconciliation.
title: ERPNext 14.44.0 before 15.122.0 Missing Authorization in Accounts Payment Unreconciliation

desc: Frappe ERPNext 13.0.0 before 15.122.0 and 16.x before 16.50.0 contains a missing authorization vulnerability in an Accounts module endpoint that reconciles Bank Transactions against caller-named vouchers, checking permission only on the Bank Transaction and not on each voucher. Authenticated users with the Accounts User role who can edit a Bank Transaction can send crafted requests naming vouchers outside their permitted scope to change the reconciliation state of vouchers belonging to other companies or outside their User Permissions.
title: Frappe ERPNext 13.0.0 before 15.122.0 Missing Authorization in Bank Reconciliation

desc: Frappe ERPNext 13.0.0 before 15.122.0 and 16.x before 16.50.0 contains a missing authorization vulnerability in an Accounts module endpoint that returns Bank Transaction amounts and bank accounts without checking whether the caller may read the requested records. Authenticated users with a common operational role can send crafted requests naming out-of-scope records to read Bank Transaction data of other companies.
title: Frappe ERPNext 13.0.0 before 15.122.0 Missing Authorization in Accounts Module Bank Transactions

desc: Frappe ERPNext 10.1.41 before 15.122.0 and 16.x before 16.50.0 contains a missing authorization vulnerability in a Manufacturing module endpoint that replaces BOMs without checking whether the caller may modify either BOM or the affected assemblies. Authenticated users who can create a BOM Update Log can send a crafted request naming two BOMs to replace the first with the second in every assembly site-wide.
title: Frappe ERPNext 10.1.41 before 15.122.0 Missing Authorization in Manufacturing BOM Replacement

desc: Frappe ERPNext 12.0.0 before 15.121.4 and 16.x before 16.36.0 contains a missing authorization vulnerability in an Accounts module dashboard chart source that returns account balance history without checking chart or account permissions. Authenticated attackers, including portal users or users with no roles, can send crafted requests naming any account to read general ledger balance history of any company.
title: Frappe ERPNext 12.0.0 before 15.121.4 Missing Authorization in Accounts Dashboard Chart

desc: Frappe ERPNext 6.18.0 before 15.124.0 and 16.x before 16.52.0 contains a missing authorization vulnerability in Payment Requests that lets authenticated Accounts User role holders read source documents they lack permission to access. Attackers can create a Payment Request through the generic record interface that references another company's document, then email its loaded content to an address they choose.
title: Frappe ERPNext 6.18.0 before 15.124.0 Unauthorized Document Access via Payment Requests

desc: Frappe ERPNext 13.0.0 before 15.122.0 and 16.x before 16.50.0 contains a missing authorization vulnerability in the make_merge_log endpoint that allows authenticated users to read POS Invoice data. Attackers can supply POS Invoice names outside their permitted scope to retrieve each invoice's customer, posting date, and grand total.
title: Frappe ERPNext 13.0.0 before 15.122.0 Missing Authorization in POS Invoice Merge Log Endpoint

desc: Frappe ERPNext 15.111.0 before 15.121.4 and 16.22.0 before 16.36.0 contains a missing authorization vulnerability in an Accounts module endpoint that returns item rows of a caller-named inter-company invoice or order and accepts a caller-supplied document type without checking read permission. Authenticated attackers, including portal users or users with no roles, can send crafted requests naming another company's document to read Sales Invoice, Purchase Invoice and order items.
title: Frappe ERPNext 15.111.0 before 15.121.4 Missing Authorization in Accounts Inter-Company Items Endpoint

desc: Frappe ERPNext 12.2.0 before 15.122.0 and 16.x before 16.50.0 contains a missing authorization vulnerability in an Assets module endpoint that returns Asset details without checking whether the caller may read the requested records. Authenticated attackers, including portal users or users with no assigned roles, can send crafted requests naming records outside their permitted scope to read restricted asset details.
title: Frappe ERPNext 12.2.0 before 15.122.0 Missing Authorization in Assets Module

desc: Frappe ERPNext 14.0.0 before 15.124.0 and 16.x before 16.52.0 contains a stored cross-site scripting vulnerability in the CRM module because notes on Leads and Opportunities are saved without passing through the HTML sanitiser. Authenticated users with the Sales User role can save a note containing a crafted payload that executes in another user's session when they open the record, acting with that user's permissions.
title: Frappe ERPNext 14.0.0 before 15.124.0 Stored XSS via CRM Notes

desc: Frappe ERPNext 8.2.5 before 15.121.4 and 16.x before 16.36.0 contains an incorrect authorization vulnerability in Manufacturing module endpoints that check only document-type write access, not permission on each Work Order. Authenticated users restricted by User Permissions can send crafted requests naming another company's Work Order to stop, resume or close it.
title: Frappe ERPNext 8.2.5 before 15.121.4 Missing Authorization in Manufacturing Work Order Endpoints

desc: Frappe ERPNext 5.0.0 before 15.121.4 and 16.x before 16.36.0 contains an incorrect authorization vulnerability in the Buying module: the endpoint that closes and reopens Purchase Orders checks only document-type write permission, not per-document User Permissions. Authenticated users with Purchase Order write access can send crafted requests naming another company's Purchase Order to change its status.
title: Frappe ERPNext 5.0.0 before 15.121.4 Missing Authorization in Purchase Order Close Endpoint

desc: Frappe ERPNext 14.47.0 before 15.122.0 and 16.x before 16.50.0 contains a missing authorization vulnerability in the Accounts module where a method on accounting vouchers creates and submits Repost Accounting Ledger documents with permission checks skipped. Authenticated users with read access to a Sales Invoice, Purchase Invoice, Payment Entry, Journal Entry, or Purchase Receipt can call it to delete and repost that voucher's General Ledger entries, an action restricted to System Managers.
title: Frappe ERPNext 14.47.0 before 15.122.0 Missing Authorization in Repost Accounting Ledger

desc: Frappe ERPNext 6.3.0 before 15.122.0 and 16.x before 16.50.0 contains a missing authorization vulnerability in an Accounts module endpoint used to choose a Tax Rule, which returns party address details without permission checks. Authenticated attackers, including portal users or users with no roles, can send crafted requests naming arbitrary customers, suppliers, or Addresses to obtain their city, state, postal code, and country.
title: Frappe ERPNext 6.3.0 before 15.122.0 Unauthorized Address Access via Tax Rule Endpoint

desc: Frappe ERPNext 5.0.0 before 15.121.4 and 16.x before 16.36.0 contains an incorrect authorization vulnerability in a Selling module endpoint that checks only document-type write permission, not permission on each Sales Order, when closing or reopening Sales Orders. Authenticated users restricted by User Permissions can send crafted requests naming another company's Sales Order to close or reopen it outside their restriction.
title: Frappe ERPNext 5.0.0 before 15.121.4 Missing Authorization in Selling Module Sales Orders

desc: Frappe ERPNext 13.0.0 before 15.124.2 and 16.x before 16.53.0 contains a missing authorization vulnerability in a Stock module endpoint that returns item cost data without checking the caller's permissions on the item, company, or warehouse. Authenticated attackers, including portal users or users restricted to other warehouses, can send crafted requests naming out-of-scope items, companies, or warehouses to obtain valuation rates and average purchase costs.
title: Frappe ERPNext 13.0.0 before 15.124.2 Missing Authorization in Stock Module Cost Endpoint

desc: Frappe ERPNext 13.0.0 before 15.124.0 and 16.x before 16.52.0 contains an incorrect authorization vulnerability in an Accounts module endpoint that returns Payment Entries for a readable bank record without checking read permission on each Payment Entry. Authenticated users with an Accounts role can request a readable record to obtain metadata of Payment Entries excluded by their user permissions, such as Cost Center restrictions.
title: Frappe ERPNext 13.0.0 before 15.124.0 Missing Authorization in Accounts Payment Entries

desc: Frappe ERPNext 7.1.0 before 15.121.0 and 16.x before 16.34.0 contains a missing authorization vulnerability in Projects module endpoints that return Timesheet data without restricting results to records the caller may read. Any authenticated user, including one with no assigned roles, can send crafted requests to read organisation-wide Timesheet work and billing details.
title: Frappe ERPNext 7.1.0 before 15.121.0 Missing Authorization in Projects Module Timesheet Endpoints

desc: Frappe ERPNext 11.0.0-beta before 15.122.0 and 16.x before 16.34.0 contains a missing authorization vulnerability in an Accounts module endpoint that returns the subscription plans linked to a caller-named invoice without checking read permission on that invoice. Authenticated attackers can send crafted requests naming invoices outside their permitted scope to learn whether they belong to subscriptions and read the billed plans.
title: Frappe ERPNext 11.0.0-beta before 15.122.0 Missing Authorization in Accounts Invoice Subscription Endpoint

desc: Frappe ERPNext 15.0.0 before 15.124.0 and 16.x before 16.52.0 contains a missing authorization vulnerability in Assets module endpoints that return a depreciation schedule for a caller-supplied asset without checking read permission on that asset. Authenticated users can name another company's asset to disclose its purchase value, value after depreciation, and depreciation entries.
title: Frappe ERPNext 15.0.0 before 15.124.0 Missing Authorization in Assets Depreciation Endpoints

desc: Frappe ERPNext 12.7.0 before 15.124.0 and 16.x before 16.52.0 stores imported Italian supplier e-invoices as public files in the Regional module, which the server returns without authentication. Unauthenticated attackers can request predictable file URLs built from the supplier's VAT number and invoice sequence to read supplier names, VAT numbers, bank account details and line items.
title: Frappe ERPNext 12.7.0 before 15.124.0 Information Disclosure via Public Supplier E-Invoice Files

desc: Frappe Framework before 15.120.1 and 16.x before 16.33.1 contains a path traversal vulnerability in file attachment handling that permits arbitrary file read. Authenticated attackers holding a single ordinary role without write permissions can abuse attachment handling to read server files outside the application boundary.
title: Frappe Framework before 16.33.1 Authenticated Arbitrary File Read via File Attachment Handling

desc: Frappe 8.8.0 before 16.30.0 contains an insecure direct object reference vulnerability in the SMS Settings get_contact_number API that lets attackers read any Contact's phone numbers without permission checks. Attackers can call the endpoint, which uses an uncorrelated EXISTS subquery, to retrieve mobile_no and phone values of arbitrary Contact records, exposing PII.
title: Frappe 8.8.0 before 16.30.0 IDOR via SMS Settings get_contact_number API

desc: Frappe ERPNext 14.0.0 before 15.121.0 and 16.x before 16.34.0 contains a missing authorization vulnerability in a Utilities module endpoint that lets any authenticated user retry failed bulk transactions without a role check. Attackers, including portal users with no roles, can send crafted requests for a chosen date to mark site-wide failed bulk transactions as retried, removing them from the normal recovery path, and add background job load.
title: Frappe ERPNext 14.0.0 before 15.121.0 Missing Authorization in Bulk Transaction Retry

desc: Frappe ERPNext 4.3.0 before 15.121.6 and 16.x before 16.37.0 contains an SQL injection vulnerability in an endpoint of the Selling and Buying modules, where a request value validated early can be overridden by caller-supplied data that reaches a database query unvalidated. Any authenticated user, including a portal user with no roles, can send crafted requests to extract sensitive data, including active session data, and take over other accounts such as administrators.
title: Frappe ERPNext 4.3.0 before 15.121.6 SQL Injection in Selling and Buying Modules

desc: pypdf 3.7.1 before 7.0.0 contains an information disclosure vulnerability that allows attackers to guess placeholders in encrypted templated documents by analyzing file identifiers. Attackers with a document sharing the same template and access to other documents' file identifiers can recover placeholder contents from encrypted PDFs.
title: pypdf 3.7.1 before 7.0.0 Placeholder Recovery via File Identifier in Encrypted Documents

desc: pypdf before 7.0.0 contains a resource exhaustion vulnerability that allows attackers to cause large memory usage by supplying crafted PDF cross-reference streams. Attackers can craft a PDF whose cross-reference stream offsets all point to one large object, exhausting memory in applications parsing the file.
title: pypdf before 7.0.0 Memory Exhaustion via Cross-Reference Streams with Identical Offsets

desc: pypdf 2.4.2 before 7.0.0 contains a resource exhaustion vulnerability in its handling of XFA forms that allows attackers to cause excessive memory consumption. Attackers can supply a crafted PDF containing XFA forms with many small fields so that loading the forms consumes large amounts of memory, causing a denial of service.
title: pypdf 2.4.2 before 7.0.0 Excessive Memory Usage via XFA Forms

desc: AzuraCast before 0.24.1 fails to escape backslashes in Liquidsoap annotation values, allowing media managers to break out of quoted annotation strings. Attackers can set a crafted ID3 title ending in a backslash to inject a process: protocol URI, achieving OS command execution in the Liquidsoap container during playback.
title: AzuraCast before 0.24.1 OS Command Injection via Liquidsoap Annotation Values

desc: Coder 2.6.0 before 2.29.21, 2.30.0 before 2.34.10, 2.35.0 before 2.35.8, 2.36.0 before 2.36.5, and 2.37.0 before 2.37.1 contains a denial of service vulnerability in the workspace agent dRPC API, whose handlers dereference unset request sub-messages and unconfigured Tailnet providers without recovering from panics. Attackers holding a workspace agent token can send UpdateLifecycle, UpdateStartup, or BatchUpdateMetadata messages lacking sub-messages, or call RefreshResumeToken or WorkspaceUpdates, to repeatedly crash coderd.
title: Coder 2.37.0 before 2.37.1 Denial of Service via Agent RPC Calls

desc: Coder 2.32.0 before 2.34.17, 2.35.0 before 2.36.12, 2.37.0 before 2.37.9, and 2.38.0 before 2.38.5 contain a symlink-following flaw in the Coder Agents read_skill_file tool, which validates skill file paths lexically but follows symlinks outside the skill directory. Attackers who place a malicious skill containing a symlinked supporting file in a victim's workspace can leak other workspace files into the model context and chat history when the victim runs a chat using that skill.
title: Coder 2.38.0 before 2.38.5 Symlink Path Traversal via read_skill_file

desc: Heym before 0.0.148 passes Playwright navigate-step URLs to page.goto() without validating the scheme and runs step-based scripts inside the backend container. A signed-in user who can run workflows can navigate to file:// URLs and use getText to read known-path files such as the Kubernetes ServiceAccount token or Docker secrets.
title: Heym before 0.0.148 Local File Read via Playwright Navigate Step

desc: Coder 2.6.0 before 2.29.26, 2.30.0 before 2.34.18, 2.35.0 before 2.37.10, and 2.38.0 before 2.38.6 contains a cross-site request forgery vulnerability because CSRF exemption patterns in coderd/httpmw/csrf.go are matched as unanchored regular expressions, letting affected API routes skip CSRF token and same-origin checks. Attackers controlling a page same-site with the deployment can make signed-in users' browsers send forged POST requests that recreate dev containers or add users whose names contain derp to organizations.
title: Coder from 2.38.0 before 2.38.6 CSRF Bypass via Unanchored Exemption Patterns

desc: AzuraCast 0.19.0 before 0.24.1 contains an improper authorization vulnerability that allows users with station media rights to add tracks to other stations' playlists by supplying foreign playlist ids to the single-file edit endpoint. Attackers can send sequential playlist ids in the playlists array to inject entries into other stations' AutoDJ rotations and public now-playing metadata, causing failed playback slots.
title: AzuraCast 0.19.0 before 0.24.1 Cross-Station Playlist Injection via Media Edit Endpoint

desc: Rclone from 1.51.0 before 1.76.0 contains an authentication bypass vulnerability in serve sftp --auth-proxy because the generateCacheKey cache key omits the authentication method. Attackers knowing a victim's base64 public key can submit it as a password from the same client IP to reuse the cached entry and gain read-write VFS access.
title: Rclone 1.51.0 before 1.76.0 Authentication Bypass via serve sftp Auth-Proxy Cache

desc: rclone before 1.76.0 leaks credentials in its swift, netstorage and seafile backends, which follow HTTP redirects using Go's default policy: swift and netstorage send auth headers or passwords on cross-host or HTTPS-to-HTTP redirects, and seafile sends API tokens or passwords on same-host HTTPS-to-HTTP redirects. Attackers receiving or observing a redirect issued by the configured endpoint can capture these credentials to access storage or replay signed requests.
title: rclone before 1.76.0 Credential Leak via Swift, NetStorage and Seafile Redirects

desc: rclone from 1.59.0 before 1.76.0 contains a confinement escape in the local backend's setXattr function that lets attackers write user.* extended attributes outside the destination root via a planted symlink. Attackers who plant a symlink to an outside directory with a pre-existing child can use --links --metadata operations to set attacker-chosen user.* xattrs on files outside the destination.
title: rclone 1.59.0 before 1.76.0 Symlink Escape via Extended Attribute Metadata Write

desc: Rclone 1.49.0 before 1.76.0 contains an improper authentication vulnerability in Proxy.Call that lets revoked users keep access because cached auth-proxy answers are never revalidated. Revoked users of serve sftp, ftp, http, or webdav can reconnect within five minutes using their original credentials to retain access indefinitely.
title: Rclone 1.49.0 before 1.76.0 Auth-Proxy Revocation Bypass via Cached Credentials

desc: AzuraCast before 0.24.1 contains an improper authorization vulnerability in the /api/station/{station_id}/profile/edit endpoint that exposes and accepts Icecast/Shoutcast passwords for users holding Manage Station Profile without Manage Station Broadcasting. Authenticated station users can read the admin, source, relay and streamer passwords via GET to administer Icecast or broadcast to listeners, or overwrite them via PUT to lock out operators.
title: AzuraCast before 0.24.1 Icecast Password Exposure via profile/edit Endpoint

desc: actix-http 3.0.0 before 3.20.3 contains a denial of service vulnerability that allows unauthenticated remote attackers to exhaust memory by sending large-window brotli request bodies. Attackers can send an 850-byte body with Content-Encoding: br declaring a 2^30 window, forcing about 1 GiB of decoder allocation per request and OOM-killing servers.
title: actix-http 3.0.0 before 3.20.3 Denial of Service via Large-Window Brotli Decompression

desc: actix-files before 0.7.4 contains an information disclosure vulnerability that allows remote unauthenticated attackers to read hidden files by requesting Windows 8.3 short-name aliases. Attackers can request short names like ENV~1 or GIT~1/config to bypass the leading-dot check in actix_files::Files and retrieve .env secrets and .git contents.
title: actix-files before 0.7.4 Hidden File Disclosure via Windows 8.3 Short Names

desc: Rclone from 1.56.0 before 1.76.0 contains a timing side-channel vulnerability in its htpasswd authentication middleware that allows unauthenticated attackers to enumerate valid usernames. Attackers can send HTTP Basic Auth requests with wrong passwords and measure response times, because bcrypt verification runs only for existing users, enabling targeted password guessing.
title: Rclone from 1.56.0 before 1.76.0 Username Enumeration via htpasswd Timing Oracle

desc: Rclone from 1.46.0 before 1.76.0 contains a memory exhaustion vulnerability in the remote control server that allows unauthenticated clients to crash rclone by sending oversized JSON bodies. Attackers can POST large JSON payloads to protected RC methods, which handlePost decodes before authorization checks, triggering out-of-memory termination and interrupting transfers.
title: Rclone from 1.46.0 before 1.76.0 Denial of Service via RC JSON Requests

desc: rclone 1.67.0 before 1.76.0 contains a credential leak vulnerability in the Ulozto backend that sends X-Auth-Token and X-User-Token headers to unintended hosts on HTTP redirect because downloads use the authenticated f.rest client instead of f.cdn. Attackers who can observe or redirect CDN download traffic can capture the long-lived API key and session token to gain persistent access to the victim's Ulozto storage.
title: rclone 1.67.0 before 1.76.0 Auth Token Leak via Ulozto Backend Redirect

desc: actix-http 3.18.10 before 3.20.2 contains an HTTP request smuggling vulnerability in its chunked decoder, which treats a bare LF after the last chunk as the start of a trailer section. Attackers can send a body ending in 0\r\n\n through a connection-reusing proxy so the next request's body is parsed as new requests, bypassing WAF or upstream protections.
title: actix-http 3.18.10 before 3.20.2 HTTP Request Smuggling via Chunked Transfer-Encoding Decoder

desc: ArcadeDB 26.2.1 before 26.11.1 contains an observable response discrepancy in MCPToolUtils.resolveDatabase, which checks database existence before authorization and returns distinct 'not authorized' and 'does not exist' errors; separately, a failed Bolt LOGON from READY leaves the previous principal bound after RESET. Authenticated MCP callers can enumerate names of databases they are not granted by probing tools such as query or get_schema.
title: ArcadeDB 26.2.1 before 26.11.1 Database Enumeration via MCP Tools and Bolt LOGON Flaw

desc: ArcadeDB 21.10.1 before 26.11.1 contains a resource-limit bypass vulnerability that allows restricted users to evade per-group readTimeout because limits are applied to shared cached statements and plans. Attackers can run SQL text previously cached by an unrestricted principal to skip timeouts, or impose their own timeout and limit on root and other users.
title: ArcadeDB 21.10.1 before 26.11.1 readTimeout Bypass via Shared Statement and Plan Cache

desc: ArcadeDB 25.8.1 before 26.11.1 contains an incorrect authorization vulnerability because per-type ACLs are keyed by type name, renames are not propagated to the permission configuration, and requestAccessOnType allows unknown type names by default. Authenticated users holding only updateSchema can run ALTER TYPE NAME on a denied type to gain read, DELETE and TRUNCATE access, immediately for TIMESERIES types and after the next security rebuild for record-backed types.
title: ArcadeDB 25.8.1 before 26.11.1 Per-Type ACL Bypass via ALTER TYPE Rename

desc: ArcadeDB from 26.11.1-SNAPSHOT before 26.11.1 contains an authorization bypass vulnerability that allows authenticated users to skip per-type ACL checks when a database is opened on demand. Attackers can send the first POST /api/v1/batch/{database} request to a closed database to read and write types they are not entitled to access.
title: ArcadeDB from 26.11.1-SNAPSHOT before 26.11.1 Authorization Bypass via Batch Endpoint

desc: ArcadeDB from 26.7.1 before 26.11.1 contains an information disclosure vulnerability because LSMTreeFullTextIndex computes BM25 corpus statistics over all buckets of the indexed type, ignoring bucket access control on subtypes. Authenticated users with read access to a supertype but not its subtype can run EXPLAIN or PROFILE on full-text queries and read totalDocs and per-term df values to count hidden subtype documents containing chosen terms.
title: ArcadeDB 26.7.1 before 26.11.1 Information Disclosure via Full-Text BM25 Statistics

desc: ArcadeDB native-image server builds 26.8.1 before 26.11.1 contain an authorization bypass vulnerability that allows authenticated clients to perform writes through read-only query paths by nesting statements in SELECT. Missing reflection metadata leaves SqlAstInspector with an empty AST, letting INSERT in projections or LET clauses persist via the query endpoint, MCP read-only mode, and HA follower routing.
title: ArcadeDB 26.8.1 before 26.11.1 Native-Image Read-Only Bypass via Nested SELECT Writes

desc: better-auth from 0.8.1-beta.5 before 1.7.16 and 1.8.0-beta.0 before 1.8.0-beta.5, and @better-auth/passkey from 1.6.25 before 1.7.16 and 1.8.0-beta.0 before 1.8.0-beta.5, let revoked sessions stay valid because secondary storage session lists are updated non-atomically and some routes trust cookie-cached sessions. An attacker holding a valid session can evade bulk revocation or bans, or use a revoked cached session to register a passkey or create a lasting session.
title: better-auth before 1.7.16 Session Revocation Bypass via Secondary Storage and Cookie Cache

desc: better-auth 0.4.12-beta.7 before 1.7.16 and 1.8.0-beta.0 before 1.8.0-beta.5 contains an improper authentication vulnerability in the phone number plugin that lets sign-up and other flows save unverified phone numbers, which phone OTP sign-in then uses to select the account. Attackers can attach a victim's number to an attacker-controlled account so the victim's valid OTP sign-in yields a session for that account, exposing data the victim then enters.
title: better-auth 0.4.12-beta.7 before 1.7.16 Unverified Phone Number Account Takeover

desc: ArcadeDB 26.3.1 before 26.11.1 contains a read-only bypass vulnerability that allows server administrators to commit writes through the MCP read-only query tool by submitting Groovy-fallback Gremlin scripts. GremlinQueryEngine.analyze() evaluates scripts like Graph API addVertex calls on the auto or groovy engine and classifies them as READ, persisting writes the read-only restriction should refuse.
title: ArcadeDB 26.3.1 before 26.11.1 MCP Read-Only Bypass via Gremlin Groovy Analysis

desc: ArcadeDB before 26.11.1 contains an authorization bypass vulnerability that allows authenticated users to read schema definitions of denied types through listings ignoring per-type ACLs. Attackers can query the PostgreSQL wire catalog, GraphQL introspection, or MCP get_schema to reveal property names, indexes, inheritance, and materialized view SQL.
title: ArcadeDB before 26.11.1 Schema Information Disclosure via Per-Type ACL Bypass

desc: @better-auth/passkey 1.4.0-beta.16 before 1.7.16 and 1.8.0-beta.0 before 1.8.0-beta.5, and the passkey plugin in better-auth 1.2.0-beta.18 before 1.4.0, do not confirm WebAuthn user verification when userVerification is "required" and take the expected origin from the request instead of configuration. Users can register or use passkeys without the required PIN or biometric check, and passkey responses created on another origin under the same relying party ID may be accepted.
title: @better-auth/passkey before 1.7.16 Improper Origin and User Verification Enforcement

desc: ArcadeDB before 26.11.1 contains a denial of service vulnerability in the Redis protocol handler, which neither replies to nor closes a pre-authentication connection when it receives an array whose first element is not a string. Unauthenticated attackers can resend such an array just within the 30-second socket idle timeout to hold connections open indefinitely and exhaust RedisNetworkExecutor threads.
title: ArcadeDB before 26.11.1 Unauthenticated Redis Connection Hold Denial of Service

desc: Better Auth (better-auth, @better-auth/kysely-adapter, and @better-auth/drizzle-adapter) before 1.7.16 and 1.8.0-beta.0 before 1.8.0-beta.5 contains a race condition with MySQL or MariaDB serial IDs because the inserted row's ID is read via a separate LAST_INSERT_ID() query that may run on a different pooled connection. Under concurrent load, a user signing in can receive another user's session and act as that user.
title: Better Auth before 1.7.16 and 1.8.0-beta.0 before 1.8.0-beta.5 Session Mix-Up via MySQL Serial IDs

desc: better-auth 1.4.0 before 1.7.16 and 1.8.0-beta.0 before 1.8.0-beta.5 contains an improper authentication vulnerability because email-change links record the old and new addresses but not the requesting user. Attackers can open a still-valid link issued for their own account after a victim registers the attacker's released old address, gaining a session and changing the victim's email to one they control.
title: better-auth 1.4.0 before 1.7.16 Account Takeover via Email-Change Links

desc: @better-auth/electron 1.5.0-beta.12 before 1.7.16 and 1.8.0-beta.0 before 1.8.0-beta.5 accepts any validly signed value as its transfer cookie and returns the full endpoint context, including the auth secret and social provider client secrets, in sign-in responses. Authenticated users can obtain these secrets to forge sessions as other users. Attackers knowing a password can exchange desktop authorization codes issued before two-factor verification to bypass the second factor.
title: @better-auth/electron before 1.7.16 Auth Secret Disclosure and Two-Factor Bypass

desc: better-auth 1.5.5 before 1.7.16 and 1.8.0-beta.0 before 1.8.0-beta.5 contains a privilege escalation vulnerability in the organization plugin, where the creator role check compares the raw invitation role string while later checks trim it. Admins or other non-creator roles that can invite can submit a padded role such as " owner" that becomes owner on acceptance, allowing deletion of the organization and removal of original owners.
title: better-auth 1.5.5 before 1.7.16 Privilege Escalation via Padded Invitation Role

desc: @better-auth/stripe 1.2.0-beta.18 before 1.7.16 and 1.8.0-beta.0 before 1.8.0-beta.5 contains an authorization bypass vulnerability because the stripeCustomerId user field accepts values from sign-up and update-user requests, letting a user replace their own Stripe customer ID with another customer's. Attackers who know another customer's Stripe ID can open that customer's billing portal to view invoices and billing details, change payment methods, and cancel or modify subscriptions.
title: @better-auth/stripe before 1.7.16 Authorization Bypass via stripeCustomerId Mass Assignment

desc: better-auth 1.3.7 before 1.7.16 and 1.8.0-beta.0 before 1.8.0-beta.5 contains a race condition in the emailOTP plugin attempt counter, collision-prone email change code keys, and accent-insensitive email lookups. Unauthenticated attackers can send concurrent guesses exceeding allowedAttempts to brute-force OTPs and sign in or reset passwords, signed-in users can verify addresses they do not own, and attackers receiving mail at accent-variant addresses can reset victims' passwords.
title: better-auth from 1.3.7 before 1.7.16 Email OTP Race Condition and Authentication Bypass

desc: better-auth 1.3.0 before 1.7.16 and 1.8.0-beta.0 before 1.8.0-beta.5 contains an incorrect authorization vulnerability in the admin plugin's /admin/update-user endpoint that lets roles holding user:update change another user's phoneNumber and phoneNumberVerified fields. Attackers can set their own verified phone number on a higher-privileged account and sign in via phone OTP to take it over.
title: better-auth 1.3.0 before 1.7.16 Privilege Escalation via admin update-user Phone Number

desc: Better Auth 0.4.9 before 1.7.16 and 1.8.0-beta.0 before 1.8.0-beta.5 contains an OAuth sign-in authentication flaw that treats unverified provider emails as verified, including string "false" email_verified claims, unchecked generic OAuth profile/ID-token subject mismatches, and ignored Zoom provider options. Attackers holding a victim's address unverified at an affected provider can sign in, link to the victim's local account, and obtain its session.
title: Better Auth 0.4.9 before 1.7.16 OAuth Unverified Email Account Takeover

desc: SurrealDB from 3.2.0 before 3.3.4 contains an authorization bypass vulnerability that allows record users to update protected rows by exploiting table-level PERMISSIONS FOR update predicates referencing COMPUTED fields. Because check_update_permissions evaluates the predicate before computed fields are populated, the field reads as NONE and deny-intended predicates like blocked != true pass, letting attackers modify records.
title: SurrealDB 3.2.0 before 3.3.4 Authorization Bypass via COMPUTED Field Permissions

desc: SurrealDB before 4.0.0 contains a guard bypass vulnerability that allows authenticated users to execute write subqueries by embedding them in LIVE query WHERE clauses or field projections. Attackers can inject CREATE, UPDATE, DELETE, or RELATE statements that run atomically inside other users' triggering transactions, amplifying writes and exfiltrating document data after permission revocation.
title: SurrealDB before 4.0.0 Write-Blocking Guard Bypass via LIVE Query Expressions

desc: SurrealKV before 1.1.0 contains an out-of-bounds read vulnerability in the safe InternalKeyRef::from_encoded constructor, which only checks key length with a debug-only assertion. Callers passing keys shorter than 16 bytes, or crafted or corrupted SSTable blocks, trigger unchecked length underflow in timestamp(), seq_num() and trailer(), reading heap bytes before the allocation or panicking.
title: SurrealKV before 1.1.0 Out-of-Bounds Read via InternalKeyRef Decoder

desc: SurrealDB before 4.0.0 contains an incorrect authorization vulnerability in filter_fields_by_permission that allows authenticated record users to read denied child field values. Attackers can query rows where overlapping items[*] and items[*].secret permissions compact arrays, causing shifted elements to retain field values denied by SELECT permissions.
title: SurrealDB before 4.0.0 Field Permission Bypass via Wildcard Array-Index Drift

desc: SurrealDB 1.0.0 before 4.0.0 contains an authorization bypass vulnerability that allows authenticated users to shadow protected $access, $auth, and $token variables by binding them as FOR loop variables. Attackers can wrap queries in nested FOR loops with forged values to satisfy table permission predicates, enabling unauthorized reads, modifications, or deletions as a VIEWER.
title: SurrealDB 1.0.0 before 4.0.0 Authorization Bypass via FOR Loop Variable Shadowing

desc: SurrealDB 3.0.0 before 4.0.0 contains a permission bypass vulnerability that allows authenticated low-privilege database users to read restricted records by calling the GET /export endpoint. Attackers can export raw records that skip table SELECT predicates and field-level SELECT permissions, exposing other users' rows and hidden fields.
title: SurrealDB 3.0.0 before 4.0.0 Permission Bypass via /export Endpoint

desc: SurrealDB 1.0.0 before 4.0.0 contains a denial of service vulnerability that allows any user able to run queries to crash the server by triggering unchecked decimal overflow in math::sum or math::product. Attackers can submit a query summing or multiplying large decimal literals or aggregate stored decimals with GROUP ALL, causing a rust_decimal panic that terminates the entire server process.
title: SurrealDB 1.0.0 before 4.0.0 DoS via Decimal Overflow in math::sum and math::product

desc: SurrealDB 3.1.0 before 4.0.0 contains an SQL injection vulnerability in its Model Context Protocol (MCP) server because the identifier validator (consume_backtick_ident and validate_identifier) treats the first backtick as the closing delimiter, ignoring escape characters that the SurrealQL parser honors. Attackers can supply MCP tool arguments containing an escaped backtick to break out of the quoted identifier and execute arbitrary SurrealQL statements.
title: SurrealDB 3.1.0 before 4.0.0 SQL Injection via MCP Tool Identifier Escaped Backticks

desc: SurrealDB 3.0.0 before 4.0.0 contains a path traversal vulnerability in its bucket storage layer on Windows, where ObjectKey::check_no_traversal splits object keys only on forward slashes while FileStore::to_os_path treats backslashes as directory separators. Attackers can supply object keys such as /..\bucket2\secret to bypass the traversal check and read or modify files in other buckets.
title: SurrealDB 3.0.0 before 4.0.0 Path Traversal via Windows Backslashes in Bucket Keys

desc: SurrealDB 3.0.0 before 4.0.0 contains a path traversal vulnerability in direct filesystem buckets because BucketController::check_permission evaluates key-based ACLs against the un-normalized object key, while FileStore::to_os_path collapses '..' sequences without a traversal check. An authenticated tenant permitted only for certain keys can supply a key such as /public/../private/confidential.txt to read, write, or delete arbitrary files within the storage root.
title: SurrealDB 3.0.0 before 4.0.0 Path Traversal in Direct Filesystem Buckets

desc: SurrealDB 3.0.4 before 4.0.0 does not apply operator-configured WebSocket frame, message, and buffer size limits to the GraphQL WebSocket upgrade handler at GET /graphql, falling back to permissive library defaults. Unauthenticated remote attackers who supply the target namespace and database in request headers can hold up to 64 MiB of in-flight data per concurrent connection, exhausting server memory and degrading availability.
title: SurrealDB 3.0.4 before 4.0.0 Memory Exhaustion via GraphQL WebSocket Upgrade

desc: SurrealDB from 2.2.0 before 4.0.0 contains an authorization bypass vulnerability in Document::purge_references that lets authenticated users bypass target table PERMISSIONS by triggering REFERENCE ON DELETE cascades. Attackers can delete a referenced record to delete, unset, or run CUSTOM expressions on referencing records despite PERMISSIONS FOR delete or update NONE.
title: SurrealDB 2.2.0 before 4.0.0 Permission Bypass via REFERENCE ON DELETE Cascade

desc: SurrealDB 3.0.0 before 4.0.0 contains an authorization bypass that allows users with the read-only VIEWER role to modify database schema, because CREATE on a nonexistent table implicitly defines it without the DEFINE TABLE permission check applied to explicit definitions. Authenticated VIEWER users can issue CREATE statements in non-STRICT databases to add arbitrary empty SCHEMALESS tables, cluttering schemas or colliding with application table names.
title: SurrealDB 3.0.0 before 4.0.0 VIEWER Role Authorization Bypass via Implicit Table Creation

desc: SurrealDB 3.0.0 before 4.0.0 contains an authorization bypass vulnerability that allows clients with table write access to persist writes refused by THROWing table events within interactive transactions. Attackers can run a guarded statement via RPC begin and query, ignore the returned error, and commit to persist the record and event side effects.
title: SurrealDB 3.0.0 before 4.0.0 Event THROW Guard Bypass via Interactive Transactions

desc: SurrealDB 2.2.0 before 4.0.0 includes the record id of a referencing row in the error returned when a delete is blocked by an ON DELETE REJECT reference, without checking the caller's SELECT permission on that row. An authenticated principal with DELETE permission can attempt to delete a referenced record and read the rejection error to learn the existence and exact ids of referencing records hidden by row-level SELECT permissions.
title: SurrealDB 2.2.0 before 4.0.0 Information Disclosure via ON DELETE REJECT Errors

desc: SurrealDB 1.0.0 before 4.0.0 contains a capability check bypass in its embedded JavaScript scripting engine, where the surrealdb.functions bridge calls the internal fnc::synchronous() and fnc::asynchronous() dispatchers without enforcing function capability checks. Authenticated users denied access to built-in functions in SurrealQL can execute them by calling them through surrealdb.functions from embedded JavaScript.
title: SurrealDB 1.0.0 before 4.0.0 Function Capability Bypass via JavaScript Built-in Bridge

desc: SurrealDB 1.0.0 before 4.0.0 prints SURREAL_PASS and SURREAL_TOKEN environment variable values in clear text in the --help and -h output of CLI commands such as surreal start, sql, import, export, and mcp, because the arguments do not set clap's hide_env_values. Anyone who later sees that terminal output, for example in shell logs, CI logs, or screen shares, can obtain root database credentials.
title: SurrealDB 1.0.0 before 4.0.0 Credential Disclosure via CLI Help Output

desc: OpenRemote core before 1.34.0 contains an authentication bypass vulnerability in UserAssetProvisioningMQTTHandler that allows unauthenticated attackers to impersonate provisioned devices without proof of private key possession. Attackers can publish a known device's public certificate to the provisioning request topic, authenticating their anonymous MQTT connection as the device's service account to read and modify assets.
title: OpenRemote before 1.34.0 Authentication Bypass via X.509 MQTT Provisioning

desc: SurrealDB 3.0.0 before 4.0.0 contains a path traversal vulnerability in its filesystem storage bucket that only canonicalizes the bucket root, not descendant symlinks. Attackers can reference paths through a pre-existing symlink inside the bucket that pass the lexical prefix check, reading and writing files across the host filesystem.
title: SurrealDB 3.0.0 before 4.0.0 Path Traversal via Filesystem Bucket Symlinks

desc: Vikunja from 0.20.5 before 2.8.0 contains a login cross-site request forgery vulnerability in the OpenID Connect callback in OpenIdAuth.vue that accepts a valueless state parameter. Attackers can send a crafted callback link with an empty state and their own authorization code to silently log victims into the attacker's account and view the victims' entered data.
title: Vikunja from 0.20.5 before 2.8.0 Login CSRF via OIDC Callback State Check

desc: Vikunja from 2.2.0 before 2.8.0 contains an information disclosure vulnerability that allows authenticated users to read other users' private projects through the tasks.overdue webhook payload. Attackers can register a personal tasks.overdue webhook with one subscribed overdue task, then receive project titles, descriptions, and owner IDs from other users' reminders at external URLs.
title: Vikunja 2.2.0 before 2.8.0 Information Disclosure via tasks.overdue Webhook Payload

desc: Vikunja from 0.14.0 before 2.8.0 contains a mass assignment vulnerability that allows authenticated users to set json-hidden fields by sending XML request bodies to the v1 API. Attackers can set BackgroundFileID on project creation to download any stored file via the background endpoint, or create bots with IsAdmin set to gain instance-admin access.
title: Vikunja 0.14.0 before 2.8.0 Arbitrary File Read and Privilege Escalation via XML Binding

desc: Vikunja from 1.0.0 before 2.8.0 contains an account takeover vulnerability that allows attackers to hijack SSO identities by planting local accounts with unverified victim emails. When emailfallback is enabled, attackers register or edit a local account using the victim's email, causing the victim's first OIDC login to link into the attacker-controlled account and expose their data.
title: Vikunja from 1.0.0 before 2.8.0 Account Takeover via OIDC Email Fallback

desc: OpenRemote from 1.2.0 before 1.34.0 contains an authorization bypass vulnerability in AlarmFacade that allows restricted users with write:rules to create alarms for assets outside their ruleset subtree. Attackers can deploy a JSON asset-scoped ruleset using target.custom asset ids to create HIGH severity alarms and trigger operator notifications about arbitrary in-realm assets.
title: OpenRemote 1.2.0 before 1.34.0 Authorization Bypass via AlarmFacade

desc: Vikunja 0.17.0 before 2.8.0 builds the task.deleted notification and webhook payload, including related tasks, with the deleting user's permissions and sends it to all project subscribers without per-recipient authorization checks. A user subscribed to a project, or owning its webhook, receives full data of related tasks in private projects they cannot read when a task in their project is deleted.
title: Vikunja 0.17.0 before 2.8.0 Information Disclosure via task.deleted Webhook Payload

desc: Vikunja from 0.8.0 before 2.8.0 contains a denial of service vulnerability that allows authenticated project readers to amplify response size by repeating requested properties in CalDAV PROPFIND requests. Attackers can send PROPFIND requests to the dav projects endpoint with hundreds of duplicate calendar-data properties to exhaust server memory, CPU, and bandwidth.
title: Vikunja 0.8.0 before 2.8.0 Denial of Service via CalDAV PROPFIND Duplicate Properties

desc: Vikunja from 0.16.0 before 2.8.0 contains an information disclosure vulnerability that writes users' Trello API tokens to application logs and Sentry by formatting provider errors verbatim in listeners.go. When a Trello migration fails with a transport error, the URL error embeds the token query parameter, letting anyone with log or telemetry access obtain the reusable third-party credential.
title: Vikunja 0.16.0 before 2.8.0 Trello API Token Exposure via Migration Logs

desc: Vikunja from 2.6.0 before 2.8.0 contains a resource exhaustion vulnerability in the Planka migration converter that multiplies task allocations for duplicate list IDs. Attackers controlling a Planka server can return boards with duplicate list IDs and many cards to exhaust memory and OOM-kill the Vikunja process.
title: Vikunja from 2.6.0 before 2.8.0 Denial of Service via Planka Migration

desc: Vikunja 2.3.0 before 2.8.0 contains an uncontrolled memory allocation in the CSV migration module because it does not de-duplicate label column mappings or cap labels per row, and enforces the item limit only after the full import is built. Authenticated users can send one request to /api/v2/migration/csv/migrate with repeated label mappings or many labels per row, exhausting memory until the server is OOM-killed.
title: Vikunja 2.3.0 before 2.8.0 Denial of Service via CSV Import Label Mappings

desc: Vikunja from 2.2.1 before 2.8.0 contains a TOTP replay protection bypass in ValidateTOTPPasscode that allows attackers to reuse consumed codes by padding them with whitespace. Attackers with valid credentials who observe a used passcode can resubmit it whitespace-padded to the login API within the validity window to obtain a session token.
title: Vikunja from 2.2.1 before 2.8.0 TOTP Replay Protection Bypass via Whitespace

desc: Vikunja from 0.21.0 before 2.8.0 contains a denial of service vulnerability that allows authenticated users to exhaust memory and CPU by creating tasks with many reminders and long titles. Attackers can store a task whose ParseAlarms rendering in pkg/caldav/caldav.go uses quadratic string concatenation, causing every CalDAV read, including other members' automatic syncs, to allocate gigabytes.
title: Vikunja 0.21.0 before 2.8.0 Denial of Service via CalDAV VALARM Rendering

desc: Vikunja from 0.18.0 before 2.8.0 contains a resource amplification vulnerability in pkg/models/export.go that allows authenticated users to exhaust server memory by exporting heavily related tasks. Attackers can relate many tasks to one task with a large description and request a user export, causing an out-of-memory crash for all users.
title: Vikunja 0.18.0 before 2.8.0 Denial of Service via User Export Amplification

desc: Vikunja from 1.0.0 before 2.8.0 contains a memory exhaustion vulnerability that allows authenticated users to crash the server by uploading extreme-width images as task attachments. Attackers can request the attachment preview endpoint so Lanczos resampling allocates width-proportional weight tables, OOM-killing the process repeatedly with sub-megabyte PNGs.
title: Vikunja from 1.0.0 before 2.8.0 Denial of Service via Attachment Preview Resizing

desc: Vikunja from 0.9.0 before 2.8.0 contains an information disclosure vulnerability that allows project admins to view share creators' email addresses via the link share list endpoint. Attackers with admin permission can request the project shares endpoint and read the shared_by email field, exposing addresses of creators including former project members.
title: Vikunja 0.9.0 before 2.8.0 Email Disclosure via Project Link Share List

desc: Vikunja from 0.21.0 before 2.8.0 contains a resource exhaustion vulnerability that allows authenticated users to trigger instance-wide database writes by setting a project position below 0.1. Attackers can repeatedly send PUT requests to /api/v2/projects/{id} so recalculateProjectPositions updates every user's root projects, holding SQLite's write lock and degrading availability.
title: Vikunja 0.21.0 before 2.8.0 Denial of Service via Project Position Recalculation

desc: Vikunja from 0.19.0 before 2.8.0 contains a denial of service vulnerability that allows authenticated CalDAV users to exhaust server CPU by uploading VTODO properties with many parameters. Attackers can PUT an iCalendar body with thousands of parameters on one line to any valid project ID, triggering superlinear parsing before permission checks.
title: Vikunja 0.19.0 before 2.8.0 CalDAV VTODO Parameter CPU Denial of Service

desc: Admidio before 5.0.18 contains an insecure direct object reference vulnerability in mylist.php that loads list configurations by the list_uuid parameter while checking only the organization, not the owner or private flag. Authenticated users with Lists module access who know a victim's list UUID can read its name, selected profile fields, sort order and filter conditions.
title: Admidio 5.0.17 IDOR in mylist.php Exposes Private List Configurations

desc: Admidio 5.0.0 before 5.0.18 contains a stored cross-site scripting vulnerability that allows role administrators to inject JavaScript by placing quote-breaking payloads in role names rendered unencoded in the data-message attribute in modules/profile/roles_functions.php. Attackers can execute scripts when a full administrator views an affected profile page, stealing the CSRF token to assign themselves the Administrator role.
title: Admidio 5.0.0 before 5.0.18 Stored XSS via Role Name in Profile View

desc: Vikunja from 2.4.0 before 2.8.0 contains a denial of service vulnerability in the richtext converter that allows authenticated project writers to exhaust server memory and CPU by storing tables with unbounded rowspan and colspan values. Any project reader or CalDAV client can trigger the expansion through markdown task reads, CalDAV GETs, or the frontend editor, producing 100 MB responses from a 64-byte description.
title: Vikunja 2.4.0 before 2.8.0 Denial of Service via Unbounded Table Rowspan/Colspan

desc: Admidio from 5.0.2 before 5.0.17 contains an arbitrary file read vulnerability that allows any logged-in member to read server files by placing local paths in img src attributes of eCard messages. Attackers can send an eCard to their own account so sendEcard() embeds files like adm_my_files/config.php via addEmbeddedImage(), disclosing database credentials and /etc/passwd.
title: Admidio 5.0.2 before 5.0.17 Arbitrary File Read via eCard Message img src

desc: Admidio 5.0.0 before 5.0.18 contains an improper authorization vulnerability in modules/profile/profile_new.php that allows authenticated Group Leaders to bypass field-level profile restrictions. Attackers can request mode=html_selection to read restricted field values and submit mode=save requests to modify restricted member profile fields.
title: Admidio 5.0.0 before 5.0.18 Authorization Bypass via Bulk Profile Edit in profile_new.php

desc: Vikunja from 0.19.0 before 2.8.0 contains a denial of service vulnerability that allows authenticated users to exhaust CPU by supplying unbounded business-day operands in datemath filters. Attackers can send task or time-tracking filters like due_date > now+999999999999b, triggering a per-day loop in go-datemath that pins CPU cores and exhausts the server.
title: Vikunja 0.19.0 before 2.8.0 Denial of Service via Datemath Business-Day Filter

desc: Admidio from 5.0.17 before 5.0.18 contains a stored cross-site scripting vulnerability that allows authenticated users to inject JavaScript by saving a crafted value in their STREET profile field. Attackers can break out of the unencoded title attribute in members_assignment_data.php with an onmouseover handler that executes in the session of role managers hovering over the address icon.
title: Admidio 5.0.17 Stored XSS via Street Field in Role Member Assignment

desc: Admidio before 5.0.18 contains an insufficient session expiration vulnerability that allows attackers to keep account access after a forgot-password reset because User::setPassword() deletes sessions using the visitor ID instead of the reset user's usr_id. Attackers already holding a victim's session or remember-me cookie can continue using it after the victim resets the password, keeping authenticated access to the account.
title: Admidio before 5.0.18 Insufficient Session Expiration After Password Reset

desc: Admidio 5.0.0 before 5.0.18 contains a path traversal vulnerability in the Documents & Files renameFile() action that allows authenticated users with folder upload rights to move files outside adm_my_files by supplying ../ sequences in adm_new_name. Attackers can relocate an uploaded SVG containing script to the web root, where it is served inline and executes stored cross-site scripting against administrators for account takeover.
title: Admidio 5.0.0 before 5.0.18 Path Traversal to Stored XSS via File Rename

desc: Admidio from 5.0.16 before 5.0.18 contains a stored cross-site scripting vulnerability that allows users with folder upload rights to store JavaScript by uploading SVG files served inline. Attackers can upload a script-bearing SVG that downloadFile() serves as image/svg+xml inline without nosniff or CSP, executing on the Admidio origin for viewers including unauthenticated visitors.
title: Admidio 5.0.16 before 5.0.18 Stored XSS via SVG Upload in Documents & Files

desc: Admidio from 5.0.0 before 5.0.18 contains a path traversal vulnerability in DocumentsService::renameFile() that allows authenticated users to move files outside adm_my_files by supplying an unvalidated adm_new_name value. Attackers with folder upload permission can submit ../ sequences to file_rename_save to write files and create directories in arbitrary writable locations, including the web root.
title: Admidio 5.0.0 before 5.0.18 Path Traversal via Documents & Files Rename

desc: Admidio from 5.0.17 before 5.0.18 contains a missing authorization vulnerability that allows authenticated regular users to upload images into the announcements module by abusing the CKEditor upload handler. Attackers can send id=ann_description to ckeditor_upload_handler.php to store images under adm_my_files/announcements/images and retrieve them via show_image.php, abusing the application as an image host.
title: Admidio 5.0.17 Missing Authorization in ckeditor_upload_handler.php Image Upload

desc: SiYuan 3.8.0 before 3.8.10 contains an incorrect authorization vulnerability that allows anonymous attackers to read indexed asset text referenced only by publish-disabled attribute-view rows. Attackers can request /api/asset/getDocAssets on a public host document to obtain the leaked asset path, then query /api/search/getAssetContentByPath to retrieve the confidential file's full indexed text.
title: SiYuan 3.8.0 before 3.8.10 Incorrect Authorization Exposes Asset Text via getAssetContentByPath

desc: SiYuan before 3.8.10 contains an authentication bypass vulnerability that allows unauthenticated attackers to gain Administrator role by spoofing X-Forwarded-For through a loopback-trusted reverse proxy. Attackers can send requests with Host set to localhost and X-Forwarded-For set to 127.0.0.1 to read private note-history contents via the /history/*path route when no lock-screen password is set.
title: SiYuan before 3.8.10 Authentication Bypass via X-Forwarded-For on History Route

desc: Grav API plugin from 1.0.16 before 1.1.11 contains an authorization bypass vulnerability that allows scoped API key holders to override page permission rules because checks read the owning account's authority instead of the key's scopes. Attackers can use keys minted on super-admin accounts to edit, delete or read pages that deny those actions, or use media-scoped keys to change media on read-only pages.
title: Grav API Plugin 1.0.16 before 1.1.11 Scoped API Key Authorization Bypass

desc: Grav API plugin from 1.0.0 before 1.1.4 contains a remote code execution vulnerability that allows publishers with media and page write rights to write theme template files through the blueprint-upload endpoint. Attackers can upload a file into a theme's Twig templates folder and include it from sandboxed page Twig to execute commands as the web-server user.
title: Grav API Plugin 1.0.0 before 1.1.4 RCE via blueprint-upload Theme Template Write

desc: SiYuan 3.6.0 before 3.8.10 contains an information disclosure vulnerability that allows authenticated Readers to read protected documents through block-reference footnote resolution in Markdown export. Attackers can request copyStdMarkdown for a public document referencing a hidden, disabled, or password-protected document to disclose its body text without the publish password.
title: SiYuan 3.6.0 before 3.8.10 Information Disclosure via copyStdMarkdown Block References

desc: Grav Form plugin 1.1.0 before 9.1.40 contains a stored cross-site scripting vulnerability in Form::uploadFiles(), which sanitizes SVG only when a file's last extension is .svg and accepts markup under unrecognized extensions. Anonymous attackers can upload files like drawing.svg.foo through public any-type upload forms, running script in an administrator's session when opened, enabling super-admin creation on Grav 2.x with Admin2.
title: Grav Form Plugin 1.1.0 before 9.1.40 Stored XSS via Unsanitized File Uploads

desc: Parse Server 2.5.0 before 8.6.121 and 9.0.0 before 9.11.1-alpha.1 does not handle a failure to serialize an object after a beforeSave trigger, leaving the request unsettled and terminating the server process. A remote attacker able to update an object in a class with a beforeSave trigger can send a dot notation key below a non-object field, such as a timestamp, to crash the server for all clients.
title: Parse Server 2.5.0 before 8.6.121 and 9.0.0 before 9.11.1-alpha.1 Denial of Service via beforeSave Trigger

desc: Parse Server before 8.6.122 and 9.0.0 before 9.11.1-alpha.2 does not prevent dot notation keys from changing a field that a beforeSave trigger keeps constant or reverts, affecting Object, Array, GeoPoint, Polygon, Bytes (on MongoDB), and ACL fields on create and update. A client allowed to write the object can modify such a field, such as a constant role list, to bypass Cloud Code authorization checks.
title: Parse Server before 8.6.122 and 9.0.0 before 9.11.1-alpha.2 beforeSave Protection Bypass via Dot Notation

desc: SiYuan 3.8.0 before 3.8.10 contains an incorrect authorization vulnerability in the serveAssets route that allows unauthenticated attackers to read password-protected document assets via name collisions. Attackers can request GET /assets/<name> when a visible document references the same relative asset name, retrieving the protected file's contents on public-publish instances with Basic Auth disabled.
title: SiYuan 3.8.0 before 3.8.10 Incorrect Authorization via /assets Cross-document Asset Collision

desc: SiYuan 3.8.0 before 3.8.10 contains an information disclosure vulnerability in LAN sync that allows adjacent unauthenticated attackers to obtain device metadata by advertising a counterfeit peer with a replayed discovery tag. The client sends the sync scope ID, device name, OS, app version, and TLS client certificate to /peer-sync/v1/session/open before validating the server proof.
title: SiYuan 3.8.0 before 3.8.10 LAN Sync Metadata Disclosure Before Peer Authentication

desc: SiYuan 3.6.0 before 3.6.2 and 3.7.3 before 3.8.10 contains a missing authorization vulnerability in the /api/block/getDOMText endpoint, which renders caller-supplied DOM without checking publish access for referenced image paths. When publish authentication is disabled, anonymous visitors can submit DOM referencing a known unpublished, non-encrypted asset path to retrieve its already-cached OCR text.
title: SiYuan 3.6.0 before 3.6.2 and 3.7.3 before 3.8.10 Missing Authorization in getDOMText Exposes Cached OCR Text

desc: @fastify/express is a compatibility layer that lets Express middleware run inside the Fastify web framework. In versions 4.0.0 through 4.0.9, when Fastify routing is configured to be case-insensitive, the router folds the request path to lower case in a way that maps certain non-ASCII Unicode characters to ASCII letters, but @fastify/express matches Express mount paths against the decoded path without applying the same folding. The two disagree, so a request that spells a letter of a mount path with an equivalent Unicode character is routed to the protected handler while the path-scoped middleware mounted on that path never matches and is skipped. An unauthenticated client can therefore reach a handler that an authentication, authorization, or rate-limiting middleware was meant to protect, though only when the application enables case-insensitive routing and the mount path contains an affected letter. The issue is fixed in @fastify/express 4.0.10, and users should upgrade to 4.0.10 or later.
title: @fastify/express vulnerable to path-scoped middleware bypass via Unicode case folding

desc: @fastify/express is a compatibility layer that lets Express middleware run inside the Fastify web framework. In versions before 4.0.10, the plugin passes Express a request URL that does not always match the path Fastify's router dispatched, so path-scoped Express middleware can be skipped while the route handler still runs. Several request forms trigger the mismatch, including percent-decoding that rewrites a backslash to a slash or double-decodes an encoded percent sign, and a request target that begins with an asterisk, so the middleware and the handler disagree on the path or on parameter and query values. An unauthenticated client can therefore reach a handler that an authentication, authorization, or rate-limiting middleware was meant to protect, with no special configuration required. The issue is fixed in @fastify/express 4.0.10, and users should upgrade to 4.0.10 or later.
title: @fastify/express vulnerable to path-scoped middleware bypass via request URL decoding and normalization mismatches

desc: @fastify/middie is the middleware engine for the Fastify web framework. In versions up to and including 9.3.7, middie matches path-scoped middleware against its own reading of the request path, which can differ from the path Fastify's router uses to dispatch the request. When the two disagree, the router can route a request to a handler covered by a middleware mount while middie skips that middleware, so an unauthenticated client reaches a handler that an authentication, authorization, or rate-limiting middleware was meant to protect, with no special configuration required. The mismatch is triggered by empty parameter or wildcard values, request targets that do not begin with a slash, and literal percent characters in a mount path. The issue is fixed in @fastify/middie 9.3.8, and users should upgrade to 9.3.8 or later.
title: @fastify/middie vulnerable to path-scoped middleware bypass via request path matching mismatches

desc: @fastify/swagger-ui is the plugin that serves Swagger UI documentation for Fastify applications. In versions 2.1.0 through 6.1.4, the authentication hooks that applications register to protect the documentation are applied to every route the plugin adds except the bundled static asset instance. When the option that serves bundled UI files from a local directory is enabled, that instance exposes every file in the directory without credentials, so a specification file an operator meant to keep behind the documentation login becomes reachable by an unauthenticated client who knows or guesses its name. Access is read-only and limited to files in that directory. The issue is fixed in @fastify/swagger-ui 6.1.5, which applies the same authentication hooks to the static asset route, and users should upgrade to 6.1.5 or later.
title: @fastify/swagger-ui vulnerable to documentation authentication bypass via the unprotected /static route

desc: @fastify/rate-limit is the rate-limiting plugin for the Fastify web framework. Starting in version 11.1.0, the plugin documented a manual flow for limiting failed login attempts that peeks at the limiter, runs the password check, and consumes a slot only on failure. Because the peek and the consume are two separate store operations with the password check in between, concurrent requests can all pass the peek before any slot is consumed, so in versions 11.1.0 through 11.2.2 a burst of requests runs far more failed attempts than the configured limit, and the sequential path also allowed one attempt more than configured. The default per-request limiter is not affected. The issue is fixed in @fastify/rate-limit 11.3.0, which makes the manual flow atomic by reserving a slot in a single operation and refunding it only on success, and users should upgrade to 11.3.0 or later.
title: @fastify/rate-limit vulnerable to failed-login limit bypass via a race condition in the documented flow

desc: @fastify/express is a compatibility layer that lets Express middleware run inside the Fastify web framework. In versions 4.0.7 through 4.0.9, the plugin does not rewrite regular-expression mount paths to account for a parameterized plugin prefix, so when middleware is mounted with a regular expression inside a plugin registered under a parameterized prefix, the Express matcher treats the prefix parameter as literal text and never matches the real request path. As a result, Express silently skips that middleware while Fastify still runs the route handler, so an application that relies on regular-expression mounted middleware for authentication or authorization inside a parameterized-prefix plugin exposes protected routes to unauthenticated clients. No special configuration is required beyond a parameterized prefix and a regular-expression mount. The issue is fixed in @fastify/express 4.0.10, and users should upgrade to 4.0.10 or later.
title: @fastify/express vulnerable to middleware bypass via RegExp mount paths under parameterized prefixes

desc: A security vulnerability has been detected in Chaterm up to 0.12.2 on Windows. The affected element is an unknown function of the file resources/app-update.yml of the component Auto-Update Mechanism. Such manipulation leads to download of code without integrity check. It is possible to launch the attack remotely. This attack is characterized by high complexity. The exploitability is described as difficult. The vendor was contacted early about this disclosure but did not respond in any way.
title: Chaterm Auto-Update Mechanism app-update.yml code download

desc: @fastify/express is a compatibility layer that lets Express middleware run inside the Fastify web framework. In versions 4.0.5 through 4.0.9, the plugin matches path-scoped Express middleware with a matcher that requires a non-empty value for a dynamic segment, while Fastify's router accepts an empty parameter or wildcard value. When a route and an Express middleware mount share a dynamic pattern, a request with an empty segment matches the Fastify route and runs the handler while the middleware mounted on that pattern is skipped, so on a scoped mount an unauthenticated request can reach a protected handler. No special configuration is required, and the practical impact depends on what the empty value selects in the application. The issue is fixed in @fastify/express 4.0.10, and users should upgrade to 4.0.10 or later.
title: @fastify/express vulnerable to middleware bypass via empty route parameters and wildcards

desc: @fastify/express is a compatibility layer that lets Express middleware run inside the Fastify web framework. In versions 4.0.0 through 4.0.9, the plugin joins a path-scoped middleware's mount path to the Fastify plugin prefix by string concatenation, so when the plugin prefix ends with a slash or the mount path omits its leading slash, the resulting Express mount path does not line up with the route the Fastify router serves. Express then fails to match and passes the request on while the Fastify router still dispatches the route, so the middleware is silently skipped. An application that uses path-scoped Express middleware for authentication or authorization inside a prefixed plugin can expose protected routes to unauthenticated clients, with no crafted request and no non-default option required, and string, array, and regular-expression mount paths are all affected. The issue is fixed in @fastify/express 4.0.10, and users should upgrade to 4.0.10 or later.
title: @fastify/express vulnerable to path-scoped middleware bypass via prefix and mount path join mismatch

desc: A flaw has been found in TRENDnet TEW-657BRM 1.00.1. Affected by this issue is some unknown functionality of the file /usr/sbin/restore_config.cgi. Executing a manipulation can lead to out-of-bounds read. The attack may be launched remotely. The exploit has been published and may be used. The vendor explains: "I am not able to confirm if such vulnerability exists as the product has been EOL for more than 15 years. We will send out an announcement letting customers know." This vulnerability only affects products that are no longer supported by the maintainer.
title: TRENDnet TEW-657BRM restore_config.cgi out-of-bounds

Improper address validation in the AMD RAID Configuration Driver could allow an attacker with administrative access to read arbitrary kernel memory, potentially resulting in loss of confidentiality.

desc: Improper input validation within the AmdPlatformRasSmm driver could allow an attacker with privileged access to overwrite SMRAM, potentially resulting in arbitrary code execution.
