Splunk Enterprise Security could then run attacker-controlled Search Processing Language (SPL) commands using the permissions of that user. With this access, the user who stored the asset data could expose or modify data available to the user who selected the value.
The vulnerability is possible because Asset Center does not escape asset values before adding them to drilldown searches.
The vulnerability requires Asset Center to process the asset data and another user to select the value. The user who stored the data should not be able to exploit the vulnerability at will.
For more information see Users and roles for Splunk Enterprise Security (https://help.splunk.com/en/splunk-enterprise-security-8/install/8.7/installation/users-and-roles-for-splunk-enterprise-security), Add asset and identity data to Splunk Enterprise Security (https://help.splunk.com/en/splunk-enterprise-security-8/administer/8.7/asset-and-identity-management/add-asset-and-identity-data-to-splunk-enterprise-security), and Asset and identity dashboards (https://help.splunk.com/en/splunk-enterprise-security-8/user-guide/8.7/analytics/asset-and-identity-dashboards) in the Splunk documentation.
title: SPL Injection through Asset Center Drilldowns in Splunk Enterprise Security

desc:
In Splunk Enterprise Security versions below 8.7.0, a user who holds the "ess_admin" Splunk Enterprise Security role could execute arbitrary code on the search head as the user account running Splunk Enterprise by combining lookup file upload and Configuration Checker functionality.
The vulnerability is possible because Splunk Enterprise Security does not restrict lookup upload file types or keep Configuration Checker module paths within the intended directory.
For more information see Users and roles for Splunk Enterprise Security (https://help.splunk.com/en/splunk-enterprise-security-8/install/8.7/installation/users-and-roles-for-splunk-enterprise-security) and Create and manage lookups in Splunk Enterprise Security (https://help.splunk.com/en/splunk-enterprise-security-8/administer/8.7/managing-security-content/create-and-manage-lookups-in-splunk-enterprise-security) in the Splunk documentation.
title: Remote Code Execution (RCE) through REST API Path Traversal in Splunk Enterprise Security

desc:
In Splunk Enterprise Security versions below 8.7.0, a user who holds the "ess_analyst" Splunk Enterprise Security role could modify a search macro associated with risk exclusions. Scheduled Risk data model acceleration searches could later run attacker-controlled Search Processing Language (SPL) commands from that macro with elevated permissions. With this access, the user who modified the search macro could expose stored credentials and modify indexes or lookup data available to those searches.
The vulnerability is possible because the Splunk Enterprise Security app metadata grants the "ess_analyst" role write access to the risk exclusion search macro.
For more information see Users and roles for Splunk Enterprise Security (https://help.splunk.com/en/splunk-enterprise-security-8/install/8.7/installation/users-and-roles-for-splunk-enterprise-security), Finding exclusions in Splunk Enterprise Security (https://help.splunk.com/en/splunk-enterprise-security-8/administer/8.3/user-and-entity-behavior-analytics/finding-exclusions-in-splunk-enterprise-security), and Use search macros in searches (https://help.splunk.com/en/splunk-enterprise/manage-knowledge-objects/knowledge-management-manual/10.4/search-macros/use-search-macros-in-searches) in the Splunk documentation.
title: Privilege Escalation through Search Macro Permissions in Splunk Enterprise Security

desc:
In Splunk Enterprise Security versions below 8.7.0, a user that holds a role with the edit_modinput_data_migrator capability could cause the data migration input to run arbitrary Search Processing Language (SPL) commands with elevated permissions. With this access, the user could read data outside the assigned role scope and write data to indexes and lookup tables.
The vulnerability is possible because the data migration input does not restrict configured searches to product-supplied migration tasks before it runs them with elevated permissions.
For more information see Capability reference for Splunk Enterprise Security (https://help.splunk.com/en/splunk-enterprise-security-8/install/8.7/installation/capability-reference-for-splunk-enterprise-security) in the Splunk documentation.
title: Privilege Escalation through One-Time Data Migrations in Splunk Enterprise Security

desc:
In Splunk Enterprise versions below 10.4.5, 10.2.9, and 10.0.12, a low-privileged user who holds the "power" Splunk role could overwrite shared application dashboard views with arbitrary Search Processing Language (SPL) commands. When another authenticated user opens an affected dashboard in Splunk Web, Splunk Enterprise executes the injected SPL using the viewing user's permissions, potentially allowing the low-privileged user to access or modify data available to that user.
The vulnerability is possible because the affected app grants the "power" Splunk role write access to shared dashboard views that should be writable only by the "admin" Splunk role.
The vulnerability is possible because the Splunk App for Splunk Observability Cloud grants the "power" Splunk role write access to shared dashboard views that should be writable only by the "admin" Splunk role
title: Privilege Escalation through Splunk Web Dashboards in Splunk App for Splunk Observability Cloud

desc:
In Splunk Enterprise Security versions below 8.7.0, a user that holds a role with the mc_view_im_data capability could cause the Mission Control incident mapping Representational State Transfer (REST) API to run arbitrary Search Processing Language (SPL) commands with elevated permissions. With this access, the user could expose all data in Splunk indexes and all stored credentials and modify protected indexes and lookup data.
The vulnerability is possible because the Mission Control incident mapping REST API does not validate incident identifiers before including them in SPL searches.
For more information see Capability reference for Splunk Enterprise Security (https://help.splunk.com/en/splunk-enterprise-security-8/install/8.7/installation/capability-reference-for-splunk-enterprise-security) and Overview of Mission Control in Splunk Enterprise Security (https://help.splunk.com/en/splunk-enterprise-security-8/user-guide/8.7/mission-control/overview-of-mission-control-in-splunk-enterprise-security) in the Splunk documentation.
title: SPL Injection through the Mission Control REST API in Splunk Enterprise Security

desc:
In Splunk Enterprise Security versions below 8.7.0, a user that holds a role with the mc_investigation_read capability could cause the Risk Event Timeline Representational State Transfer (REST) API to run arbitrary Search Processing Language (SPL) commands with elevated permissions. With this access, the user could expose stored credentials and modify indexes and lookup data available to those permissions.
The vulnerability is possible because the affected REST API does not validate request values before including them in search macro arguments.
For more information see Capability reference for Splunk Enterprise Security (https://help.splunk.com/en/splunk-enterprise-security-8/install/8.7/installation/capability-reference-for-splunk-enterprise-security) and Risk analysis (https://help.splunk.com/en/splunk-enterprise-security-8/user-guide/8.7/analytics/risk-analysis) in the Splunk documentation.
title: SPL Injection through the Risk Event Timeline REST API in Splunk Enterprise Security

desc:
In Splunk Enterprise Security versions below 8.7.0, a user who holds the "ess_analyst" Splunk Enterprise Security role could create an attacker-controlled saved search. Threat intelligence lookup generation could later run the saved search with elevated permissions, which could let the user who created the saved search run arbitrary Search Processing Language (SPL) commands with those permissions.
The vulnerability is possible because Splunk Enterprise Security does not restrict threat intelligence lookup generation to the intended saved searches.
For more information see Users and roles for Splunk Enterprise Security (https://help.splunk.com/en/splunk-enterprise-security-8/install/8.7/installation/users-and-roles-for-splunk-enterprise-security) and Turn on threat matching searches in Splunk Enterprise Security (https://help.splunk.com/en/splunk-enterprise-security-8/administer/8.0/threat-intelligence/turn-on-threat-matching-searches-in-splunk-enterprise-security) in the Splunk documentation.
title: Privilege Escalation through Threat Matching Searches in Splunk Enterprise Security

desc:
In Splunk Enterprise versions below 10.4.5, 10.2.9, 10.0.12, and 9.4.17, an unauthenticated user could inject arbitrary fields into Splunk Enterprise audit records via the Representational State Transfer (REST) API. 
Successful exploitation could allow the unauthenticated user to forge audit evidence, compromising the integrity of audit reviews and security detections that rely on legacy audit-field parsing.
The vulnerability exists because Splunk Enterprise does not neutralize field delimiters in user-supplied data before writing the data to a legacy audit record. The affected workflow also does not create a corresponding structured audit record.
For more information see Auditing activities in a Splunk platform instance (https://help.splunk.com/en/splunk-enterprise/administer/manage-users-and-security/10.0/audit-activity-in-splunk-enterprise/auditing-activities-in-a-splunk-platform-instance) and About structured audit trail logs (https://help.splunk.com/en/splunk-enterprise/administer/manage-users-and-security/10.2/audit-activity-in-splunk-enterprise/about-structured-audit-trail-logs) in the Splunk documentation.
title: Audit Log Injection through the REST API in Splunk Enterprise

desc:
In Splunk Enterprise versions below 10.4.5, 10.2.9, 10.0.12, and 9.4.17, an unauthenticated user could access RapidDiag process metadata and log file inventory information through the Representational State Transfer (REST) API.
The vulnerability is possible because certain RapidDiag REST API endpoints accept a factory-default shared key for node authentication, which lets requests bypass Splunk user authentication.
For more information see Using RapidDiag (https://help.splunk.com/en/splunk-enterprise/administer/troubleshoot/9.0/contact-splunk-support/using-rapiddiag) and Secure Splunk Enterprise services with pass4SymmKey (https://help.splunk.com/en/splunk-enterprise/administer/manage-users-and-security/10.0/secure-distributed-and-clustered-splunk-environments/secure-splunk-enterprise-services-with-pass4symmkey) in the Splunk documentation.
title: Authentication Bypass through the RapidDiag REST API in Splunk Enterprise

desc:
In Splunk Enterprise versions below 10.6.1, 10.4.5, 10.2.9, 10.0.12, and 9.4.17, an unauthenticated user could access live event data from the indexing pipeline through the Representational State Transfer (REST) API on a standalone instance or a search head that is not an indexer cluster member.
The vulnerability is possible because Splunk Enterprise accepts an empty shared key during service authentication.
title: Authentication Bypass through the REST API in Splunk Enterprise

desc:
In Splunk Enterprise versions below 10.4.5, 10.2.9, 10.0.12, and 9.4.17, a user holding a role with the edit_token_http capability could create a persistent HTTP Event Collector (HEC) token that cannot be disabled or deleted via the Representational State Transfer (REST) API or Splunk Web. As a result, the token remains active and can continue ingesting events even after administrative attempts to revoke it.
The vulnerability is possible because HTTP Event Collector token creation accepts names that later management operations cannot process.
For more information see authorize.conf (https://help.splunk.com/en/splunk-enterprise/administer/admin-manual/10.4/configuration-file-reference/10.4.5-configuration-file-reference/authorize.conf) and Set up and use HTTP Event Collector in Splunk Web (https://help.splunk.com/en/splunk-enterprise/get-data-in/get-started-with-getting-data-in/10.6/get-data-with-http-event-collector/set-up-and-use-http-event-collector-in-splunk-web) in the Splunk documentation.
title: Improper Input Validation through HTTP Event Collector Token Names in Splunk Enterprise

desc:
In Splunk Enterprise versions below 10.4.5, 10.2.9, 10.0.12, and 9.4.17, an unauthenticated user could send repeated HTTP PubSub channel subscription requests that cause a Denial of Service (DoS) by permanently increasing memory usage until Splunk Enterprise exhausts available memory. 
The vulnerability affects instances that turn on the [pubsubsvr-http] stanza in server.conf because the HTTP PubSub broker does not release memory associated with a channel after the client disconnects.
title: Denial of Service (DoS) through HTTP PubSub Channel Subscriptions in Splunk Enterprise

desc:
In Splunk Enterprise versions below 10.4.5, 10.2.9, 10.0.12, and 9.4.17, a user who does not hold the "admin" or "power" Splunk roles could read private index configuration values for other users through the deployment server Representational State Transfer (REST) API.
The deployment server REST API does not limit a supplied repository location to configured deployment repositories before it reads indexes.conf stanzas.
title: Sensitive Information Disclosure through the Deployment Server REST API in Splunk Enterprise

desc:
In Splunk Enterprise versions below 10.4.4, 10.2.8, 10.0.11, and 9.4.16, a low-privileged user who holds the "power" Splunk role could inject malicious content into a Splunk Web view. When another authenticated user opens the affected view in Splunk Web, the injected content executes unauthorized JavaScript code within the viewing user's browser session.
The vulnerability is possible because Splunk Web does not properly validate content in a view definition before rendering the view.
For more information see Define roles on the Splunk platform with capabilities (https://help.splunk.com/en/splunk-enterprise/administer/manage-users-and-security/10.2/manage-splunk-platform-users-and-roles/define-roles-on-the-splunk-platform-with-capabilities) in the Splunk documentation.
title: Stored Cross-Site Scripting (XSS) through Splunk Web Views in Splunk Enterprise

desc:
In Splunk Enterprise versions below 10.4.5, 10.2.9, 10.0.12, and 9.4.17, an unauthenticated user who can connect to a Splunk-to-Splunk (S2S) data forwarding receiver could cause the Splunk daemon to terminate unexpectedly. The unexpected termination interrupts data indexing and access to the management API and Splunk Web until the Splunk Enterprise process restarts.
The vulnerability is possible because the S2S data forwarding receiver does not validate an optional field in forwarded event data, which results in a null pointer dereference when the field is missing.
For more information see Intermediate data routing using universal and heavy forwarders (https://help.splunk.com/en/splunk-enterprise/get-started/splunk-validated-architectures/getting-data-in-forwarding-and-preprocessing/intermediate-data-routing-using-universal-and-heavy-forwarders) in the Splunk documentation.
title: Denial of Service (DoS) through Splunk-to-Splunk Data Forwarding in Splunk Enterprise

desc:
In Splunk Enterprise versions below 10.4.5, 10.2.9, 10.0.12, and 9.4.17, a user who holds the "power" Splunk role could store malicious Search Processing Language (SPL) in a shared dashboard. The malicious SPL could run using the permissions of the user who opened the dashboard and could access or modify data available to that user and disrupt Splunk Enterprise availability.
The vulnerability is possible because Splunk Enterprise does not preserve quoted search argument boundaries when it processes a dashboard search.
The vulnerability requires the attacker to phish the affected user by tricking them into initiating a request within their browser. The attacker, a user who holds the "power" Splunk role, should not be able to exploit the vulnerability at will.
title: SPL Injection through Shared Dashboards in Splunk Enterprise

desc:
In Splunk Enterprise versions below 10.6.1, 10.4.5, 10.2.9, 10.0.12, and 9.4.17, a low-privileged user who does not hold the "admin" or "power" Splunk roles could inject a malicious script into the name of a private saved search. If another user subsequently enables, disables, or edits the corresponding platform alert in the Monitoring Console, the injected script executes within that user's browser session, potentially allowing the low-privileged user to view sensitive information or modify data in Splunk Enterprise.
The vulnerability is possible because the Monitoring Console does not safely handle saved-search names in the platform alert workflow.
For more information see Enable and configure platform alerts (https://help.splunk.com/en/splunk-enterprise/administer/monitor/10.4/configure-the-monitoring-console/enable-and-configure-platform-alerts) and About configuring role-based user access (https://help.splunk.com/en/splunk-enterprise/administer/manage-users-and-security/10.4/manage-splunk-platform-users-and-roles/about-configuring-role-based-user-access) in the Splunk documentation.
title: Stored Cross-Site Scripting (XSS) through Monitoring Console Platform Alerts in Splunk Enterprise

desc:
In Splunk Enterprise versions below 10.4.5, 10.2.9, 10.0.12, and 9.4.17, a user who does not hold the "admin" or "power" Splunk roles could use the apps backup and restore Representational State Transfer (REST) API to prevent subsequent apps backup or restore operations until Splunk Enterprise restarts. This could result in a Denial of Service (DoS).
The vulnerability is possible because the apps backup and restore REST API handlers do not correctly enforce authorization.
title: Denial of Service (DoS) through the Apps Backup and Restore REST API in Splunk Enterprise

desc:
In Splunk Enterprise versions below 10.6.1, 10.4.5, and 10.2.9, a low-privileged user who does not hold the "admin" or "power" Splunk roles could access file path and metadata listings from search head knowledge bundles via the Representational State Transfer (REST) API. This unauthorized access could expose sensitive metadata, including Splunk platform usernames, private knowledge-object configuration file names, installed application directories, and the file path names of security-sensitive configuration and key files.
The vulnerability is possible because the REST API actions that list bundle contents and denied files use a capability available to the "user" role instead of requiring distributed-search administration capabilities.
For more information see Knowledge bundle replication overview (https://help.splunk.com/en/splunk-enterprise/administer/distributed-search/10.6/knowledge-bundle-replication/knowledge-bundle-replication-overview) in the Splunk documentation. For more information see Define roles on the Splunk platform with capabilities (https://help.splunk.com/en/splunk-enterprise/administer/manage-users-and-security/10.6/manage-splunk-platform-users-and-roles/define-roles-on-the-splunk-platform-with-capabilities) in the Splunk documentation.
title: Sensitive Information Disclosure through Knowledge Bundle Replication in Splunk Enterprise

desc:
In Splunk Enterprise versions below 10.4.5, 10.2.9, 10.0.12, and 9.4.16, a user who does not hold the "admin" or "power" Splunk roles could use Data Model Acceleration to run malicious Search Processing Language (SPL) commands and perform actions through the Representational State Transfer (REST) API that the user cannot perform directly.
The vulnerability is possible because Splunk Enterprise does not neutralize user-provided data before it adds that data to a generated search.
For more information, see Accelerate data models (https://help.splunk.com/en/splunk-enterprise/manage-knowledge-objects/knowledge-management-manual/10.2/use-data-summaries-to-accelerate-searches/accelerate-data-models), Define roles on the Splunk platform with capabilities (https://help.splunk.com/en/splunk-enterprise/administer/manage-users-and-security/10.2/manage-splunk-platform-users-and-roles/define-roles-on-the-splunk-platform-with-capabilities), and About the search language (https://help.splunk.com/en/splunk-enterprise/search/search-manual/10.6/search-overview/about-the-search-language).
title: Search Processing Language (SPL) Injection in Data Model Acceleration in Splunk Enterprise

desc:
In Splunk Enterprise versions below 10.4.5, 10.2.9, 10.0.12, and 9.4.17, a low-privileged user who holds the "power" Splunk role could inject arbitrary Search Processing Language (SPL) commands into a Classic Dashboard search. When another user opens the affected dashboard in Splunk Web, those injected commands execute with the viewing user's permissions, potentially allowing the low-privileged user to access stored credentials and write data to indexes.
The vulnerability is possible because Splunk Enterprise does not correctly escape user-supplied content when it rewrites a search, which lets the rewritten search include additional SPL commands.
The vulnerability requires another user to open the dashboard in Splunk Web. Consequently, a user who holds the "power" Splunk role should not be able to exploit the vulnerability at will.
For more information see SPL safeguards for risky commands (https://help.splunk.com/en/splunk-enterprise/administer/manage-users-and-security/10.6/best-practices-for-splunk-platform-security/spl-safeguards-for-risky-commands) and Define roles on the Splunk platform with capabilities (https://help.splunk.com/en/splunk-enterprise/administer/manage-users-and-security/10.6/manage-splunk-platform-users-and-roles/define-roles-on-the-splunk-platform-with-capabilities) in the Splunk documentation.
title: SPL Injection through Classic Dashboard in Splunk Enterprise

desc:
In Splunk Enterprise versions below 10.4.5, 10.2.9, 10.0.12, and 9.4.17, a user that holds a role with the list_deployment_server capability could access sensitive information from inputs.conf files outside the intended deployment app directory through the Representational State Transfer (REST) API.
The vulnerability is possible because the REST API does not restrict a deployment app name to an existing deployment app before reading input configurations.
For more information see authorize.conf (https://help.splunk.com/en/splunk-enterprise/administer/admin-manual/10.4/configuration-file-reference/10.4.4-configuration-file-reference/authorize.conf), Deployment server architecture (https://help.splunk.com/en/splunk-enterprise/administer/update-your-deployment/9.0/deployment-server-and-forwarder-management/deployment-server-architecture), and inputs.conf (https://help.splunk.com/en/splunk-enterprise/administer/admin-manual/9.4/configuration-file-reference/9.4.16-configuration-file-reference/inputs.conf) in the Splunk documentation.
title: Path Traversal in Deployment Server Remote Input Listing in Splunk Enterprise

desc:
In Splunk Enterprise versions below 10.4.4, 10.2.8, 10.0.11, and 9.4.16, an unauthenticated user could craft a malicious link that, if opened by an authenticated user, executes arbitrary Search Processing Language (SPL) searches with the victim's permissions. 
Successful exploitation could allow the unauthenticated user to access or modify data, alter Splunk platform configurations, and disrupt operations available to the affected user.
The vulnerability is possible because the Portable Document Format (PDF) generation component processes request data before it rejects deprecated GET requests and does not apply SPL safeguards for risky commands to subsearches.
For more information see Generate PDFs of your reports and dashboards (https://help.splunk.com/en/splunk-enterprise/create-dashboards-and-reports/reporting-manual/10.4/report-management/generate-pdfs-of-your-reports-and-dashboards) and SPL safeguards for risky commands (https://help.splunk.com/en/splunk-enterprise/administer/manage-users-and-security/10.4/best-practices-for-splunk-platform-security/spl-safeguards-for-risky-commands) in the Splunk documentation.
title: SPL Command Safeguards Bypass through Cross-Site Request Forgery (CSRF) in Portable Document Format (PDF) Generation in Splunk Enterprise

desc:
In Splunk Enterprise versions below 10.4.5, 10.2.9, 10.0.12, and 9.4.16, a user who does not hold the "admin" or "power" Splunk roles could make unauthorized changes when restoring archived indexed data or cause a Denial of Service (DoS) on the Splunk Enterprise instance.
The vulnerability is possible because the Representational State Transfer (REST) API does not require the indexes_edit capability for archived-data restoration actions.
For more information see Define roles on the Splunk platform with capabilities (https://help.splunk.com/en/splunk-enterprise/administer/manage-users-and-security/10.6/manage-splunk-platform-users-and-roles/define-roles-on-the-splunk-platform-with-capabilities) in the Splunk documentation.
For more information see Restore archived indexed data (https://help.splunk.com/en/splunk-enterprise/administer/manage-indexers-and-indexer-clusters/10.6/back-up-and-archive-your-indexes/restore-archived-indexed-data) in the Splunk documentation.
title: Missing Authorization when Restoring Archived Indexed Data through the REST API in Splunk Enterprise

desc:
In Splunk Enterprise versions below 10.4.4, 10.2.8, 10.0.11, and 9.4.16, a user who holds the "power" Splunk role could create and share a metric alert that causes Analytics Workspace to run a malicious Search Processing Language (SPL) when another authenticated user opens a link to the alert. The malicious SPL could expose data, modify data, or disrupt services available in the affected session. 
The vulnerability is possible because Analytics Workspace does not fully neutralize metric alert names before including the names in SPL.
The vulnerability requires the attacker to phish the user by tricking them into opening a link that the attacker creates. The user who holds the "power" Splunk role should not be able to exploit the vulnerability at will.
For more information see Alerts in the Analytics Workspace (https://help.splunk.com/en/splunk-enterprise/create-dashboards-and-reports/analytics-workspace/10.4/using-the-analytics-workspace/alerts-in-the-analytics-workspace) and Define roles on the Splunk platform with capabilities (https://help.splunk.com/en/splunk-enterprise/administer/manage-users-and-security/10.4/manage-splunk-platform-users-and-roles/define-roles-on-the-splunk-platform-with-capabilities) in the Splunk documentation.
title: SPL Injection through Analytics Workspace Metric Alerts in Splunk Enterprise

desc:
In Splunk Enterprise versions below 10.4.4, 10.2.9, 10.0.12, and 9.4.16, a user who does not hold the "admin" or "power" Splunk roles could run arbitrary Search Processing Language (SPL) searches with elevated privileges through saved search dispatch and access stored credentials and indexed data or modify lookup data.
The vulnerability is possible because Splunk Enterprise does not correctly neutralize caller-supplied saved search dispatch values before it places the values into an SPL search.
For more information see Search endpoint descriptions (https://help.splunk.com/en/splunk-enterprise/leverage-rest-apis/rest-api-reference/10.4/search-endpoints/search-endpoint-descriptions) in the Splunk documentation.
title: SPL Injection through Saved Search Dispatch in Splunk Enterprise

desc:
In Splunk Enterprise versions below 10.4.5, 10.2.9, 10.0.12, and 9.4.17, a user who holds the "power" Splunk role could create and share a dashboard that contains attacker-controlled Search Processing Language (SPL). The SPL could run using the permissions of the user who opens the dashboard. With this access, the user who created the dashboard could expose stored credentials and write data to an index.
The vulnerability is possible because Splunk Enterprise does not correctly escape field names in searches that use the rename command.
For more information see rename (https://help.splunk.com/en/splunk-enterprise/spl-search-reference/10.4/search-commands/rename) and SPL safeguards for risky commands (https://help.splunk.com/en/splunk-enterprise/administer/manage-users-and-security/10.4/best-practices-for-splunk-platform-security/spl-safeguards-for-risky-commands) in the Splunk documentation.
title: SPL Injection through the rename Command in Splunk Enterprise

desc:
In Splunk Enterprise versions below 10.4.4, 10.2.8, 10.0.11, and 9.4.17, a user that holds a role with the edit_own_objects capability but does not hold the edit_view_html capability could create or modify a private Hypertext Markup Language (HTML) view through the Representational State Transfer (REST) API.
The vulnerability is possible because the REST API applies the edit_own_objects capability when it creates or modifies private HTML-based views instead of requiring the edit_view_html capability.
For more information see Define roles on the Splunk platform with capabilities (https://help.splunk.com/en/splunk-enterprise/administer/manage-users-and-security/10.2/manage-splunk-platform-users-and-roles/define-roles-on-the-splunk-platform-with-capabilities) in the Splunk documentation.
title: Missing Authorization for HTML-Based Views through the REST API in Splunk Enterprise

desc:
In Splunk Enterprise versions below 10.4.5, 10.2.9, 10.0.12, and 9.4.17, a user who holds the "power" Splunk role could craft a shared Classic Dashboard that runs arbitrary Search Processing Language (SPL) commands for another authenticated user. Exploitation requires the dashboard viewer to open the shared dashboard. The injected commands could access data available to the dashboard viewer, modify data available to the dashboard viewer, and partially disrupt Splunk Enterprise.
For more information see Add sparklines to search results (https://help.splunk.com/en/splunk-enterprise/search/search-manual/10.6/calculate-statistics/add-sparklines-to-search-results), Configure dashboard permissions (https://help.splunk.com/en/splunk-enterprise/create-dashboards-and-reports/simple-xml-dashboards/10.6/manage-and-share-dashboards/configure-dashboard-permissions), and SPL safeguards for risky commands (https://help.splunk.com/en/splunk-enterprise/administer/manage-users-and-security/10.6/best-practices-for-splunk-platform-security/spl-safeguards-for-risky-commands) in the Splunk documentation.
title: SPL Injection through Classic Dashboard Searches in Splunk Enterprise

desc:
In Splunk Enterprise versions below 10.4.5, 10.2.9, 10.0.12, and 9.4.17, a user who holds the "power" Splunk role could add attacker-controlled Search Processing Language (SPL) to a shared dashboard. When another user opens the dashboard in Splunk Web, Splunk Enterprise could run the attacker-controlled SPL using the permissions of that dashboard viewer. The attacker-controlled SPL could expose stored credentials, modify indexed data, and reduce availability.
The vulnerability is possible because Splunk Enterprise does not neutralize special elements in search filter values before it builds optimized search jobs.
The vulnerability requires the attacker to phish the affected user by tricking them into initiating a request within their browser. The attacker should not be able to exploit the vulnerability at will.
title: Search Processing Language (SPL) Injection through Splunk Web in Splunk Enterprise

desc: Tamari is a fully-featured recipe manager web application built using Python and the Flask Framework. Prior to 1.7.2, an authenticated user can bypass the recipe-autofill SSRF check by submitting a hostname under the user's control through the Autofill from URL feature; the hostname can resolve to a public address during validation and a private or internal address during the later connection. In app/myrecipes/routes.py, is_safe_autofill_url validates the first DNS response, but recipe autofill passes the original URL to requests.get, which independently resolves the hostname and can connect to the internal address. The fetched response is parsed into recipe fields, enabling internal-service reconnaissance and potential data exposure; no redirect is required, and disabling redirects does not stop this DNS-rebinding bypass. This issue is fixed in 1.7.2.
title: Tamari: SSRF via DNS rebinding bypasses is_safe_autofill_url() in recipe autofill

desc: aMQTT is an open source MQTT broker and client. From 0.11.0 until 0.12.1, the QoS 2 transaction handler in amqtt/mqtt/protocol/handler.py, _handle_qos2_message_flow(), can retain transaction state and packet identifiers when a client disconnects before the handshake completes, unlike QoS 1 flows that expire after the default five-second timeout. A remote client can repeatedly begin QoS 2 flows and disconnect without maintaining long-lived connections; anonymous clients can do this with the default configuration, while authenticated deployments remain affected when a client may initiate QoS 2 flows. The retained state grows broker memory until resource exhaustion can terminate the process; no confidentiality or integrity impact is identified. This issue is fixed in version 0.12.1.
title: aMQTT: Denial of Service (DoS) via Memory Leak in Unmanaged QoS 2 Session Handshakes

desc: The MongoDB C Driver places a submitted connection-string option value into a diagnostic message without redaction when that option fails validation. The message is returned to the calling application and is also written to the process's standard error by the driver's default logging behavior. A party that can influence the connection string given to an application using the driver may cause that field's contents to be recorded, which may result in unintended disclosure of information the application placed in that field.
title: Credential exposure via unmasked connection string in driver parse-error messages for the C driver

desc: The MongoDB Go driver's connection string parser includes the raw, undecoded value of a query option in the error it returns when that value contains invalid percent encodings. When the option holds a secret, such as a TLS key file password or an AWS session token, the secret appears in plain text in the error. A party with low-privileged read access to wherever the application records or displays that error may learn the secret.
title: Credential exposure via unmasked option values in Go driver connection string parse errors

desc: The MongoDB Go Driver does not neutralize NUL characters in the user name and password values it places into the message it builds for SASL PLAIN authentication. A party who can choose the login values that an application passes to the driver can alter where the fields of that message begin and end. This may result in a receiving system reading a login name and secret that differ from the values the application supplied. Authenticating as a different account still requires that account's password. Only deployments that use SASL PLAIN authentication are affected.
title: Authentication identity confusion via NUL-byte injection in SASL PLAIN credentials

desc: A MongoDB C# Driver component that interprets connection configuration supplied by the hosting application can include the caller-supplied configuration value in the text of the error it raises when that value cannot be interpreted. The redaction applied to that text does not cover all forms in which secret material may appear, so authentication material embedded in the configuration value can be preserved in the resulting error text and in anything that records it. Exploitation requires only the low privilege needed to observe the application's own error output or logs on the system where the driver runs; no database credentials or server connectivity are required. The result is disclosure of sensitive information to parties whose access to error output is broader than their intended access to the configuration secret.
title: Credential exposure via unmasked connection string in driver parse-error messages

desc: The MongoDB C# Driver does not neutralize NUL characters in the user name and password values it places into the message it builds for SASL PLAIN authentication. A party who can choose the login values that an application passes to the driver can alter where the fields of that message begin and end. This may result in a receiving system reading a login name and secret that differ from the values the application supplied. Authenticating as a different account still requires that account's password. Only deployments that use SASL PLAIN authentication are affected.
title: Authentication identity confusion via NUL-byte injection in SASL PLAIN credentials

desc: An improper neutralization of delimiters in the MongoDB C# driver's DNS SRV connection-string resolution lets an unauthenticated party who can answer the client's DNS SRV query place a host outside the trusted domain into the client's server list. When an application resolves the connection string through the affected API and connects with the result, application data, authentication credentials and query results may pass through that host. This may result in unintended disclosure of data and credentials and in forged query results.
title: Attacker able to redirect a client's database traffic to a host they control via a comma in an SRV target, bypassing the SRV parent-domain guard

desc: The MongoDB Ruby driver can include unmasked connection string content in the error it raises when a connection string cannot be parsed. If that connection string carries a secret, the secret may be disclosed in cleartext through the application's error output or logs. No privileges on the driver and no network access are needed to produce the error; a party able to read the application's error output may obtain the secret.
title: Credential exposure via unmasked connection string in driver parse-error messages for the Ruby driver

desc: The MongoDB Ruby Driver does not neutralize NUL characters in the user name and password values it places into the message it builds for SASL PLAIN authentication. A party who can choose the login values that an application passes to the driver can alter where the fields of that message begin and end. This may result in a receiving system reading a login name and secret that differ from the values the application supplied. Authenticating as a different account still requires that account's password. Only deployments that use SASL PLAIN authentication are affected.
title: Authentication identity confusion via NUL-byte injection in SASL PLAIN credentials

desc: The MongoDB Python Driver does not neutralize NUL characters in the user name and password values it places into the message it builds for SASL PLAIN authentication. A party who can choose the login values that an application passes to the driver can alter where the fields of that message begin and end. This may result in a receiving system reading a login name and secret that differ from the values the application supplied. Authenticating as a different account still requires that account's password. Only deployments that use SASL PLAIN authentication are affected.
title: Authentication identity confusion via NUL-byte injection in SASL PLAIN credentials

desc: A credential-handling weakness in the MongoDB Python Driver allows a configuration option value that protects private key material to be written in clear text into the embedding application's own output and log records when a driver object is converted to text. A party able to read that output may obtain the credential. Obtaining it requires read access to the application's local output or log files.
title: Credential exposure via unmasked option value in Python driver object text output

desc: The MongoDB PHP extension includes the full connection string it was given in the error it raises when that string cannot be parsed. A party able to influence any part of the connection string, including a part that holds no secret, can cause the resulting message to carry credentials into the application's standard error output and log files. This may result in unintended disclosure of authentication material to anyone able to read that output.
title: Credential exposure via unmasked connection string in driver parse-error messages for the PHP driver

desc: The MongoDB Node.js Driver does not neutralize NUL characters in the user name and password values it places into the message it builds for SASL PLAIN authentication. A party who can choose the login values that an application passes to the driver can alter where the fields of that message begin and end. This may result in a receiving system reading a login name and secret that differ from the values the application supplied. Authenticating as a different account still requires that account's password. Only deployments that use SASL PLAIN authentication are affected.
title: Authentication identity confusion via NUL-byte injection in SASL PLAIN credentials

desc: A weakness in the MongoDB Node.js driver can place sensitive information taken from an application-supplied connection string into the text of an error produced while that connection string is being parsed. The error is generated inside the application process before any database connection is made, so no database account and no network access are needed for it to occur. A party able to read the application's error output or log files may thereby obtain database credentials that the application's configuration source would otherwise keep to a narrower audience.
title: Credential exposure via unmasked connection string in driver parse-error messages for the Node driver

desc: The MongoDB Rust Driver does not neutralize NUL characters in the user name and password values it places into the message it builds for SASL PLAIN authentication. A party who can choose the login values that an application passes to the driver can alter where the fields of that message begin and end. This may result in a receiving system reading a login name and secret that differ from the values the application supplied. Authenticating as a different account still requires that account's password. Only deployments that use SASL PLAIN authentication are affected.
title: Authentication identity confusion via NUL-byte injection in SASL PLAIN credentials

desc:
ServiceNow has addressed a code injection security issue that was identified in the ServiceNow AI Platform. This issue could enable an authenticated user with template editing privileges to execute code in the context of another user's session. 


ServiceNow deployed an update to hosted instances, and provided the update to our partners and self-hosted customers. We are not currently aware of malicious exploitation against ServiceNow instances. We recommend customers promptly apply appropriate updates or upgrade to a patched release if they have not already done so.
title: Authenticated Code Execution via Template Evaluation

desc: Authorization bypass through a user-controlled key in the PuppetDB facts terminus used by Puppet Server allows a client holding any valid agent certificate to overwrite the facts, including trusted facts, that PuppetDB stores for a different node. In Puppet Enterprise deployments where task permissions are scoped to node groups defined by facts or trusted facts, this can allow a user to run tasks on nodes outside their permitted scope.
title: Cross-node trusted facts overwrite in PuppetDB facts terminus

desc: Go-Guerrilla SMTP Daemon is a lightweight SMTP server written in Go. In 1.6.7 and earlier, according to the repository advisory's structured affected range, server.go defines the seven-byte cmdXCLIENT token, but the XCLIENT handler slices input[8:] after matching only that seven-byte verb, so a bare command causes an out-of-bounds panic in handleClient and terminates the daemon because that connection goroutine does not recover the panic. The issue is reachable by an unauthenticated client when the non-default xclient_on setting is enabled; no HELO command is required. The repository fix is present in version 1.6.7-1.
title: go-guerrilla crashes on a bare XCLIENT command (7-byte slice off-by-one panic)

desc: Poweradmin is a web-based DNS administration tool for PowerDNS server. From 4.0.0 until 4.2.6, 4.3.5, and 4.4.1, lib/Domain/Service/MfaService.php verifies email second-factor codes through MfaService::verifyCode() without limiting failed attempts, and lib/Application/Controller/MfaVerifyController.php logs failures without throttling them. An attacker who knows the user's password can repeatedly guess the six-digit code during its ten-minute validity period when email MFA is enabled, potentially bypassing the second factor; the advisory notes MFA is disabled by default and that the practical request rate was not measured. This issue is fixed in versions 4.2.6, 4.3.5, and 4.4.1.
title: Poweradmin: The email second factor is an mt_rand() six-digit code verified with no attempt limit or lockout, so an attacker holding the password can brute-force it within the validity window

desc: aMQTT is an open source MQTT broker and client. From 0.11.0 until 0.11.4, add_subscription() in amqtt/broker.py accepts malformed single-level + wildcard placement because it checks substrings instead of validating each slash-delimited level. The _matches() function converts each + into a greedy regular-expression fragment and evaluates it with re.fullmatch(), allowing a filter containing many adjacent + characters to trigger catastrophic backtracking when compared with a topic that partially matches but ultimately fails. Because matching runs synchronously in _run_broadcast(), one subscription followed by a publish can block the broker event loop, stopping message delivery and new connection processing until restart. Anonymous clients can trigger the issue with the default configuration. Any authenticated client permitted to create arbitrary subscriptions and publish messages may still exploit it when authentication is enabled. This issue is fixed in version 0.11.4.
title: aMQTT: Inefficient Regular Expression Complexity and Uncontrolled Resource Consumption and Improper Input Validation

desc: OpenRemote is an open-source internet-of-things platform. Prior to 1.31.0, an authenticated user who obtains another user's MQTT session ID can disconnect that session across realm boundaries through the GET route GET {realm}/disconnect/{sessionID}. In manager/src/main/java/org/openremote/manager/security/UserResourceImpl.java, disconnectUserSession ignores the requested realm and calls mqttBrokerService.disconnectSession(sessionID) without checking session ownership; model/src/main/java/org/openremote/model/security/UserResource.java exposes the route without an @RolesAllowed restriction. The earlier cross-realm read-method guards did not cover this disconnect method, and same-realm users can also disconnect sessions they do not own. Session IDs are not trivially brute-forceable but may be exposed through monitoring, logs, or correlated API calls, and the unauthorized disconnect can disrupt MQTT connectivity across tenant boundaries without directly disclosing session data. This issue is fixed in 1.31.0.
title: OpenRemote: Cross-realm MQTT session disconnect without authorization

desc: Fabio is an HTTP(S) and TCP router for deploying applications managed by consul. Prior to 1.7.3, route/table.go selects targets using raw req.URL.Path, while proxy/http_proxy.go applies per-route ACL and basic-auth checks to the selected target and forwards the raw path to the origin. Dot-segment, encoded-dot, or repeated-slash variants can fall through to a less restrictive route that reaches the same backend; the backend then normalizes the path and serves the protected resource without the configured access controls. A less restrictive fallback route must reach the same backend; without one, the request returns 404. This issue is fixed in version 1.7.3.
title: Fabio: Access-control bypass through unnormalized request paths

desc: bep/imagemeta is a Go library for reading EXIF, IPTC and XMP image meta data from JPEG, TIFF, PNG, and WebP files. Prior to 0.17.3, imagemeta.Decode could exhaust memory when parsing PNG zTXt chunks whose keyword is "Raw profile type iptc": the declared chunk length can drive an allocation far larger than the input file, and the embedded zlib stream is decompressed without an output limit. The advisory reports a 42-byte input causing a 256 MB allocation and a 127 KB input inflating to 460 MB. The oversized-allocation path's memory effect depends on platform overcommit and configured GOMEMLIMIT or cgroup limits, while the decompression path reliably creates resident memory. Applications that decode untrusted PNGs with IPTC metadata processing can therefore suffer denial of service through memory exhaustion. This issue is fixed in 0.17.3.
title: bep/imagemeta: Unbounded memory allocation decoding PNG `zTXt` "Raw profile type iptc" chunks

desc: An improper input validation vulnerability in WatchGuard Dimension's database snapshot restore feature allows an authenticated Dimension Administrator to execute arbitrary operating system commands as root by uploading a specially crafted database snapshot archive.
title: Dimension Improper Input Validation in Database Snapshot Restore Allows Root Code Execution

desc: A missing authorization vulnerability in WatchGuard Dimension's legacy system settings configuration handler allows a low-privileged authenticated user to execute arbitrary commands with elevated privileges on the underlying OS.
title: Dimension Missing Authorization in System Settings Endpoint Allows Remote Code Execution

desc: An insufficient session expiration vulnerability in WatchGuard Dimension's administrator session management allows an attacker holding a valid Super Administrator WebUI session to retain full Super Administrator privileges after that account has been downgraded or deleted by another administrator.
title: Dimension Insufficient Session Expiration Allows Persistent Super Administrator Access

desc: An improper authorization vulnerability in WatchGuard Dimension's device management registration process allows an attacker who controls one enrolled managed device's credentials to take over another managed device's identity. This allows the attacker to receive the victim device's queued configuration and apply attacker-supplied configurations under the victim device's identity.
title: Dimension Improper Authorization in Device Registration Allows Managed Device Takeover

desc: Incus is a system container and virtual machine manager. Prior to 7.3.0, the six network address set handlers in cmd/incusd/network_address_sets.go resolved the effective project with project.NetworkProject(), which returns default when features.networks is unset. The expandProject authorization switch in cmd/incusd/daemon.go omitted auth.ObjectTypeNetworkAddressSet, so authorization used the requested project instead of the effective project. This issue is fixed in version 7.3.0.
title: Incus: Project-restricted client can write to the default project's network address sets

desc: WatchGuard Dimension returns unredacted session identifiers for logged-in users in a management API response. A low-privileged Dimension Administrator can retrieve the active session IDs of other administrators, including Super Administrators, while they are logged in, enabling account takeover.
title: Dimension Session Hijack via Exposed Session Tokens in Management API

desc:
WatchGuard Dimension records unredacted session identifiers for logged-in users in its web UI diagnostic log. A low-privileged Dimension Administrator can retrieve this log and extract a Super Administrator's session token while that administrator is logged in, enabling account takeover.

This vulnerability is a secondary unmitigated attack path for CVE-2026-78174.
title: Dimension Session Hijack via Exposed Session Tokens in Diagnostic Logs

desc: A Cross-Site Request Forgery (CSRF) vulnerability in WatchGuard Dimension's user management interface allows a remote, unauthenticated attacker to create a persistent local Super Administrator account by tricking an authenticated Super Administrator into visiting a malicious web page.
title: Dimension CSRF Vulnerability in User Management Allows Super Administrator Account Creation

desc: A missing authentication vulnerability in WatchGuard Dimension's log collection service allows a remote, unauthenticated attacker to execute arbitrary SQL statements and ultimately execute arbitrary code as the Dimension WebUI process user by sending specially crafted network requests.
title: Dimension Improper Authentication in Log Collection Service Allows Unauthenticated Remote Code Execution

desc: A SQL injection vulnerability in WatchGuard Dimension's log collection service allows an authenticated managed device, or an attacker in possession of a valid device logging key, to achieve arbitrary code execution on the Dimension appliance.
title: Dimension SQL Injection in Log Collector Allows Remote Code Execution

desc: A code injection vulnerability in WatchGuard Dimension's log notification processing allows an authenticated managed device, or an attacker in possession of a valid device logging key, to achieve arbitrary code execution on the Dimension appliance.
title: Dimension Code Injection in Log Notification Processing Allows Remote Code Execution

desc: A reflected Cross-Site Scripting (XSS) vulnerability in WatchGuard Dimension's Device Configuration History page allows an authenticated attacker with view permission on a device to execute arbitrary JavaScript in another authenticated user's browser by enticing the victim to open a specially crafted link.
title: Dimension Reflected XSS in Device Configuration History Page

desc: A vulnerability in WatchGuard Dimension's system upgrade process allows an authenticated administrator to create or overwrite arbitrary files on the appliance filesystem by uploading a specially crafted upgrade archive.
title: Dimension Arbitrary File Write in System Upgrade Process

desc: @fastify/http-proxy is a Fastify plugin that proxies HTTP and WebSocket traffic to an upstream server. In versions from 7.1.0 up to but not including 11.6.10, when the plugin is registered with websocket support enabled, it opens the upstream WebSocket connection with a header set built by the default header rewriter, which forwards the client cookie but never sets the upstream origin option, so the browser origin header is dropped while the authenticating cookie is forwarded. Many WebSocket servers defend against cross-site hijacking by checking the origin and treat a missing origin as a trusted non-browser client, so behind the proxy that check never sees the foreign origin. A malicious page visited by a logged-in user can therefore open a WebSocket through the proxy to an upstream that authenticates the handshake with a cookie, and read or send messages on the user's behalf. The issue is fixed in @fastify/http-proxy 11.6.10, and users should upgrade to 11.6.10 or later. As a workaround, provide a header rewriter that sets a correct origin, or validate the origin before the proxy.
title: @fastify/http-proxy vulnerable to Cross-Site WebSocket Hijacking via dropped Origin header

desc: @fastify/reply-from is a Fastify plugin that forwards requests to an upstream HTTP server. In versions 12.8.1 through 12.8.3, its buildURL function checked the attacker-supplied source string for parent-directory segments, but when the source begins with the same special scheme as the base, such as http or https, the WHATWG URL parser drops the scheme and resolves the remainder as a relative path. A payload that glues the scheme to a percent-encoded parent-directory sequence therefore passes the check, because the inspected segment reads as the scheme plus the dots rather than a bare parent-directory token, while the proxy forwards the encoded traversal unchanged. An upstream that percent-decodes the request path before resolving dot-segments then serves a path outside the configured prefix, so an unauthenticated client scoped to an upstream prefix, or relying on Fastify route guards in front of the proxy, can escape that prefix and reach sibling or parent upstream endpoints. The per-segment check added in 12.8.1 is what the scheme prefix bypasses, and releases up to 12.8.0 already rejected the decoded form. The issue is fixed in @fastify/reply-from 12.8.4, and users should upgrade to 12.8.4 or later.
title: @fastify/reply-from vulnerable to path traversal via scheme-prefixed encoded dot-segments

desc: @fastify/http-proxy is a Fastify plugin that proxies HTTP and WebSocket traffic to an upstream server. In versions from 9.0.0 up to but not including 11.6.10, when the plugin is registered with websocket support enabled, a WebSocket upgrade that is pipelined behind another HTTP request on the same cleartext connection arrives while that request's response is still attached to the socket. The shared upgrade listener sees the socket is already claimed and returns early without taking the upgrade, but it does not attach an error listener to the raw socket, and Node.js has already removed its own error listener before emitting the upgrade event. A later socket error on that connection, such as a client connection reset, is therefore unhandled and terminates the Node.js process. A single unauthenticated connection that pipelines an upgrade behind a normal request and then resets is enough to crash the server, and it can be repeated to keep the process down. Upgrades over TLS are not affected. The issue is fixed in @fastify/http-proxy 11.6.10, and users should upgrade to 11.6.10 or later.
title: @fastify/http-proxy vulnerable to Denial of Service via a pipelined WebSocket upgrade

desc: RepoManager is a self-hosted deb/rpm package repository. Prior to 5.13.3, the authenticated get-unit-log action accepts a caller-controlled logfile value. Validate::string() escapes HTML but leaves path traversal components unchanged. The action joins the caller-controlled logfile to SERVICE_LOGS_DIR without enforcing containment, so traversal can resolve the file read outside that directory. www/controllers/ajax/status/service.php reads and returns the resolved file, and any authenticated user can invoke the action to retrieve files readable by the www-data service account, including application configuration, source code, and the GPG signing-key passphrase. Fixed in 5.13.3.
title: RepoManager: Authenticated Path Traversal allows arbitrary file read via service unit log viewer

desc: RepoManager is a self-hosted deb/rpm package repository. Prior to 5.13.3, an authenticated user can supply a user-controlled, array-valued GPG key identifier to the key deletion action. Validate::string() filters HTML characters but not shell metacharacters. The user-controlled identifier reaches the delete action without shell-safe encoding. controllers/Gpg.php contains the vulnerable deletion path. Process::execute() passes the command string through proc_open() and /bin/sh -c, allowing the attacker to execute arbitrary OS commands as the web/PHP process. This can expose secrets or poison packages. Authentication is required, but the advisory makes an administrator-only restriction conditional on the intended access policy and does not establish an administrator role as a prerequisite. Fixed in 5.13.3.
title: RepoManager: Authenticated OS command injection (RCE) via GPG key deletion

desc: RepoManager is a self-hosted deb/rpm package repository. Prior to 5.13.3, a registered host or a party with its host/API credential can submit package metadata. Inventory reporting accepts package name and version, while available-update reporting accepts package name, version, and repository; the repository field exists only on that path. RepoManager stores these values, and stored values are rendered on the host's package detail page without preventing stored HTML or JavaScript from executing. An administrator must later view the page for script execution. The script runs in the administrator's authenticated browser session and can expose administrative data or forge privileged requests; the advisory describes possible escalation through admin-only functionality. Fixed in 5.13.3.
title: RepoManager: Stored XSS via host-reported package metadata

desc: Joomla Extension - akeeba.com - Account takeover through missing OAuth state validation in Akeeba SocialLogin extension 1.0.0-4.11.0 - The OAuth callback did not validate a session-bound state parameter, allowing an attacker to link their own social provider identity to the account of a logged-in user who opens a crafted callback link and subsequently log in as that user.
title: Joomla Extension - akeeba.com - Account takeover through missing OAuth state validation in Akeeba SocialLogin extension 1.0.0-4.11.0

desc: Joomla Extension - joomlatools.com - Unauthenticated blind server-side request forgery in FILEman extension < 6.1.4 - The frontend file view did not restrict requested files to their container and passed URLs to the framework URL fetch, allowing unauthenticated attackers to make the server issue requests to arbitrary addresses, including internal network resources.
title: Joomla Extension - joomlatools.com - Unauthenticated blind server-side request forgery in FILEman extension < 6.1.4

desc: @fastify/http-proxy is a Fastify plugin that proxies HTTP and WebSocket traffic to an upstream server. In versions from 9.0.0 up to but not including 11.6.10, when the plugin is registered with websocket support enabled, it takes every upgraded socket and dispatches the request through the Fastify router before the WebSocket library takes ownership of the socket. Node.js removes its own error listener from the socket before emitting the upgrade event, and the plugin does not attach one of its own during routing, so a socket error such as a client connection reset that arrives before the WebSocket library takes over is unhandled and terminates the Node.js process. The error window is open whenever anything asynchronous runs between dispatch and the route handler, such as an async hook on the proxied route or any unrelated async route in the application. A single unauthenticated upgrade request followed by a connection reset is enough to crash the server, and it can be repeated to keep the process down. The issue is fixed in @fastify/http-proxy 11.6.10, and users should upgrade to 11.6.10 or later.
title: @fastify/http-proxy vulnerable to Denial of Service via unhandled error on the WebSocket upgrade socket

desc: @fastify/http-proxy is a Fastify plugin that proxies HTTP and WebSocket traffic to an upstream server. In versions from 9.4.0 up to but not including 11.6.10, when the plugin is registered with websocket support enabled, a WebSocket upgrade request whose path carries a URL fragment is matched by the router and answered with a successful upgrade before the upstream link is created. Building the upstream target then throws, the error is only logged, and the accepted client socket is left open with no error listener, so the next frame the client sends becomes an unhandled error and terminates the Node.js process. A request target that is not a valid URL reference reaching a parameterized prefix triggers the same path. A single unauthenticated upgrade request followed by one frame is enough to crash the server, and it can be repeated to keep the process down. The issue is fixed in @fastify/http-proxy 11.6.10, and users should upgrade to 11.6.10 or later.
title: @fastify/http-proxy vulnerable to Denial of Service via a URL fragment in a WebSocket upgrade

desc: RepoManager is a self-hosted deb/rpm package repository. Prior to 5.13.3, an attacker who controls an upstream RPM repository mirrored by a RepoManager instance can provide a package filename through the primary.xml <location href> field; the mirror passes that filename into a shell-interpreted RPM query, allowing shell metacharacters to execute commands as the www-data service account. The target must mirror an upstream repository controlled by the attacker, and the default "Check GPG signatures" option triggers the vulnerable call. The command executes before a later signature-verification failure, so a valid signed package is not required. Fixed in 5.13.3.
title: RepoManager: Command injection (RCE) via unsanitized RPM package filename when mirroring a repository

desc: Joomla Extension - phoca.cz - Stored XSS through YouTube links in Phoca Gallery extension 4.2.0-6.1.6 - The YouTube upload feature did not validate the supplied video URL and embedded the derived video ID without escaping, allowing users with frontend upload permission to inject HTML attributes into the gallery detail view.
title: Joomla Extension - phoca.cz - Stored XSS through YouTube links in Phoca Gallery extension 4.2.0-6.1.6

desc: NLTK (Natural Language Toolkit) is a suite of open source Python modules, data sets, and tutorials supporting research and development in Natural Language Processing. Prior to 3.10.4, the CCG lexicon parser's matchBrackets and augParseCategory functions recursively process nested parenthesized categories without a depth bound. An attacker-controlled lexicon string with excessive nesting can raise RecursionError through nltk.ccg.lexicon.fromstring and terminate the parse operation or request worker. This issue is fixed in version 3.10.4.
title: NLTK: Uncontrolled recursion in CCG lexicon parser causes denial of service via deeply nested category input

desc: NLTK (Natural Language Toolkit) is a suite of open source Python modules, data sets, and tutorials supporting research and development in Natural Language Processing. Prior to 3.10.4, ToolboxSettings.parse builds a deeply nested attacker-controlled settings tree iteratively, but the later public helpers to_settings_string, remove_blanks, add_default_fields, sort_fields, and add_blank_lines recursively traverse that tree without a depth bound. Invoking any of those helpers on input nested beyond the interpreter recursion limit can raise RecursionError and abort the operation or request worker. This issue is fixed in version 3.10.4.
title: NLTK: Uncontrolled recursion in Toolbox settings helpers causes denial of service via deeply nested input

desc: NLTK (Natural Language Toolkit) is a suite of open source Python modules, data sets, and tutorials supporting research and development in Natural Language Processing. From 3.9.4 until 3.10.4, NLTK corpus-reader path pointers and view methods validate a requested relative path without consistently resolving intermediate directory symlinks against the reader's scoped root. A local attacker who can place such a symlink can make abspaths or words reach a readable file outside the corpus root and disclose its contents. On releases with pathsec enforcement, the file must remain inside a global NLTK allowed root; version 3.9.4 has enforcement disabled and permits a broader escape. This issue is fixed in version 3.10.4.
title: NLTK corpus-reader view methods bypass the scoped root sandbox via intermediate-directory symlinks

desc: @fastify/reply-from is a Fastify plugin that forwards requests to an upstream HTTP server. In versions before 12.8.4, its buildURL function rejects parent-directory path segments by an exact string match, so a segment that carries a semicolon path parameter, such as a dot-dot segment followed by a semicolon and an optional parameter, is not equal to the plain dot-dot form and passes the traversal check, and the WHATWG URL parser keeps it as an ordinary segment so the base-prefix containment check also passes. Backends that strip semicolon path parameters before resolving dot-segments, such as Apache Tomcat, Jetty, WildFly, and Spring Boot, turn the segment back into a parent-directory reference and resolve it, so an unauthenticated client can escape the intended upstream prefix and reach internal paths such as admin or internal API endpoints, including with state-changing methods. Deployments that proxy to Node.js, nginx, or Express upstreams are not affected. The issue is fixed in @fastify/reply-from 12.8.4, and users should upgrade to 12.8.4 or later.
title: @fastify/reply-from vulnerable to path traversal via semicolon path-parameter dot-segments

desc:
The glob functions in the GNU C Library versions 2.44 and earlier may free the same heap block twice when a memory allocation fails while glob prepends the directory name to the names it matched.  The names already rewritten are freed, but their pointers stay in the result vector, and the error path frees them again with globfree.

The allocation must fail after at least one name has been rewritten, so the issue can only be reached when the process is already close to its memory limit, for example under an address space limit (RLIMIT_AS) or on a 32-bit system.  The attacker needs control to make the result large enough to make the program or service run out of memory, either by controlling the glob pattern and having knowledge of the filesystem layout or through other means.  This issue affects all architectures and ABIs supported by the GNU C Library.
title: Double free after allocation failure in glob

desc: @fastify/http-proxy is a Fastify plugin that proxies HTTP and WebSocket traffic to an upstream server. In versions before 11.6.10, it rejects destinations containing parent-directory path segments by an exact string match, so a segment that carries a semicolon path parameter, such as a dot-dot segment followed by a semicolon and an optional parameter, is not equal to the plain dot-dot form and passes the check, and the WHATWG URL parser keeps it as an ordinary segment so the rewrite-prefix containment check also passes. Servlet containers such as Apache Tomcat and Jetty strip semicolon path parameters from each segment before resolving dot-segments, so a request routed through the configured prefix is rewritten and reaches the upstream where it resolves above the intended subtree, escaping the path the proxy is meant to expose and, on some containers, crossing application contexts. Both the HTTP and WebSocket proxy paths are affected. The issue is fixed in @fastify/http-proxy 11.6.10, and users should upgrade to 11.6.10 or later.
title: @fastify/http-proxy vulnerable to prefix escape via semicolon path-parameter dot-segments

desc: storyblok-backup is an npx CLI tool to create backups of a Storyblok space and restore individual resources. Prior to 0.7.1, the writeJson function used the editable Storyblok component name field as a filename without path containment. A person with component-management access in a Storyblok space could store a component name containing path traversal sequences; when another user later ran a backup for that space, the stored name escaped the configured backup directory and caused a JSON file to be written outside it on the backup host. Depending on the path chosen and the backup process's permissions, this could overwrite existing files at attacker-chosen locations. The vulnerability is specific to components: stories and datasources use numeric identifiers, and asset names are reduced to a final path segment. This issue is fixed in version 0.7.1.
title: storyblok-backup: Stored path traversal via unsanitized Storyblok component names in backup output

desc: A broken access control vulnerability in WatchGuard Dimension's Device Summary feature allows an authenticated, low-privileged user to retrieve a device's detailed summary data by bypassing restrictions that would otherwise hide this information.
title: Dimension Broken Access Control in Device Summary Allows Unauthorized Data Disclosure

desc: In Autonomy Logic OpenPLC Runtime versions 4.2.4 and prior, a race condition allows multiple concurrent requests to pass the existence check before any user is committed, resulting in several unauthenticated admin accounts being created.
title: Concurrent Execution using Shared Resource with Improper Synchronization in Autonomy Logic OpenPLC Runtime

desc: pREST (PostgreSQL REST) is an API that delivers an application on top of a Postgres database. Prior to 2.4.0, the vulnerable parameter is _groupby, handled by GroupByClause in adapters/postgres/postgres.go. adapters/postgres/postgres.go uses the weaker isSafeSQLExpression check for this function-expression branch instead of the stricter single-field validator used for _select. That check validates only the outer function name against a 13-function allowlist and permits nested subqueries, trailing UNION syntax, and inner pg_ functions. controllers/crud.go concatenates the GROUP BY expression while parameterizing only WHERE values, allowing attacker-controlled SQL structure into the clause. Default configuration permits unauthenticated access; a restricted installation may require a low-privilege table reader. UNION-based extraction requires compatible column counts and types and was not verified end to end, but a delay-producing function can cause denial of service without that alignment. This issue is fixed in 2.4.0.
title: pREST _groupby function-expression SQL injection (incomplete fix of CVE-2025-58450)

desc: Paymenter is a free and open-source webshop solution for management of hosting services. Prior to 1.5.7, the HasConfirmation trait in app/Livewire/Traits/HasConfirmation.php, included by app/Livewire/Component.php across 36 client-facing Livewire components, exposed executeConfirmedAction as a public action that invoked any component method accepted by method_exists. The action could call inherited InteractsWithProperties::fill(), whose data_set() writes arbitrary public properties, including state marked with #[Locked] and dotted paths into hydrated Eloquent models. Depending on the methods and properties exposed by an individual component, an unauthenticated caller could use this path to bypass intended authorization and modify server-side state intended to be immutable or protected from client-side manipulation. This issue is fixed in version 1.5.7.
title: Paymenter: Unauthenticated arbitrary method invocation in Livewire components

desc: A CRLF injection vulnerability in WatchGuard Dimension's outgoing email server configuration allows an authenticated Dimension Administrator to execute arbitrary operating system commands on the Dimension appliance with the privileges of the local mail-handling account.
title: Dimension CRLF Injection in Email Server Configuration Allows Remote Code Execution

desc: An OS command injection vulnerability in WatchGuard Dimension's package update functionality allows an authenticated Dimension Administrator to execute arbitrary operating system commands as root by submitting a specially crafted package update request.
title: Dimension OS Command Injection in Package Update Allows Remote Code Execution as Root

desc: TeamPass is a self-hosted collaborative password manager. Prior to 3.2.1.2, the update_folder action in app/sources/folders.queries.php allowed an authenticated, non-read-only user to re-parent a folder without checking whether the target folder or submitted parentId belonged to the caller's user-accessible_folders set. Selecting a personal folder as the new parent passed the personal-folder guard and set personal_folder on the target, transferring the credential subtree into the attacker's accessible space after the next login and hiding it from the organization, including administrators. The change exposed credential labels, logins, URLs, email addresses, and descriptions, while sharekey-protected passwords remained protected; hiding the subtree also denied other users access. This issue is fixed in version 3.2.1.2.
title: TeamPass folder re-parenting authorization bypass

desc:
The preview mode of the OPC (OnPage Composer) page
builder of JTL-Shop is activated by a request parameter alone and
renders page data supplied in the request without checking for an authenticated
backend session with the corresponding permission. Several portlet properties
are output without output encoding. An unauthenticated remote attacker
can thereby cause script code to be executed in the browser of a
visitor or administrator who opens a crafted link; in the case of an
administrator, actions can be performed with the administrator's privileges. Third-party
plugins whose portlets evaluate property values as templates can
additionally be made to execute template code through the same entry point. This is
a separate flaw in such plugins and does not affect the portlets of JTL-Shop itself.
title: Missing authentication for critical function leading to reflected cross-site scripting in JTL-Shop

desc: A flaw was found in Keycloak. An authenticated remote user with a pending required security action, such as configuring multi-factor authentication (MFA), can bypass the mandatory action by submitting a specially crafted request to the consent endpoint without a valid session code. Keycloak incorrectly interprets the submission as a page refresh and completes the authentication process, allowing the user to access the application without fulfilling the required security policies.
products: red hat:red hat build of keycloak
title: Org.keycloak.authentication: pending required actions (e.g. configure_totp) can be bypassed via post to login-actions/consent without a valid session_code

desc: Joomla Extension - vi-solutions - SQL injection in backend data search and export in Visforms extension 1.0.0-5.6.4, 6.0.0-6.2.1 - Search filters and form IDs in the backend data view and export were not properly sanitized, allowing SQL injection by backend users.
title: Joomla Extension - vi-solutions - SQL injection in backend data search and export in Visforms extension 1.0.0-5.6.4, 6.0.0-6.2.1

desc: Joomla Extension - vi-solutions - Improper per-form authorization for field management in Visforms extension 1.0.0-5.6.4, 6.0.0-6.2.1 - Field creation, editing and ordering checked permissions against a user-supplied form ID instead of the form the field belongs to, allowing backend users to manage fields of other forms.
title: Joomla Extension - vi-solutions - Improper per-form authorization for field management in Visforms extension 1.0.0-5.6.4, 6.0.0-6.2.1

desc: Joomla Extension - vi-solutions - Missing core.create check in example data generation and BreezingForms import in Visforms extension 1.0.0-5.6.4, 6.0.0-6.2.1 - Example data generation and the BreezingForms import did not check the core.create permission for the affected forms, allowing backend users to create records without permission.
title: Joomla Extension - vi-solutions - Missing core.create check in example data generation and BreezingForms import in Visforms extension 1.0.0-5.6.4, 6.0.0-6.2.1

desc: @fastify/static is the Fastify plugin for serving static files. In versions up to and including 10.1.11, when it is configured to deny or ignore dotfiles together with directory listing enabled, a request for a denied dot-directory returns its directory listing instead of being refused. The underlying send step answers with a forbidden response, but the listing fallback misreads that response on a path ending in a slash as a directory without an index file and serves the listing anyway.
