HtmlSanitizer is a .NET library for cleaning HTML fragments and documents from constructs that can lead to XSS attacks. Prior to 9.0.967 and 9.1.968-beta, HtmlSanitizer CSS style-declaration sanitization can process an attacker-controlled style attribute with quadratic cost because SanitizeStyleDeclaration repeatedly causes the complete declaration to be serialized while removing disallowed CSS properties. One unauthenticated request can occupy a synchronous application worker for seconds, and concurrent requests can saturate all workers and sustain denial of service. This issue is fixed in versions 9.0.967 and 9.1.968-beta.
title: HtmlSanitizer: CSS Removal DoS

desc: Chevereto before 4.5.8 contains a server-side request forgery vulnerability that allows authenticated administrators to cause the server to issue arbitrary requests by supplying a malicious URL to the uploadToWebsite function, which fetches the raw source via fetch_url before the Upload::checkValidUrl SSRF guard can be invoked. Attackers can target loopback addresses, RFC1918 internal services, cloud instance metadata endpoints, and file/gopher/dict schemes through the /json upload action to disclose internal responses or credentials when the fetched content is stored and served back as a public image URL.
title: Chevereto before 4.5.8 SSRF via Image::uploadToWebsite

desc: Pi-hole FTL is the core engine of the Pi-hole network-level advertisement and tracker blocker. From 6.0 until 6.7, CivetWeb permits unauthenticated clients to flood the WebUI login page and API invalid paths without connection or request-rate limits. Repeated requests can consume substantial CPU in request processing and session authentication, making the WebUI sluggish or unresponsive and potentially affecting the wider system and DNS service. Requests to selected invalid or redirecting paths also generate a log entry for each request, allowing network traffic to expand logs and exhaust constrained storage such as an SD card, while other request forms consume CPU without producing a corresponding request log. This vulnerability is fixed in 6.7.
title: Pi-hole FTL: WebUI (& API) DoS mechanism - Lack of rate limiting : Silent CPU consumption and/or Log file expansion

desc: Mistune is a Python Markdown parser with renderers and plugins. Prior to 3.3.4, parse_link_href performs an unbounded parenthesis-balancing scan to the end of the document for each unmatched opening parenthesis reached through an empty [] link label. In src/mistune/helpers.py and src/mistune/inline_parser.py, the empty label bypasses no_close_bracket_before, and no_link_before advances only past the short label, so successive [] ( candidates repeatedly scan the remaining document. Rendering untrusted Markdown with the default HTML renderer and no plugins can perform quadratic CPU work and keep a worker at 100 percent utilization. This issue is fixed in version 3.3.4.
title: Mistune: Quadratic-time DoS in parse_link_href via unbounded parenthesis scan on empty-label links

desc: Mistune is a Python Markdown parser with renderers and plugins. Prior to 3.3.4, inline image parsing sends nested ![ openers through precedence_scan because the no_link_before and _label_contains_link linearization guards are gated by not is_image. In src/mistune/inline_parser.py, each outer image opener can therefore search the remaining image body, while max_image_depth does not apply because the failed scans do not produce image tokens. Rendering untrusted Markdown with the default HTML renderer and no plugins can perform quadratic CPU work and keep a worker at 100 percent utilization. This issue is fixed in version 3.3.4.
title: Mistune: Quadratic-time DoS in inline image parsing (precedence_scan) bypasses not-is-image guards

desc:
The SOCKS5 client in subsys/net/lib/socks/socks.c built the CONNECT request in socks5_tcp_connect() by choosing the SOCKS5 address type from the address family of the proxy (proxy->sa_family) while reading the bytes out of the destination address supplied to connect(). A SOCKS5 request encodes the destination independently of the transport used to reach the proxy, so the two families are unrelated and nothing in the path forces them to agree: set_context_proxy() only requires the proxy family to match the socket, and zsock_connect_ctx() enters the SOCKS branch before any destination validation. With an IPv6 proxy and an AF_INET destination the code treated an 8-byte struct net_sockaddr_in as a struct net_sockaddr_in6 and copied the 16-byte sin6_addr from it, reading 12 bytes past the end of the object and transmitting them to the proxy.

With CONFIG_USERSPACE enabled, z_vrfy_zsock_connect() copies only addrlen user bytes into a stack-resident struct net_sockaddr_storage and enforces no per-family minimum length, so the oversized read stays within the storage but returns stale, uninitialised kernel-stack bytes. An unprivileged user-mode thread can therefore open an AF_INET6 stream socket, point setsockopt(SO_SOCKS5) at a proxy it controls, and call connect() with a short AF_INET destination to have the kernel send it 12 bytes of supervisor stack residue per attempt. Without CONFIG_USERSPACE the read runs past the end of the caller's own struct net_sockaddr_in, disclosing adjacent memory to the proxy; the family mismatch can arise unintentionally when a destination is obtained from DNS while an IPv6 proxy is configured.

Impact is limited to information disclosure of at most 12 bytes per connect() call, with no write primitive; the leak is delivered to whoever operates the SOCKS5 proxy. The mirrored pairing (IPv6 destination through an IPv4 proxy) is memory-safe but encoded the destination as SOCKS5_ATYP_IPV4 from the first four bytes of the IPv6 address, causing the proxy to connect to an unrelated host. Exploitation requires the non-default CONFIG_SOCKS option, a socket with SO_SOCKS5 configured, and both IPv4 and IPv6 support in the image.

The fix moves the encoding into a helper that selects the address type from dest->sa_family and validates dest_len against the matching struct net_sockaddr_in/struct net_sockaddr_in6 before copying, rejecting under-length or unsupported destinations with an error.
title: Out-of-bounds read and kernel stack disclosure in the SOCKS5 client when the destination address family differs from the proxy address family

desc: Dell SupportAssist OS Recovery, versions prior to 5.5.16.3, contain a Missing Authorization vulnerability. A low privileged attacker with local access could potentially exploit this vulnerability, leading to Unauthorized access.

Dell SupportAssist OS Recovery, versions prior to 5.5.16.3 contain an Improper Authorization vulnerability. A low privileged attacker with local access could potentially exploit this vulnerability, leading to Elevation of Privilege.

Dell SupportAssist OS Recovery, versions prior to 5.5.16.3, contain an Insecure Inherited Permissions vulnerability. A low privileged attacker with local access could potentially exploit this vulnerability, leading to unauthorized file operations with elevated privileges.

Dell SupportAssist OS Recovery, versions prior to 5.5.16.3, contain an Untrusted Search Path vulnerability. A low privileged attacker with local access could potentially exploit this vulnerability, leading to Elevation of privilege.

Dell SupportAssist OS Recovery, versions prior to 5.5.16.3, contain an External Control of System or Configuration Setting vulnerability. An unauthenticated attacker with adjacent network access could potentially exploit this vulnerability, leading to Elevation of Privileges.

Dell SupportAssist OS Recovery, versions prior to 5.5.16.3, contain an Insufficient Verification of Data Authenticity vulnerability. An unauthenticated attacker with adjacent network access could potentially exploit this vulnerability to bypass manifest signature validation, potentially leading to execution of unauthorized code with elevated privileges.

Bludit through 3.22.0 contains a missing authorization vulnerability that allows authenticated low-privileged users to modify the site logo by calling unprotected AJAX endpoints. Attackers with Author or Editor roles can send requests to logo-upload.php or logo-remove.php under /admin/ajax/ to replace the site logo with an uploaded image or delete it.
title: Bludit through 3.22.0 Missing Authorization via logo-upload and logo-remove AJAX Endpoints

desc: Bludit through 3.22.0 contains an improper session invalidation vulnerability that allows demoted users to retain revoked privileges because Login::isLogged() never re-reads the session-stored role. Attackers holding a session issued while their account was an administrator can keep using it after demotion to perform administrator actions such as creating new administrator accounts.
title: Bludit through 3.22.0 Improper Session Invalidation After User Role Demotion

desc: Dell SupportAssist OS Recovery, versions prior to 5.5.16.3, contain a Download of Code Without Integrity Check vulnerability. A highly privileged attacker with local access could potentially exploit this vulnerability, leading to Code execution.

Dell SupportAssist OS Recovery, versions prior to 5.5.16.3 contain a Download of Code Without Integrity Check vulnerability. A low privileged attacker with local access could potentially exploit this vulnerability, leading to Code execution.

Dell SupportAssist OS Recovery, versions prior to 5.5.16.3, contain an Improper Certificate Validation vulnerability. An unauthenticated attacker with local access could potentially exploit this vulnerability, leading to Protection mechanism bypass.

Dell SupportAssist OS Recovery, versions prior to 5.5.16.3, contain an Acceptance of Extraneous Untrusted Data With Trusted Data vulnerability. An unauthenticated attacker with physical access could potentially exploit this vulnerability, leading to Information tampering.

Kiwi TCMS is an open source test management system. From 16.1 until 16.2, the account confirmation page’s incomplete validation of the next parameter accepts protocol-relative URLs because the version 16.1 fix for CVE-2026-54724 only requires the value to start with a slash. An unauthenticated attacker can craft a confirmation URL on a trusted Kiwi TCMS hostname that redirects a user to an external site, enabling phishing and related downstream confidentiality or integrity impacts when the user follows the link. This issue is fixed in version 16.2.
title: Kiwi TCMS : Incomplete fix for CVE-2026-54724: open redirect bypass via protocol-relative URL in account confirmation

desc: Seerr before 3.5.2 contains an uncontrolled resource consumption vulnerability that allows unauthenticated attackers to exhaust disk space through unnormalized /imageproxy cache keys. Attackers can request the same TMDB image using many equivalent dot-segment path spellings, storing unlimited duplicate copies that fill the shared SQLite configuration volume and break logins and requests.
title: Seerr before 3.5.2 Unauthenticated Disk Exhaustion via /imageproxy Cache Keys

desc: tac_plus-ng before commit d8493e0 contains a stack-based buffer overflow vulnerability that allows clients holding the TACACS+ shared key to overflow a stack buffer due to an operator precedence error in author_pak_looks_bogus() and accounting_pak_looks_bogus(). Attackers can send packets whose argument-length table exceeds the payload, causing eval_args() to read past the packet and memcpy() oversized cmd values into cmdline, crashing the daemon or executing code.
title: tac_plus-ng before commit d8493e0 Stack-Based Buffer Overflow via packet length checks

desc: GreaterWMS through 2.1.54 contains a predictable authentication token vulnerability that allows unauthenticated attackers to forge openid tokens by recomputing an unsalted MD5 hash of username and registration timestamp. Attackers who know a username and can bound its registration time can brute-force candidate openid values in the Token header to gain full read and write access to warehouse, staff, customer, supplier and order data.
title: GreaterWMS through 2.1.54 Predictable openid Authentication Token Generation

desc: ClearFlask before 2.7.3 contains an improper authorization vulnerability that allows any account holding an invitation ID to accept it regardless of invited email. Attackers who obtain a forwarded or shared invitation link can redeem it via accountAcceptInvitationAdmin or accountSignupAdmin to become project administrators.
title: ClearFlask before 2.7.3 Improper Authorization via Project Admin Invitation Acceptance

desc: Pytition before 2.10 contains an insecure direct object reference vulnerability in the show_signatures view that allows registered users to delete other petitions' signatures by supplying foreign signature IDs. Attackers can post sequential signature IDs to their own petition's signatures page to permanently delete signatures from any user-owned petition and trigger confirmation emails to other signers.
title: Pytition before 2.10 IDOR Signature Deletion via show_signatures View

desc: Ruby Central cfp-app through 2.0 contains a missing authorization vulnerability in CommentsController#create that allows any authenticated user to comment on any proposal by supplying a numeric proposal_id. Attackers can send POST requests to /public_comments or /internal_comments to post into reviewers' private discussions and trigger notifications to event team members.
title: Ruby Central cfp-app through 2.0 Missing Authorization in CommentsController#create

desc: linkdotnet Blog through 17.1 contains an open redirect vulnerability that allows unauthenticated attackers to redirect users by passing unvalidated redirectUri values on the Login and Logout pages. Attackers can craft login links sending victims to attacker-controlled sites after authentication, and inject persistent returnTo destinations into other users' logout redirects via the shared AuthInformation instance.
title: linkdotnet Blog through 17.1 Open Redirect via redirectUri Parameter

desc: ep3-bs through 1.9.1b contains an improper authorization vulnerability that allows staff users with only user management privilege to delete administrator accounts. Authenticated assistant accounts can invoke the backend UserController deleteAction against administrator targets to remove or mark them deleted, locking administrators out.
title: ep3-bs through 1.9.1b Improper Authorization via UserController deleteAction

desc: BeikeShop through 2.0.0.32 contains a stored cross-site scripting vulnerability that allows registered customers to inject script by submitting an unsanitized RMA comment rendered unescaped in mail templates. Attackers can submit a return request with malicious script saved to mail_logs.content, executing in an administrator's browser session when they view the Mail Logs entry.
title: BeikeShop through 2.0.0.32 Stored XSS in Admin Mail Logs via RMA Comment

desc: Coyote before commit d6e8fb9 contains a missing authorization vulnerability in Wiki\CommentController::save that allows authenticated users to edit other users' wiki comments. Attackers can send POST requests to /Comment/Save/{wiki}/{id} with another user's comment id, bypassing the WikiCommentPolicy update check, so altered text appears under the original author's name.
title: Coyote before commit d6e8fb9 Missing Authorization via Wiki Comment Save Endpoint

desc: Pastefy 7.2.1 before 7.2.7 contains a stored cross-site scripting vulnerability in MermaidViewer.vue that passes attacker-supplied %%{init}%% directives to mermaid.mermaidAPI.updateSiteConfig(). Unauthenticated attackers can create Mermaid or Markdown pastes setting securityLevel to loose with a permissive dompurifyConfig to steal viewers' API session keys and act on their accounts.
title: Pastefy 7.2.1 before 7.2.7 Stored XSS via Mermaid Init Directive

desc: UrlHub before 1.20.1 contains a missing authorization vulnerability that allows any authenticated user to create accounts via the POST /admin/user/store route because role:admin middleware only covers view and create actions. Attackers, including self-registered users, can submit a request with role=admin to create an administrator account and gain full administrative control.
title: UrlHub before 1.20.1 Missing Authorization via /admin/user/store Endpoint

desc: ArtisanCloud PowerX through 1.0.2 contains a missing authorization vulnerability in the IAM role management API that allows authenticated tenant members to escalate privileges. Attackers holding even the lowest built-in role can call the permissions/grant-ids, permissions/grant, or bind/member routes to grant permissions or bind privileged roles, gaining tenant administrative access.
title: ArtisanCloud PowerX through 1.0.2 Privilege Escalation via IAM Role Endpoints

desc: wireguard_webadmin before 0.9981 contains a missing authorization vulnerability in scheduler/views.py that allows low-privilege authenticated users to manage peer schedules without Peer Manager level. View Only or Debugging Analyst users can create, modify, and delete schedule profiles and time slots to disable WireGuard peers or keep disabled peers off.
title: wireguard_webadmin before 0.9981 Missing Authorization via Scheduler Views

desc: GreaterWMS through 2.1.54 contains an unauthenticated path traversal vulnerability in the css, js, statics and fonts routes in greaterwms/views.py, which concatenate raw request.path_info without normalization. Attackers can send URL-encoded ../ sequences to read db.sqlite3 and obtain user openid tokens, enabling impersonation of any account.
title: GreaterWMS through 2.1.54 Unauthenticated Path Traversal via Static Asset Routes

desc: 53AIHub before 0.5.5 contains a missing authentication vulnerability that allows remote unauthenticated attackers to reinitialize installed instances by calling the public POST /api/init endpoint. Attackers can reset an existing account's password, assign the top creator role, and obtain an access token to take over accounts and use admin-only API routes.
title: 53AIHub before 0.5.5 Missing Authentication via POST /api/init Reinitialization

desc: FS PBX through 2.2.5 contains a missing authorization vulnerability in FaxesController, PaymentGatewayController and VirtualReceptionistController API routes that only check authentication. Any authenticated user can delete other tenants' fax records by UUID, deactivate or modify the platform-wide payment gateway, and change another tenant's IVR greeting.
title: FS PBX through 2.2.5 Missing Authorization in Fax, Payment Gateway and IVR Routes

desc: Flagr before 1.2.5 contains an authentication bypass vulnerability that allows unauthenticated remote attackers to access the flag management write API through an insecure default FLAGR_BASIC_AUTH_WHITELIST_PATHS including /api/v1/flags. Because basicAuth.whitelist() in pkg/config/middleware.go matches only path prefixes regardless of HTTP method, attackers can create, modify, enable, disable, and delete flags, variants, segments, constraints, and distributions.
title: Flagr before 1.2.5 Authentication Bypass via Default Basic-Auth Whitelist

desc: Bonsai through 6.0 contains an incorrect authorization vulnerability that allows authenticated Editor users to access admin pages because AdminAuthHandler accepts both Administrator and Editor roles. Attackers can use UsersController and DynamicConfigController to reset administrator passwords, promote accounts to Administrator, and change global settings to take over the instance.
title: Bonsai through 6.0 Incorrect Authorization in Admin Users and Config Controllers

desc: EveryDocs Core before 1.6.1 contains an authorization bypass vulnerability that allows authenticated users to access other users' records through unscoped Model.find(params[:id]) lookups in multiple controllers. Self-registered attackers can enumerate sequential ids to read, modify, or delete other users' documents and stored files, and rename or delete their folders, tags and people.
title: EveryDocs Core before 1.6.1 Authorization Bypass via Unscoped Record Lookups

desc: Habitat through 1.7.1 contains an insecure direct object reference vulnerability in CreatePostController::addAttachmentsToPost() that allows authenticated users to claim other users' unposted image uploads. Email-verified attackers can submit sequential attachmentIds when creating a post to attach another user's pending image, exposing it publicly and removing it from the uploader's post.
title: Habitat through 1.7.1 IDOR via Post Creation Attachment IDs

desc: LaraCollab through 0.18.2 contains a stored cross-site scripting vulnerability that allows authenticated client-role users to inject script by posting unsanitized task comments rendered via dangerouslySetInnerHTML. Attackers can post malicious comments that execute when users, including administrators, open the task or view dashboard recent comments, allowing actions in their session.
title: LaraCollab through 0.18.2 Stored XSS via Task Comments

desc: wishthis through 1.2.3 contains a missing authentication vulnerability in the PUT branch of src/api/wishes.php that allows unauthenticated attackers to modify wish URLs across all users. Attackers who know a wish link from a public wishlist can supply wish_url_current and wish_url_proposed parameters to redirect owners and gift-givers to attacker-controlled URLs.
title: wishthis through 1.2.3 Missing Authentication via Wishes API URL Update

desc: AudioBookRequest 1.9.0 through 2.0.1 contains a stored cross-site scripting vulnerability that allows low-privileged authenticated users to inject script through manual book request fields due to disabled Jinja2 autoescaping. Attackers can submit malicious title, author, narrator or info values via POST /api/requests/manual to execute script in an administrator's browser and access admin-only endpoints.
title: AudioBookRequest 1.9.0 through 2.0.1 Stored XSS via Manual Request Fields

desc: BZFlag bzfs before 2.4.32 contains a heap out-of-bounds write vulnerability in NetHandler::tcpReceive() that allows remote unauthenticated attackers to corrupt heap memory by sending a TCP message with a body length of exactly 1024. Attackers can overwrite the tcplen receive offset with a negative value to write controlled bytes before the buffer, crashing the server or executing commands as the bzfs user.
title: BZFlag bzfs before 2.4.32 Heap Out-of-Bounds Write via NetHandler::tcpReceive()

desc: wishthis through 1.2.3 contains an authorization bypass vulnerability in User::ownsWishlist() that allows authenticated users to modify other users' wishes and wishlists. Attackers can supply sequential wish_id and wishlist_id values to the wishes and wishlists API handlers to edit wishes, add wishes, or rename and delete wishlists.
title: wishthis through 1.2.3 Authorization Bypass via ownsWishlist Ownership Check

desc: Nexterm through 1.2.2-BETA contains a privilege escalation vulnerability that allows users with permissions.manage to gain unauthorized permissions because addGroupMember and setUserGroups lack the grantsBeyondCaller check. Attackers can add their own account to custom groups via the group membership endpoints to inherit permissions like users.impersonate and settings.backup.
title: Nexterm through 1.2.2-BETA Privilege Escalation via Permission Group Membership

desc: HyperFrames before 0.8.73 contains a path traversal vulnerability in the Studio server waveform and thumbnail routes that percent-decode paths without containment checks. Unauthenticated attackers, including script in a malicious composition, can send encoded ../ sequences to probe file existence and extract waveform data from files outside the project.
title: HyperFrames before 0.8.73 Path Traversal via Studio Waveform and Thumbnail Routes

desc: HyperFrames before 0.8.216 contains a server-side request forgery vulnerability in the engine URL downloader because isBlockedHost() only checks IP literals and never resolves DNS host names. Attackers can supply compositions with remote media, image or font URLs whose host names resolve to private addresses, making preview or render processes send HTTPS requests to internal services.
title: HyperFrames before 0.8.216 SSRF via DNS Names in Engine URL Downloader

desc: Dolibarr ERP CRM through 24.0.3 contains a code injection vulnerability in Website::importWebSite() that allows website editors without PHP permission to execute code by importing templates. Attackers can import a template zip whose javascript.js.php contains PHP code, which the public javascript.js.php endpoint includes, executing code as the web server user.
title: Dolibarr ERP CRM through 24.0.3 Code Injection via Website Template Import

desc: HyperFrames before 0.9.30 contains a missing Origin and Host validation vulnerability in the unauthenticated Studio API that allows malicious web pages to write project files. Attackers can send CORS-simple POST requests to /api/projects/:id/files/* or use DNS rebinding to plant package.json scripts or agent configs, leading to command execution.
title: HyperFrames before 0.9.30 Cross-Site File Write via Studio Preview API

desc: CodeIgniter4 before 4.7.5 contains a cross-site scripting vulnerability in the View Parser (system/View/Parser.php) that allows attackers to bypass auto-escaping through re-scanned substitutions. Attackers controlling one rendered value can inject Parser syntax like {other|raw} or {!other!} to emit unescaped attacker-controlled values, executing scripts in viewers' browsers.
title: CodeIgniter4 before 4.7.5 XSS via View Parser Auto-Escaping Bypass

desc: AppFlowy-Web before 0.20.0 contains a stored cross-site scripting vulnerability in the TextareaAutosize component that allows workspace members with edit access to inject markup by copying unescaped values into a hidden mirror via innerHTML. Attackers can store a database row title or checklist task containing an element with an event handler to execute script in browsers of users opening the row, including unauthenticated published page visitors.
title: AppFlowy-Web before 0.20.0 Stored XSS via TextareaAutosize Measurement Mirror

desc: Dolibarr ERP CRM before 24.0.2 contains an improper authorization vulnerability in the Users REST API put() method that allows non-admin API users to set administrator passwords. Authenticated users with user modification and password rights can send a PUT request to the users endpoint with a chosen pass value for a SuperAdmin account and then log in as that administrator.
title: Dolibarr ERP CRM before 24.0.2 Improper Authorization via Users REST API

desc: GPAC before 26.07.0 contains an invalid pointer free vulnerability in gf_sg_command_del() in src/scenegraph/commands.c that allows attackers to corrupt the heap via crafted XMT scene files. Attackers can supply an XMT-A file whose command field_ptr references the embedded new_node member, causing free() on an interior address and crashing MP4Box.
title: GPAC before 26.07.0 Invalid Pointer Free in gf_sg_command_del()

desc: GPAC before 26.07.0 contains a heap-based out-of-bounds read vulnerability in xmt_parse_mf_field() in loader_xmt.c caused by unchecked cursor advancement when splitting multi-value XMT-A fields. Attackers can supply a crafted XMT scene file opened with MP4Box to make xmt_parse_string() read past the heap buffer and crash the process.
title: GPAC before 26.07.0 Heap Out-of-Bounds Read via xmt_parse_mf_field()

desc: BISHENG before 3.0.0 contains an authentication bypass vulnerability that allows unauthenticated remote attackers to impersonate administrators by abusing a hard-coded default jwt_secret used by AuthJwt. Attackers can forge an HS256 token offline naming user_id 1 with the admin role, send it as access_token_cookie, and gain full administrative access to users, workspaces, knowledge bases and workflows.
title: BISHENG before 3.0.0 Authentication Bypass via Hard-coded JWT Signing Secret

desc: Radicale 3.3.0 before 3.8.3 contains an authorization bypass vulnerability that allows unauthenticated attackers to inherit group-based rights by reusing group memberships never reset between requests. Attackers can send credential-less requests after a group member logs in to read and write group-shared calendar and address book collections evaluated by the from_file rights backend.
title: Radicale 3.3.0 before 3.8.3 Authorization Bypass via Stale Group Memberships

desc: ModelScope 1.11.0 to before 1.40.1 contains an unsafe reflection vulnerability in the image-to-3D SyncDreamer pipeline that allows remote attackers to execute code via crafted model configuration. Attackers can publish a model whose syncdreamer.yaml target field makes instantiate_from_config() import and instantiate any class with controlled params, without an allowlist or trust_remote_code check, executing code when victims load it.
title: ModelScope 1.11.0 to before 1.40.1 Unsafe Reflection RCE via syncdreamer.yaml

desc: ioBroker.lovelace before 7.0.0 contains a path traversal vulnerability in the onCards() request handler that allows unauthenticated remote attackers to read arbitrary files via unsanitized dot-dot segments. Attackers can send crafted requests to the /cards/_static_/, /hacsfiles/, or /local/custom_ui/ routes to read files including ioBroker configuration and stored credentials.
title: ioBroker.lovelace before 7.0.0 Unauthenticated Path Traversal via cards Route

desc: GPAC before 26.07.0 contains a use-after-free vulnerability in load_xmt_done() in src/scene_manager/loader_xmt.c that releases references for duplicate node stack entries. Attackers can supply a crafted XMT-A scene file encoded with MP4Box to crash the process and potentially corrupt heap memory.
title: GPAC before 26.07.0 Use-After-Free via load_xmt_done() XMT Scene Loader

desc: GPAC before 26.07.0 contains a use-after-free vulnerability in xmt_parse_element() that allows attackers to corrupt memory by supplying XMT-A elements that define and use the same node identifier. Attackers can craft an XMT scene file processed by MP4Box so xmt_text_content() accesses the freed node, crashing the process and possibly corrupting heap memory.
title: GPAC before 26.07.0 Use-After-Free via xmt_parse_element() DEF/USE Handling

desc: GPAC before 26.07.0 contains a NULL pointer dereference vulnerability in xmt_parse_element() in src/scene_manager/loader_xmt.c that allows attackers to crash the process via ROUTE elements. Attackers can supply a crafted XMT-A scene file placing a ROUTE element before any scene command creates an access unit, crashing MP4Box during encoding and causing denial of service.
title: GPAC before 26.07.0 NULL Pointer Dereference via xmt_parse_element() ROUTE Handling

desc: GPAC before 26.07.0 contains a use-after-free vulnerability in xmt_parse_command() in loader_xmt.c that allows attackers to access freed memory via a dangling command buffer pointer. Attackers can supply a crafted XMT scene file whose Replace command frees a Conditional node, crashing MP4Box and potentially corrupting the heap.
title: GPAC before 26.07.0 Use-After-Free via xmt_parse_command() XMT Scene Loader

desc: Storyden before 1.26.17 contains a missing authorization vulnerability in the AccountRemoveRole handler that allows non-administrator users with MANAGE_ROLES to remove administrator roles. Attackers can send DELETE requests to the account roles endpoint to demote other administrators, potentially leaving the instance with no administrator.
title: Storyden before 1.26.17 Missing Authorization via AccountRemoveRole Administrator Role Removal

desc: Phoboslab pl_mpeg through commit c871f2b contains an integer underflow in plm_demux_seek() that allows attackers to trigger heap out-of-bounds reads via crafted MPEG-PS files. Attackers can supply a PES packet with payload under 6 bytes, wrapping the packet->length - 6 loop bound during force_intra seeking to crash applications.
title: Phoboslab pl_mpeg through commit c871f2b Heap Out-of-Bounds Read via plm_demux_seek

desc: GPAC before 26.07.0 contains a use-after-free vulnerability in xmt_parse_element() in src/scene_manager/loader_xmt.c that frees a node when a DEF attribute names a previously referenced undefined node. Attackers can convince a user to process a crafted XMT file with MP4Box, causing freed heap memory to be used and crashing the process.
title: GPAC before 26.07.0 Use-After-Free via XMT DEF Node Resolution

desc: GPAC before 26.07.0 contains a NULL pointer dereference vulnerability in xmt_new_od_link_from_node() in src/scene_manager/loader_xmt.c that allows attackers to crash the process. Attackers can supply a crafted XMT scene file with an MFURL object-descriptor link lacking an OD ID and name, crashing MP4Box for denial of service.
title: GPAC before 26.07.0 NULL Pointer Dereference via xmt_new_od_link_from_node()

desc: Frappe HR (hrms) before 16.9.0 contains a missing authorization vulnerability in the hrms.api.roster.get_events method that allows authenticated employees to view other employees' leave and shift data by bypassing User Permissions. Attackers with the Employee role can call get_events with empty filters for any date range to retrieve every employee's approved leave applications and shift assignments, including leave types, dates, shift locations and times.
title: Frappe HR (hrms) before 16.9.0 Missing Authorization via Roster get_events

desc: GPAC before 26.07.0 contains a type confusion vulnerability in the XMT scene loader that allows local attackers to corrupt memory by supplying unbalanced command buffer closing elements. Attackers can convince a user to open a crafted XMT-A file with MP4Box, causing xmt_node_end() to treat a GF_Command as an SFCommandBuffer and crash the process.
title: GPAC before 26.07.0 Type Confusion via XMT Command Buffer Unwinding

desc: GPAC through 26.07.0 contains a use of uninitialized variable vulnerability in xmt_parse_element() that allows local attackers to corrupt memory by supplying duplicate PROTO field names. Attackers can trick a user into opening a crafted XMT file with MP4Box, causing xmt_parse_sf_field() to write through an uninitialized pointer and crash the process.
title: GPAC through 26.07.0 Uninitialized Variable via Duplicate XMT PROTO Field Names

desc: GPAC before 26.07.0 contains a use-after-free vulnerability in the XMT scene loader that leaves dangling MFURL pointers when xmt_node_end() discards nodes. Attackers can convince a user to open a crafted XMT file with MP4Box, causing xmt_resolve_od_links() to access freed heap memory and crash the process.
title: GPAC before 26.07.0 Use-After-Free in xmt_resolve_od_links via Discarded XMT Nodes

desc: Flowise 3.1.3 through 3.1.4 contains an information disclosure vulnerability that allows unauthenticated attackers to read MCP server bearer tokens via the GET /api/v1/public-chatflows/:id handler. Attackers can use the leaked mcpServerConfig token on the POST /api/v1/mcp/:chatflowId route to invoke chatflows, bypassing API key protection and consuming the owner's model quota.
title: Flowise 3.1.3 through 3.1.4 MCP Server Token Disclosure via Public Chatflow Endpoint

desc: GPAC before 26.07.0 contains a stack-based buffer overflow vulnerability in gf_filter_pid_resolve_file_template_ex() in src/filter_core/filter_pid.c that allows local attackers to write past fixed GF_MAX_PATH stack buffers. Attackers can convince a user to segment a crafted NHML input referencing an overly long media file name with MP4Box -dash to crash the process.
title: GPAC before 26.07.0 Stack-Based Buffer Overflow via gf_filter_pid_resolve_file_template_ex

desc: GPAC before 26.07.0 contains an integer underflow in gf_xml_sax_parse_intern() in src/utils/xml_parser.c that causes a heap-based buffer overflow when completing partially buffered entities. Attackers can convince a user to process a crafted XML or XMT file with MP4Box, overflowing xml_sax_append_string() size arithmetic to corrupt heap memory and crash the process.
title: GPAC before 26.07.0 Heap Buffer Overflow via XML SAX Parser Entity Handling

desc:
Incorrect authorization in the credential loading logic in AWS Private CA Connector for Kubernetes (aws-privateca-issuer) before 1.12.0 might allow an authenticated remote user with permission to create namespace-scoped issuers to obtain certificates, including subordinate CA certificates, signed by another namespace's AWS Private CA with that namespace's stored AWS credentials, via a namespace-scoped issuer that references a credentials Secret in that namespace.



To remediate this issue, users should first copy any credentials Secret they intend a namespace-scoped issuer to use into that issuer's namespace and update the issuer's secretRef.namespace to match. Then, upgrade aws-privateca-issuer to version 1.12.0 or the AWS Private CA Connector for Kubernetes EKS add-on to version v1.12.0-eksbuild.1.
title: Incorrect authorization in credential loading in AWS Private CA Connector for Kubernetes (aws-privateca-issuer)

desc:
Incorrect authorization in the credential handling for namespace-scoped issuers in AWS Private CA Connector for Kubernetes (aws-privateca-issuer) before 1.12.0 might allow an authenticated remote user with permission to create namespace-scoped issuers to obtain certificates, including subordinate CA certificates, from every AWS Private CA and certificate template reachable by the controller's own AWS identity or by any IAM role that identity can assume. This happens because a namespace-scoped issuer that supplies no credentials, or sets only a role, falls back to the controller's own identity.



To remediate this issue, users should first update any namespace-scoped issuers that rely on the controller's identity to use their own credentials. Then, upgrade aws-privateca-issuer to version 1.12.0 or the AWS Private CA Connector for Kubernetes EKS add-on to version v1.12.0-eksbuild.1.
title: Incorrect authorization in credential handling for namespace-scoped issuers in AWS Private CA Connector for Kubernetes (aws-privateca-issuer)

desc: gosaml2 is a Pure Go implementation of SAML 2.0. Prior to 0.12.0, ValidateEncodedResponse() calls decryptAssertions() on an EncryptedAssertion before signature or content validation completes, and EncryptedAssertion.DecryptBytes() in types/encrypted_assertion.go slices decoded ciphertext without first validating the required nonce or initialization-vector length. A CipherValue shorter than the 12-byte AES-GCM nonce causes a slice-bounds panic, and an empty AES-CBC CipherValue passes the modulo block-size check before causing a slice-bounds panic at the 16-byte initialization-vector split. An attacker needs only the service provider's public certificate to wrap a symmetric key, and no valid identity-provider signature or relationship is required. The unrecovered panic can terminate the request goroutine or the service process. This issue is fixed in version 0.12.0.
title: gosaml2: Unauthenticated panic decrypting an EncryptedAssertion with a short or empty CipherValue

desc: WPS Limit Login (wps-limit-login) before 1.5.9.5 contains an improper access control vulnerability that allows unauthenticated attackers to bypass login lockout protections by keying the per-attempt login counter and lockout map on the raw, non-canonicalized IPv6 client address. Attackers controlling a routable IPv6 /64 prefix can send each login attempt from a fresh address within that range, preventing any counter from reaching the lockout threshold and enabling effectively unlimited brute-force password guessing against WordPress accounts.
title: WPS Limit Login < 1.5.9.5 Brute Force via IPv6 Address Rotation

desc: Kadence Security plugin for WordPress (better-wp-security) before 10.0.6.1 contains a brute-force protection bypass vulnerability that allows unauthenticated attackers to evade per-host login lockouts by exploiting IPv6 address handling in ITSEC_Lib::get_ip(), which keys failed-login counters on the full 128-bit IPv6 address rather than a /64 prefix. Attackers who control a routed IPv6 /64 can send each login attempt from a new address within that prefix, resetting the per-host counter each time to perform password spraying and username enumeration, and can similarly evade the auto_ban_admin immediate ban via address rotation.
products: nexcess:kadence security – password, two factor authentication, and brute force protection
title: Kadence Security WordPress Plugin < 10.0.6.1 IPv6 Lockout Bypass

desc: HomeBox is a home inventory and organization system. Prior to 0.27.0, the unauthenticated GET /swagger/doc.json endpoint copies the client-supplied X-Forwarded-Host header into the OpenAPI host field without requiring a trusted proxy or validating the value. An attacker can therefore make the served OpenAPI document direct Swagger UI Try it out requests to an attacker-controlled host. When a shared cache or CDN stores and serves that poisoned document to an authenticated user, Swagger UI sends the user's API requests and bearer token to the attacker, enabling disclosure and modification of the user's HomeBox data. Without a shared cache, the attacker can affect only the attacker's own response. This issue is fixed in version 0.27.0.
title: HomeBox: Unauthenticated X-Forwarded-Host injection into /swagger/doc.json lets an attacker control the host of the served OpenAPI spec

desc: HomeBox is a home inventory and organization system. Prior to 0.27.0, a HomeBox password change revokes the user's other session tokens but does not revoke the user's API keys, and API keys have no default API-key expiration. An attacker who has obtained an API key can therefore retain full API-level access after the account owner changes the password and can keep that access indefinitely unless the owner discovers and manually deletes the key by ID. Because the password change terminates other sessions, the surviving API credential can evade the owner's expected containment and detection. This issue is fixed in version 0.27.0.
title: HomeBox: API keys are not revoked on password change and never expire by default, so a leaked key survives full credential rotation

desc: FreeSWITCH is a Software Defined Telecom Stack enabling the digital transformation from proprietary telecom switches to a software implementation that runs on any commodity hardware. In 1.11.2 and earlier, rtp_common_read() in src/switch_rtp.c uses one session-wide autoadj_tally to learn RTP sources that differ from the address negotiated in SDP. An unauthenticated remote attacker who sends plaintext RTP during call setup can make packets from one or more non-advertised sources reach the threshold before the legitimate endpoint, causing FreeSWITCH to adopt the source of the threshold-crossing packet as the media peer. The attacker can then receive call audio, inject media, and deny media to the legitimate endpoint without being on the media path. FreeSWITCH 1.11.2 adds two opt-in controls, but both default to zero and the release remains affected unless both are configured before RTP session creation. This vulnerability is fixed in 1.11.2.
title: FreeSWITCH RTP Inject and RTP Bleed during auto adjustment, plus SRTP media denial of service

desc: fzf is a command-line fuzzy finder. Prior to 0.74.5, bin/fzf-tmux validates separately supplied layout sizes but does not validate attached -l and -u layout values before Bash arithmetic expansion, allowing command substitution in a crafted operand to execute as the invoking user during option parsing. The same validation failure lets space-bearing popup geometry options -x, -y, -w, -h, and -p reach an unquoted tmux popup option string and inject additional tmux flags. Exploitation requires less-trusted project configuration, a wrapper, or a plugin to supply the poisoned value and requires the victim to invoke fzf-tmux; normal values are usually trusted, and the script has been superseded by built-in tmux options. This issue is fixed in version 0.74.5.
title: fzf: Arbitrary command execution via bash arithmetic expansion on unvalidated layout size in fzf-tmux (-l/-u attached value)

desc: Forge, also called node-forge, is a native implementation of Transport Layer Security in JavaScript. Prior to 1.4.1, publicKey.verify() with the default RSASSA-PKCS1-V1_5 scheme in lib/rsa.js parses the recovered DigestInfo with the lenient BER parser asn1.fromDer() and validates its structure with digestInfoValidator without requiring canonical DER bytes. Non-minimal or indefinite lengths, malformed parameter values, and non-canonical object identifier encodings with padded subidentifiers or trailing bytes can leave attacker-controlled data inside an accepted DigestInfo. When the verifying RSA public key uses a low exponent such as e=3, an attacker can use that encoding slack to forge a signature without the private key. The same path is used by X.509 certificate and PKCS#7 signature verification. This issue is fixed in version 1.4.1.
title: Forge: RSA PKCS#1 v1.5 signature forgery via non-canonical DigestInfo encoding

desc: fzf is a command-line fuzzy finder. Prior to 0.74.5, trigger-driven zsh completion in shell/completion.zsh uses _fzf_feed_fifo to create a FIFO at the predictable shared path ${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/fzf-complete-fifo-$$ and continues after removal or creation errors. On a multi-user host, a local attacker can pre-create that path as a symlink so the victim's completion stream overwrites a victim-writable file, potentially enabling code execution when that file is later sourced. A pre-created FIFO can instead disclose a bounded stream of completion candidates or block completion. On default modern hosts, fs.protected_symlinks blocks the overwrite variant, and protected_fifos and protected_regular further limit the FIFO disclosure and blocking variants, so exploitation depends on the relevant kernel protections being disabled and on the victim invoking the affected completion. This issue is fixed in version 0.74.5.
title: fzf: Predictable FIFO path in zsh completion allows local symlink attack / arbitrary file overwrite as the victim user (_fzf_feed_fifo)

desc: FreeSWITCH is a Software Defined Telecom Stack enabling the digital transformation from proprietary telecom switches to a software implementation that runs on any commodity hardware. Prior to 1.11.2, after FreeSWITCH has learned and closed source learning for an RTP peer, read_rtp_packet() and rtp_common_read() in src/switch_rtp.c reject RTP from an unrecognized source only after packet classification and, for encrypted calls, SRTP processing. An unauthenticated attacker with UDP reachability to an active RTP or SRTP media port can sustain a foreign-source packet flood that occupies the media read path and prevents legitimate media from entering FreeSWITCH on calls that consume incoming media for relay or echo. The resulting one-way audio allows the affected endpoint to continue hearing the other party, but the other party loses that endpoint's audio, leaving SIP signaling established while the call is unusable for conversation. Transmit-only playback was unaffected in testing. A caller can learn the media port from the SDP answer, while a third party must first discover an active port, and no valid SRTP key is required. This issue is fixed in version 1.11.2.
title: FreeSWITCH late RTP/SRTP source validation permits one-way media starvation

desc: Effect is a TypeScript framework that consists of several packages that work together to help build TypeScript applications. Prior to 3.22.1, Schema.TemplateLiteral schemas containing at least two Schema.String spans compile each span to the ambiguous lazy wildcard [\s\S]*?. Decoding a non-matching untrusted string causes cubic regular expression backtracking, which can block the JavaScript event loop. The issue affects Schema.decodeUnknown, Schema.decodeUnknownSync, Schema.is, and consumers such as HttpApi and @effect/rpc payload decoding. This issue is fixed in version 3.22.1.
title: Effect: ReDoS in Schema.TemplateLiteral compiled regex

desc: Rucio is a scientific data management framework. From 1.14.0 until 35.9.1, 38.6.1, 40.4.2, and 41.1.1, validate_auth_token in lib/rucio/core/authentication.py does not distinguish short-lived SSH challenge nonces from authentication tokens stored in the same token table. An unauthenticated attacker can request /auth/ssh_challenge_token for an arbitrary account by supplying X-Rucio-Account, then present the returned X-Rucio-SSH-Challenge-Token as X-Rucio-Auth-Token to authenticate to other API endpoints as that account, including an administrative account. This issue is fixed in versions 35.9.1, 38.6.1, 40.4.2, and 41.1.1.
title: Rucio: Improper Authentication via SSH Challenge Tokens

desc: tiny-secp256k1 is a tiny secp256k1 native/JS wrapper. From 2.1.0 until 2.2.5 for tiny-secp256k1 and from 2.2.2 until 2.2.5 for @bitcoin-js/tiny-secp256k1-asmjs, the three-argument xOnlyPointAddTweakCheck path ignores the backend failure return from xOnlyPointAddTweak when a tweak produces the point at infinity. The shared X_ONLY_PUBLIC_KEY_INPUT buffer then still contains the original point, so a caller-controlled resultToCheck equal to that point can make the stale-buffer comparison return true even though no tweaked key exists. Protocols that rely on this helper to validate caller-controlled internal keys, tweaks, and comparison values can accept an invalid derived key. This issue is fixed in version 2.2.5.
title: tiny-secp256k1: Stale buffer after ignored wasm failure accepts invalid infinity tweak

desc: libp2p is a JavaScript implementation of the libp2p networking stack. Prior to 5.1.22, the @libp2p/crypto code reached by the default Identify service accepts a remote peer’s crafted publicKey before peer-id or signature verification and passes it through publicKeyFromProtobuf to the ASN.1 DER decoder. readLength in packages/crypto/src/keys/rsa/der.ts accepts long-form element lengths larger than the remaining buffer, causing readInteger and related readers to loop synchronously over an attacker-claimed length from a very small key blob. Because decoding occurs in one event-loop tick before the remotePeer equality check in packages/protocol-identify/src/identify.ts, the Identify timeout cannot interrupt it, allowing repeated unauthenticated connections to stall all timers and peers and transiently exhaust memory. This issue is fixed in version 5.1.22.
title: libp2p: ASN.1 DER decoder drives an unbounded synchronous loop on attacker-controlled length fields, stalling the Node event loop pre-auth

desc: Linkwarden is a self-hosted, open-source collaborative bookmark manager to collect, organize and archive webpages. Prior to 2.15.0, .github/workflows/check-branch.yml runs on the privileged pull_request_target event and interpolates the attacker-controlled github.head_ref source branch name unquoted into a run: shell script. An unauthenticated attacker can open a pull request from a fork with shell metacharacters in its branch name, causing arbitrary commands to execute in the base repository's privileged CI job before the branch comparison result matters. The job has access to GITHUB_TOKEN and any exposed secrets, allowing secret exfiltration and, when workflow token permissions allow repository writes, modification of repository content. This issue is fixed in version 2.15.0.
title: Linkwarden: Script injection via `github.head_ref` in privileged `pull_request_target` workflow (.github/workflows/check-branch.yml)

desc: A maliciously crafted DXF file containing crafted VBA project data, when parsed through Autodesk AutoCAD, can force an Out-of-Bounds Read vulnerability. A malicious actor can leverage this vulnerability to read sensitive data from process memory.
title: DXF VBA Project Out-of-Bounds Read in Autodesk AutoCAD

desc: A maliciously crafted DWG file, when parsed through Autodesk AutoCAD or processed by the installed DWG thumbnail handler, can force an Out-of-Bounds Write vulnerability resulting in heap corruption. A malicious actor can leverage this vulnerability to cause a crash or execute arbitrary code in the context of the current process.
title: DWG Parsing Out-of-Bounds Write in Autodesk AutoCAD

title: DGN File Parsing Heap-Based Buffer Overflow in Autodesk AutoCAD

A malicious actor can leverage this vulnerability to disclose NTLM authentication information from the current user.

A malicious actor can leverage this vulnerability to disclose NTLM authentication information from the current user.
title: DXF Scene-Background NTLM Authentication Information Disclosure in Autodesk AutoCAD

desc: matrix-hookshot is a Matrix bot for connecting to external services like GitHub, GitLab, JIRA, and more. Prior to 7.3.3, Hookshot can crash in src/Bridge.ts while processing a modern Matrix reply whose m.relates_to.m.in_reply_to.event_id identifies an event that the bot cannot read. Bridge event handling calls botClient.getEvent() for the parent event without catching the resulting M_NOT_FOUND error, allowing the rejected request to escape reply processing and terminate the service. This issue is fixed in version 7.3.3.
title: matrix-hookshot: Denial of service by replying to an event Hookshot can not read

desc: Filament Curator is a media picker plugin for Filament panels. From 3.0.0 until 3.7.9, 4.1.2, and 5.1.2, the Curator media panel accepts image/svg+xml files by default and stores and serves their markup inline without sanitization. An authenticated user with media-upload permission can store an SVG containing scripts, event-handler attributes, or javascript: URIs. When another panel user selects the View action, the SVG opens as a top-level browser document and its active content executes in the Filament application's origin. The script can perform authenticated same-origin actions as the viewing user and read same-origin data and script-accessible tokens. Panel thumbnails are not affected because they render through an image element that does not execute SVG script. This issue is fixed in versions 3.7.9, 4.1.2, and 5.1.2.
title: Filament Curator: Stored XSS via unsanitized SVG upload served inline

desc: ZoneMinder is a free, open source closed-circuit television software application. Prior to 1.38.4, any authenticated user can use the /api/configs/edit/{name}.json endpoint to modify protected configuration settings because ConfigsController::edit() does not enforce the System=Edit authorization requirement and its system-variable protection is ineffective. An attacker can set ZM_PATH_FFMPEG to a command-bearing value and trigger an exec() sink in web/views/image.php or web/includes/Event.php by requesting frame extraction. This permits arbitrary command execution with the privileges of the web server user and can expose private camera feeds, recordings, and database data or establish persistence. This issue is fixed in version 1.38.4.
title: ZoneMinder: Post-Auth RCE in config api

desc: A maliciously crafted DXF file, when parsed through Autodesk AutoCAD, can force a Heap-Based Buffer Overflow vulnerability. A malicious actor can leverage this vulnerability to cause a crash or execute arbitrary code in the context of the current process.
title: DXF File Parsing Heap-Based Buffer Overflow in Autodesk AutoCAD

desc: A maliciously crafted DWG file containing an attacker-controlled Excel Data Link connection string, when processed through Autodesk AutoCAD, can cause AutoCAD to execute an attacker-controlled program. A malicious actor can leverage this vulnerability to execute arbitrary code in the context of the current user.
title: DWG Data Link Exposed Dangerous Method in Autodesk AutoCAD

desc:
A time-of-check time-of-use (TOCTOU) race condition in the local port selection in AWS efs-utils (amazon-efs-utils) before 3.3.5 might allow a user that can start EFS mounts on a shared host to read and write a different Amazon EFS or S3 Files file system that is mounted on that same host, under that mount's IAM identity and access point, via concurrent mount operations. Only file systems mounted on the same host at the same time can be affected. Every mount involved was configured by the owner of that host, using credentials and access points that owner controls, against file systems whose owners had already granted that host access, so the issue grants no access beyond what the host was already permitted and does not cross AWS account boundaries unless the host's owner configured a cross-account mount. The practical risk is lateral access between workloads on the same host at the same time, for example one container reading another container's file system under that container's identity. The issue does not expose the other mount's IAM credentials or TLS session keys.



To remediate this issue, users should upgrade amazon-efs-utils to version 3.3.5 or later. Users of the Amazon EFS CSI Driver should upgrade to version 3.5.4 or later, and users of the Amazon EKS EFS CSI add-on should update to v3.5.4-eksbuild.1 or later.
title: Time-of-check time-of-use race condition in the local port selection in AWS efs-utils

desc: libp2p is a JavaScript implementation of the libp2p networking stack. Prior to 17.0.0, the @libp2p/gossipsub default configuration allows a connected remote peer to submit unsigned subscription RPC metadata for arbitrarily many distinct topic strings. handleReceivedSubscription in packages/gossipsub/src/gossipsub.ts creates a persistent topics-map entry for each accepted topic, while allowedTopics is unset by default, decodeRpc maxSubscriptions limits only one RPC rather than aggregate topic bytes, and peer scoring has no subscription-volume penalty. A single peer can therefore grow the topics map and committed heap toward out-of-memory conditions, and disconnecting additionally causes removePeer to scan all accumulated topic entries. This issue is fixed in version 17.0.0.
title: libp2p: gossipsub creates a permanent topics-map entry per distinct subscription with no cap in the default config

desc: ESP-IDF is the Espressif Internet of Things (IoT) Development Framework. Prior to 5.2.8, 5.3.6, 5.5.6, and 6.0.3, the Bluedroid BLE Mesh GATT server read handler bt_mesh_bta_gatts_cb in esp_ble_mesh stores a signed attribute-read callback length in an unsigned 16-bit variable. A negative ATT error code is therefore interpreted as a very large successful length and used for a memory copy from a small stack buffer into the GATT response structure. A remote attacker within Bluetooth LE range who can connect to an exposed PB-GATT provisioning or Mesh Proxy service can trigger a failed attribute read with a crafted request. On devices where the affected attributes are accessible without pairing, exploitation requires neither pairing nor user interaction; access requirements depend on device configuration. The resulting out-of-bounds read and stack-based buffer overflow corrupts the Bluetooth host task stack, causing a crash and device restart and potentially further memory corruption. The issue affects devices built with CONFIG_BT_BLUEDROID_ENABLED=y and BLE Mesh GATT enabled; the NimBLE host path is not affected. This issue is fixed in versions 5.2.8, 5.3.6, 5.5.6, and 6.0.3.
title: ESP-IDF: Buffer Overflow in BLE Mesh GATTS Read Callback Handler

desc: A maliciously crafted DWG file, when parsed by Autodesk AutoCAD, can trigger an Integer Overflow vulnerability in RLE bitmap decompression, resulting in an undersized heap allocation and subsequent heap buffer overflow. A malicious actor can leverage this vulnerability to cause a crash or potentially execute arbitrary code in the context of the current process.
title: DWG RLE Bitmap Integer Overflow in Autodesk AutoCAD

desc: ZoneMinder is a free, open source closed-circuit television software application. Prior to 1.38.4, detaintPath() in web/includes/functions.php can be bypassed with a PHP stream-wrapper path when sanitizing modal.php input. A remote unauthenticated attacker can submit such a path through the affected input and potentially read unauthorized local files through local file inclusion. This issue is fixed in version 1.38.4.
title: ZoneMinder: bypass detaintPath function

desc: code16 Sharp is a Laravel-based framework for building content-management and administrative interfaces. Prior to 9.23.0, an authenticated attacker can call the autocomplete API with a request endpoint that contains the configured remote endpoint only as a substring. The endpoint validation uses an unanchored regular expression, so a different internal route can satisfy the check and be invoked server-side through the autocomplete request. The vulnerable path uses SharpFormAutocompleteRemoteField::setRemoteEndpoint(); applications using SharpFormAutocompleteRemoteField::setRemoteCallback() are not affected by this endpoint-selection flaw. This issue is fixed in version 9.23.0.
title: code16/sharp: Server-side request forgery through an unanchored autocomplete endpoint check

desc: code16 Sharp is a Laravel-based framework for building content-management and administrative interfaces. Prior to 9.23.0, an authenticated attacker can submit an arbitrary PHP class name through the embed_key parameter to multiple embed API endpoints. The application passes the selected class to the Laravel service container, which invokes the class's __construct() method and recursively instantiates constructor dependencies, potentially causing unauthorized integrity or availability effects. The attacker cannot supply constructor parameter values or invoke an arbitrary method. This issue is fixed in version 9.23.0.
title: code16 Sharp: Arbitrary Class Instantiation via an API parameter

desc: Teable is an AI spreadsheet for business. Prior to release.2026-07-17T05-20-38Z.2264, the routes for PluginService::regenerateSecret and PluginService::delete carry no @Permissions decorator, and the methods omit plugin ownership checks. An authenticated attacker can directly target another plugin's identifier to rotate and disclose its OAuth secret or delete the plugin, including system plugins. Separately, PermissionGuard authorizes several nested API requests using a caller-controlled parent tableId, baseId, or spaceId, while the services resolve the requested child object only by its globally unique identifier. An authenticated attacker can provide a parent resource the attacker owns together with a victim's child identifier. ViewService::getViewById can then disclose another tenant's view configuration, embedded filter values, field layout, and shareId. DashboardService::updatePluginStorage and the view-position updatePluginStorage path can overwrite another tenant's plugin storage because the plugin installation is not rebound to the authorized base, dashboard, table, or view. This issue is fixed in release.2026-07-17T05-20-38Z.2264.
title: Teable: child-resource lookups permit cross-tenant data access and modification

desc: Under specific conditions, PingAuthorize in Gateway mode can continue an asynchronous upstream request after its 30-second gateway timeout. If the underlying keep-alive connection is reused for another request before the original response arrives, the late response can be written to the newer exchange. This could cause a subsequent caller to receive response data intended for an earlier request. This behaviour affects all releases and primarily risks unauthorized information disclosure between separate requests.
title: Cross-request response leakage in PingAuthorize after asynchronous timeout and connection reuse

desc:
This High severity Security Misconfiguration vulnerability was introduced in versions 10.2.0, 11.0.0, 12.0.0, and 12.1.0 of Bamboo Data Center.

This Security Misconfiguration vulnerability, with a CVSS Score of 8.9, allows an authenticated attacker to to get into the system utilizing loopholes exposed from security best-practices being overlooked.

Atlassian recommends that Bamboo Data Center customers upgrade to latest version, if you are unable to do so, upgrade your instance to one of the specified supported fixed versions:
 Bamboo Data Center 10.2: Upgrade to a release greater than or equal to 10.2.26

 Bamboo Data Center 12.1: Upgrade to a release greater than or equal to 12.1.13

 Bamboo Data Center 13.0: Upgrade to a release greater than or equal to 13.0.1

See the release notes ([https://confluence.atlassian.com/bambooreleases/bamboo-release-notes-1189793869.html]). You can download the latest version of Bamboo Data Center from the download center ([https://www.atlassian.com/software/bamboo/download-archives]).

This vulnerability was reported via our Atlassian (Internal) program.

	This BASM (Broken Authentication & Session Management) vulnerability, with a CVSS Score of 8.7, allows an unauthenticated attacker to perform actions as another user. 
	
	Atlassian recommends that Jira Service Management Data Center customers upgrade to latest version, if you are unable to do so, upgrade your instance to one of the specified supported fixed versions:
		
		* Jira Service Management Data Center 10.3: Upgrade to a release greater than or equal to 10.3.27
		
		* Jira Service Management Data Center 11.3: Upgrade to a release greater than or equal to 11.3.13
		
		
	
	See the release notes (https://confluence.atlassian.com/servicemanagement/jira-service-management-release-notes-780083086.html). You can download the latest version of Jira Service Management Data Center from the download center (https://www.atlassian.com/software/jira/service-management/download-archives). 
	
	This vulnerability was discovered by Nagli and reported via our Bug Bounty program

This High severity Stored XSS vulnerability was introduced in version 10.3.26 of Jira Core Data Center and Jira Software Data Center. 
	
	This Stored XSS vulnerability, with a CVSS Score of 7.4, allows an authenticated attacker to execute arbitrary HTML or JavaScript code on a victims browser. 
	
	Atlassian recommends that Jira Core Data Center and Jira Software Data Center customers upgrade to latest version, if you are unable to do so, upgrade your instance to one of the specified supported fixed versions:
		
		* Jira Core Data Center and Jira Software Data Center 10.3: Upgrade to a release greater than or equal to 10.3.27
		
		* Jira Core Data Center and Jira Software Data Center 11.3: Upgrade to a release greater than or equal to 11.3.13

	This vulnerability was reported via our Penetration Testing program.

The following description summarizes the vulnerability reported via our Penetration Testing program:

Crucible do not account for path parameters when validating protected paths requested through the static-resource route. A crafted path segment passes validation, after which Jetty removes the path parameter during dispatch and resolves the request to a protected resource. This can expose files under WEB-INF and permit direct invocation of admin-area JSPs outside the normal interceptor and administrative password checks. An ordinary authenticated user can exploit the issue, and unauthenticated exploitation is possible when anonymous access is enabled.

The SimpleSAMLphp SAML2 library is a PHP library for SAML2 related functionality. From 6.2.2 until 6.2.4 and 7.0.0-rc2, HTTPArtifact::receive() in src/Binding/HTTPArtifact.php verifies a signed outer ArtifactResponse but returns an unsigned embedded SAML Response before calling verifyMessageSignature(). The signed path verifies with the artifact issuer's metadata keys without requiring the embedded Response issuer to match that artifact issuer. In a multi-IdP federation, an attacker controlling one trusted IdP can therefore return a validly signed outer ArtifactResponse containing an unsigned Response that claims a different IdP, bypassing the binding's embedded-message authentication. End-to-end impersonation requires a service provider using HTTP-Artifact and a downstream consumer that relies on the binding to authenticate the embedded Response rather than independently requiring a signature. This issue is fixed in versions 6.2.4 and 7.0.0-rc2.
title: SAML2: Incomplete fix of CVE-2026-49283: unsigned embedded Response bypasses HTTP-Artifact signature verification (no embedded-Issuer binding)

desc: Teable is an AI spreadsheet for business. Prior to release.2026-07-21T11-27-40Z.2320, a registered user can supply path traversal sequences in the hash field accepted by POST /api/attachments/signature when the default local storage provider is in use. In apps/nestjs-backend/src/features/attachments/plugins/local.ts, LocalStorage.presigned uses the client-controlled hash as the storage filename, and LocalStorage.save resolves that path and copies the uploaded request body without calling assertPathWithinStorage on the write path. The read path uses the jail, but the write path does not, allowing the resolved destination to escape the configured storage directory. Because the backend container runs as uid 0, the attacker can write or overwrite arbitrary root-owned files, which can corrupt the instance or lead to root code execution. Object-storage deployments that do not use LocalStorage.save are not affected by this sink. This issue is fixed in release.2026-07-21T11-27-40Z.2320.
title: Teable: Arbitrary root file write via attachment presign hash path traversal

desc:
Allocation of Resources Without Limits or Throttling vulnerability in Plug.Parsers.MULTIPART in elixir-plug plug allows an unauthenticated remote attacker to exhaust memory via a multipart request body built from parts without headers, or from header lines without a name and a value. The parser charges the :length limit only with the name and value bytes of each part header and the bytes of each part body. The part delimiter, the header separator, and the line endings cost nothing.

In lib/plug/parsers/multipart.ex, Plug.Parsers.MULTIPART.parse_multipart_headers/5 keeps an entry for every part without a content-disposition header, together with its header list, until the whole body is read. A request made of such parts does not reach the limit at any size, and the parser process holds a multiple of the request size in memory until parsing completes. Any endpoint that uses Plug.Parsers with the :multipart parser is reachable.

This issue affects plug: from 1.13.0 before 1.20.4.
title: Multipart `:length` limit not charged for part and header framing in Plug.Parsers.MULTIPART
