desc: The Custom Block Builder  WordPress plugin before 3.0.0 does not properly deny unauthorised requests to its REST routes, as its permission checks return a non-error response that WordPress treats as granted, allowing unauthenticated users to execute arbitrary PHP code on the server.

desc: The Auth Armor  WordPress plugin through 1.0.3 does not require authentication on several handlers available to logged-out users, which leak the site's stored API credentials and allow an unauthenticated attacker to reset an administrator's enrollment and take over that administrator account.

desc: Zr.Admin.NET commit 85cff6a through commit eb9228a contains an insecure direct object reference vulnerability in GET /workflow/instance/{instanceId} that lets logged-in users view others' workflow instances. title: Zr.Admin.NET commit 85cff6a through eb9228a IDOR via Workflow Instance Endpoint

desc: Zr.Admin.NET commit 0ee1ab8 through commit eb9228a contains a path traversal vulnerability that allows any logged-in user to read arbitrary server files via the path parameter of /common/DownloadFile. title: Zr.Admin.NET commit 0ee1ab8 through eb9228a Path Traversal via DownloadFile

desc: Zr.Admin.NET commit af07ffc through commit eb9228a contains an insecure direct object reference vulnerability in SysProfileController.UpdateProfile that allows any authenticated user to modify other accounts via UserId. title: Zr.Admin.NET commit af07ffc through eb9228a IDOR via /system/user/profile

desc: Zr.Admin.NET commit 1845017 through commit eb9228a contains a missing authorization vulnerability in TasksController.Get that allows any logged-in user to read scheduled task details without the monitor:job permission. title: Zr.Admin.NET commit 1845017 through eb9228a Missing Authorization via /system/Tasks/get

desc: Zr.Admin.NET commit e6ceaf4 through commit eb9228a contains an insecure direct object reference vulnerability in FrontArticleController that allows authenticated users to change other users' article visibility and pin state. title: Zr.Admin.NET commit e6ceaf4 through eb9228a IDOR via front/article API

desc: In FRRouting, bgpd frees the sub-TLV chain of a Tunnel Encapsulation attribute (type 23) while routes stored by bgpd still point to it, if the attribute is received from a neighbor that has "soft-reconfiguration inbound" configured. A cache added to speed up attribute interning while processing the prefixes of an UPDATE checks whether an interned attribute set may be reused by comparing the parsed attributes with themselves, so the check always succeeds. Interning the parsed attributes for the Adj-RIB-In removes the Tunnel Encapsulation sub-TLVs from them, and the copy that bgpd then interns for the route reuses the cached attribute set, which still holds the sub-TLVs, without taking a reference on them. When the route is later replaced, withdrawn or cleared, for example when the session goes down, the sub-TLV chain is freed while still in use, and bgpd then reads it, decrements a reference count inside it and frees it a second time. In the reporter's build without AddressSanitizer this ended in an assertion failure in bgpd's memory accounting, aborting bgpd and dropping all BGP sessions on the router, and the neighbor can repeat it each time bgpd restarts. Because freed heap memory is written to and freed again, consequences beyond a crash cannot be ruled out. An established BGP session is required, and the attribute does not need to be malformed. bgpd processes attribute 23 from every neighbor, including eBGP neighbors, unless it is explicitly discarded, although RFC 9012 requires it to be filtered on eBGP sessions by default. Neighbors without "soft-reconfiguration inbound" are not affected.
title: frr: bgpd use-after-free of Tunnel Encapsulation sub-TLVs via the attribute intern reuse cache with soft-reconfiguration inbound

desc:
Dancer versions before 1.3400 for Perl pass unvalidated session ids from the session cookie to the session engine.

read_session_id returns the cookie value as the session id without checking its characters, and Dancer hands it to the session engine to load the session.

A remote attacker may cause path traversal or injection in a session engine that uses the id in a file path, cache command or query without checking it.
title: Dancer versions before 1.3400 for Perl pass unvalidated session ids from the session cookie to the session engine
